items.name: Fullscreen Video Hero Section with Overlay Content
items.promptText:
Create a full-viewport-height hero whose background is an autoplaying, looping, muted video that fills the entire section edge-to-edge. Layer a semi-transparent dimming gradient over the video so all foreground content remains readable.

**Top overlay** is a horizontal navigation bar absolutely positioned at the top of the section, sitting above both the video and the dimming layer.

**Bottom overlay** is a left-aligned or centered vertical stack anchored to the lower portion of the section, containing in order: a heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width; a horizontal row of two CTA buttons sitting side by side on the same baseline (a primary button on the left and a secondary button on the right), placed directly below the paragraph. All overlay content sits above the video and above the dimming gradient layer.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column stack for the bottom content, let the navigation bar compress or collapse into a mobile menu, and preserve reading order.

items.name: Centered Hero with Video Thumbnail
items.promptText:
Create a hero as one centered vertical stack inside a horizontally centered container with a bounded max width and generous vertical padding that increases at larger breakpoints. The full-width section background carries a very subtle repeating geometric pattern or grid texture anchored to one corner (kept low-contrast); all content layers above this texture. Stack from top to bottom, center-aligned:

- a large centered heading reading "Build with TypeUI" on its own line, set in a heavy weight with tight letter-spacing and a type size that scales up across breakpoints, constrained — together with the paragraph below it — to a 672px max-width centered column; - a centered supporting paragraph directly below the heading, sharing the same 672px max-width column so the line length stays readable; - a horizontal row of two CTA buttons sitting side by side on the same baseline, centered as a pair, separated from the copy above it by 32px of vertical spacing: a primary button on the left that pairs a small leading icon with its label, and a lower-emphasis secondary button on the right; - a centered social-proof row directly below the buttons, with 48px of margin above and 48px of margin below it (separating it from the buttons above and the video below). It is composed of two groups split by a thin vertical divider: on the left, a cluster of slightly overlapping circular user avatars (each with a thin buffer-colored ring); on the right of the divider, a compact rating mark or star-logo followed by a short line of text stating a review count with the numeric figure set in a stronger weight and higher-contrast color than the surrounding words; - finally, a large centered video placed directly below the social-proof row, presented inside a framed container — a thick padded bezel with rounded corners — capped at a moderate max width that is narrower than the container. The frame holds either an embedded video player or a static thumbnail image; if a static thumbnail is used, overlay a circular play button at the exact visual center of the image.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack, collapse the two CTA buttons into a vertically stacked pair, keep the social-proof groups and their divider centered and legible, and allow the framed video to span the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Split Hero with Stats and Login Card
items.promptText:
Create a hero laid out as a twelve-column grid on large 1280px width breakpoints on a full-width section surface that may include a very subtle geometric grid or dot texture in one area of the background. Horizontally center the grid within the section using a bounded max width with generous vertical padding so the pair does not stretch edge to edge on very wide viewports. Split the grid into a seven-column left region and a five-column right region. On large breakpoints vertically center the left column's content as a single unit so it aligns with the vertical midpoint of the login card, anchor the left content toward the start (push it away from the card), and push the card toward the end of its region.

**Left column** (the wider seven-column region) is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a prominent heading on its own line, set in a heavy weight with tight letter-spacing and a type size that scales up across breakpoints, constrained to a bounded reading width; a supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width; one primary CTA button composed of a small leading video-style icon beside a short label on its own line directly below the paragraph (inline, auto-width — not full-width). Below the button, place a horizontal row of three stat blocks on the same baseline with a 32px gap between each block, sitting above a full-width top divider that separates them from the content above. Each stat block is a horizontal pair, not a vertical stack: one large prominent numeric or short value on the left — set at a 30px type size in a heavy weight with tight letter-spacing — and a two-line descriptive label immediately to its right, with the value and the label vertically centered relative to each other so they share a common horizontal center line. This stat row is revealed only at the large breakpoint and is hidden below it.

**Right column** (the narrower five-column region) is a single rounded card with a light elevated treatment — a subtle border, a soft shadow, and a fill one step distinct from the section surface — capped at a fixed comfortable width and pushed to the end of its region on large breakpoints. The card wraps a single form. Inside the card, stack from top to bottom: a login title line on its own line at the top; a secondary line of copy directly below the title containing a short sentence with an inline "sign up" text link at the end of the same line; a horizontal row of two equal-width secondary buttons sitting side by side for third-party sign-in (each button is composed of a small provider icon on the left and a short provider label to the right of the icon, centered as a pair); a horizontal "or" separator made of a thin full-width rule with a centered short word breaking it; two labeled input rows stacked vertically (email and password) — each label sits on its own line directly above its input. Draw the input fills and their borders from the design system, set one step lighter than the card's background so the fields and their outlines lift off the card with clear, accessible contrast (colors must come from the design system, never hard-coded). Then a single horizontal row composed of a small square "remember me" checkbox — using the same fill and border as the inputs — paired with an inline label on the left and a "lost password" text link pushed to the right; one full-width primary submit button directly below; and a final short line of fine print centered or left-aligned at the bottom of the card containing a sentence with an inline "create account" text link.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the left column first and the login card directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order, and let the two third-party sign-in buttons stack vertically.

items.name: Centered Hero with Image Gallery
items.promptText: Create a hero as one centered vertical stack on a full-width section background. Stack from top to bottom: a large centered heading on its own line; a centered supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width; a horizontal row of two CTA buttons sitting side by side on the same baseline (a primary button on the left and a secondary button on the right), centered as a pair beneath the paragraph; finally, an asymmetric image collage placed directly below the button row inside a single bounding row. The collage is composed of one large image on the left occupying roughly two-thirds of the row width and two smaller images stacked vertically on the right occupying the remaining width (the two right images share the same total height as the single left image, separated by a small vertical gutter). On narrow viewports keep the heading, paragraph, and buttons in a single-column centered stack, and collapse the collage into a single vertical column of images in reading order (large image first, then the two smaller images beneath it).

items.name: Centered Hero with Dashboard Mockup
items.promptText:
Create a hero as one centered, text-centered vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable horizontal padding and vertical padding that increases on larger viewports.

**Copy region** is a centered vertical stack constrained to a maximum width of 768px and centered horizontally, containing in order: a small horizontal announcement pill rendered as a single rounded-full link on a soft brand-tinted background with a subtle brand border and tight inner padding, composed of a tiny solid rounded-full tag label on the left, a short sentence immediately to its right, and a trailing chevron icon at the end; a large bold heading on its own line directly below the pill that scales responsively from a moderate size up to a very large size on big screens; a supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a slightly enlarged body size.

**CTA row** sits directly below the copy region: a row of two CTA buttons centered as a pair—a solid brand-colored primary button with a short label only on the left, and a secondary neutral button on the right composed of a small leading video-style play icon paired with a short label.

**Mockup** sits directly below the CTA row: a single large dashboard mockup, centered horizontally and constrained to a maximum width wider than the copy container, wrapped in a thick neutral rounded border frame so it reads as a contained, framed product UI fully visible within the section (not clipped). Do not use a photograph or raster screenshot image for this mockup—it is strictly forbidden. Instead construct the mockup as a self-drawn vector/SVG illustration of an analytics dashboard using simple shapes and placeholder elements: a top app bar with a leading menu glyph, a long pill-shaped search field, and a few small trailing icons; a left sidebar of stacked navigation rows, each a small dot followed by a short muted bar; and a main content area containing a wide hero card with a multi-line smooth line/area chart, a row of smaller cards below it (a bar-chart card, an area-chart card, and a second bar-chart card), and a bottom row of compact list/stat cards made of short placeholder bars (include one small solid brand-colored button accent among them). Use neutral grays for structure with subtle borders and rounded corners so it reads as a clean, abstract UI rather than real content.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack, stack the two CTA buttons vertically at full width and switch them to a centered side-by-side row at the small breakpoint, and let the framed mockup span the available content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Centered App Hero with Phone Mockup and Social Proof
items.promptText:
Create a hero as one centered vertical stack on a full-width section background. Constrain the whole hero to a centered maximum content width with comfortable horizontal padding and generous vertical padding that increases on larger viewports.

**Copy region** is center-aligned and contains a bold heading on its own line, scaling responsively from a moderate size up to a very large size on big screens; allow the heading to read as two lines by forcing its latter part onto its own line at medium breakpoints and up. Directly beneath the heading place a centered supporting paragraph constrained to a comfortable reading width and centered horizontally.

**Badge row** sits directly below the paragraph, centered as a horizontal pair of app-distribution buttons on the same baseline with a comfortable gap. Make these buttons prominent and large: generous horizontal and vertical padding and larger label text than a default button, and render them in the brand color (solid brand-colored background at every breakpoint, never neutral or dark). Each badge is composed of a platform glyph icon on the left and, to the right of it, two stacked lines of label text: a small thin "download on" line on top and a larger bold store-name line directly beneath.

**Phone mockup** sits directly below the badge row with generous vertical spacing: one large centered portrait phone mockup rendered as a premium, realistic device frame—a thick dark bezel with strongly rounded corners, short side-button accents along the left and right edges, and a subtle drop shadow for depth. Inside, the screen has strongly rounded corners that clip a high-quality, premium-looking in-app interface filling the screen edge-to-edge (use either a polished app screenshot image or a richly rendered app-screen mockup built from layout primitives, charts, and controls).

**Social proof row** sits directly below the phone mockup as a single centered horizontal row split into two groups by a thin vertical divider. On the left, a cluster of slightly overlapping circular user avatars, each with a thin ring/border. On the right of the divider, a compact two-line stack: the top line is a row of star icons (with the final star muted to imply a partial score) followed by a numeric rating value on the same baseline; the bottom line is a short review-count sentence with the count figure emphasized.

On narrow viewports keep the column centered, allow the badge row and social-proof row to wrap into stacked arrangements while preserving reading order, and let the phone mockup scale to fit the content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Hero Section with Stats and Converter Panel
items.promptText:
Create a hero as one centered vertical stack inside a horizontally centered container with a bounded max width and generous vertical padding that increases at larger breakpoints. All content is center-aligned on a single full-width section background. Stack from top to bottom: top region, stat row, then converter panel.

**Top region** is a narrow centered column capped at a maximum width of 672px (tighter than the section container) containing a large centered heading on its own line — set in a heavy weight with tight letter-spacing and a type size that scales up across breakpoints — with a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath it at a comfortable reading width. The paragraph may emphasize a key inline figure or term by rendering it in a stronger weight and higher-contrast color than the surrounding text.

**Stat row** sits directly below the top region: a single horizontal row of five equal-width stat cards on the same baseline with a consistent gap between them. Each card is a compact outlined container with rounded corners and comfortable internal padding, composed of one prominent numeric or short value on its own line at the top and a short descriptive label directly beneath the value. Build the cards from the design system's brand color family: a soft, low-saturation brand tint for the fill and a subtle brand-toned border, with both the value and label text set in a noticeably darker, stronger shade of that same brand color so the type keeps strong contrast against the tint and the row reads as one cohesive, brand-colored set.

**Converter panel** sits directly below the stat row: one large full-width centered panel with rounded corners and a subtle border, styled as an interactive product mockup with generous internal padding. Optionally treat the panel interior with a faint grain, noise, or geometric grid texture layered behind the content (kept low-opacity) so it reads as a distinct product surface; all panel content must layer above this texture. Inside the panel, stack from top to bottom:

- a two-option segmented control (or tab pair) centered horizontally on its own line, where one option is selected by default and the other shows a clear hover/inactive state; - a centered, width-bounded body region holding two side-by-side field groups on the same baseline with an even gap between them. Each field group is a single combined input control: a small fixed leading affix box (carrying a unit icon or symbol) joined flush to the left edge of a numeric input that fills the remaining width, the two reading as one seamless control with a shared rounded outline. Provide an accessible label for each field even if it is visually hidden; - directly below the field groups, a short left-aligned helper line of fine print stating an indicative conversion rate or equivalence; - one primary CTA button at the bottom of the panel.

Toggling the segmented control swaps the order/contents of the two field groups (e.g. the two sides switch roles) while keeping the layout stable.

On narrow viewports reflow the five stat cards into a stacked or two-column wrapped layout, stack the two field groups vertically inside the converter panel, and keep the segmented control, helper line, and primary CTA centered and legible.

items.name: Full-Width Hero with Overlay and Metric Row
items.promptText:
Create a full-width hero composed of two nested layers. The outer layer is a full-viewport-height section with a uniform 24px inset padding on all sides so the inner hero reads as a framed panel. The inner layer fills the remaining height (full height minus the 24px padding) as a tall rounded panel whose background is a photographic image covering the panel edge-to-edge (cover, centered, no repeat). Apply a dark multiply-style blend over the image so foreground text stays readable; all hero copy uses light foreground color.

Inside the inner panel, place a relatively positioned full-width content container with generous padding and left-aligned stacks, with the whole content block vertically centered within the panel. **Main content block** contains, top to bottom: a heading on its own line at a 60px font size, constrained to a maximum width of 640px; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a 20px font size, also constrained to a maximum width of 640px, rendered in a muted tint of the light foreground (for example roughly 75% opacity); then a horizontal row of two CTA buttons on the same baseline directly below the paragraph—a solid primary button with a short label only on the left, and a secondary neutral outlined button on the right composed of a small leading video-style play icon paired with a short label.

**Metric row** sits below the main content block in normal document flow (not absolutely positioned), separated from the copy above by a top border and additional top spacing. On extra-large viewports and up, show a left-aligned horizontal row of three or four metric items on the same baseline with a 64px gap between items; hide the entire metric row on viewports below that breakpoint. Each metric item is a horizontal pair: one prominent numeric value on the left at a large semibold scale, and a two-line descriptive label immediately to the right on the same axis in the same muted light foreground tint as the paragraph (suitable for plan highlights, trust figures, or comparable copy).

On narrow viewports keep the heading, paragraph, and buttons in a single left-aligned vertical stack; stack the two buttons with full width on the smallest screens, then place them side by side on wider narrow breakpoints. Keep the metric row hidden until the extra-large breakpoint.

items.name: Editorial Hero with Featured Post and Article List
items.promptText:
Create a hero inside a centered page container with comfortable horizontal padding and generous vertical padding that increases on larger viewports. Lay the content out as a single column on small screens that becomes a two-column grid at the large breakpoint, with generous spacing between the two columns.

**Left column** is one featured article as a vertical stack with even vertical spacing between its parts, containing in order: a large wide image with rounded corners at the top spanning the full column width; a small category tag directly below the image, rendered as a compact rounded (not fully pill-shaped) chip with a soft tinted background, a subtle matching border, a tiny leading icon, and a short label; a prominent left-aligned headline on its own line directly below the tag; an author row composed of a small rounded avatar on the left with, to its right, a two-line stack of the author name on top and a publication date label directly beneath the name; a short excerpt paragraph below the author row; and a text-style "read more" link in the brand color composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon at the bottom.

**Right column** is a vertical stack of three compact article blocks with equal structure and even spacing between blocks. Each block is a vertical stack with even internal spacing composed of: a small category tag at the top (same compact rounded chip with a soft tinted background, subtle border, tiny leading icon, and short label), where each block's tag uses a different category accent color so the three tags read as distinct categories; a medium headline on its own line directly below the tag; a short excerpt paragraph directly below the headline (let the excerpts get progressively shorter down the list); and the same brand-color text-style "read more" link with a trailing arrow icon at the bottom of the block. These blocks have no image and no author row.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the featured column first and the list of three articles directly beneath it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Split Hero Section with Product Screenshot and Floating Cards
items.promptText:
Create a hero split into two columns on large breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding, with the left content column and the right media column vertically centered relative to each other.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a small inline trust/rating badge composed of a single star icon followed by a bold rating value and a short platform-name label on the same baseline; a large bold left-aligned heading directly below the badge that wraps across multiple lines, with two expressive accents woven into the headline text—a small cluster of slightly overlapping circular user avatars sitting inline within the heading flow, and one emphasized keyword rendered in the brand color and a contrasting display/accent style drawn from the design system's typography; a supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width; a single prominent primary CTA button in the brand color with a fully rounded shape and a short label, placed beneath the paragraph; finally, a left-aligned horizontal stat row of three stat blocks separated by generous spacing, each a compact vertical stack of one large bold number on top and a short muted label beneath. Separate this stat row from the CTA above it with a top border and 32px of padding above the row. The entire left column stack (badge, heading, paragraph, CTA, and stat row) is treated as one group that is vertically centered against the right image so its midpoint aligns with the middle of the image.

**Right column** holds one large portrait image card with strongly rounded corners that fills the column area, with several small floating UI cards overlaid around its edges: a vertical pair of stacked check-pill chips near the top-right (each a rounded-full chip composed of a small check icon and a short label); one brand-colored rounded stat card near the left edge showing a large number above a short two-line label; one light/white rounded card overlapping the lower-left of the image titled with a short label and containing a row of small outlined tag chips (each chip a short label with a leading plus sign); and one brand-colored rounded stat card near the bottom-right showing a large number above a short two-line label. Each floating card has a soft elevated shadow.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the content column first and the portrait image directly below it; keep the stat row beneath the CTA in reading order and let the floating cards maintain their relative positions on the image.

items.name: Split Hero Section with Feature Blocks and Portrait Image
items.promptText:
Create a hero laid out as a twelve-column grid on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with a bounded max width, generous vertical padding that increases at larger breakpoints, and a 32px gap between the left and right columns. Let the hero height follow its content rather than forcing a full-viewport height. Split the grid into an eight-column left region and a four-column right region (roughly a two-thirds / one-third split).

**Left column** (the wider eight-column region) is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a heading on its own line, set in a heavy weight with tight letter-spacing and a type size that scales up across breakpoints; a supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width; a horizontal divider spanning the full width of the column on its own line directly below the paragraph. Below the divider, place two side-by-side feature blocks separated by a generous horizontal gap (no divider between them), aligned on the same baseline. Each feature block is a vertical stack composed of a small leading icon at the top, a bold title line on its own line directly below the icon, a short description paragraph directly below the title, and one inline (auto-width, not full-width) CTA button at the bottom of the block: the left block uses a primary button that pairs its label with a trailing arrow icon, and the right block uses a lower-emphasis secondary button that pairs a small leading icon with its label.

**Right column** (the narrower four-column region) holds one tall portrait-oriented photograph with rounded corners, covering its area edge-to-edge. Keep the image inside the normal grid flow — it must never sit on top of or overlap the left content, and the 32px gap between the two columns must always be preserved on the image's left side. The image may read larger than its cell by extending only outward, away from the text: let it grow taller than the left content (about 30% beyond its height) and bleed toward the section's right/outer edge (about 25% past its column), clipped by the section's overflow. It never expands leftward into the gap or the left column. This image column is revealed only at the large breakpoint.

On viewports below the large breakpoint, collapse to a single column: hide the image column entirely and let the left content span the full container width. The two feature blocks stack vertically in reading order with comfortable spacing between them.

items.name: Map Contact Form With FAQ and Newsletter
items.promptText:
Create a long contact-support page made of three sequential modules inside a centered page container constrained to a 1280px width with comfortable side padding. Each module is separated from the next by generous vertical spacing.

**First module** splits into two columns on large breakpoints with equal column widths and a comfortable column gap.

The *left column* embeds an interactive map element that fills the column width and carries standard map chrome (zoom controls, a recenter button, and an optional directions entry point) showing a pinned business location.

The *right column* is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a headline on its own line inviting contact; a short supporting paragraph on its own line beneath the headline; single-line input fields stacked vertically for name, email address, phone number, and subject (each label sits above its input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker where applicable); a labeled multi-line message textarea directly below (the textarea carries a placeholder inviting the message body and allows vertical expansion); one full-width submit control beneath the textarea (text-style or solid, depending on the design system).

**Second module** splits into two columns on large breakpoints.

The *left column* is a left-aligned vertical stack containing: a small uppercase or label-style tag reading as an FAQ marker on its own line; a medium heading about remaining questions on its own line beneath the tag; a short supporting paragraph beneath the heading.

The *right column* is a vertical accordion list of question items. One item is expanded by default: its question title sits on its own line paired with a collapse affordance (chevron or minus icon) at the right end, and a paragraph answer is visible directly beneath the title. The remaining items are collapsed: each shows only the question title paired with an expand affordance (chevron or plus icon) at the right end, with no visible answer beneath.

**Third module** is a single centered vertical stack (no column split). It contains, in order: a small uppercase or label-style tag centered on its own line; a heading inviting newsletter subscription centered on its own line beneath the tag; a short supporting paragraph centered beneath the heading; a horizontal inline field group centered beneath the paragraph, composed of an email input (with placeholder) at the left and a compact circular or square send control carrying only an icon (arrow or send glyph) flush to the right of the input, both on the same baseline.

On narrow viewports, stack the two-column modules (first and second) into single columns with the left column content above the right column content; keep the third module centered.

items.name: Two-Column Contact Form Section
items.promptText:
Create a contact section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The two columns share the same vertical top alignment.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a main heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly below the heading (one to three lines covering technical issues, product feedback, and business-plan questions); then three stacked contact blocks separated by comfortable vertical spacing. Each contact block is a small horizontal row at the top pairing a small leading icon (keyed to the block theme) at the left with a bold short block title to the right on the same baseline, followed by body lines directly beneath the title that sit flush-left under the icon-and-title row. The first block titles an office or regional brand name with a full multi-line postal address as body; the second block titles information and sales with a single mailto sales email address as body; the third block titles support with a short descriptive sentence and a mailto support email address as body.

The **right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing a form whose fields read top to bottom in this order: a labeled email input row (the label sits above the input on its own line and pairs a short label text with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting a company email address); a labeled subject input row in the same shape directly below (the label pairs with an optional small circular question-mark information affordance to the right; the input carries a placeholder inviting a short subject line); a labeled multi-line message textarea directly below that (the label pairs with an optional small circular information affordance; the textarea carries a placeholder inviting the user to describe their inquiry); a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text states that submitting confirms reading and agreeing to the product terms of service (with the terms-of-service phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width primary submit button beneath the checkbox row whose label combines short send text and a trailing send-arrow glyph.

On narrow viewports, stack the two columns vertically with the contact-blocks column first and the form column second; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Multi-Band Newsletter Footer
items.promptText:
Create a footer section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding, composed of four distinct bands separated by generous vertical space.

**Newsletter band** — a centered vertical stack containing a large centered multi-line heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a single inline form row composed of a text input with a leading email icon and placeholder text on the left and a compact primary submit button directly to its right on the same baseline, centered as a pair beneath the heading.

**Sitemap band** — a horizontal row of four equal-width link columns on large breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each column is a left-aligned vertical stack containing a bold category heading on its own line at the top followed by a vertical list of plain text links, one per line, directly beneath the heading.

**Contact band** — a horizontal row of three contact blocks on the same baseline with consistent spacing between them. Each block is a horizontal composition of a small icon anchored to the left (representing the contact channel — phone, email, or location) and a text group to the right of the icon containing a short descriptive label on its own line and a prominent contact value directly beneath the label.

**Bottom bar** — a horizontal row spanning the full container width containing, from left to right: a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline; a centered copyright line; and a compact language selector composed of a small flag icon paired with a language label and a trailing chevron, anchored to the right end of the bar.

On narrow viewports stack each band's columns vertically in reading order; the newsletter form input and button stack vertically; the bottom bar elements center and stack in order: brand mark, copyright, language selector.

items.name: Contact Info Band With Centered Form
items.promptText:
Create a contact section in two vertical stages inside a centered page container constrained to a 1280px width with comfortable side padding.

**Top stage** is a three-column row on large breakpoints with equal column widths and comfortable column gaps. Each cell is a left-aligned vertical stack opening with a small icon at the top (keyed to the cell theme), followed by a bold short title on its own line, then body lines beneath the title: the first cell titles address with city or region name, street line, and postal code each on their own lines; the second cell titles company information with legal entity name and tax identifier each on their own lines; the third cell titles contact info with a short sentence about when to email on its own line and a single general mailto address on the next line. On narrow viewports stack the three cells vertically in reading order with generous spacing between cells.

**Bottom stage** is a form constrained to 640px width and centered horizontally beneath the info band. The form arranges personal fields in a two-column grid on wide layouts with comfortable column gaps: required first-name input on the left (label above with required-field marker; short example placeholder inside) and last-name input on the right (same shape); required email input on the left (label above with required-field marker; company-style placeholder inside) and phone-number composite on the right (a narrow country-or-region prefix select control beside a wider numeric input with spaced-digit placeholder, both on the same baseline); a country single-select on the left (label above; defaulting sensibly) and a language single-select on the right (same shape). Beneath the two-column grid, span a full-width labeled multi-line message textarea (the label sits above on its own line with a required-field marker and an optional small circular question-mark information affordance to the right; the textarea carries a placeholder and allows vertical expansion). Finish with a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text links to the terms of service, then one full-width primary submit button beneath the checkbox whose label combines short send text and a trailing send-arrow glyph.

On narrow viewports collapse the two-column field grid into a single-column stack, keeping the same top-to-bottom reading order.

items.name: Centered Contact Form Section
items.promptText:
Create a contact section as a single centered vertical stack on a 640px width page background, constrained to a comfortable reading max width and centered horizontally with generous side padding.

At the very top, place a main page heading on its own line, centered horizontally. Directly below the heading, place a short supporting paragraph (one to two lines) that references technical issues, product feedback, and business-plan questions, also centered.

Below the supporting paragraph, stack a vertical form whose fields read top to bottom in this order: a labeled email input row (the label sits above the input on its own line and pairs a short label text with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting a company email address); a labeled subject input row in the same shape directly below (the label sits above with a required-field marker; the input carries a leading pen or tag icon affordance and a placeholder inviting a short subject line); a labeled multi-line message textarea directly below that (the label sits above with a required-field marker and an optional small circular question-mark information affordance to the right of the label; the textarea carries a placeholder inviting the user to write their message and allows vertical expansion).

Finish the section with a horizontal flex row of two actions placed beneath the form, separated by a small inline gap: a secondary control at the left whose label combines a leading back-arrow glyph and short text that navigates back to the homepage; a primary control at the right whose label combines short send text and a trailing send-arrow glyph. Both controls sit on the same baseline and stretch to equal widths within the row.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column stack, let the form occupy full content width with comfortable side padding, and stack the two action controls vertically (secondary above primary) if horizontal space is insufficient.

items.name: Team Showcase With Contact Strip
items.promptText:
Create a contact-related page segment inside a centered page container constrained to a 1280px width with comfortable side padding. The segment is composed of two stacked zones: a team showcase zone at the top and a contact strip zone beneath it.

**Team showcase zone** is a single horizontal row (or wrapped grid) of member cards on wide breakpoints with equal card widths and comfortable gaps. Each card is a vertical stack containing, in order: a portrait media element at the top (square or slightly tall aspect ratio with rounded corners); an all-caps or emphasized name line on its own line directly below the portrait; a job-title line on its own line beneath the name; a short italic or quote-styled sentence about their craft on its own line beneath the title. On narrow viewports the row wraps into two columns or stacks into a single column.

**Contact strip zone** splits into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints directly below the team showcase with generous top spacing.

The **left column** is a two-by-two grid of equal destination cells with small gaps between them. Each cell is a vertical stack containing a small ordinal numeral in one corner (top-left or top-right), a platform icon centered or near-centered in the cell, and a short platform-name label at the bottom. The four cells represent major social or chat channels (for example an image-oriented network, a professional network, a messenger app, and a chat app).

The **right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a short imperative headline about working together on its own line; three single-line input fields stacked vertically (each with its label either above or rendered as a floating placeholder — for full name, phone number, and email address respectively); a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label referencing agreement with a linked privacy policy (the privacy-policy phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width prominent submit button beneath the checkbox row whose label combines short send text and a trailing directional-arrow glyph.

On narrow viewports, stack the two columns vertically with the social grid first and the form column second; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Alternating Portfolio Case Studies
items.promptText:
Create a portfolio section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a horizontal row composed of a left-aligned heading on the left and one compact outlined button (a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon) anchored to the right, both sitting on the same baseline. Directly below the heading, place a left-aligned supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the header, stack three case-study entries vertically with generous spacing between them. Each entry is a two-column split on large 1280px width breakpoints with consistent gutters. Alternate the column positions so the first entry places the image on the left and the content on the right, the second entry places the content on the left and the image on the right, and the third entry repeats the first arrangement.

Inside each **image column**, place one large image with rounded corners that fills the column area.

Inside each **content column**, stack a left-aligned vertical composition from top to bottom: a prominent project title on its own line; a text link on its own line directly below the title composed of a URL label paired with a small trailing external-link icon; a supporting paragraph directly below the link at a comfortable reading width; a horizontal row of small tech-stack or tool icons sitting side by side on the same baseline; and a text-style link at the bottom composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

On narrow viewports, stack each entry as a single column with the image first and the content directly below it; preserve all internal reading order.

items.name: Centered Portfolio Card Grid
items.promptText:
Create a portfolio section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the header block, place a three-column by two-row grid of six equal-width cards with consistent gutters between columns and rows. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a brand logo or mark centered on its own line; a project title centered on its own line directly below the logo; a short centered description paragraph directly below the title; and a text-style link at the bottom of the card composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon inside a compact outlined container.

On narrow viewports, collapse the grid stepwise from three columns to two, then to a single column on the narrowest breakpoints; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Alternating Detailed Portfolio Case Studies
items.promptText:
Create a portfolio section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width. Directly below the paragraph, place a horizontal row of two text links sitting side by side on the same baseline, each link composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, stack several detailed case-study entries vertically with generous spacing between them. Alternate the entry layouts so consecutive entries feel visually distinct.

**Full-width entry** — stack from top to bottom: a single large full-width screenshot or product image spanning the container width; a horizontal row of small tech-stack or tool icons sitting side by side on the same baseline directly below the image; a prominent left-aligned project title on its own line directly below the icon row; a multi-paragraph left-aligned description at a comfortable reading width directly below the title; and a text-style link at the bottom composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

**Split entry with stats** — a two-column split on large 1280px width breakpoints. One column is a left-aligned vertical stack containing: a prominent project title on its own line; a text link on its own line directly below the title composed of a URL label paired with a small trailing external-link icon; a multi-line description paragraph directly below the link; a horizontal row of small tech-stack or tool icons; and a text-style link composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon. The other column holds one large image with rounded corners. Below the two-column block, place a horizontal row of stat blocks on the same baseline, each stat composed of one large prominent number on its own line at the top and a short descriptive label directly beneath the number. Alternate which side carries the image and which carries the content between consecutive split entries.

**Split entry with image collage and stats** — similar to the split entry above, but the image column holds a small collage of two or three images arranged in an overlapping composition with rounded corners, and the stat row beneath the two-column block uses more items (up to six) spread across the full container width.

On narrow viewports, stack all entry elements in a single column in reading order: image or collage first, then title, description, icons, links, and stats; preserve all internal reading order within each entry.

items.name: Stacked Portfolio Image Overlay Cards
items.promptText:
Create a portfolio section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered text link composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, stack three full-width cards vertically with consistent spacing between them. Each card is a large rounded container whose background is a full-bleed photographic or screenshot image covering the entire card area edge-to-edge. Layer a semi-transparent dimming gradient over the image so all foreground content remains readable. Anchor all foreground content to the lower-left area of the card with comfortable inset padding.

Inside each card overlay, stack from bottom to top (visually anchored to the card's lower-left corner): a short description paragraph on its own line; a prominent project title on its own line directly above the description; a horizontal row of small tech-stack or tool icons sitting side by side on the same baseline directly above the title.

On narrow viewports, keep the same stacked full-width card layout; reduce card height proportionally and ensure the overlaid text and icons remain legible with sufficient contrast against the dimmed background.

items.name: Featured Portfolio Asymmetric Grid
items.promptText:
Create a portfolio section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width. Directly below the paragraph, place a horizontal row of two text links sitting side by side on the same baseline, each link composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header block, place a three-column asymmetric grid on large 1280px width breakpoints. The **left column** and the **right column** are narrow and equal in width; each stacks two small cards vertically with consistent spacing between them. The **center column** is wider and holds a single tall featured card whose height spans both rows of the side columns.

Inside each **small card**, stack from top to bottom: a brand logo or mark centered on its own line; a project title centered on its own line directly below the logo; a short centered description paragraph directly below the title; and a text-style link at the bottom of the card composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

Inside the **featured center card**, stack from top to bottom: a brand logo or mark centered on its own line; a project title centered on its own line directly below the logo; a two-column checklist of service or scope labels (each row composed of a small circular check icon at the left and a short label to its right on the same baseline); and a horizontal row of two action elements at the bottom — a text-style link on the left composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon, and a primary button on the right composed of a small leading icon and a short label.

On narrow viewports, stack all five cards in a single column with the featured card first, followed by the side cards in left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order.

items.name: Pricing Cards with Seat Slider
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Directly below the paragraph, place one wide control card spanning the full container width with rounded corners and a light border. Inside the control card, arrange a horizontal row containing: a short label on the left (e.g. "Number of seats"), a horizontal range slider track in the middle whose thumb position reflects the current value, and the current numeric value displayed in a small inline container on the right — all three elements sitting on the same baseline.

Below the control card, place a horizontal row of three pricing cards of equal width with consistent gutters between them. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a plan name on its own line; a short single-line description directly below the name; a large dominant price that updates dynamically with the slider value, paired with a small "/month" suffix on the same baseline to the right of the amount; one full-width primary call-to-action button; and a vertical list of feature rows (each row composed of a small circular check icon at the left and a short feature label to its right on the same baseline).

On narrow viewports the slider control card sits above the plan cards on its own line (the label, slider, and value may stack vertically within the card), and the three cards stack vertically in their original left-to-right order; each card stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Split Pricing Card with Feature Grid
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block on a full-width background inside a max-width container. At the top, place a full-width left-aligned heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a left-aligned supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the heading block, place one full-width bordered card whose interior is split into two columns on large 1280 px width breakpoints with a thin vertical divider running between them.

**Left column** of the card is a vertically centered, padded vertical stack containing, in order: a plan name on its own line; a short single-line description directly below the name; a very large dominant price paired with a small "/month" suffix sitting on the same baseline to the right of the amount; and one full-width primary call-to-action button whose label text is centered within the button.

**Right column** of the card contains a two-column grid of short feature labels (roughly five rows by two columns of items); each cell is composed of a small circular check icon anchored at the left and a short feature label to its right on the same baseline.

Below the card, centered directly beneath it on its own line, place a single small helper-text line (e.g. a money-back guarantee notice) at a muted weight.

On narrow viewports the card's two columns stack vertically with the plan-and-price column first and the feature grid second; the helper line remains centered below.

items.name: Pricing Table with Billing Toggle
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a full-width left-aligned heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a left-aligned supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Directly below the paragraph, place a horizontal two-option toggle control (one segment labeled "Monthly", the other labeled "Yearly") with one segment visually selected at a time. Anchored to the right of the "Yearly" segment on the same baseline, place a small pill badge displaying a savings percentage (e.g. "Save X%").

Below the toggle, place one full-width bordered card surface whose interior is divided into three equal-width plan columns separated by thin vertical dividers (the three plans live inside a single shared card, not as three separate cards). Inside each column, stack from top to bottom: a plan name on its own line; a short single-line description directly below the name; a large dominant price with a billing-cadence suffix (e.g. "/month" or "/year") on the same baseline to the right of the amount; a secondary line of smaller copy directly below the price showing the alternate-cadence price; one full-width primary call-to-action button; and a vertical list of feature rows (each row composed of a small circular check icon at the left and a short feature label to its right on the same baseline).

On narrow viewports the toggle stays centered on its own line, and the three plan columns break out of the shared card and stack vertically as individual cards in their original left-to-right reading order; each card stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Selectable Pricing Cards with Plan Picker
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section split into two columns on large 1280 px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large left-aligned heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly below the heading in a muted body weight at a comfortable reading width; a short vertical list of three value- proposition rows (each row composed of a small tinted icon container at the left and a concise label to its right on the same baseline); and a social-proof row placed below the value list after extra vertical space, combining a tight horizontal cluster of overlapping small circular avatar thumbnails on the left with a single line of copy to their right containing a credible global usage count.

**Right column** contains a vertical stack of three full-width plan cards that behave as a radio group (exactly one plan is selected at a time). Each card is a rounded surface with generous padding. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a top row pairing the plan name (bold, left-aligned) with a circular radio indicator anchored in the top-right corner, and a single-line description directly below the name; a thin horizontal divider spanning the full card width; a dominant price line with a large numeric amount and a small "/month" suffix aligned on the same baseline to the right of the amount; and a short paragraph directly below the price summarizing what the plan includes (storage tiers, scope, or similar). Unselected cards use a plain surface with a hairline neutral border and an empty radio ring; the selected card uses a very light tinted background, a stronger accent border, a filled radio dot, and the price text rendered in the accent color.

Below the card stack, place a footer row spanning the right column width: on the left, a compact currency selector styled as a small dropdown (e.g. "$ USD" with a trailing chevron); on the right, two actions sitting side by side — a ghost or soft-outlined secondary button for terms (label may include a trailing arrow) and a solid primary button for checkout (label may include a trailing arrow), with the primary sized to its label rather than stretched full width.

On narrow viewports, stack the two columns vertically in reading order with the marketing block first and the selectable cards plus footer controls second; preserve tap targets and clear selected-versus-unselected visual states throughout.

items.name: Two Pricing Cards with Highlighted Plan
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the heading block, place exactly two pricing cards side by side, each taking half of the container width with a consistent gutter between them. The right card is the highlighted plan and carries a small "Recommended" pill badge anchored to the center of its top edge. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a plan name on its own line; a short single-line description directly below the name; a large dominant price with a small "/month" suffix on the same baseline to the right of the amount; one full-width primary call-to-action button (the highlighted card's button may use a contrasting treatment); a thin horizontal divider spanning the full card width; and a vertical list of feature rows (each row composed of a small circular check icon at the left and a short feature label to its right on the same baseline).

On narrow viewports the two cards stack vertically in their original left-to-right order; each card stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Tabbed Pricing Card
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Directly below the paragraph, place a horizontal row of plan tabs centered on the page (one short text label per plan). The active tab is indicated by a short underline flush with the bottom edge of the tab row and stronger typographic emphasis than inactive tabs. Below the tab row, show one large bordered card with rounded corners whose interior content swaps based on the currently active tab.

Inside the card, split into two equal-width columns on large 1280 px width breakpoints.

**Left column** is a padded vertical stack containing, in order: the current plan name on its own line; a very large dominant price on a line directly below the name; a single secondary line of billing-detail copy directly below the price (e.g. "billed annually"); one full-width primary call-to-action button; and directly below it one full-width secondary call-to-action button whose label begins with a small leading icon glyph followed by short action copy.

**Right column** contains a vertical list of feature rows with comfortable vertical spacing; each row is composed of a small circular check icon anchored at the left and a feature label to its right on the same baseline, where inline segments of the label may read as emphasized (e.g. numeric limits or durations called out within the same line).

Below the main card, separated from it by a comfortable gap, place a thin full-width footer bar with rounded corners and a light border. Inside the bar, center a horizontal cluster of two text links separated by a thin vertical divider; each link begins with a small leading icon glyph followed by short label copy.

On narrow viewports the tab row scrolls horizontally or wraps, the card's two columns stack vertically with the pricing column first and the feature list second, and the footer links stack or wrap while staying horizontally centered.

items.name: Three Pricing Cards
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block on a full-width background inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered section heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the heading block, place a horizontal row of three pricing cards of equal width with consistent gutters between them. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a plan name on its own line; a single-line plan description directly below the name; a large dominant price paired with a small "/month" suffix sitting on the same baseline to the right of the amount; a thin horizontal divider spanning the full card width; a vertical list of feature rows (each row composed of a small circular check icon anchored at the left and a short feature label to its right on the same baseline); and one full-width primary call-to-action button whose label text is centered within the button, placed at the bottom of the card.

On narrow viewports the three cards stack vertically in their original left-to-right reading order; each card stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Pricing Table with Filters
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the paragraph, center a compact control row on its own line: a short question label followed by two dropdown fields sitting side by side (for example seat or user count in the first, billing cadence in the second); each dropdown shows a small leading icon or text prefix where helpful and a chevron anchored at the trailing edge.

Below the controls, place three equal-width tier columns in one horizontal row. Inside each column, stack from top to bottom: the plan name on its own line; a large dominant price with a small "/month" suffix sitting on the same baseline to the right of the amount; one full-width call-to-action button (the highlighted middle column uses the solid primary treatment while side columns use a secondary treatment); and a text link on its own line directly below the button whose label includes a small trailing arrow glyph. The middle column carries a small "Most popular" pill badge centered on its top edge and reads as the featured tier.

Directly beneath the three tier headers — without a visual break that separates the grid — continue into one wide comparison table whose columns align vertically with the three tiers above. The middle table column shares the same highlighted band as the middle tier (a continuous outer border and subtle fill running from the tier row through every table row beneath it). The table body is grouped into category sections: each section opens with a full-width category title row spanning all columns on its own line, followed by feature rows. Each feature row contains a feature label in the first column (with an optional small hint icon beside the name and an optional inline text link in parentheses after the label); the three plan columns each hold either a small positive check icon or a small negative cross icon, vertically centered within the row.

On narrow viewports the tier row stacks vertically or becomes horizontally scrollable, the control row wraps its two dropdowns vertically, and the comparison table either gains a horizontal scroll affordance or collapses into one stacked card per plan that repeats the feature list with the same icons.

items.name: Four Pricing Cards with Enterprise Option
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the heading block, place a horizontal row of four cards of equal width with consistent gutters between them. The first three cards are standard pricing cards; inside each, stack from top to bottom: a plan name on its own line; a short single-line description directly below the name; a large dominant price with a small "/month" suffix on the same baseline to the right of the amount; one full-width primary call-to-action button; and a vertical list of feature rows (each row composed of a small circular check icon at the left and a short feature label to its right on the same baseline).

The fourth card is an enterprise contact card whose composition differs: stack from top to bottom: a plan name on its own line; a longer descriptive paragraph (occupying the space where a price would normally sit) explaining the tier's scope; one full-width call-to-action button whose label reads as a contact prompt (e.g. "Contact sales"); and a short vertical list of high-level feature labels (each on its own line, without leading check icons).

On narrow viewports all four cards stack vertically in their original left-to-right order; each card stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Pricing Comparison Table
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the heading block, place one wide comparison table spanning the full container width. The first row of the table is a sticky header row containing an empty top-left cell followed by one column header per plan; inside each header cell, stack from top to bottom: the plan name on its own line, the dominant price on a line directly below (large numeric amount with a small billing-cadence suffix on the same baseline), and one call-to-action button at the bottom of the cell whose label text is centered within the button.

The table body is grouped into category sections. Each section opens with a full-width category title row spanning all columns on its own line, followed by feature rows. Each feature row contains a feature label in the left-most column; for every plan column the cell holds either a small positive check icon, a small neutral dash icon, or a short text value — all vertically centered within the row.

On narrow viewports the table collapses into one stacked card per plan, each card repeating its own heading information and the full feature list with the same icons; cards stack vertically in the original column order.

items.name: Featured Middle Pricing Card
items.promptText:
Create a pricing section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the heading block, place a horizontal row of three pricing cards of equal width. The middle card is visually elevated (taller than the two side cards, sitting on a distinct filled background) and carries a small "Most popular" pill badge anchored to the center of its top edge. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a plan name on its own line; a short single-line description directly below the name; a large dominant price with a small "/month" suffix on the same baseline to the right of the amount; one full-width primary call-to-action button (the middle card's button may use a contrasting treatment to reinforce its featured status); and a vertical list of feature rows (each row composed of a small circular check icon at the left and a short feature label to its right on the same baseline).

On narrow viewports the three cards stack vertically with the highlighted middle card preserving its position in the sequence; each card stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Partner Logo Matrix Section
items.promptText:
Create a customer logos section as one centered vertical stack inside a page-width container with comfortable side padding.

The **header block** sits at the top of the stack, centered horizontally, and contains in order from top to bottom: a primary heading on its own line; one supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading, held at a restrained max width; and below the paragraph a single horizontal row of two text links sitting side by side with a small gap between them (each link label includes a trailing arrow character at the end of the wording).

Leave substantial vertical space beneath the header block, then present a single rectangular grid of exactly twelve partner cells arranged in three rows and four columns, centered as a whole and capped at a comfortable max width that keeps each cell legible. Lay the grid out so adjacent cells share continuous horizontal and vertical dividing rules, reading as one aligned matrix rather than detached floating cards.

Inside **every cell**, stack three pieces in order from top to bottom: the partner mark centered horizontally within the cell; a single short metadata line directly under the mark providing partnership context (for example how long the relationship has run); and at the bottom of the cell a compact control for opening the partner's site whose label text is paired with a small external-link affordance icon to the right. Use the same stacking order, alignment, and internal padding in each cell so rows and columns line up cleanly across the matrix.

On narrow viewports reflow the matrix into fewer columns (for example two columns or one) while preserving reading order left-to-right then top-to-bottom. If collapsing to a single column would crowd the per-cell stack, introduce horizontal scrolling for the grid container only. Keep the header block centered above the grid and allow the link row to wrap onto a second line when space is tight.

items.name: Compact Customer Logo Ribbon
items.promptText: Create a customer logos section that reads as one shallow horizontal band spanning the full content width with comfortable vertical padding above and below the marks. Inside the band, center a single horizontal row of partner marks with uniform spacing between each mark; do not place any heading or supporting copy inside the band itself (any heading may sit above the band as a sibling block in the parent layout if needed). Set the band height to fit the tallest mark plus comfortable vertical padding so the strip reads as a compact ribbon rather than a tall hero region. On narrow viewports the marks wrap into additional centered rows inside the same band while maintaining even horizontal spacing and consistent vertical gaps between wrapped lines.

items.name: Staggered Integration Logo Lanes
items.promptText:
Create a customer logos section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order from top to bottom: a multi-line primary heading on its own line that may include an inline segment naming the product or integration surface being promoted; one supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading describing automating or connecting existing tools; and a single full-width primary call-to-action control whose label invites exploration of integrations (the label text ends with a trailing arrow or chevron character after the wording).

The **right column** presents a field of partner marks organized as several parallel vertical lanes of tall portrait-oriented cells. Each lane stacks multiple cells one above another, and each cell holds exactly one centered partner mark. Offset neighboring lanes vertically so cells in adjacent columns do not share the same horizontal baselines, producing a staggered brick rhythm instead of a flush rectangular grid. Allow the composition to clip or fade at the top and along one outer side so the field implies more marks continue beyond the visible frame without listing every partner in view.

On narrow viewports stack the columns with the heading, paragraph, and CTA first and the staggered logo field second; reduce the lane count and simplify vertical offsets while preserving one mark per cell and maintaining the staggered rhythm where space allows.

items.name: Customer Case Study Card Grid
items.promptText:
Create a customer logos section that presents customers as individual cards rather than a bare logo strip, arranged inside a page-width container with comfortable side padding. Use a responsive grid of equal-width cards on large 1280px width breakpoints (for example three or four cards per row).

Inside **each card**, stack from top to bottom: the customer mark centered horizontally at the top of the card; a one-line company name or story title on its own line directly beneath the mark; a single short supporting sentence below the title providing context for the case study; and at the bottom of the card a text link whose label includes a trailing arrow character, pointing to the full case study. Limit each card to one primary mark so the section stays scannable and visually uniform.

On narrow viewports the cards reflow into a single column, each card occupying the full content width with comfortable side padding; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Centered Customer Logo Band
items.promptText: Create a customer logos section as one centered vertical stack inside a page-width container with comfortable side padding. At the very top, place a short centered kicker line on its own row naming the social-proof intent (for example a sentence stating that the product is trusted by teams worldwide). Below the kicker, leave a small vertical gap, then center a single horizontal flex row of exactly six partner marks or logotypes that share one visual weight; space the marks with even horizontal gaps so they read as one unified band. No secondary heading is required unless you add a very small optional sub-line directly beneath the kicker on its own centered row. On narrow viewports the mark row wraps into additional centered rows while keeping even horizontal spacing between items and consistent vertical gaps between wrapped lines.

items.name: Two-Column Customer Proof Section
items.promptText:
Create a customer logos section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order from top to bottom: a prominent heading on its own line that may open with a large numeric or shorthand claim about client volume or reach; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading that contrasts or enumerates audiences served; a single horizontal band split into two equal columns where each column holds one stat block (each stat block stacks from top to bottom: a small pictogram, a concise one-line title directly below the pictogram, and one short supporting sentence beneath the title); and below the stat band, one full-width primary call-to-action control whose label invites deeper exploration of work or proof and may pair with a small leading icon to the left of the label text.

The **right column** contains only a two-by-two grid of four partner cells whose interior dividing rules (one vertical rule and one horizontal rule crossing at the center) make the block read as one tight quad. Inside each cell, stack from top to bottom: a centered partner mark; a single short partnership metadata line directly under the mark (for example how long the relationship has run); and at the bottom of the cell a compact "visit website" control whose label pairs with a small external-link affordance icon to the right.

On narrow viewports stack the columns with the left narrative-and-stats column first and the partner quad second; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Vertical-Rule Logo Matrix
items.promptText:
Create a customer logos section as one rectilinear grid inside a page-width container with comfortable side padding, arranged on large 1280px width breakpoints with exactly four columns and three rows for twelve partner entries in reading order left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Draw thin vertical dividing rules between whole columns so the grid reads as four lanes separated by hairlines; do not run horizontal rules between rows, relying instead on consistent vertical spacing and uniform row padding to separate the three tiers visually.

Within **each cell**, treat the partner identity as a single horizontal unit: a compact brand mark or pictogram on the leading side and the company wordmark or name on the trailing side, aligned on the same baseline as one pair. Center that icon-and-wordmark pair as a whole inside the cell both horizontally and vertically. Keep column widths equal and cell padding uniform so the matrix stays balanced across all twelve entries.

On narrow viewports reflow into fewer columns (for example two columns or a single column) while keeping the icon-plus-wordmark pairing intact per cell. Adjust the vertical rules so they only separate adjacent columns of cells that appear on the same row, not individual stacked rows.

items.name: Featured Blog Article With Card Row
items.promptText:
Create a blog section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width. Below the header, add a thin horizontal divider spanning the full container width.

**Featured article** sits directly below the divider as a two-column split on large breakpoints. The left sub-column holds a theme-colored image placeholder box with a centered image icon and rounded corners that spans the full sub-column width and height. The right sub-column is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a bold multi-line headline rendered as a clickable link on its own line; a horizontal author row composed of a small circular avatar on the left, the author name to the right of the avatar, a small calendar icon and publication date to the right of the name — all on the same baseline; a short multi-line excerpt paragraph directly below the author row at a comfortable reading width; a text-style "Read more" link composed of a small leading icon and a short label on its own line at the bottom.

**Three-card row** sits directly below the featured article as three equal-width cards in one horizontal row with consistent gutters between them.
