Each card is a vertical stack containing, in order: a theme-colored image placeholder box with a centered image icon and rounded corners spanning the full card width; a bold headline rendered as a clickable link on its own line directly below the image; a short excerpt paragraph directly below the headline; a text-style "Read more" link with a small leading icon at the bottom of the card.

On narrow viewports stack the featured article's two sub-columns vertically (image first, text second), then stack the three cards beneath it in a single column in their original left-to-right reading order.

items.name: Blog Card Grid With Newsletter Signup
items.promptText:
Create a blog section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a header row composed of a large left-aligned heading on the left and a compact pill-shaped "View more" link with a trailing arrow icon anchored to the right of the same baseline; directly below the heading, a left-aligned supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the header block, place a two-column by two-row grid of four article cards with consistent gutters between all cards. Each card is a rounded panel with a thin outer boundary and generous internal padding. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a top row composed of a small pill-shaped category badge with a tiny leading icon and short label on the left and a small time-ago indicator with a tiny clock icon and short label anchored to the right of the same baseline; a bold multi-line headline rendered as a clickable link on its own line directly below the top row; a short excerpt paragraph directly below the headline; a bottom row composed of a small circular avatar on the left, the author name and a publication date with read-time label stacked in two lines to the right of the avatar, and a text-style "Read more" link with a trailing arrow icon anchored to the far right of the same baseline.

Below the card grid, separated by generous vertical space, place a full-width newsletter signup block as a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a bold sub-heading on its own line (e.g. "Sign up for our newsletter"); a short supporting paragraph directly below the sub-heading; a horizontal row composed of an email input field with a placeholder label and a small leading mail icon on the left and a compact primary "Subscribe" button immediately to the right of the input on the same baseline; a short line of fine-print copy directly below the input row referencing a privacy policy text link.

On narrow viewports collapse the card grid into a single column with the four cards stacked in their original reading order, and keep the newsletter block below them; preserve all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Trending Topics Blog Panels
items.promptText:
Create a blog section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a left-aligned header row with a large heading on the left (e.g. "Trending topics") and a text-style link anchored to the right of the same baseline whose label includes a small leading icon and the text "See all topics".

Below the header, place three equal-width columns on large breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each column is a rounded panel with a thin outer boundary. Inside each panel, stack from top to bottom: a header row composed of a small icon on the left, a bold category name to the right of the icon on the same baseline, and a compact pill-shaped "View all" link anchored to the right of that same row whose label includes a trailing arrow; below the header row, a vertical list of five to six article link rows with consistent vertical spacing. Each link row is a horizontal composition of a small circular placeholder avatar on the left, a short article title rendered as a clickable link to the right of the avatar filling the available width, and a small trailing arrow icon anchored to the far right of the row — all elements on the same baseline.

On narrow viewports stack the three columns vertically in their original left-to-right reading order; each panel stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Centered Bordered Blog Card Grid
items.promptText:
Create a blog section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the header block, place a three-column by two-row grid of six article cards with consistent gutters between all cards. Each card is a rounded panel with a thin outer boundary. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a theme-colored image placeholder box with a centered image icon and rounded corners spanning the full card width at the top; a small pill-shaped category badge composed of a tiny leading icon and a short label on its own line directly below the image; a bold multi-line headline rendered as a clickable link on its own line directly below the badge; a short multi-line excerpt paragraph directly below the headline; a bottom row composed of a small circular avatar on the left, the author name on its own line to the right of the avatar, and a publication date paired with a read-time label on a second line directly beneath the author name — both text lines left-aligned to the right of the avatar.

Below the entire card grid, centered on its own line, place a single text-style "View more" link composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

On narrow viewports reduce the column count stepwise (three columns, then two, then one) until the cards form a single column on the narrowest breakpoints; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout and keep the "View more" link centered below the card stack.

items.name: Alternating Portfolio Case Studies
items.promptText:
Create a portfolio section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a horizontal row composed of a left-aligned heading on the left and one compact outlined button (a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon) anchored to the right, both sitting on the same baseline. Directly below the heading, place a left-aligned supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the header, stack three case-study entries vertically with generous spacing between them. Each entry is a two-column split on large 1280px width breakpoints with consistent gutters. Alternate the column positions so the first entry places the image on the left and the content on the right, the second entry places the content on the left and the image on the right, and the third entry repeats the first arrangement.

Inside each **image column**, place one large image with rounded corners that fills the column area.

Inside each **content column**, stack a left-aligned vertical composition from top to bottom: a prominent project title on its own line; a text link on its own line directly below the title composed of a URL label paired with a small trailing external-link icon; a supporting paragraph directly below the link at a comfortable reading width; a horizontal row of small tech-stack or tool icons sitting side by side on the same baseline; and a text-style link at the bottom composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

On narrow viewports, stack each entry as a single column with the image first and the content directly below it; preserve all internal reading order.

items.name: Centered Blog Card Grid
items.promptText:
Create a blog section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width.

Below the header block, place a three-column by two-row grid of six article cards with consistent gutters between all cards. Each card is a vertical stack containing, in order: a theme-colored image placeholder box with a centered image icon and rounded corners spanning the full card width at the top; a bold headline rendered as a clickable link on its own line directly below the image; a horizontal author row composed of a small circular avatar on the left, the author name to the right of the avatar, a small calendar icon and publication date to the right of the name — all on the same baseline directly below the headline; a short multi-line excerpt paragraph directly below the author row; a text-style "Read more" link composed of a small leading icon and a short label on its own line at the bottom of the card.

On narrow viewports reduce the column count stepwise (three columns, then two, then one) until the cards form a single column on the narrowest breakpoints; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Featured Blog Grid Section
items.promptText:
Create a blog section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line (e.g. "Our Blog"); directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph of one to two lines at a comfortable reading width.

Below the header block, place a three-column grid on large breakpoints. The grid has three rows: the featured card in the left column spans all three rows in height, while the middle and right columns hold two standard cards each (filling four cells across two rows), plus a third row with one standard card in each of the middle and right columns — seven article cards total (one featured, six standard).

**Featured card** (left column, spanning all three rows in height) is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a theme-colored image placeholder box with a centered image icon and rounded corners spanning the full card width, occupying roughly the top half of the card; a bold multi-line headline rendered as a clickable link on its own line directly below the image; a short multi-line excerpt paragraph directly below the headline at a comfortable reading width; a compact outlined "View more" button with a trailing arrow icon pushed to the bottom of the card.

**Standard cards** (filling the middle and right columns, two per row across three rows) each stack from top to bottom: a bold headline rendered as a clickable link on its own line; a short two-to-three-line excerpt paragraph directly below the headline; a compact outlined "View more" button with a trailing arrow icon at the bottom of the card. These cards carry no image placeholder. Consistent vertical and horizontal gutters separate all cards.

On narrow viewports collapse the grid into a single column with the featured card first and the remaining six articles stacked beneath it in their original left-to-right, top-to-bottom reading order.

items.name: FAQ Header Search With Link Columns
items.promptText:
Create a FAQ section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a horizontal header row on large breakpoints containing a left-aligned block on the left and a search input anchored to the right on the same baseline. The left block is a vertical stack composed of a large left-aligned heading on its own line and a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width. The search input contains a small leading search icon inside the field and placeholder text.

Below the header, place a thin horizontal rule spanning the full container width.

Below the rule, place two equal-width columns on large breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each column is a left-aligned vertical stack containing a bold category heading on its own line at the top followed by a vertical list of question links, one per line, directly beneath the heading. Each link reads as plain text on its own line.

Below the two-column block, place a full-width footer bar separated by a thin horizontal rule. The bar is a horizontal row containing a short support prompt on the left and a compact button on the right on the same baseline, with the button label preceded by a small leading icon.

On narrow viewports stack the heading block above the search input, stack the two link columns vertically in reading order, and center the footer bar elements vertically.

items.name: Threaded QA With Sort Search And Ask Drawer
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce help-center threaded Q&A: a heading with a sort select, search field, and ask action, an alternating stack of question cards and indented answer cards (with helpful-vote controls), pagination, and an "ask a question" side drawer. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section (and its drawer) so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1024 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up) and a 24-pixel rhythm between regions. **Header.** A block that becomes a bottom-aligned space-between row with a 16-pixel gap from the large breakpoint up: a non-shrinking, growing ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Questions (147)", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) and a **controls cluster** (16px above it on mobile; becoming an end-aligned, 16-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up): a non-shrinking **sort select** (host select input, options "Most helpful" / "Most recent", host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, ~10px vertical / ~10px start / ~40px end padding for its chevron, ~14px text, screen-reader-only label) and a search form pairing the same **search field** as variant 1 (capped ~384 pixels) with an **"Ask a question" brand button** that opens the side drawer. **Thread.** A stack with a consistent **24-pixel gap between every card** — including between each question card and its following answer card, and between one question/answer pair and the next — so the cards never sit flush against each other: - **Question cards** — a card with a ~12-pixel internal rhythm, host rounded corners, a thin border, the host primary/neutral surface, a small shadow, and 24px padding: a header row (12-pixel gap) with a ~16px semibold hover-underline author link and a ~14px muted timestamp; a ~16px muted question body; and a footer row (16-pixel gap) pairing a ~14px medium muted "I have the same question" prompt with a **helpful/vote radio pair** (per the vote rule, e.g. "Yes: 8" / "No: 0"). - **Answer cards** — the same card indented ~48px from the start at the small breakpoint up, leading with an **"Answer" success badge** (inline-flex, host rounded corners, ~10px/2px padding, ~12px medium label, leading 12-by-12-pixel check glyph), then the same author/timestamp header, a ~16px muted answer body, and a footer pairing a ~14px medium muted "Was it helpful to you?" prompt with a helpful/vote radio pair. Use about four question/answer pairs. **Vote radio rule.** A helpful/vote pair is two single-select radios (16-by-16 pixels) with ~14px medium labels 8px after them (e.g. "Yes: 8" and "No: 0"), grouped on one row with a 16-pixel gap and rendered as the host design system's radio component. **Pager.** A centered joined numbered pager (24px above it, 32 from the small breakpoint up, 48 from the large breakpoint up): a 32px-tall row with overlapping 1px borders of a previous-arrow control (leading rounded side), numbered page links (~14px, ~12px horizontal padding), an overflow ellipsis, the last page, and a next-arrow control (trailing rounded side); the current page uses the host's brand-tinted surface, border, and text. **Ask drawer.** A right-anchored, full-height side drawer (full-width, capped ~448 pixels, ~16px padding, host surface, slide-in transition): a ~14px semibold, uppercase muted "Ask a question" label, a top-right icon-only close button (~20px glyph), and the shared ask-a-question form (from variant 1) in a single-column arrangement (the type and priority selects stacked), ending with a full-width "Submit question" brand button. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the sort select, search field, ask button, question/answer cards, the "Answer" badges, the vote radios, author links, the pager, and the drawer with its form controls and buttons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the sort select, the search input, the vote radios, and the drawer's textarea/selects/file/checkbox — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Ask a question" and "Submit question" primary buttons use ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with ~14px medium labels; the pager controls are 32px-tall with ~12px horizontal padding; the drawer close is an icon-only button; primaries use the host brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1024 pixels, the search field at ~384 pixels, the answer-card indent at ~48 pixels, the drawer at ~448 pixels, the badge glyph at 12-by-12 pixels, the vote radios at 16-by-16 pixels, and the pager row at 32 pixels tall. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/semantic accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The header stacks the title over the sort/search/ask controls until the small/large breakpoints; the answer cards lose their indent below the small breakpoint; the drawer spans the available width up to its cap; the pager stays centered.

items.name: Static FAQ Card Grid
items.promptText:
Create a FAQ section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line.

Below the heading, place a three-column grid of almost 16 FAQ entry cards with consistent gutters between columns and rows on large breakpoints. Each card is a rounded rectangular panel containing a left-aligned vertical stack, in order: a bold question title on its own line at the top of the card; a multi-paragraph answer block directly below the title, left-aligned with comfortable internal padding on all sides. All entries are permanently visible (no accordion collapse). Inline text links may appear within the answer copy.

Distribute the entries across rows of three cards, filling left-to-right top-to-bottom. Allow varying card heights based on content length while keeping cards within each row top-aligned.

On narrow viewports collapse the grid to two columns first, then to a single column on the narrowest breakpoints; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: FAQ Accordion With Helpful Votes
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce FAQ accordion: a heading, a flush accordion of questions that each expand to an answer (author, date, body, and helpful-vote controls), and a closing "ask a question" prompt. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up) and a 24-pixel rhythm between regions. A ~20px semibold heading-color title ("General questions", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) sits at the top. **Accordion.** A flush accordion (24px below the heading). Each item is: - A full-width **trigger** (a header button): a space-between, vertically-centered row with a 12-pixel gap, a bottom divider, ~20px of vertical padding, a left-aligned **16px, medium-weight** (not normal, not semibold/bold) heading-color question, and a trailing 20-by-20-pixel chevron glyph that rotates when the panel is open; the active item shows its heading-color text, inactive items the muted color. - An expandable **answer panel** (collapsed by default except the first): a body with a ~16px rhythm, a bottom divider, and ~20px of vertical padding — a header row (12-pixel gap) with a ~16px semibold heading-color author name and a ~14px muted date; one or more ~16px muted answer paragraphs (some may begin with a bolded heading-color lead-in label); and a footer row (16-pixel gap) pairing a ~14px medium muted "Was it helpful to you?" prompt with a helpful/vote radio pair (two 16-by-16-pixel radios with ~14px medium labels such as "Yes: 16" / "No: 3"). Use about ten accordion items, the first expanded. **Closing prompt.** Below the accordion (24px above it, 32 from the small breakpoint up), a ~18px muted line ("Didn't find the answer?") containing a brand, underlined, hover-no-underline "Ask a question" link. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the accordion triggers and panels, the chevron glyphs, author/date text, answer paragraphs, the vote radios, and the ask link — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the helpful/vote radios — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The accordion triggers are full-width header buttons with ~20px vertical padding and no horizontal box padding (flush), driven by the host's accordion/disclosure component; the vote radios and ask link follow the host's radio and link components. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the trigger chevrons are 20-by-20 pixels, the vote radios 16-by-16 pixels, the trigger question text 16px medium, the answer text ~16px, and the closing prompt ~18px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/semantic accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The accordion is full-width at every breakpoint; triggers keep their question and chevron on one space-between row (the question wrapping as needed); the closing prompt wraps naturally.

items.name: FAQ Support Blocks Panel
items.promptText:
Create a FAQ section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line.

Below the heading, place one large rounded container that spans most of the container width. Inside that container, arrange three equal-width support blocks in a single horizontal row on large breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each block is a left-aligned horizontal composition of a small icon anchored to the left and a text group to the right of the icon containing a bold title on its own line, a short multi-line description paragraph directly below the title, and a text-style link on its own line at the bottom of the block whose label includes a trailing arrow icon.

On narrow viewports stack the three support blocks vertically in reading order within the rounded container; each block stretches to the full available width with comfortable internal padding.

items.name: Questions List With Search And Ask Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce help-center "questions & answers" list: a heading with a search field and an ask-a-question action, a divided list of question entries (answer-count badge, question, answer excerpt, attribution), a load-more action, and an "ask a question" modal. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section (and its modal) so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1024 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Header.** A block that becomes a space-between, vertically-centered row with a 16-pixel gap from the large breakpoint up: a non-shrinking ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Questions (147)", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) and a **search/ask cluster** (16px above it on mobile, removed from the large breakpoint up; full-width, becoming an end-aligned, 16-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up): a **search field** (full-width, growing, capped ~384 pixels from the large breakpoint up) as a relative input with a leading 16-by-16-pixel search glyph (text inset ~36px on the start side), host rounded corners, a thin border, a soft secondary fill, ~16px horizontal / ~10px vertical padding, ~14px text, and a "Search Questions & Answers" placeholder; and an **"Ask a question" brand button** (full-width then auto-width from the small breakpoint up, non-shrinking, ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium label) that opens the ask modal. **Questions list.** A flow-root 24px below the header holding a stack of question entries with thin dividers between them; each entry has ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up) and a ~16-pixel internal rhythm: - An **answer-count badge** (per the badge rule) such as "3 answers". - A ~20px semibold heading-color hover-underline **question** link. - A ~16px muted **answer excerpt** paragraph. - A ~14px medium muted **attribution** line ("Answered 1 day ago by") containing a heading-color hover-underline author link. Use about five question entries. **Answer-count badge rule.** A small inline-block pill with host rounded corners, ~10px horizontal / ~2px vertical padding, and a ~12px medium label, tinted from the host's semantic tokens — a success tint for entries that have answers (e.g. "3 answers") and a neutral tint for "No answers". **Load more.** Below the list (24px above it), a centered (start-aligned from the large breakpoint up) bordered neutral "View more questions" button (full-width then auto-width from the small breakpoint up, ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium label). **Ask-a-question form (shared).** The ask modal/drawer body throughout this file is a form with a two-column grid (16-pixel gaps) and these fields: - A full-span **question textarea** with a ~14px medium label ("Your question") and a muted "(150–1000 characters)" hint, over a ~6-row textarea (host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, ~10px padding, ~14px text). - A full-span row that splits into two columns from the medium breakpoint up: a **question-type select** whose label carries a trailing 16-by-16-pixel info glyph with a hover tooltip ("Choose your question type to get a faster answer."), with options like "Technical Question", "Shipment Question", "Payment Issue", "Other"; and a **priority select** with options like "Very High", "High", "Medium", "Low". Both are host select inputs. - A full-span **upload files** group: a ~14px medium label with a muted "(Optional)" hint over a 192-pixel-tall dashed-border dropzone on a soft secondary surface (hover state) containing a centered 32-by-32-pixel upload glyph, a ~14px message ("Click to upload or drag and drop" with the lead bolded), and a ~12px muted format/size hint, wrapping a visually-hidden file input. - A full-span **terms checkbox** (16-by-16 pixels) with a ~14px muted label containing a brand "terms and conditions" link. **Ask modal.** A centered, scroll-locked overlay with a ~576-pixel panel on a neutral surface, host rounded corners, and a shadow: a header (16px padding, 20 from the medium breakpoint up, bottom border) with a ~18px semibold "Ask a question" title and a 32-by-32-pixel icon-only close button (12-by-12-pixel glyph); the shared ask form as the body (16px padding, 20 from the medium breakpoint up); and a footer separated by a top border (16px above, 20 from the medium breakpoint up) with a "Submit question" brand button and a "Cancel" bordered neutral button. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the search field, ask buttons, question entries, answer-count badges, author links, the load-more button, and the ask modal with its textarea, selects, tooltip, dropzone, checkbox, and buttons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the search input, the textarea, the type/priority selects, the file input, and the terms checkbox — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Ask a question", "View more questions", "Submit question", and "Cancel" buttons use ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the close button is a 32-by-32-pixel icon button; primaries use the host brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1024 pixels, the search field at ~384 pixels, the modal at ~576 pixels, the search/info glyphs at 16-by-16 pixels, the upload glyph at 32-by-32 pixels, the close glyph at 12-by-12 pixels, the dropzone at 192 pixels tall, the badge label at ~12px, and the question link at ~20px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/semantic accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The header stacks the title over the search/ask cluster (the search and button full-width) until the small/large breakpoints; each question entry stays stacked; the modal fields collapse the type/priority pair to one column until the medium breakpoint; the load-more button is full-width until the small breakpoint.

items.name: Split 404 Page with Resource Cards
items.promptText:
Create a 404 page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints that spans the full available width of the viewport with no outer margin.

**Left column** uses a plain page background and contains a left-aligned vertical stack with comfortable inset padding, vertically centered within the column height. Stack from top to bottom: a large multi-line heading stating the error status and a short apology on its own line; a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, containing an inline bold text link pointing to the homepage embedded naturally within the sentence; a horizontal row of short text links placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, with a small leading label (e.g. "Here are some helpful links:") followed by the links sitting side by side on the same baseline separated by consistent spacing.

**Right column** uses a distinct filled background that spans the full column area edge-to-edge, with a very subtle geometric wave or line texture layered behind the content. Inside the column, place a vertical stack of three resource cards with consistent spacing between them, vertically centered within the column height. Each card is a left-aligned vertical stack composed of a small rounded-square icon container at the top (holding a single centered glyph); a bold title on its own line directly below the icon; a short two-line description paragraph directly below the title; and a text-style link on its own line below the paragraph whose label includes a trailing arrow icon at the end of the link text.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the left column first and the resource column directly below it; each internal stack preserves its original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Split 404 Page With Quick Links
items.promptText:
Create a 404 page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack, vertically centered within the column height, containing in order: a large multi-line heading stating the error status and a brief descriptive phrase on its own line; a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width suggesting the user refresh or return to the homepage; a horizontal row of three compact card-style link blocks placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, sitting side by side on the same baseline with consistent gutters between them. Each link block is a centered vertical stack composed of a small icon centered at the top (holding a single glyph) and a short label centered directly below the icon; the entire block behaves as a single clickable surface.

**Right column** holds one large illustrative scene that fills most of the column area, vertically centered within the column. The illustration depicts a figure or character in a questioning or searching pose alongside oversized question-mark shapes, conveying a lighthearted "lost" theme without relying on photographic imagery.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the content column first and the illustration directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Playful Illustrated 404 Page
items.promptText:
Create a 404 page as one centered vertical stack on a full-width section background, vertically centered within the viewport height. Stack from top to bottom: a large decorative composition of the numerals "404" where the middle digit is replaced by a rounded illustrative character or expressive icon that conveys a lighthearted error mood (the three elements — first digit, illustration, last digit — sit side by side on the same baseline and read as a single oversized display group); a bold centered heading on its own line directly below the illustration group (e.g. a playful acknowledgment like "Oops! Wrong Turn"); a centered paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, containing an inline bold text link pointing back to the homepage embedded naturally within the sentence.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack; allow the decorative digit group to scale down proportionally while preserving center alignment and comfortable side padding.

items.name: Split Social Proof Intro With Stat List
items.promptText:
Create a social proof section split into two equal-width columns on large 1280px width breakpoints that spans the full available width of the page container.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack with comfortable internal padding containing, in order: a large left-aligned multi-line heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a social-proof row composed of a tight horizontal cluster of slightly overlapping small circular avatar thumbnails on the left and a single line of caption copy to their right that includes a numerically emphasized segment (e.g. a user count rendered in bold); and a compact outlined button on its own line below the social-proof row whose label includes a trailing arrow icon.

The **right column** uses a contrasting filled background surface that spans the full column area. Allow a very subtle geometric wave or line texture behind the column content so it reads as a soft decorative surface without competing with the text. Inside the column, place a vertical list of three to four stat entries with consistent spacing between them. Each entry is a horizontal row composed of a small rounded-square icon container anchored to the left (holding a single centered glyph) and a text block to the right of the icon containing a bold stat headline on its own line (combining a prominent numeric value with a short label) and a short multi-line description paragraph directly beneath the headline.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the intro column first and the stat-list column second; each column stretches to the full content width and preserves all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Two-Column Social Proof Narrative With Stats Row
items.promptText:
Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a two-column layout on large 1280px width breakpoints.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large left-aligned multi-line heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width.

The **right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing multiple body paragraphs stacked vertically with consistent spacing between them, providing extended narrative or descriptive copy.

Below the two-column block, after generous vertical space, place a single horizontal row of four stat blocks spanning the full container width on the same baseline with consistent spacing between them. Each stat block is a centered vertical stack composed of one large prominent numeric value on its own line at the top and a short descriptive label directly beneath the value.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically in reading order with the heading column first and the narrative column second; the stat row collapses into a two-column grid preserving left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order.

items.name: Social Proof Bento Showcase
items.promptText:
Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a large heading centered on its own line followed by a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath it at a moderate reading width. Below the paragraph, place a horizontal row of two text links sitting side by side on the same baseline, centered as a pair; each link label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, place a bento-style grid composed of four stat cards arranged around a tall central showcase panel. On large 1280px width breakpoints, the layout reads as a three-column structure: the left column stacks two stat cards vertically, the center column holds the tall showcase panel spanning the full height of both rows, and the right column stacks two stat cards vertically.

Each stat card is a rounded rectangular panel containing a left-aligned vertical stack composed of, in order: a small rounded-square icon container at the top (holding a single centered glyph); a bold stat headline on its own line directly below the icon (combining a prominent numeric value with a short label); a short multi-line description paragraph directly beneath the headline; and a compact outlined button at the bottom of the card whose label is composed of a small leading icon and a short action label on the same baseline.

The central showcase panel is a tall rounded rectangular region containing a centered vertical stack composed of a loose cluster of small technology or brand logo icons arranged in an organic scattered composition in the upper portion, followed by a large bold headline on its own line centered below the logo cluster and a short centered description paragraph directly beneath the headline.

On narrow viewports collapse the bento grid into a single column stacking the top-left card, the central panel, the top-right card, the bottom-left card, and the bottom-right card in reading order; each card and the showcase panel stretch to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Centered Social Proof Stats Panel
items.promptText:
Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a large heading centered on its own line followed by a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath it at a moderate reading width. Below the paragraph, place a horizontal row of two text links sitting side by side on the same baseline, centered as a pair; each link label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, place one wide rounded container spanning the full container width. Inside the container, arrange four stat blocks in a single horizontal row on the same baseline, separated by thin vertical dividers between adjacent blocks. Each stat block is a left-aligned vertical stack composed of one large prominent numeric value on its own line at the top and a short descriptive label directly beneath the value.

On narrow viewports the two text links stack vertically, and the four stat blocks collapse into a two-column grid with the vertical dividers removed; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Centered Social Proof Stats Row
items.promptText:
Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Place a single horizontal row of three stat blocks centered on the page on the same baseline with generous spacing between them. Each stat block is a centered vertical stack composed of one large prominent numeric value (e.g. "73M+") on its own line at the top and a short descriptive label directly beneath the value. Keep all text within each block horizontally centered.

On narrow viewports collapse the three stat blocks into a single column, stacking them vertically in left-to-right reading order with consistent spacing between them.

items.name: Split Social Proof Stats With Illustration
items.promptText:
Create a social proof section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large left-aligned heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a vertical list of three stat entries with consistent spacing between them — each entry is a horizontal row composed of a small rounded-square icon container anchored to the left (holding a single centered glyph) and a text block to the right of the icon containing a bold stat headline on its own line (combining a prominent numeric value with a short label, e.g. "500+ successful projects") and a short multi-line description paragraph directly beneath the headline. Below the stat list, after extra vertical space, place a social-proof row composed of a tight horizontal cluster of slightly overlapping small circular avatar thumbnails on the left and a single line of caption copy to their right that includes a numerically emphasized segment (e.g. a user count rendered in bold).

The **right column** is dominated by one large illustrative scene that spans most of the column area, vertically centered within the column. Allow simple supporting shapes (geometric accents or soft background forms) behind the scene if needed to fill the column without competing with the primary illustration.

On narrow viewports stack with the text column first and the illustration column directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Social Proof Carousel With Stats Row
items.promptText:
Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a large heading centered on its own line followed by a single centered text link on its own line directly beneath the heading whose label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, place a horizontal carousel region spanning the full container width. The carousel displays two large rounded rectangular image placeholders side by side in the visible frame with consistent gutters between them. Position a circular previous-arrow navigation control on the left edge of the carousel and a circular next-arrow navigation control on the right edge, both vertically centered relative to the image placeholders.

Below the carousel, place a single horizontal row of six stat blocks on the same baseline with consistent spacing between them. Each stat block is a centered vertical stack composed of one large prominent numeric value on its own line at the top and a short descriptive label directly beneath the value. Keep all content within each block horizontally centered.

On narrow viewports the carousel shows one image placeholder at a time, the navigation controls remain anchored to the left and right edges, and the stat row collapses into a two-column or three-column wrapped grid preserving left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order.

items.name: Centered Customer Logo Band
items.promptText: Create a customer logos section as one centered vertical stack inside a page-width container with comfortable side padding. At the very top, place a short centered kicker line on its own row naming the social-proof intent (for example a sentence stating that the product is trusted by teams worldwide). Below the kicker, leave a small vertical gap, then center a single horizontal flex row of exactly six partner marks or logotypes that share one visual weight; space the marks with even horizontal gaps so they read as one unified band. No secondary heading is required unless you add a very small optional sub-line directly beneath the kicker on its own centered row. On narrow viewports the mark row wraps into additional centered rows while keeping even horizontal spacing between items and consistent vertical gaps between wrapped lines.

items.name: Centered Social Proof Stats Row
items.promptText:
Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Place a single horizontal row of three stat blocks centered on the page on the same baseline with generous spacing between them. Each stat block is a centered vertical stack composed of one large prominent numeric value (e.g. "73M+") on its own line at the top and a short descriptive label directly beneath the value. Keep all text within each block horizontally centered.

On narrow viewports collapse the three stat blocks into a single column, stacking them vertically in left-to-right reading order with consistent spacing between them.

items.name: Feature Cards With Action Links
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce promotional feature section: a centered heading over a grid of icon feature cards, each ending in an action link. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on a soft secondary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Heading block.** A center-aligned block with 16 pixels beneath it (32 from the medium breakpoint up): a ~24px bold heading-color title with tight tracking and 12 pixels beneath it (~36px from the medium breakpoint up, e.g. "Why [Brand] Shop?") over a ~16px muted subtitle (~20px from the medium breakpoint up). **Feature grid.** A one-column grid that becomes two columns from the small breakpoint up and three from the large breakpoint up with a 16-pixel gap (32 from the xl breakpoint up; 32 pixels above it from the small breakpoint up). Each cell is a **feature card** — a thin-bordered, host-rounded card on the host primary surface with a small shadow, 16 pixels of padding (24 from the small breakpoint up), and center-aligned content: - A centered 48-by-48-pixel muted feature glyph with 16 pixels beneath it. - A ~20px semibold heading-color title with 12 pixels beneath it. - A muted supporting paragraph with 16 pixels beneath it. - An **action link** — a centered row in the brand foreground color, ~18px medium weight, underlining on hover, trailing an 18-by-18-pixel arrow glyph 4 pixels after its label (e.g. "How to make the payments", "Get premium delivery", "Activate your account"). Use about three feature cards. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the heading and subtitle, the feature cards (glyphs, titles, paragraphs, and action links) — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. Every link must be the host design system's own link component, with its color, states, focus ring, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The action links are ~18px inline text links trailing an 18-by-18-pixel arrow glyph; there are no box buttons in this section. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the feature glyphs at 48-by-48 pixels, the action links at ~18px with 18-by-18-pixel arrows, the heading at ~24–36px, the subtitle at ~16–20px, and the card titles at ~20px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The feature grid steps from one to two to three columns across the small and large breakpoints; each card stays center-aligned with its glyph, title, paragraph, and action link stacked.

items.name: Featured Testimonials Mosaic
items.promptText:
Create a testimonials section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a large heading centered on its own line; a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a moderate reading width; and a horizontal row of two text links sitting side by side on the same baseline, centered as a pair beneath the paragraph — each link label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, place a three-column layout on large 1280px width breakpoints. The **center column** is wider than the side columns and holds one tall featured testimonial card. The **left column** and the **right column** are narrower and equal in width; each stacks two smaller testimonial cards vertically with consistent spacing between them.

The **featured center card** is a tall rounded rectangular panel containing a centered vertical stack composed of, in order: a large decorative opening quotation mark glyph centered at the top; a centered multi-paragraph testimonial quote at a moderate reading width directly below the quotation mark; and a centered author attribution row at the bottom composed of a small circular avatar thumbnail on the left, with a bold author name on its own line to the right of the avatar and a role or company label on a second line directly beneath the name, aligned with the name text.

Each **small side card** is a compact rounded rectangular panel containing a left-aligned vertical stack composed of, in order: a bold testimonial title on its own line at the top; a short multi-line quote paragraph directly below the title; and an author attribution row at the bottom composed of a small circular avatar thumbnail on the left, with a bold author name on its own line to the right of the avatar and a role or company label on a second line directly beneath the name, aligned with the name text.

Below the three-column layout, centered directly beneath it on its own line, place a single compact button composed of a small leading icon and a short action label (e.g. "View more") on the same baseline.

On narrow viewports collapse the layout into a single column stacking the featured center card first, then the left-column cards, then the right-column cards in top-to-bottom reading order; each card stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Framed Social Proof Stats Card
items.promptText:
Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Place one large rounded outer container with a thin outer boundary that frames the entire section content so it reads as a single card.

Inside the container, place a horizontal row of four equal-width stat tiles on the same baseline with consistent gutters between them. Each tile is its own rounded rectangular panel containing a centered vertical stack composed of, in order: a small icon centered at the top; one large prominent numeric value on its own line directly below the icon; a short descriptive label directly beneath the value. Keep all content within each tile horizontally centered.

Below the stat tiles, after comfortable vertical space, place a left-aligned trust row composed of a short introductory label (e.g. "Trusted by:") followed by a horizontal row of brand logos, each rendered as a small monochrome glyph with consistent spacing between them, all sitting on the same baseline as the label.

On narrow viewports collapse the four tiles into a two-column grid first, then into a single column on the narrowest breakpoints; the trust row wraps naturally beneath the label.

items.name: Centered Testimonials Card Grid
items.promptText:
Create a testimonials section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a large heading centered on its own line; a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a moderate reading width; and a horizontal row of two text links sitting side by side on the same baseline, centered as a pair beneath the paragraph — each link label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, place a three-column by three-row grid of nine testimonial cards with consistent gutters between columns and rows. Each card is a rounded rectangular panel containing a left-aligned vertical stack composed of, in order: a bold testimonial title on its own line at the top; a short multi-line quote paragraph directly below the title; and an author attribution row at the bottom of the card composed of a small circular avatar thumbnail on the left, with a bold author name on its own line to the right of the avatar and a role or company label on a second line directly beneath the name, aligned with the name text. Allow a very subtle geometric pattern (such as a honeycomb or hexagonal motif) behind the grid area so it reads as a soft decorative surface without competing with the card content.

Below the grid, centered directly beneath it on its own line, place a single compact button composed of a small leading icon and a short action label (e.g. "View more") on the same baseline.

On narrow viewports reduce the column count stepwise (three columns, then two, then one) until the cards form a single column on the narrowest breakpoints; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Tabbed Author Testimonials Section
items.promptText:
Create a testimonials section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding, split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints.

The **left column** contains a vertical list of author entries that behave as a tab group (exactly one entry is selected at a time). Each entry is a horizontal row composed of a small circular avatar thumbnail anchored to the left, and a text block to the right of the avatar containing a bold author name on its own line and a role or company label on a second line directly beneath the name. The selected entry uses a visually distinct background to indicate the active state; unselected entries use a plain surface. Below the author list, after comfortable vertical space, place a single centered button whose label is composed of a small leading icon and a short action label (e.g. "View all testimonials") on the same baseline.

The **right column** is the content area whose contents swap based on the currently selected author tab. The content area is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large decorative opening quotation mark glyph on its own line at the top; a bold testimonial heading on its own line directly below the quotation mark; one or more body paragraphs of testimonial text stacked vertically with consistent spacing between them directly below the heading; and an author attribution row at the bottom composed of a small circular avatar thumbnail on the left, with a bold author name on its own line to the right of the avatar and a role or company label on a second line directly beneath the name, aligned with the name text.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the author tab list first and the testimonial content area directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Centered Quote Testimonial
items.promptText:
Create a testimonials section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Place a single centered vertical stack composed of, in order: a large decorative opening quotation mark glyph centered on its own line at the top; a centered multi-line quote paragraph directly below the quotation mark at a moderate reading width; and a centered author attribution row on its own line directly below the quote. The author row is a horizontal composition of a small circular avatar thumbnail on the left, the author name immediately to the right of the avatar on the same baseline, a short separator character, and a role or company label to the right of the separator on the same baseline.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack; allow the quote paragraph to span the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Centered 500 Error Page
items.promptText:
Create a 500 error page as one centered vertical stack on a full-width section background, vertically centered within the viewport height. Stack from top to bottom: a small brand icon or logo mark centered horizontally on its own line; a brand name label centered on its own line directly below the icon; a large bold centered heading on its own line directly below the brand name stating the error status and a playful or empathetic descriptor (e.g. "Error, The internet gods are not happy"); a single centered paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, explaining that the site is experiencing issues and will return with improvements.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack with comfortable side padding; allow the heading to wrap naturally while preserving center alignment throughout.

items.name: Split 500 Error Page With Contact Support
items.promptText:
Create a 500 error page as one centered vertical stack on a full-width section background, vertically centered within the viewport height. Stack from top to bottom: a small brand icon or logo mark centered horizontally on its own line; a brand name label centered on its own line directly below the icon; a large bold centered heading on its own line directly below the brand name stating the error status and a playful or empathetic descriptor (e.g. "Error, The internet gods are not happy"); a single centered paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, explaining that the site is experiencing issues and will return with improvements.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack with comfortable side padding; allow the heading to wrap naturally while preserving center alignment throughout.

items.name: Full-Width Split 500 Error With Resources
items.promptText:
Create a 500 error page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints that spans the full available width of the viewport with no outer margin.

**Left column** uses a plain page background and contains a left-aligned vertical stack constrained to a 512px max width with comfortable inset padding, vertically and horizontaly centered within the column height. Stack from top to bottom: a large multi-line heading stating the error status and a reassuring message on its own line (e.g. "500 — Internal Server Error. We're on It!"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, explaining that the site is experiencing issues and will return with improvements; a social proof row placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, composed of slightly overlapping circular user avatars on the left and a short line of bold text immediately to the right of the avatars on the same baseline stating a usage metric (e.g. "Used by over 15M people around the world"); a compact outlined button placed below the social proof row on its own line, composed of a small leading chat or message icon paired with a short label (e.g. "Speak with us").

**Right column** uses a distinct filled background that spans the full column area edge-to-edge, with a very subtle geometric wave or line texture layered behind the content. Inside the column, place a vertical stack of three resource cards with consistent spacing between them, vertically centered within the column height. Each card is a left-aligned vertical stack composed of a small rounded-square icon container at the top (holding a single centered glyph); a bold title on its own line directly below the icon; a short two-line description paragraph directly below the title; and a text-style link on its own line below the paragraph whose label includes a trailing arrow icon at the end of the link text.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the left column first and the resource column directly below it; each internal stack preserves its original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Segmented Feature Cards with Layered UI Mockups
items.promptText:
Create a feature section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header stack composed of the following elements in order: a small pill-shaped label row that combines a tiny leading icon on the left with a short label text to its right, both sitting on the same baseline inside a rounded container; a large centered multi-line headline directly below the pill label, where at least one word in the headline is paired with a small inline icon inside a rounded-square frame so the icon reads as part of the title line (sitting on the same baseline as the adjacent text).

Below the headline, place a single horizontal pill-shaped control that behaves like segmented navigation: a row of short text links arranged inline inside one continuous rounded container, with one link carrying a distinct filled background to mark the active segment while the remaining links use plain text.

Beneath the segmented navigation, place three equal-width cards in one row on large 1280px width breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each card is a rounded rectangular panel containing two vertical zones: the **upper zone** stacks a small numeric index anchored to the top corner of the card beside a medium heading on the same line, with a short supporting paragraph directly below the heading; the **lower zone** dedicates the remaining card height to a dense composition of overlapping simplified UI mockups (small readouts, mini cards, and compact controls) that may spill slightly past the card's inner text block edges to create a layered collage effect.

On narrow viewports, stack the three cards vertically in reading order; keep the header stack and segmented navigation centered above the card column.

items.name: Two-Column Feature List with CTA
items.promptText:
Create a feature section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a large heading centered on its own line followed by a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath it at a moderate reading width.

Below the header, place a two-column layout on large 1280px width breakpoints separated by a single thin vertical divider running the full height of the column area. Each column stacks three feature items vertically (six items total across both columns) with consistent spacing between them. Each item is a horizontal row composed of a small circular icon container anchored to the left (holding a single centered glyph) and a text block to the right of the icon containing a medium-weight heading on its own line and a short multi-line paragraph directly beneath the heading.

Below the two-column block, place one centered pill-shaped primary button on its own line whose label includes a trailing arrow icon at the end of the button text.

On narrow viewports, stack the two columns vertically in reading order and replace the vertical divider with a thin horizontal rule between the two halves; keep the primary button centered below both column stacks.

items.name: Split Feature Section with Illustration
items.promptText:
Create a feature section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is dominated by one large illustrative scene that spans most of the column height, vertically centered within the column. Allow simple supporting shapes (geometric accents or soft background forms) behind the scene if needed to fill the column area without competing with the primary illustration.

The **right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large left-aligned heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a vertical list of three feature entries framed by thin horizontal rules (one rule sits above the first entry and one sits below the last entry, creating a ruled band). Each entry is a horizontal row composed of a small rounded-square icon container on the left and a text block to the right of the icon containing a medium heading on its own line, a short paragraph directly beneath the heading, and a text-style link on its own line below the paragraph whose label includes a trailing arrow icon. Below the bottom rule, finish the column with one closing paragraph that spans the full text column width.

On narrow viewports, stack with the illustration column first and the text column second; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Six-Block Feature Grid
items.promptText:
Create a feature section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a left-aligned header block composed of a large multi-line heading on its own line followed by a short supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading (constrain the paragraph to a moderate reading width so it does not span the full container).

Below the header, place a three-column by two-row grid of six feature blocks with consistent gutters between columns and rows. Each block is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a small rounded-square icon container at the top (the container holds a single glyph centered inside it); a medium-weight title on its own line directly below the icon container; a short multi-line description paragraph directly below the title, left-aligned and matching the block width.

On narrow viewports collapse the grid to two columns first, then to a single column on the narrowest breakpoints, preserving left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Centered Two-Feature Grid
items.promptText:
Create a feature section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding where every primary text block is horizontally centered. At the top, place a large heading centered on its own line followed by a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath it (constrain the paragraph to a restrained line width so it reads as a compact centered block).

Below the header, place a two-column grid on large 1280px width breakpoints with one feature in each column and consistent gutters between them. Each feature is a centered vertical stack containing, in order: a small rounded-square icon container centered above the text (holding a single centered glyph); a bold heading centered on its own line directly below the icon; a centered description paragraph directly below the heading, constrained to the column width.

Beneath the two-column grid, add a single centered text link on its own line whose label includes a trailing arrow icon at the end of the link text.

On narrow viewports, stack the two features vertically in reading order with the same centered alignment inside each feature block; keep the footer link centered below both.

items.name: Three-Column Feature Lists
items.promptText:
Create a feature section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a left-aligned header block composed of a large heading on its own line followed by a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width.

Below the header, place three equal-width columns on large 1280px width breakpoints, separated by thin vertical dividers running the full height of the column area. Each column is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a small rounded-square icon container at the top (holding a single centered glyph); a medium-weight category heading on its own line directly below the icon; a vertical list of approximately five items directly below the heading. Each list item is a horizontal row composed of a small circular marker containing a checkmark icon on the left followed by a single line of text to the right on the same baseline. Keep all column content left-aligned with consistent internal padding.

On narrow viewports, stack the three columns vertically in reading order and replace the vertical dividers with thin horizontal rules between each column section.

items.name: Eight Feature Cards Grid
items.promptText:
Create a feature section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a large heading centered on its own line followed by a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath it (constrain the paragraph to a moderate reading width).

Below the header, place a responsive grid of eight feature cards arranged as four columns and two rows on the widest breakpoint, with consistent gutters between all cards. Each card is its own rounded rectangular panel with a thin outer border. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a small rounded-square icon container at the top (holding a single centered glyph); a bold short title on its own line directly below the icon; a left-aligned supporting paragraph directly below the title that fills the remaining card width with comfortable internal padding on all sides.

On smaller breakpoints, reduce the column count stepwise (four columns, then two, then one) until the cards form a single column on the narrowest viewports; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Split Feature Card Layout
items.promptText:
Create a feature section framed as one large rounded outer container with comfortable outer margin on all sides so the entire section reads as a single card floating within the page.

Inside the container, use a three-column split on large 1280px width breakpoints.

The **left column** is wider than the other two and carries a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large left-aligned heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a text-style link on its own line below the paragraph whose label includes a trailing arrow icon at the end of the link text.

The **middle column** and the **right column** are narrower and equal in width; each stacks two feature blocks vertically with consistent spacing between them (four blocks total across both columns). Each feature block is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a small rounded-square icon container (holding a single centered glyph); a short bold sub-heading on its own line directly below the icon; a supporting paragraph directly below the sub-heading that aligns flush-left with the icon and heading above it.

Allow a very subtle geometric grid texture to appear only behind part of the card interior (for example occupying one corner or a diagonal band) so it reads as a soft decorative surface without competing with the text content.

On narrow viewports, stack the three columns in reading order with the intro column first, the middle feature column second, and the right feature column third; keep all internal stacks in their original order.

items.name: Alternating Split Features with Diamond Media
items.promptText:
Create a feature section composed of two stacked bands separated by generous vertical space inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Each band is a two-column split on large 1280px width breakpoints.

**First band** — the **left column** carries the text stack and the **right column** carries the media block.

**Second band** — swap so the **left column** carries the media block and the **right column** carries the text stack.

In each **text column**, stack a left-aligned vertical composition containing, in order: a large left-aligned heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a thin horizontal rule spanning the column width; a vertical list of items where each item is a horizontal row composed of a small checkmark icon anchored to the left and a single line of descriptive text to the right on the same baseline; optionally a second thin horizontal rule below the list followed by a short closing paragraph on its own line.

In each **media column**, place one photograph inside a square frame with rounded corners that is rotated approximately 45 degrees so the photograph reads as a diamond shape. Behind the diamond frame, position a faint dotted diamond or lattice motif that extends slightly past the photo frame on all sides, creating a soft decorative halo around the image.

On narrow viewports, stack each band as a single column with the media block first and the text stack second; preserve all internal reading order within each stack.

items.name: Split Feature Intro with Card Rows
items.promptText:
Create a feature section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large left-aligned heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a text-style link on its own line below the paragraph whose label includes a trailing arrow icon at the end of the link text.

The **right column** contains a vertical stack of three identical card rows separated by consistent vertical spacing. Each card is a horizontal row composed of three inline elements: a small rounded-square icon container anchored to the left (holding a single centered glyph); a middle text block to the right of the icon containing a bold title on its own line and a short description directly beneath the title; a compact arrow control (a small forward-pointing chevron or arrow icon) anchored to the far right of the row on the same vertical center as the icon. Cards may carry subtle boundaries (thin borders or faint background fills) to distinguish each row.

On narrow viewports, stack with the intro column first and the card stack second; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Alternating Three-Band CTA
items.promptText:
Create a CTA section composed of three separate vertical bands stacked with generous spacing between them, all inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Each band is a two-column split on large 1280 px width breakpoints; alternate which side carries the illustration and which carries the text so the stacking pattern reads as illustration–text for the first band, text–illustration for the second band, and illustration–text for the third band.

In every **text column**, stack from top to bottom in this order: a large heading on its own line; one or two body paragraphs at a comfortable reading width directly beneath the heading; a vertical feature list where each item begins with a small leading icon at the left followed by either a single descriptive line to the right of the icon on the same baseline, or a bold title line on the same baseline as the icon with a short supporting line stacked directly beneath the title (choose one style per band and keep it consistent within that band); a closing sentence on its own line beneath the feature list; a horizontal row containing a solid primary button (the primary button may pair with a small trailing arrow or a small leading icon, varying per band) and a bordered secondary button to its right (the secondary button may pair with a small leading icon). The two buttons stay **side by side on one row** and never wrap to a second line (treat this as the global two-button row rule).

In every **illustration column**, place one vector or raster illustration sized to fill the column area comfortably, vertically centered relative to the adjacent text column.

On narrow viewports, stack each band's columns so that the illustration sits above the text in the first and third bands and below the text in the second band, preserving the alternating visual rhythm.

items.name: Centered Dual-Button CTA
items.promptText:
Create a CTA section as one centered vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large multi-line primary heading centered horizontally on its own line.
