Below the heading, place a supporting paragraph set at a restrained max width and centered horizontally so long lines do not stretch edge to edge.

Below the paragraph, center a single horizontal row containing two buttons sitting side by side with a small gap between them (approximately 16 px). The first button is a solid primary brand button with a short label; the second button is a secondary outlined button with a short label. Both buttons use pill-shaped or softly rounded corners and share the same height so they read as one balanced pair. The row itself is centered beneath the paragraph (one flex row, items centered, never wrapping to a second line on any viewport wider than the minimum supported width).

items.name: Centered Logo Navbar With Split Nav And CTA Actions
items.promptText: Create a self-contained marketing-site navbar with a centered brand mark flanked by primary navigation on the start side and sales plus auth CTAs on the end side. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome (hero, page body, footer) beyond what is described; output only this navbar so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width bar on the primary surface with 16 pixels of vertical padding and a thin bottom divider. Its content is centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). The bar is a single row with three regions — start navigation, centered brand, and end actions — vertically centered. **Primary links (start).** A horizontal link list, hidden below the large breakpoint, with a 24-pixel gap (32 from the medium breakpoint up): each is a ~14px medium-weight link in the heading color that shifts to the brand foreground on hover. Provide "Home", "Products" (with a trailing 16-by-16-pixel chevron indicating a dropdown), "Blog", and "Contact". **Brand (center).** A non-shrinking logo link about 32 pixels tall, absolutely or grid-centered so it sits in the visual center of the bar regardless of the start/end cluster widths. It pairs a small brand glyph with a ~16px semibold heading-color wordmark on the same baseline. **Actions (end).** A row with an 8-pixel gap from the small breakpoint up: - A **"Talk to sales"** text link — a ~14px medium heading-color row with a trailing 16-by-16-pixel phone glyph, hidden below the medium breakpoint, with **16 pixels** of space before the button group. - A secondary **"Login"** button — bordered, on the host primary/neutral surface, host-rounded corners, ~14px medium heading-color label, 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, subtle hover fill, focus ring. - A primary **"Upgrade to PRO"** button — brand fill, inverse ~14px medium label, host-rounded corners, 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, darker brand hover, brand focus ring. - A **menu toggle** — shown only on viewports **768px wide and below**, an icon button (8px padding, host rounded corners, subtle hover) holding a 20-by-20-pixel hamburger glyph with a screen-reader "Open Menu" label. **Mobile menu.** A collapsible panel beneath the bar with 16 pixels above it, on a soft secondary surface with a thin default border, host-token rounded corners, and 16px horizontal / 12px vertical padding; it stacks the primary links with 12 pixels between them, each a ~14px heading-color link shifting to the brand foreground on hover. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any control styling. Every control and component here — buttons, icon-buttons, triggers, links, and the mobile menu surface — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, reusing its built-in variants, tokens, and interaction states rather than ad-hoc or hardcoded values. Pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** Icon-only triggers use 8 pixels of padding on all sides. Primary and secondary labeled buttons use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; spacing, the 32-pixel logo height, and icon sizes are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** Below the large breakpoint the primary-link list hides; the menu toggle appears only on viewports **768px wide and below**; "Talk to sales" hides below the medium breakpoint. **Navbar item rules.** - Every navbar icon glyph is **18 pixels wide × 18 pixels tall** with **8 pixels** of space between the icon and its label or link text. - **Icon-only button groups.** In action and utility rows, group adjacent icon-only buttons and icon-buttons (no visible label) together; use **4 pixels** of gap between controls within each icon-only group. - **Text-labeled spacing.** Use **16 pixels** of gap between adjacent labeled buttons, text links, pickers, and other navbar items that include visible text; also **16 pixels** between an icon-only button group and the nearest text-labeled item. - Every **dropdown trigger with a text label** (nav submenus, language/currency pickers, category selectors) includes a **chevron or angle-down icon** indicating it opens a menu — never on ellipsis overflow triggers (see below). - The **user avatar** is always a **profile dropdown** — a circular avatar trigger that opens a profile/account menu; never a static, non-interactive avatar. The avatar trigger stands alone — **never** place a chevron, angle-down, or any other icon beside it; the avatar itself is the only affordance. - An **ellipsis overflow trigger** (three dots) stands alone — never place a chevron or second icon beside it; the overflow affordance is implied by the ellipsis. **Icon-only triggers** use a single glyph only — never stack a second icon on the same control. - **Menu toggle (hamburger).** The three-bar icon must **not** appear on screens **wider than 768px** — show it only on **mobile and tablet** viewports (**768px and below**), where it opens the collapsible navigation menu. Hide it entirely above 768px. Implement with the host design system's menu-toggle modifier (e.g. `.ds-menu-toggle`) and an explicit `@media (min-width: 768px) { display: none }` rule — **never** rely on utility `hidden`/`md:hidden` alone on icon-button components whose base styles set `display: inline-flex`, or the hamburger will remain visible on desktop.

items.name: Dual Subsection App CTA
items.promptText:
Create a CTA section as two large vertical subsections separated by generous vertical space, all inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**First subsection:** split into two columns on large 1280 px width breakpoints. The left column is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order from top to bottom: a horizontal row of two small square platform icons sitting side by side on one line; a large heading on its own line beneath the icon row; a body paragraph at a comfortable reading width directly beneath the heading; a vertical list of approximately three items where each item begins with a small circular check icon at the left and a single descriptive line to the right of the icon on the same baseline; a short closing sentence on its own line beneath the list; a text link whose label includes a small trailing rightward arrow at the end of the link text (the link sits on its own line beneath the closing sentence). The right column centers one phone mockup whose screen shows a dashboard-style layout with a chart region and a map region visible inside the device frame. Vertically center the mockup relative to the text column.

**Second subsection:** reverse the column order so the phone mockup sits on the left and the text column sits on the right. The left column centers one phone mockup whose screen shows several stacked floating metric cards with softly rounded corners and light elevation (the cards appear to float above a background surface inside the device frame). The right column is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order from top to bottom: a large heading on its own line; a first body paragraph directly beneath the heading; a second body paragraph directly beneath the first; a thin horizontal divider spanning the column width; a vertical list of approximately five items where each item begins with a small circular check icon at the left and a single descriptive line to the right of the icon on the same baseline; a horizontal row containing a solid primary button (with a small trailing rightward arrow at the right of its label) and a bordered secondary button placed to the right of the primary button **beside each other on one row** (the row never wraps to a second line — treat this as the global two-button row rule).

On narrow viewports, stack each subsection's columns so copy appears before the phone mockup in both blocks (text column first, mockup second) for consistent reading order; state this choice in implementation.

items.name: Left-Aligned Resource Card CTA
items.promptText:
Create a CTA section as one vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a left-aligned copy block containing, in order from top to bottom: a large heading on its own line; a first supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a second supporting paragraph directly beneath the first (the two paragraphs are separate elements, not one merged block); a short bold sub-heading on its own line that introduces the interactive card area below (for example a "see more" style label).

Below the copy block, leave clear vertical space, then place a two-column by two-row grid of horizontal resource cards on large 1280 px width breakpoints. Each card is laid out as a single horizontal row containing, from left to right: a small square brand mark (icon or logo glyph) flush to the left edge of the card; a middle vertical stack pairing a bold title line on top with a smaller description paragraph directly beneath it; a trailing rightward arrow affordance flush to the right edge of the card indicating navigation. One card may use a filled surface treatment (subtle background tint) so it reads as featured or hovered, while the remaining cards stay bordered with a light surface. Give every card thin outer borders, softly rounded corners, and consistent internal padding.

On narrow viewports, collapse the grid to a single column and stack the four cards in their original reading order (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right).

items.name: Two-Column Diamond Image CTA
items.promptText:
Create a CTA section split into two columns on large 1280 px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order from top to bottom: a large two-line heading on its own line; a first body paragraph at a comfortable reading width directly beneath the heading; a second body paragraph directly beneath the first; a single horizontal row containing a pill-shaped primary button with a small trailing rightward arrow at the right of its label and a plain text link with a small trailing rightward arrow placed to the right of the button **on the same horizontal row** (one flex row, items vertically centered on the same baseline, never stacked — the button sits at the leading edge of the row and the text link follows after a small gap).

The **right column** shows one photograph inside a square frame that is rotated forty-five degrees so the media reads as a diamond shape. Keep the frame's own corners softly rounded so the diamond silhouette stays legible and does not appear as a sharp rhombus. Vertically center the diamond frame relative to the text column when the two columns differ in height. Clip the photograph to the rotated frame so no overflow is visible.

On narrow viewports, stack with the text column first and the diamond-framed image beneath it, centered horizontally.

items.name: Centered Market Table CTA
items.promptText:
Create a CTA section as one vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the very top, place a centered primary heading on its own line.

Below the heading, place a five-column data table whose rows are separated by thin horizontal rules only (no vertical dividers inside the table body). Each row contains, in column order: a first column stacking a primary line label on top with a smaller secondary ticker line directly beneath it (the two lines read as one compound cell); a second column showing a single numeric price value; a third column showing a signed percentage change (positive or negative); a fourth column showing a large numeric market-cap style value; a fifth column holding a compact inline sparkline chart whose slope direction matches the sign of the change value in that row (rising slope for positive change, falling slope for negative change).

Below the table, leave generous vertical space, then place a full-width band whose interior carries a subtle rectilinear grid motif with sparse small square accents distributed across the surface so the band reads as a decorated field. Inside that band, center a vertical stack containing, in order: a large heading on its own line; a single supporting sentence directly beneath the heading; one pill-shaped primary button centered horizontally beneath the supporting line. Keep the band's internal padding generous so the copy and button breathe within the patterned surface.

items.name: Two-Column Newsletter CTA
items.promptText:
Create a CTA section split into two columns on large 1280 px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Align both columns to the top so the heading in the left column sits level with the top edge of the first benefit card in the right column.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack with no card chrome (no border, no background fill) containing, in order from top to bottom: a large two-line primary heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width directly beneath the heading; generous vertical space; a small required-style field label paired with a tiny circular question-mark information affordance sitting immediately to the right of the label text on the same baseline; one horizontal row containing a wide email text input (the input carries a small leading envelope icon inside the field and placeholder copy) plus a compact solid primary button whose width hugs its single short word label, placed at the trailing end of the same row **on the same line** as the input (the email field flexes to fill all remaining horizontal space while the button never wraps below the input — treat this as the global input-plus-button row rule); a small helper line of secondary text directly beneath that row.

The **right column** stacks two equal-width benefit cards separated by a small vertical gap. Each card has a thin outer border, softly rounded corners, and generous internal padding. Inside each card, the first element is a single horizontal row placing a small circular check icon at the left and a bold single-line title to the right of the icon on the same baseline. Directly below that icon-and-title row, stack a multi-line supporting paragraph that sits flush-left under the full width of the icon-and-title row (the paragraph is not indented further under the title text alone). Keep both cards the same width and let their heights flow naturally with their content.

On narrow viewports, collapse to a single column with the newsletter block first and the two benefit cards stacked beneath it in their original top-to-bottom order.

items.name: Two-Column QR CTA
items.promptText:
Create a CTA section split into two columns on large 1280 px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order from top to bottom: a large heading on its own line; a short sub-headline line directly beneath the heading on its own line; a multi-line body paragraph at a comfortable reading width directly beneath the sub-headline; a text link whose label includes a small trailing rightward arrow affordance at the end of the link text (the link sits on its own line beneath the paragraph).

The **right column** centers one square QR code graphic both horizontally and vertically within the column. The QR code is framed by a light "corner bracket" treatment — four small right-angle bracket shapes positioned at the four corners of the code so it reads as a scanning target. Vertically center the entire QR block relative to the text column when the two columns differ in height.

On narrow viewports, stack with the text column first and the QR code block beneath it, centered horizontally.

items.name: Centered Team Card Grid
items.promptText:
Create a team section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a large heading centered on its own line followed by a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath it at a moderate reading width. Below the paragraph, place a single centered text link on its own line whose label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, place a responsive grid of team member cards arranged as four columns and two rows on the widest breakpoint, with consistent gutters between all cards. Each card is a rounded rectangular panel with a thin outer border. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a large rectangular photograph that spans the full card width at the top (cropped to a landscape or portrait aspect ratio); the team member's name on its own line directly below the image in medium weight with comfortable horizontal padding; a single-line job title directly below the name in lighter weight; a short multi-line description paragraph directly below the title at the card's internal reading width; and a horizontal row of small social-media icon links sitting side by side on the same baseline at the bottom of the card with comfortable padding.

On smaller breakpoints reduce the column count stepwise (four, then two, then one) until the cards form a single column on the narrowest viewports; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Team Narrative With Profile Grid
items.promptText:
Create a team section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large left-aligned multi-line heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a second paragraph directly below the first that elaborates on the team narrative at the same reading width. Below the paragraphs, after extra vertical space, place a horizontal row of three stat blocks on the same baseline; each block is a compact vertical stack composed of one large prominent numeric value (e.g. "10k+") on its own line at the top and a short descriptive label directly beneath the value. Below the stat row, place a single compact outlined button on its own line whose label is composed of a small leading icon and a short action label on the same baseline.

The **right column** contains a two-column by two-row grid of four team member blocks with consistent gutters between them. Each block is a centered vertical stack containing, in order: a medium circular avatar image at the top; the team member's name on its own line directly below the avatar in medium weight; a single-line job title directly below the name in lighter weight; and a horizontal row of small social-media icon links sitting side by side on the same baseline directly below the title.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the description column first and the team grid directly beneath it; preserve all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Team Grid With Header Action
items.promptText:
Create a team section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a header row split into two halves on the same baseline: a left-aligned vertical stack containing a large heading on its own line and a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; and a single compact outlined button anchored to the right end of the row whose label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, place one large transparent container with no shadow or borders. Inside the container, build a four-column by two-row grid of eight team member blocks with consistent gutters between columns and rows. Each block is a centered vertical stack containing, in order: a medium circular avatar image at the top; a small pill-shaped badge on its own line directly below the avatar (composed of a tiny leading icon and a short role-category label); the team member's name on its own line directly below the badge in medium weight; a single-line job title directly below the name in lighter weight; and a compact outlined button at the bottom of the block whose label is composed of a small leading icon and a short action label (e.g. "Contact me") on the same baseline.

On smaller breakpoints reduce the column count stepwise (four columns, then two, then one) until the blocks form a single column on the narrowest viewports; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Team Contact Card Grid With Logo Row
items.promptText:
Create a team section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a header row split into two halves on the same baseline: a left-aligned vertical stack containing a large heading on its own line and a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; and a single compact outlined button anchored to the right end of the row whose label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, place a responsive grid of team member cards arranged as four columns and three rows on the widest breakpoint, with consistent gutters between all cards. Each card is a rounded rectangular panel with a thin outer border. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a large rectangular photograph that spans the full card width at the top (cropped to a consistent aspect ratio); the team member's name on its own line directly below the image in medium weight with comfortable horizontal padding; a single-line job title directly below the name in lighter weight; a contact-detail row composed of a small leading icon and an email address on the same baseline; and a second contact-detail row composed of a small leading icon and a phone number on the same baseline directly below the email row.

Below the card grid, after extra vertical space, place a centered horizontal row of brand logos, each rendered as a small monochrome glyph with consistent spacing between them.

On smaller breakpoints reduce the column count stepwise (four, then two, then one) until the cards form a single column on the narrowest viewports; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Team Testimonial With Photo Grid
items.promptText:
Create a team section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

At the top of the section, place a left-aligned header block composed of a large heading on its own line followed by a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width. Below the paragraph, place a single text-style link on its own line whose label includes a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, the **left column** contains a single tall testimonial card with rounded corners and a thin outer border. Inside the card, stack from top to bottom: a large decorative quotation mark centered horizontally; a multi-line quote paragraph centered within the card; and an attribution row composed of a small circular avatar on the left, the testimonial author's name to the right of the avatar on the same baseline, and a secondary line of the author's role or handle directly beneath the name.

The **right column** contains a two-column by two-row grid of four team member photo blocks with consistent gutters between them. Each block is a rounded rectangular container filled edge-to-edge by a large portrait photograph. At the bottom of each photo container, overlay a compact content strip containing the team member's name on its own line and a single-line job title directly below the name — the strip sits above the image with a short accent bar or indicator along one edge to visually frame the text.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the testimonial card first and the photo grid directly beneath it; the four photo blocks reflow into a two-column arrangement or a single column on the narrowest breakpoints.

items.name: Filterable Team Photo Grid
items.promptText:
Create a team section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header stack composed of a small pill-shaped badge on its own line (containing a tiny leading icon and a short label); a large centered multi-line heading directly below the badge; and a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a moderate reading width.

Below the header, place a single horizontal row of category filter controls centered on the page (e.g. "Board members", "Developers", "Designers", "Marketing", "Support"). Each control is composed of a small leading icon and a short label on the same baseline; one control carries a distinct active treatment while the remaining controls use a plain text appearance.

Below the filter row, place a responsive grid of team member photo blocks arranged as four columns and two rows on the widest breakpoint, with consistent gutters between all blocks. Each block is a large rounded rectangular container filled edge-to-edge by a portrait photograph. At the bottom of each container, overlay the team member's name on its own line and a single-line job title directly below the name — both positioned over the lower portion of the image.

Below the grid, place a centered footer bar on its own line composed of a small leading icon, a short bold prompt (e.g. "Want to join?"), a supporting sentence to its right on the same baseline, and a text-style link with a trailing arrow icon anchored to the right end of the bar.

On smaller breakpoints reduce the column count stepwise (four, then two, then one); the filter row scrolls horizontally or wraps; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Newsletter Social Grid And Store Locator Bar
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce footer with a newsletter + social top bar, a large multi-group link grid, a centered payment-logo band, and a bottom area with a store-locator note, copyright, legal links, and a language dropdown. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this footer so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Footer frame.** A full-width footer on the host primary surface; each region's content is centered in a max-width container with a hard cap of 1280 pixels and 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Top bar.** A block with a **full-width bottom border drawn from the design system's border token** that runs the full width of the container as the midway divider between this region and the columns region, and ~32px of vertical padding, laid out as a space-between, vertically-centered row with a 16-pixel gap from the small breakpoint up (stacked otherwise): a full-width **newsletter form** — a row pairing a relative, growing email field (~16px end margin, capped ~384 pixels from the medium breakpoint up; host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, ~12px padding, ~14px text, "Enter your email address" placeholder, label visually hidden) with a "Subscribe" brand button (~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding, ~14px medium label) — and a **social row** (16px above it on mobile, end-aligned from the small breakpoint up) of ~8px-gapped icon-only social links, each a 40-by-40-pixel host-rounded ghost button holding a 24-by-24-pixel brand social glyph with a hover fill. **Columns region.** A block with ~24px of vertical padding (64 from the small breakpoint up, 32 from the medium breakpoint up): a one-column grid that becomes two columns from the small breakpoint up and four from the large breakpoint up, with 32-pixel gaps. Each grid cell **stacks several link groups** 24px apart (32 from the medium breakpoint up). Each link group is a ~14px semibold uppercase heading-color heading with 16px beneath it over a vertical list of muted links 12px apart that shift to the heading color on hover (headings such as "Make money with us", "Company", "Payment Methods", "Orders & Shipment"). **Payment band.** A full-width band on a soft secondary surface with **full-width top and bottom borders drawn from the design system's border token** that serve as the midway dividers separating it from the columns region above and the bottom area below, and ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up); inside the 1280-pixel-capped container a centered, wrapping row of payment/partner brand logos at ~40–44px tall with ~32px gaps (~64px from the small breakpoint up), each keeping its own mark. **Bottom area.** A block with ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up) in the 1280-pixel-capped container: a **store-locator note** with a bottom divider and ~16px bottom padding — a ~14px muted line ("More ways to shop: Find a [Brand] Store or other authorized retailer near you. Or call [phone]") with brand, underlined, hover-no-underline inline links — then a ~16px-padded row that becomes a space-between, vertically-centered, 16-pixel-gapped row from the xl breakpoint up (stacked otherwise): a ~14px muted copyright line ("© [year] [Brand], Inc. All rights reserved." with the brand a hover-underline link), a wrapping, 16-pixel-gapped row of ~14px medium heading-color hover-underline legal links ("Conditions of Use & Sale", "Privacy Notice", "Cookies Notice", "Ads Notice"), and a non-shrinking **language dropdown** (a ~14px medium muted trigger with a ~20px flag glyph, an "English (US)" label, and a trailing ~16px chevron, opening a ~176-pixel menu of language rows with ~16px flag thumbnails). **Design system rule.** Every element here — the newsletter input and Subscribe button, the social buttons, link groups and links, the payment logos, the store-locator note and inline links, the copyright and legal links, and the language dropdown with its menu — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the email input — and every button, link, or menu must be the host design system's own form-control, button, link, and menu components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; payment, social, and flag marks keep their conventional colors. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Subscribe" brand button uses ~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the social buttons are 40-by-40-pixel icon buttons; the language trigger is a ghost/text button (its menu rows use ~12px horizontal / ~8px vertical padding). Primaries use the host brand button. **Sizing rules.** The containers cap hard at 1280 pixels, the email field at ~384 pixels, the social buttons at 40-by-40 pixels around 24-by-24-pixel glyphs, the payment logos at ~40–44 pixels tall, the language flag glyph at ~20px, the menu at ~176 pixels, the menu flag thumbnails at ~16px, the group headings at ~14px, and link rows 12px apart. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The top bar stacks the newsletter form above the social row until the small breakpoint; the columns grid steps from one to two to four columns across the small and large breakpoints (each cell stacking its link groups); the payment band centers and wraps; the bottom area stacks the copyright, legal links, and language dropdown until the xl breakpoint.

items.name: Service Blocks Columns And Certificates
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce footer with a row of icon service blocks, a four-column region mixing link groups with a newsletter/app block and certificate logos, and a bottom bar with the logo, copyright, legal links, and an accessibility note. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this footer so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Footer frame.** A full-width footer on the host primary surface; content centered in a max-width container with a hard cap of 1280 pixels and 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Service blocks.** A block with a bottom divider and ~24px of vertical padding (64 from the small breakpoint up, 32 from the medium breakpoint up): a one-column grid that becomes three columns from the large breakpoint up, with ~64px column gaps and 24px row gaps (32 from the medium breakpoint up). Each block is a top-aligned, 16-pixel-gapped row: a 36-by-36-pixel muted service glyph and a growing body with a **link-group heading** (~14px semibold uppercase), a ~14px muted description (12px beneath), and a vertical list (12px apart) of ~14px medium brand, underlined, hover-no-underline action links. Use three blocks ("Order Tracking & Shipping", "Our Credit Card", "Contact Us" — the last with a ~14px muted address line and contact rows each leading with a 16-by-16-pixel muted glyph). **Columns region.** A block separated from the service blocks above it by a **full-width divider/border drawn from the design system's border token** that runs the full width of the container midway between the two regions (i.e. the service-blocks block's bottom border doubles as the columns region's top border); it has its own bottom divider and ~24px of vertical padding (64 from the small breakpoint up, 32 from the medium breakpoint up): a one-column grid that becomes two columns from the small breakpoint up and four from the large breakpoint up, with ~48px column gaps and 24px row gaps (32 from the medium breakpoint up): - Two columns each stacking two **link groups** (24px apart, 32 from the medium breakpoint up) — "Make money with us"/"Company" and "Payment Methods"/"Orders & Shipment". - A column stacking a **newsletter group** ("Get the latest deals and more" heading over the newsletter form, the email label visually hidden) and an **app group** ("Our app" heading, a ~14px muted blurb, and the two stacked app-store buttons). - A column of **certificate logos** — an 32-pixel-gapped row (centered from the xl breakpoint up) of two ~96px-tall responsive certificate marks. **Bottom bar.** A block separated from the columns region above it by a **full-width divider/border drawn from the design system's border token** that runs the full width of the container midway between the two regions (the columns region's bottom border doubles as this bar's top border), with ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up), laid out as a vertically-centered, 32-pixel-gapped row from the xl breakpoint up (stacked otherwise): a non-shrinking ~32px-tall logo, then (from the xl breakpoint up, with a leading vertical divider and ~32px start padding) a **single vertically-centered flex-wrap row** (~14px, 16-pixel gap) that keeps the copyright, the legal links, and the accessibility note all on the **same line** — a muted copyright line ("© [year-range] [Brand]. All rights reserved."), then on that same baseline-aligned line a wrapping group of ~14px medium heading-color hover-underline legal links ("Conditions of Use & Sale", "Privacy Notice", "Cookies Notice", "Ads Notice"), then a muted accessibility/assistance note; they sit inline and vertically centered, only wrapping to a new line when there is truly no horizontal room. **Newsletter rule.** A vertically-stacked form (16-pixel rhythm): a relative, full-width email field (host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, ~12px padding, ~14px text, "Enter your email address" placeholder, label visually hidden) over a full-width "Subscribe" brand button (~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding, ~14px medium label). **App-store rule.** Two full-width, 16px-stacked dark badge buttons (host rounded corners, ~16px horizontal / 10px vertical padding) each with a 28-by-28-pixel store glyph (12px end margin) and a two-line label (~12px caption over ~14px semibold store name). **Link-group rule.** A ~14px semibold, uppercase, heading-color heading with 16px beneath it over a vertical list of links 12px apart; muted body links shift to the heading color on hover. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the service glyphs and their action links, link groups and links, the newsletter input and Subscribe button, the app-store buttons, the certificate logos, the logo, and the legal/copyright/note text — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the email input — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; the app-store pills' dark fill and the certificate marks may keep their conventional appearance. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Subscribe" brand button uses ~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the app-store pills use ~16px horizontal / 10px vertical padding; action links are inline text links. Primaries use the host brand button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the service glyphs at 36-by-36 pixels, the contact glyphs at 16-by-16 pixels, the certificate logos at ~96 pixels tall, the app-store glyphs at 28-by-28 pixels, the logo at ~32 pixels tall, the group headings at ~14px, and link rows 12px apart. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The service blocks step from one to three columns at the large breakpoint; the columns region steps from one to two to four columns across the small and large breakpoints (each link/newsletter column stacking its groups); the certificate logos center from the xl breakpoint up; the bottom bar stacks the logo above the copyright/legal/note cluster until the xl breakpoint.

items.name: Three-Band Sitemap Footer
items.promptText:
Create a footer section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding, composed of four distinct bands separated by generous vertical space.

**Newsletter band** — a centered vertical stack containing a large centered multi-line heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a single inline form row composed of a text input with a leading email icon and placeholder text on the left and a compact primary submit button directly to its right on the same baseline, centered as a pair beneath the heading.

**Sitemap band** — a horizontal row of four equal-width link columns on large breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each column is a left-aligned vertical stack containing a bold category heading on its own line at the top followed by a vertical list of plain text links, one per line, directly beneath the heading.

**Contact band** — a horizontal row of three contact blocks on the same baseline with consistent spacing between them. Each block is a horizontal composition of a small icon anchored to the left (representing the contact channel — phone, email, or location) and a text group to the right of the icon containing a short descriptive label on its own line and a prominent contact value directly beneath the label.

**Bottom bar** — a horizontal row spanning the full container width containing, from left to right: a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline; a centered copyright line; and a compact language selector composed of a small flag icon paired with a language label and a trailing chevron, anchored to the right end of the bar.

On narrow viewports stack each band's columns vertically in reading order; the newsletter form input and button stack vertically; the bottom bar elements center and stack in order: brand mark, copyright, language selector.

items.name: Multi-Band Newsletter Footer
items.promptText:
Create a footer section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding, composed of four distinct bands separated by generous vertical space.

**Newsletter band** — a centered vertical stack containing a large centered multi-line heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a single inline form row composed of a text input with a leading email icon and placeholder text on the left and a compact primary submit button directly to its right on the same baseline, centered as a pair beneath the heading.

**Sitemap band** — a horizontal row of four equal-width link columns on large breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each column is a left-aligned vertical stack containing a bold category heading on its own line at the top followed by a vertical list of plain text links, one per line, directly beneath the heading.

**Contact band** — a horizontal row of three contact blocks on the same baseline with consistent spacing between them. Each block is a horizontal composition of a small icon anchored to the left (representing the contact channel — phone, email, or location) and a text group to the right of the icon containing a short descriptive label on its own line and a prominent contact value directly beneath the label.

**Bottom bar** — a horizontal row spanning the full container width containing, from left to right: a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline; a centered copyright line; and a compact language selector composed of a small flag icon paired with a language label and a trailing chevron, anchored to the right end of the bar.

On narrow viewports stack each band's columns vertically in reading order; the newsletter form input and button stack vertically; the bottom bar elements center and stack in order: brand mark, copyright, language selector.

items.name: Locations Newsletter Footer
items.promptText:
Create a footer section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding, composed of three distinct bands separated by generous vertical space.

**Locations band** — a horizontal row of three equal-width office blocks on large breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each block is a left-aligned vertical stack containing a bold city name on its own line at the top; a multi-line street address directly below the city name; a phone row composed of a small phone icon anchored to the left and a phone number to its right on the same baseline; and an email row composed of a small email icon anchored to the left and an email address to its right on the same baseline.

**Newsletter band** — a single horizontal row spanning the full container width containing a short label on the left (e.g. "Sign up to our newsletter") and an inline form group to its right on the same baseline, composed of a text input with a leading email icon and placeholder text paired with a compact primary submit button directly to its right.

**Bottom bar** — a horizontal row spanning the full container width containing, from left to right: a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline; a centered copyright line; and a compact language selector composed of a small flag icon paired with a language label and a trailing chevron, anchored to the right end of the bar.

On narrow viewports stack the location blocks vertically in reading order; the newsletter label sits above the form input and button on its own line with the input and button stacking vertically beneath it; the bottom bar elements center and stack in order: brand mark, copyright, language selector.

items.name: Primary Navigation Footer
items.promptText:
Create a footer section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding, composed of two horizontal rows separated by generous vertical space.

**Primary row** — a single horizontal bar spanning the full container width containing, from left to right: a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline; a centered horizontal row of navigation links sitting side by side on the same baseline with consistent spacing between them; and a horizontal row of small social-media icon links anchored to the right end of the bar on the same baseline with consistent spacing between them.

**Copyright row** — a single centered copyright line on its own line below the primary row.

On narrow viewports stack the primary row elements vertically in order: brand mark centered, navigation links centered (wrapping into multiple lines if needed), social icons centered; the copyright line remains centered at the bottom.

items.name: Country Bar Language And Five Columns
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce footer with a country/language top bar, a five-column link grid, and a tinted legal bottom bar. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this footer so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Footer frame.** A full-width footer on the host primary surface. The top bar and the columns region share one centered max-width container with a hard cap of 1280 pixels and 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up); the bottom bar is a separate full-width band that holds its own identical 1280-pixel-capped container. **Top bar.** A block with a **bottom border drawn from the design system's border token** and ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up); its content is a column with 16-pixel spacing that becomes a vertically-centered, 16-pixel-gapped row from the large breakpoint up: a **logo + country cluster** (full-width; stacked, then becoming a vertically-centered, 32-pixel-gapped row from the medium breakpoint up) pairing a ~32px-tall responsive brand mark with a **country list** (16px above it on mobile, removed from the medium breakpoint up) — a wrapping, 16-pixel-gapped row (centered from the xl breakpoint up) of ~14px medium heading-color hover-underline country links ("United States", "Canada", "Australia", "France", "Spain", "Germany", "UK") each separated by a 6-by-6-pixel round muted dot; and a non-shrinking **language dropdown** (per the language rule; 12px above it on mobile, removed from the small breakpoint up). **Columns region.** A block with ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up, 64 from the large breakpoint up): a one-column grid that becomes three columns from the small breakpoint up and five from the xl breakpoint up, with 24-pixel gaps (32 from the medium breakpoint up). Each column is a **link group** (per the link-group rule) with headings such as "Make money with us", "Company", "Payment methods", "Help center", "Orders & shipment"; use five groups with four to ten links each. **Bottom bar.** A **full-width band** spanning the viewport edge to edge on a soft secondary/tinted surface (a tinted surface token clearly distinct from the primary footer surface above) with a **top border drawn from the design system's border token** and ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up); its text is start/left-aligned on mobile and centered from the small breakpoint up. Inside the band sits its own centered max-width container with a hard cap of 1280 pixels (and 16px horizontal padding): a wrapping, 16-pixel-gapped row of ~14px medium heading-color hover-underline legal links ("Conditions of Use & Sale", "Privacy Notice", "Cookies Notice", "Ads Notice") — centered from the small breakpoint up — then, **16px below that row**, a ~14px muted copyright line ("© [year-range] [Brand], Inc. All rights reserved." with the brand name a hover-underline link). **Link-group rule.** A ~14px semibold, uppercase, heading-color heading with 16px beneath it, over a vertical list of links 12px apart; each link is muted body text that shifts to the heading color on hover. **Language rule.** A ~14px medium muted trigger button (shifting to heading color on hover) holding a ~20px flag glyph (8px end margin), an "English (US)" label, and a trailing ~16px chevron; on open it shows a ~176-pixel menu (host rounded corners, shadow, thin dividers) of language rows, each a ~14px muted row with ~12px horizontal / ~8px vertical padding, a ~16px flag thumbnail (8px end margin), a hover fill, and a language label. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the logo, country links and dots, the language dropdown and its menu, the link groups and links, and the legal/copyright links — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. Every interactive control — the language trigger, menu items, and links — must be the host design system's own button, menu, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; flag glyphs may keep their conventional colors. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The language trigger is a ghost/text button with no box fill (its menu rows use ~12px horizontal / ~8px vertical padding); links are inline text links. All states follow the host design system. **Sizing rules.** The container and bottom-bar container cap hard at 1280 pixels, the logo at ~32 pixels tall, the country dots at 6-by-6 pixels, the language flag glyph at ~20px, the menu at ~176 pixels, the menu flag thumbnails at ~16px, the group headings at ~14px, and link rows 12px apart. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The top bar stacks the logo/country cluster over the language dropdown until the large breakpoint (the logo and country list stacking until the medium breakpoint); the columns grid steps from one to three to five columns across the small and xl breakpoints; the bottom bar's legal links and copyright are start/left-aligned on mobile and centered from the small breakpoint up, with the copyright always sitting on its own line 16px below the legal-links row.

items.name: Framed Portrait Newsletter Signup
items.promptText:
Create a newsletter section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Position four large circular portrait photographs as decorative anchors around the perimeter of the section — one near the top-left, one near the top-right, one near the bottom-left, and one near the bottom-right — so they frame the central content without overlapping it.

In the center of the section, place a vertical stack containing, in order: a large centered heading on its own line; a centered supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width; a horizontal row on the same baseline composed of a full-width email text input on the left and a primary subscribe button on the right (the button label includes a trailing arrow icon), centered as a pair beneath the paragraph and constrained to a moderate width. Directly below the subscribe row, place a centered social-proof line composed of a tight horizontal cluster of slightly overlapping small circular user avatars on the left, a small "+" separator, and a short caption stating a subscriber count — all sitting on the same baseline.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack; let the email input and subscribe button wrap into a vertical pair if needed; keep the social-proof row centered below.

items.name: Split Newsletter Signup With Image
items.promptText:
Create a newsletter section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a small pill-shaped badge composed of a short label on its own line; a large left-aligned heading on its own line directly below the badge; a supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width; a full-width email text input on its own line placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space; a full-width primary subscribe button directly below the input (the button label includes a trailing arrow icon); and a horizontal row of short category labels sitting side by side on the same baseline directly below the button, each label composed of a small checkmark icon on the left and a short text to its right.

**Right column** holds one large image with rounded corners that fills the column area, vertically centered relative to the left column content.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the content column first and the image directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Framed Newsletter Signup Card
items.promptText:
Create a newsletter section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding, framed as one wide rounded container that reads as a single card spanning the full container width. Allow a very subtle geometric grid or line texture to appear in one area of the card background as a soft decorative accent without competing with the content.

Inside the card, split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints with comfortable internal padding on all sides.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a left-aligned heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width; and a social-proof row placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, composed of a tight horizontal cluster of slightly overlapping small circular user avatars on the left and a single line of caption copy to their right that includes a numerically emphasized segment (e.g. a subscriber or reader count rendered in bold) — both sitting on the same baseline.

**Right column** is vertically centered relative to the left column and contains a compact form stack, in order: a horizontal row on the same baseline composed of a full-width email text input with a small leading mail icon on the left and a primary subscribe button anchored to the right of the input; and a short line of privacy copy directly below the form row, containing an inline text link (e.g. "Privacy Policy").

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the copy column first and the form column directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order and the card container at full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Quad Bar Navbar With Rating Announcement Search And Secondary Nav
items.promptText: Create a self-contained four-tier marketing-site navbar: a trust/rating utility bar, an announcement banner, a main bar with search and auth utilities, and a secondary navigation row. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this navbar so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width stack of four tiers; every tier centers its content in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Trust utility bar.** A band on a soft brand-tinted surface with 8 pixels of vertical padding and a thin bottom divider, splitting start rating and end feature highlights: - **Rating (start).** Five 16-by-16-pixel amber stars + a ~14px semibold heading-color "5.0" label (stars keep fixed color). - **Features (end).** A row with a 24-pixel gap (hidden below the medium breakpoint), each a 16px brand-foreground glyph + ~14px medium heading-color label: truck / "Fast & Free delivery", wallet / "Fair prices", headset / "Support 24/7". **Announcement bar.** Same centered announcement row as variant 4 (rocket glyph, launch message, "Check it out →" brand link) on the primary surface with 10px vertical padding and a thin bottom divider. **Main bar.** A row with 16 pixels of vertical padding and a thin bottom divider: - **Brand (start).** A non-shrinking logo link about 32 pixels tall. - **Search (center, grows).** A full-width search input capped at about 480 pixels (hidden below the medium breakpoint): host-rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, leading 16px search glyph, "Search" placeholder, 12px/16px padding. - **Nav + utilities (end).** A row with an 8-pixel gap: link list (hidden below large) — "Docs", "Terms & Conditions", "Blog", "Pro Version"; notification icon button; theme-toggle icon button; secondary **"Login"** button (leading 16px login glyph + label, 20px/10px padding). **Secondary nav bar.** A row with 10 pixels of vertical padding and a thin bottom divider, holding a start-aligned link list with a 24-pixel gap: "Home", "Company", "Products" (chevron), "Team", "Features", "Services", "Features", "Contact", plus an ellipsis overflow trigger. Hidden below the large breakpoint except via mobile menu. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any control styling. All controls must use the host design system's components and tokens. Rating stars keep fixed amber color. **Button padding rule.** Icon-only triggers use 8px padding. Login button uses 20px/10px padding. **Sizing rules.** Container caps at ~1280 pixels. Search field caps at ~480 pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** Feature highlights hide below medium; search collapses below medium; link lists collapse below large. **Navbar item rules.** - Every navbar icon glyph is **18 pixels wide × 18 pixels tall** with **8 pixels** of space between the icon and its label or link text. - **Icon-only button groups.** In action and utility rows, group adjacent icon-only buttons and icon-buttons (no visible label) together; use **4 pixels** of gap between controls within each icon-only group. - **Text-labeled spacing.** Use **16 pixels** of gap between adjacent labeled buttons, text links, pickers, and other navbar items that include visible text; also **16 pixels** between an icon-only button group and the nearest text-labeled item. - Every **dropdown trigger with a text label** (nav submenus, language/currency pickers, category selectors) includes a **chevron or angle-down icon** indicating it opens a menu — never on ellipsis overflow triggers (see below). - The **user avatar** is always a **profile dropdown** — a circular avatar trigger that opens a profile/account menu; never a static, non-interactive avatar.
