items.name: Two-Column Editorial Content Section
items.promptText:
Create a content section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The two columns share the same vertical center line.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large heading on its own line; three supporting paragraphs arranged one after another directly beneath the heading (each paragraph separated by consistent vertical spacing); then a horizontal row of two CTA buttons sitting side by side (a secondary button whose label pairs with a small leading book or document icon at the left end, and a primary button whose label pairs with a small trailing arrow icon at the right end). Keep the entire text-and-button stack at a comfortable reading width within the column.

The **right column** contains one large illustrative scene or image that fills the column width and stretches to match the height of the left column's content. Vertically center the illustration relative to the left column so both columns share the same visual midpoint.

On narrow viewports, stack the text-and-buttons column above the illustration; the illustration may scale down proportionally to fit the single-column width.

items.name: Centered Chapter List Content Section
items.promptText:
Create a content section as a vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **heading** sits at the top and is horizontally centered on its own line.

The **chapter container** sits below the heading. Place one large rounded rectangular container that spans most of the content width (roughly three-quarters to full width) and is horizontally centered. Inside the container, stack six chapter entries vertically with consistent spacing between them; each entry is a vertical pair containing a bold chapter title line on top and a multi-line descriptive paragraph directly beneath the title. Separate each entry from the next with enough vertical space to read as distinct sections. The container carries a visible border or subtle filled surface so it reads as a single cohesive card.

The **footer link** sits below the chapter container. Center a single text-style link whose label includes a small trailing arrow icon, placed on its own centered line with comfortable spacing above it.

On narrow viewports, keep the chapter container at full content width with comfortable horizontal padding; preserve all six entries in their original stacking order.

items.name: Split Intro With Stat Row
items.promptText:
Create a content section as a vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **top band** is a two-column split on large 1280px width breakpoints. The two columns share the same vertical center line.

The **left column** of the top band is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; and one CTA button whose label pairs with a small trailing arrow icon at the right end of the label. Keep consistent vertical spacing between each element.

The **right column** of the top band is a left-aligned vertical stack containing three short paragraphs arranged one after another with consistent spacing between them; the paragraphs together form a continuous narrative block.

The **stat row** sits below the two-column band as a full-width horizontal row spanning the entire content area. Place four equal-width stat blocks side by side with consistent gutters. Each block is a compact vertical stack showing one prominent numeric or shorthand value (set at a large display size) on top and a short descriptive label directly beneath it.

On narrow viewports, stack the left column above the right column, then place the stat row beneath both; allow the four stat blocks to wrap into a two-by-two grid or scroll horizontally as needed.

items.name: Narrative Header With Three-Card Grid
items.promptText:
Create a content section as a vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **section label** sits at the top left. Place a small typographic label (for example a short slash-prefixed word) at the top-left corner or flush-left above the heading so it reads as a category marker.

The **narrative header** sits below the section label. Stack a large multi-line heading on its own line and a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width, both left-aligned.

The **card grid** sits beneath the narrative header as three equal-width columns on large 1280px width breakpoints with consistent gutters between them.

The **first card** (left column) is a media-forward card: a background image or texture fills the card area; a short title is placed toward the top of the card (left-aligned with comfortable inset padding); and a longer caption paragraph is anchored toward the bottom of the card (left-aligned with comfortable inset padding). The card carries rounded corners.

The **second card** (center column) follows the same media-forward structure as the first card: background image or texture filling the area, a short title toward the top, and a caption paragraph anchored toward the bottom, with the same rounded corners and inset padding.

The **third card** (right column) is a solid contrast panel with rounded corners: it stacks a short prompt heading and one primary button (centered or left-aligned within the panel) so the panel reads as a call-to-action tile rather than a content card.

On narrow viewports, stack the three columns vertically with consistent spacing between them; keep each card's internal layout intact.

items.name: Centered Header With Staggered Image Grid
items.promptText:
Create a content section as a vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **header block** sits at the top and is horizontally centered: a large heading on its own line, then a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width.

The **CTA row** sits directly below the header block. Center two CTA buttons in a horizontal row (a primary button whose label includes a small trailing arrow icon at the right end, and a secondary button whose label pairs with a small leading eye icon at the left end). Keep consistent spacing between the two buttons.

The **image grid** sits below the CTA row. Lay out a two-row arrangement on a four-column underlying grid with consistent gutters. The top row contains, from left to right: one wide tile spanning the first two columns, a square-ish tile occupying the third column, and a square-ish tile occupying the fourth column. The bottom row contains, from left to right: a square-ish tile occupying the first column, one wide tile spanning the second and third columns, and a square-ish tile occupying the fourth column — so that wide and narrow tiles alternate for a staggered composition. Every cell holds a single image or placeholder region with rounded corners.

On narrow viewports, reflow the grid into a two-column or single-column stack while keeping top-to-bottom, left-to-right reading order sensible; allow tiles to fill the available width with comfortable horizontal padding.

items.name: Split Content With Video CTA
items.promptText:
Create a content section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The two columns share the same vertical center line.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large multi-line heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; then a horizontal row of two CTA buttons sitting side by side (a primary button whose label pairs with a small trailing arrow icon at the right end of the label, and a secondary button whose label pairs with a small leading eye icon at the left end of the label). Keep consistent vertical spacing between the heading, paragraph, and button row.

The **right column** contains one large rectangular media block sized to a 16 : 9 video-frame aspect ratio that fills the column width. Center a circular play-button control on top of the media block (the control sits at the exact horizontal and vertical center of the rectangle and carries a small triangular play glyph inside it). The media block may carry a placeholder background image or a solid filled surface behind the play control.

On narrow viewports, stack the two columns vertically with the text-and-buttons column first and the media block beneath it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Centered Timeline Content Section
items.promptText:
Create a content section as a vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **header block** sits at the top and is horizontally centered: a large heading on its own line, then a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading constrained to a restrained max line width (roughly two-thirds of the content area) so it does not span the full container.

The **timeline band** sits below the header block. A thin horizontal baseline rule runs the full content width with small circular markers placed along it at even intervals. Anchor four milestone columns above or along the baseline, evenly spaced across the width. Each milestone is a vertical stack containing, in order: a small date badge at the top (the badge is a compact inline row pairing a small leading calendar icon with a short date string on the same baseline); a bold short title on its own line directly beneath the badge; a placeholder description paragraph of two to three lines beneath the title; and a text-style link whose label includes a small trailing arrow icon anchored at the bottom of the milestone stack. Maintain equal horizontal gutters between milestone columns.

On narrow viewports, reflow the timeline into a single-column vertical stack while preserving chronological top-to-bottom order; each milestone keeps its internal stacking sequence intact.

items.name: Product Hero With Split Detail Band
items.promptText:
Create a content section as a vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **header row** sits at the top. Place a large left-aligned product or brand heading on its own line; on the same row or directly beneath the heading, place two text-style links in a horizontal row (one link may pair with a small leading external-link icon and the other with a small trailing arrow icon). Keep consistent spacing between the heading and the link row.

The **hero image** sits below the header row. Span one wide horizontal image that fills the full content width; the image carries rounded corners and a placeholder or photographic background.

The **body band** sits below the hero image as a two-column split on large 1280px width breakpoints. The two columns share the same top alignment.

The **left column** of the body band is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: an introductory paragraph on its own; then a vertical list of eight feature lines with consistent spacing between them — each line is a horizontal row pairing a small leading icon at the left with a single-line label to the right of the icon on the same baseline.

The **right column** of the body band is a left-aligned vertical stack containing three multi-line paragraphs arranged one after another with consistent vertical spacing between them.

On narrow viewports, stack the left column above the right column; the hero image remains full width and the feature list and prose paragraphs occupy the single column in their original reading order.

items.name: Centered Header With Card Row and Stats Bar
items.promptText:
Create a content section as a vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **header block** sits at the top and is horizontally centered: first a small pill-shaped badge combining a tiny leading icon at the left with a short label to its right (the badge sits on its own centered line); then a large centered heading on its own line directly beneath the badge; then a single centered text-style link whose label includes a small trailing arrow icon directly beneath the heading.

The **card row** sits below the header block. Arrange three equal-width cards in one horizontal row with consistent gutters between them. Each card is a vertical stack containing, in order: a circular icon or illustration region at the top (centered horizontally within the card); a medium heading on its own line directly beneath the icon; a short description paragraph beneath the heading at the card's reading width; and a compact secondary button whose label pairs with a small leading book icon at the left end, anchored at the bottom of the card stack.

The **statistics bar** sits below the card row as a full-width band spanning the entire content area. Place four horizontal stat items in one row with consistent spacing. Each stat item is a compact inline group showing one large numeric or shorthand value and a short descriptive label beside or directly beneath it.

On narrow viewports, stack the three cards vertically with consistent spacing between them; reflow the statistics bar into a two-by-two grid or a vertical stack as needed.

items.name: Two-Column Event Schedule Panel
items.promptText:
Create an event schedule section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container. At the top, place a left-aligned header block composed of a large heading on its own line followed by a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width.

Below the header, place one large rounded panel spanning the full container width. Inside the panel, split the content into two equal-width columns on large 1280px width breakpoints with a consistent gutter between them. Each column carries a centered column heading on its own line at the top (e.g. "Morning" and "Afternoon").

Below each column heading, stack a vertical list of alost 16 session blocks divided by an horizontal line with consistent vertical spacing between them. Each session block is a left-aligned horizontal row composed of two regions on the same baseline:

**Time column** — a small inline time-range element composed of a tiny clock icon and a short start–end time label on the same baseline, occupying a fixed-width leading area.

**Content column** — a left-aligned vertical stack to the right of the time column containing: a medium-weight session title on its own line — every session title must be a link; a short multi-line description paragraph directly below the title; a speaker row directly below the description composed of a small circular avatar on the left and a two-line text block to its right on the same baseline containing the speaker name on the first line and the speaker role or affiliation on the second line.

On narrow viewports, stack the two columns vertically with the morning column first and the afternoon column directly below it; each session block preserves its internal reading order; the panel stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Three-Day Event Schedule Panels
items.promptText:
Create an event schedule section as one vertically stacked block on a full-width background inside a max-width container. At the top, place a centered vertical stack containing: a small inline element composed of a tiny clock icon and a short timezone label on the same baseline, centered on its own line; a large centered heading on its own line directly below the timezone element; a centered date or date-range line directly below the heading.

Below the header block, place three equal-width day columns in one horizontal row on large 1280px width breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each column is a rounded panel with a day title (e.g. "Wednesday 27th") anchored at the top of the panel on its own line.

Below the day title, stack a vertical list of 16 session blocks separated by comfortable vertical spacing and an horizontal divider. Each session block is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a small inline time-range element composed of a tiny clock icon and a short start–end time label on the same baseline, on its own line; a medium-weight session title on its own line directly below the time range — every session title must be a link; an optional short description or talk title directly below the session title.

Session blocks that represent talks include a speaker row directly below the title: a horizontal element composed of a small circular avatar on the left, and a two-line text block to its right on the same baseline containing the speaker name on the first line and the speaker role or affiliation on the second line. When a session has multiple speakers, stack additional speaker rows vertically beneath the first, each following the same avatar-plus-text pattern.

Session blocks that represent breaks or social events (e.g. coffee, networking, after-party) replace the speaker row with a sponsor row: a short "Sponsors:" label on its own line followed by a horizontal row of small brand logos sitting side by side on the same baseline directly below the label.

On narrow viewports, stack the three day columns vertically in their original left-to-right reading order; each column stretches to the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Filtered Metric Bar Chart Widget
items.promptText:
Create an application dashboard widget as a self-contained surface card intended to sit inside a dashboard grid cell. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent widgets; only output this widget component code.

**Widget shell.** Wrap the entire widget in a surface card container with a fixed canvas height of 540 pixels, 24 pixels of internal padding on large screens and 16 pixels on mobile and small screens, 12 pixels of corner radius using the medium (md) radius token, background set to the host design system's primary surface color, an optional 1 pixel default border, and optional subtle elevation shadow.

**Header row.** At the top, place a horizontal row with space between regions. On the left, stack a large bold primary metric value (such as "385,756") using tabular numerals above a short metric label (such as "Users by country") in a muted secondary weight. On the right end, group two compact filter dropdown triggers side by side on the same baseline: one showing a small flag glyph, a region label (such as "United States"), and a trailing chevron; the other showing a small device icon, a device label (such as "Desktop"), and a trailing chevron. Separate the header from the body with a thin horizontal divider below it.

**Chart body.** Below the header, fill the remaining canvas height with a responsive single-series vertical bar chart spanning seven time buckets labeled Mon through Sun on the x-axis. Render each bar in a solid brand color with flat tops. Center a numeric data label directly above each bar (such as "2139", "2466", "2856") using tabular numerals and a small semibold weight. Omit grid lines to keep the chart minimal.

**Footer row.** Below the chart, separated by a thin horizontal divider above it, place a horizontal footer row with space between regions. On the left, place a period dropdown trigger styled as a bordered pill with a calendar icon, a range label (such as "Last 7 days"), and a trailing chevron. On the right, place a secondary outlined button labeled "View report".

**Chart implementation.** Wire the chart to realistic typed sample data — not a static SVG mock, CSS-only placeholder, or decorative illustration. Use the chart library already present in the target project; if none exists, add a well-supported option with the target app's package manager and install dependencies only in that app workspace (do not assume npm, yarn, pnpm, bun, or any specific package name). Keep the visualization responsive within the widget shell. Enable hover tooltips with human-readable labels and formatted values (currency, counts, or percentages as appropriate). Map fills and strokes to host design system tokens (such as brand, success, and danger). Use smooth curves for line and area series where supported; round bar corners where appropriate.

**Sizing rules.** The widget spans the full width of its grid cell with a fixed canvas height of exactly 540 pixels. Use tabular numerals for all metrics and data labels. Colors, borders, chart treatments, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

**Padding rule.** Use 24 pixels of internal card padding on large screens and 16 pixels on mobile and small screens.

**Divider rule.** Use horizontal divider lines only below the widget header and above the widget footer. Do not place horizontal dividers between other widget sections; separate them with spacing only.

**Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button and dropdown trigger uses padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px.

**Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports preserve the 540-pixel widget height, use 16-pixel card padding on mobile and small screens, stack the header vertically: metric and label first, then the two filter dropdowns wrapping to full width. The chart scales to full card width. The footer stacks period dropdown above the view-report button. Preserve reading order throughout.
