items.name: Dual KPI Line Chart Widget
items.promptText:
Create an application dashboard widget as a self-contained surface card intended to sit inside a dashboard grid cell. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent widgets; only output this widget component code.

**Widget shell.** Wrap the entire widget in a surface card container with a fixed canvas height of 540 pixels, 24 pixels of internal padding on large screens and 16 pixels on mobile and small screens, 12 pixels of corner radius using the medium (md) radius token, background set to the host design system's primary surface color, an optional 1 pixel default border, and optional subtle elevation shadow.

**Header row.** At the top, place a horizontal row with space between regions. On the left, group two KPI blocks side by side with consistent horizontal spacing between them. Each block stacks a muted label with a small trailing info icon button on the same baseline (such as "Clicks" and "CPC") above a large bold metric value (such as "234,5K" and "$1.20") using tabular numerals. On the right end, place a bordered period dropdown trigger (such as "Last week" with a trailing chevron). Separate the header from the body with a thin horizontal divider below it.

**Chart body.** Below the header, fill the remaining canvas height with a responsive dual-series smooth line chart. Render one thick brand-colored primary line and one thinner pale secondary line, both using curved interpolation rather than sharp angles. Include muted horizontal dashed grid lines across the plot area but omit vertical grid lines. Label the x-axis with short date stamps (such as "Jan 21" through "Jan 27") rotated slightly for readability when space is tight.

**Footer row.** Below the chart, separated by a thin horizontal divider above it, place a secondary outlined button on the left labeled "View report" with a small leading eye icon on the same baseline.

**Chart implementation.** Wire the chart to realistic typed sample data — not a static SVG mock, CSS-only placeholder, or decorative illustration. Use the chart library already present in the target project; if none exists, add a well-supported option with the target app's package manager and install dependencies only in that app workspace (do not assume npm, yarn, pnpm, bun, or any specific package name). Keep the visualization responsive within the widget shell. Enable hover tooltips with human-readable labels and formatted values (currency, counts, or percentages as appropriate). Map fills and strokes to host design system tokens (such as brand, success, and danger). Use smooth curves for line and area series where supported; round bar corners where appropriate.

**Sizing rules.** The widget spans the full width of its grid cell with a fixed canvas height of exactly 540 pixels. Use tabular numerals for all metrics. Chart line weights, grid treatments, borders, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

**Padding rule.** Use 24 pixels of internal card padding on large screens and 16 pixels on mobile and small screens.

**Divider rule.** Use horizontal divider lines only below the widget header and above the widget footer. Do not place horizontal dividers between other widget sections; separate them with spacing only.

**Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button and dropdown trigger uses padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. Icon-only info buttons use equal compact padding on all sides instead.

**Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports preserve the 540-pixel widget height, use 16-pixel card padding on mobile and small screens, stack the header vertically: the two KPI blocks side by side on the first row when space allows, period dropdown on the second row spanning full width. The chart scales to full card width. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Semi-Circular Gauge Widget
items.promptText:
Create an application dashboard widget as a self-contained surface card intended to sit inside a dashboard grid cell. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent widgets; only output this widget component code.

**Widget shell.** Wrap the entire widget in a surface card container with a fixed canvas height of 320 pixels, 24 pixels of internal padding on large screens and 16 pixels on mobile and small screens, 12 pixels of corner radius using the medium (md) radius token, background set to the host design system's primary surface color, an optional 1 pixel default border, and optional subtle elevation shadow.

**Header row.** At the top, place a horizontal row with space between regions. On the left, stack a large bold primary metric value (such as "345k") using tabular numerals above a short metric label (such as "Visits by OS") in a muted secondary weight. On the right end, place a compact inline legend with two items sitting side by side: each item shows a small colored circle followed by a category label (such as "macOS" and "Windows"). Separate the header from the body with a thin horizontal divider below it.

**Chart body.** Below the header, fill the remaining canvas with a responsive semi-circular radial bar or gauge chart sized to the full card width. Keep a two-to-one width-to-height container ratio and scale the gauge as large as possible within the space between the header and footer so the arc occupies roughly half to three-fifths of the total card height, centered vertically in that chart area with balanced spacing above and below the arc. Render a thick arc track in a very light neutral color with a brand-colored fill segment covering roughly three quarters of the arc and a neutral remainder segment on the trailing end. Use flat butt caps on segment ends rather than rounded caps.

**Footer row.** Below the chart, separated by a thin horizontal divider above it, place a horizontal footer row with space between regions. On the left, place a period dropdown trigger (such as "Last 7 days" with a trailing chevron). On the right, place a compact text link to a detailed report (such as "Users report" with a trailing chevron icon).

**Chart implementation.** Wire the chart to realistic typed sample data — not a static SVG mock, CSS-only placeholder, or decorative illustration. Use the chart library already present in the target project; if none exists, add a well-supported option with the target app's package manager and install dependencies only in that app workspace (do not assume npm, yarn, pnpm, bun, or any specific package name). Keep the visualization responsive within the widget shell. Enable hover tooltips with human-readable labels and formatted values (currency, counts, or percentages as appropriate). Map fills and strokes to host design system tokens (such as brand, success, and danger). Use smooth curves for line and area series where supported; round bar corners where appropriate.

**Sizing rules.** The widget spans the full width of its grid cell with a fixed canvas height of exactly 320 pixels. Use tabular numerals for the primary metric. Gauge track, segment colors, borders, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

**Padding rule.** Use 24 pixels of internal card padding on large screens and 16 pixels on mobile and small screens.

**Divider rule.** Use horizontal divider lines only below the widget header and above the widget footer. Do not place horizontal dividers between other widget sections; separate them with spacing only.

**Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button and dropdown trigger uses padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px.

**Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports preserve the 320-pixel widget height, use 16-pixel card padding on mobile and small screens. The header stacks metric block above the inline legend. The gauge scales to full card width, preserves the two-to-one semicircle aspect ratio, and stays centered between the header and footer. The footer stacks period dropdown above the report link. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Top Navbar Sidebar Application Shell
items.promptText:
Create an application shell composed of a fixed top navbar spanning the full viewport width and a fixed left sidebar below the navbar, with the remaining space to the right of the sidebar and below the navbar given entirely to the main content area.

**Top navbar** is pinned to the top of the viewport as a full-width horizontal bar. From left to right on the same baseline: a hamburger menu icon; a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right; a search input field with a leading search icon and placeholder text; then grouped on the right end of the bar, a compact primary action button composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label, a small icon-only theme toggle button, a small icon-only notification bell button, a small circular user avatar, and a text logout link.

**Left sidebar** is a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to the left edge of the viewport below the navbar, stretching from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport. Inside the sidebar, stack a vertical navigation list from top to bottom. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Some items include a trailing chevron icon indicating an expandable submenu; when expanded, indented child links appear directly below the parent item as plain text labels without icons. One section carries a highlight state (active color on the label and an expanded submenu visible). One navigation item includes a small colored numeric badge to the right of the label indicating a count. Below the main navigation group, separate a secondary group of utility links at the bottom of the sidebar (such as Docs, Components, Help), each following the same icon-plus-label row pattern.

**Main content area** fills the remaining space to the right of the sidebar and below the navbar. Content placeholder regions are arranged as a dashboard grid inside a centered container with comfortable padding: a full-width region at the top row; a three-column equal-width row of regions in the middle; a two-column unequal-width row (wider left, narrower right) below; and a full-width region at the bottom.

**Sizing rules.** The shell occupies the full viewport: it spans the viewport width edge to edge and stretches from the very top to the very bottom of the viewport with no surrounding page padding, no outer rounded frame, and no enclosing max-width container around the shell itself. Every dotted (dashed-outline) placeholder region inside the main content area is a short horizontal block approximately 240 pixels tall and never grows to absorb remaining vertical space; empty space below the last placeholder remains visible as the content-area background. Every visible action button inside the shell (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, full-width submit, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links or tab triggers, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports the sidebar collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via the hamburger icon in the navbar. The main content area expands to the full viewport width. Grid columns stack vertically in reading order.

items.name: Contact Info Band With Centered Form
items.promptText:
Create a contact section in two vertical stages inside a centered page container constrained to a 1280px width with comfortable side padding.

**Top stage** is a three-column row on large breakpoints with equal column widths and comfortable column gaps. Each cell is a left-aligned vertical stack opening with a small icon at the top (keyed to the cell theme), followed by a bold short title on its own line, then body lines beneath the title: the first cell titles address with city or region name, street line, and postal code each on their own lines; the second cell titles company information with legal entity name and tax identifier each on their own lines; the third cell titles contact info with a short sentence about when to email on its own line and a single general mailto address on the next line. On narrow viewports stack the three cells vertically in reading order with generous spacing between cells.

**Bottom stage** is a form constrained to 640px width and centered horizontally beneath the info band. The form arranges personal fields in a two-column grid on wide layouts with comfortable column gaps: required first-name input on the left (label above with required-field marker; short example placeholder inside) and last-name input on the right (same shape); required email input on the left (label above with required-field marker; company-style placeholder inside) and phone-number composite on the right (a narrow country-or-region prefix select control beside a wider numeric input with spaced-digit placeholder, both on the same baseline); a country single-select on the left (label above; defaulting sensibly) and a language single-select on the right (same shape). Beneath the two-column grid, span a full-width labeled multi-line message textarea (the label sits above on its own line with a required-field marker and an optional small circular question-mark information affordance to the right; the textarea carries a placeholder and allows vertical expansion). Finish with a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text links to the terms of service, then one full-width primary submit button beneath the checkbox whose label combines short send text and a trailing send-arrow glyph.

On narrow viewports collapse the two-column field grid into a single-column stack, keeping the same top-to-bottom reading order.

items.name: Avatar Tag Filter Dropdown
items.promptText: Create a self-contained dropdown menu triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its dropdown panel so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "User filter") whose label is followed by a 16-by-16-pixel chevron glyph set 6 pixels after the text; activating it toggles the dropdown panel. **Dropdown panel.** A floating panel anchored directly beneath the trigger on a raised stacking layer, constrained to a fixed width of 288 pixels, with 12 pixels of internal padding, the primary surface background, a thin default border, a host-token medium (md) corner radius, and a large elevation shadow. **Body.** A vertical stack of labeled sections. Each section opens with a 14-pixel semibold heading in the heading color; the first heading has 12 pixels beneath it, and every later heading has 16 pixels above it and 12 pixels beneath it. Provide these sections in order: - An assignee section: a wrapping row of selectable round avatar swatches with 8 pixels of gap. Each swatch is a 32-by-32-pixel circular selectable control with 2 pixels of inner padding, a thin default border, and the primary surface; it holds a round avatar image and, when selected, takes a brand-colored border and brand-tinted fill. Render about ten avatars with one pre-selected. - A status section: a two-column grid of selectable option cards with 10 pixels of gap. Each card is a full-width centered small-size medium-weight label with 8 pixels of padding, a muted neutral fill, a thin border, and host-token rounded corners; on hover and when selected it switches to a brand-tinted fill, border, and text. Render four cards (such as "Completed", "In progress", "To Do", "Cancelled") with some pre-selected. - A type section: a checkbox list with 2 pixels between rows and 16 pixels below it; each row (8 pixels of padding, subtle hover surface, rounded corners) pairs a 16-by-16-pixel checkbox with a small-size medium-weight label (such as "All", "Issue", "Feature", "Planned", "Sprint", "Milestone"), some pre-checked. - A labels section: a wrapping row of small pill-shaped tag chips with 10 pixels of gap. Each chip is a bordered, muted-filled, rounded link with 6 pixels horizontal and 2 pixels vertical padding, an extra-small medium-weight heading-color label, and a leading 12-by-12-pixel icon glyph 4 pixels before the text (such as "Design", "React", "SEO", "Issue", "Marketing", "Flowbite"). - A priority section: a checkbox list (2 pixels between rows, 16 pixels below) of about four rows (such as "High", "Medium", "Low", "Lowest"), some pre-checked. - An assigned-to section: a checkbox list (2 pixels between rows, 16 pixels below) of two rows (such as "Assigned to me", "All team"), one pre-checked. **Footer.** With 16 pixels of space above it, a horizontal action row of two equal full-width buttons separated by 12 pixels: a secondary outlined reset button (such as "Reset") followed by a primary apply button (such as "Apply"). **Label wrapping rule.** Each checkbox, option-card, and tag label stays on a single line and never wraps, truncating with an ellipsis if it would overflow so every row, card, and chip stays one line tall and the controls stay aligned. The avatar swatches and tag chips themselves may wrap onto new rows as a group. **Sizing rules.** The panel stays fixed at its 288-pixel width. Avatar swatches, option cards, checkbox controls, tag chips and their icons, surfaces, borders, focus rings, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system; brand accents come from host tokens. **Panel radius and concentric item rule.** The dropdown panel uses the host design system's medium (md) corner radius — not the base radius — together with 12 pixels of internal padding. Every interactive nav/option row inside the panel uses 8 pixels of padding and a smaller, concentric corner radius derived from the panel's medium radius minus the panel padding, so the inner rounding nests cleanly inside the panel's corners (for example, a 16-pixel panel radius pairs with an 8-pixel row radius). **Section heading rule.** Every panel section heading uses a 14-pixel semibold type size in the heading color with 12 pixels of margin beneath it. **Button padding rule.** The trigger uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the footer reset and apply buttons use padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. **Checkbox style rule.** Every checkbox is exactly 16 by 16 pixels with a 4-pixel corner radius. In the unchecked state the box uses a host design-system surface and border. In the checked state the box is filled with the brand color AND a clearly visible check (tick) mark is explicitly drawn and centered on top of that fill. That tick mark is always solid white (#ffffff) — it must never inherit the brand color, the current/body text color, or the fill color, and it must never be omitted, so the white tick always contrasts against the brand fill and stays visible in every design system. Do not rely on a native, unstyled, or `appearance-none` control with no glyph; always render an actual white checkmark whenever the checkbox is checked. **Check icon rule.** When a checkbox is checked, a check (tick) icon is always present and always white (#ffffff) — never missing, never the brand color, never the fill or text color — so it stays clearly visible against the brand fill in every design system. **Input surface rule.** Give the checkbox backgrounds a filled host secondary/muted neutral surface that reads as a clearly bounded control, and keep the host default border and focus ring. **Control border rule.** The borders of any checkboxes, radios, text inputs, and selects in this panel are taken from the host design system tokens — their resting, hover, focus, and checked-state border colors all come from the design system rather than any hard-coded value. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the panel may grow toward the available width while staying anchored to the trigger; the avatar swatches and tag chips keep wrapping, the status option-card grid keeps two columns, and the checkbox lists keep single-column rows above the inline reset-then-apply footer.

items.name: Two-Column Customer Proof Section
items.promptText:
Create a customer logos section split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order from top to bottom: a prominent heading on its own line that may open with a large numeric or shorthand claim about client volume or reach; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading that contrasts or enumerates audiences served; a single horizontal band split into two equal columns where each column holds one stat block (each stat block stacks from top to bottom: a small pictogram, a concise one-line title directly below the pictogram, and one short supporting sentence beneath the title); and below the stat band, one full-width primary call-to-action control whose label invites deeper exploration of work or proof and may pair with a small leading icon to the left of the label text.

The **right column** contains only a two-by-two grid of four partner cells whose interior dividing rules (one vertical rule and one horizontal rule crossing at the center) make the block read as one tight quad. Inside each cell, stack from top to bottom: a centered partner mark; a single short partnership metadata line directly under the mark (for example how long the relationship has run); and at the bottom of the cell a compact "visit website" control whose label pairs with a small external-link affordance icon to the right.

On narrow viewports stack the columns with the left narrative-and-stats column first and the partner quad second; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Checklist Date Range Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Create item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a surface-card dialog constrained to a comfortable two-column form width, with internal padding, host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, a soft elevation shadow, and internal scrolling when tall. **Header.** A top row with a short title (such as "Add item") on the left and a small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) on the right, separated from the body by a thin bottom divider. **Body.** A form laid out as a responsive grid (one column on mobile, two from the small breakpoint up). Include, in reading order: a primary name text input, a category-style single-select, a numeric value input, a secondary short text input, then a full-width checklist subsection enclosed by thin top and bottom dividers — a group label above a vertical list of checkbox rows (each a checkbox with a wrapping text label, some pre-checked) followed by a full-width outlined "Add new entry" button with a leading plus icon. After the checklist: a tag-style text input whose label carries a trailing muted "N remaining" counter, a secondary text input, a full-width date-range picker composed of two side-by-side date inputs (a start and an end) each with a leading calendar icon, a status single-select, a notification-period single-select, and a full-width multi-line description textarea. Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk beside the label. **Footer.** A top-divider-separated action row with a primary submit button (such as "Add item") and a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close"). **Sizing rules.** The dialog width stays bounded and never spans edge to edge. The checklist subsection is visually fenced by dividers and its rows share consistent spacing. Checkbox controls, surfaces, borders, focus rings, dividers, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button (trigger, submit, dismiss, and "Add new entry") uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Input padding rule.** Plain inputs and selects use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; date-range inputs reserve start padding for the leading calendar icon; the textarea uses 14px of padding on all sides. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control with a tint pulled from the same neutral tone as the dialog surface, nudged one step lighter — the identical hue and shade, only brighter, never a different color — so the fields separate from the dialog background through a soft, subtle contrast rather than a color shift. Apply this same fill uniformly across all text inputs, numeric inputs, selects, the date-range start and end inputs, the tag input, and the textarea, and keep the host default border and focus ring so each field reads as a cleanly bounded, slightly lifted surface. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the dialog grows toward full width, the field grid collapses to a single column in reading order, the date-range picker stacks its start and end inputs vertically, the checklist and "Add new entry" button span full width, and the footer stacks actions in primary-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Eight Feature Cards Grid
items.promptText:
Create a feature section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a large heading centered on its own line followed by a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath it (constrain the paragraph to a moderate reading width).

Below the header, place a responsive grid of eight feature cards arranged as four columns and two rows on the widest breakpoint, with consistent gutters between all cards. Each card is its own rounded rectangular panel with a thin outer border. Inside each card, stack from top to bottom: a small rounded-square icon container at the top (holding a single centered glyph); a bold short title on its own line directly below the icon; a left-aligned supporting paragraph directly below the title that fills the remaining card width with comfortable internal padding on all sides.

On smaller breakpoints, reduce the column count stepwise (four columns, then two, then one) until the cards form a single column on the narrowest viewports; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Full-Viewport Application Shell With Dual Rails
items.promptText:
Create an application shell composed of a fixed top navbar spanning the full viewport width, a narrow icon-only rail on the far left edge, an expanded text sidebar panel adjacent to the icon rail, the main content area in the center, and a narrow icon-only rail on the far right edge.

**Top navbar** is pinned to the top of the viewport as a full-width horizontal bar spanning above all columns. From left to right on the same baseline: a hamburger menu icon; a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right; a search input field with a leading search icon and placeholder text; then grouped on the right end of the bar, a compact primary action button composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label, a small icon-only theme toggle button, a small icon-only notification bell button, a small circular user avatar, and a text logout link.

**Left icon rail** is a narrow fixed-width vertical strip anchored to the far left edge of the viewport below the navbar, stretching from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport. It contains a vertical stack of small icon-only buttons, each representing a top-level navigation category, centered horizontally in the strip with consistent vertical spacing between them.

**Expanded sidebar panel** sits immediately to the right of the icon rail as a wider fixed-width vertical panel stretching from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport. At the top of the panel, place a header row composed of a short title label on the left and a compact icon-only add button on the right on the same baseline. Below the header, place a search input field with a leading search icon and placeholder text spanning the full panel width. Below the search field, stack a vertical navigation list. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a text label on the left and a trailing chevron icon on the right. One section carries a highlight state (active color) and is expanded to show indented child links below the parent. One item includes a small colored numeric badge to the right of the label. At the very bottom of the panel, anchor a user identity block composed of a small circular avatar on the left, a two-line text group (user name on the first line and email on the second line) to the right of the avatar, and a small trailing chevron or caret icon.

**Right icon rail** is a narrow fixed-width vertical strip anchored to the far right edge of the viewport below the navbar, mirroring the left icon rail in width and structure. It contains a vertical stack of small icon-only buttons centered horizontally with consistent vertical spacing.

**Main content area** fills the remaining horizontal space between the expanded sidebar panel and the right icon rail, and vertically from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport. Content placeholder regions are arranged as a dashboard grid: a top row of three equal-width regions, a middle row of three equal-width regions, and a full-width region at the bottom.

**Sizing rules.** The shell occupies the full viewport: it spans the viewport width edge to edge and stretches from the very top to the very bottom of the viewport with no surrounding page padding, no outer rounded frame, and no enclosing max-width container around the shell itself. Every dotted (dashed-outline) placeholder region inside the main content area is a short horizontal block approximately 240 pixels tall and never grows to absorb remaining vertical space; empty space below the last placeholder remains visible as the content-area background. Every visible action button inside the shell (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, full-width submit, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links or tab triggers, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports both icon rails and the expanded sidebar panel collapse off-screen. The sidebar becomes accessible via the hamburger icon. The main content area expands to the full viewport width. Grid columns stack vertically in reading order.

items.name: Multi-Band Newsletter Footer
items.promptText:
Create a footer section as one vertically stacked block inside a max-width container with comfortable side padding, composed of four distinct bands separated by generous vertical space.

**Newsletter band** — a centered vertical stack containing a large centered multi-line heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a single inline form row composed of a text input with a leading email icon and placeholder text on the left and a compact primary submit button directly to its right on the same baseline, centered as a pair beneath the heading.

**Sitemap band** — a horizontal row of four equal-width link columns on large breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each column is a left-aligned vertical stack containing a bold category heading on its own line at the top followed by a vertical list of plain text links, one per line, directly beneath the heading.

**Contact band** — a horizontal row of three contact blocks on the same baseline with consistent spacing between them. Each block is a horizontal composition of a small icon anchored to the left (representing the contact channel — phone, email, or location) and a text group to the right of the icon containing a short descriptive label on its own line and a prominent contact value directly beneath the label.

**Bottom bar** — a horizontal row spanning the full container width containing, from left to right: a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline; a centered copyright line; and a compact language selector composed of a small flag icon paired with a language label and a trailing chevron, anchored to the right end of the bar.

On narrow viewports stack each band's columns vertically in reading order; the newsletter form input and button stack vertically; the bottom bar elements center and stack in order: brand mark, copyright, language selector.

items.name: Centered Customer Logo Band
items.promptText: Create a customer logos section as one centered vertical stack inside a page-width container with comfortable side padding. At the very top, place a short centered kicker line on its own row naming the social-proof intent (for example a sentence stating that the product is trusted by teams worldwide). Below the kicker, leave a small vertical gap, then center a single horizontal flex row of exactly six partner marks or logotypes that share one visual weight; space the marks with even horizontal gaps so they read as one unified band. No secondary heading is required unless you add a very small optional sub-line directly beneath the kicker on its own centered row. On narrow viewports the mark row wraps into additional centered rows while keeping even horizontal spacing between items and consistent vertical gaps between wrapped lines.

items.name: Three-Bar Application Shell With Two-Column Content
items.promptText:
Create an application shell composed of three fixed horizontal bars stacked at the top of the viewport, with the remaining vertical space below given entirely to the main content area. There is no sidebar in this layout.

**Announcement bar** is pinned to the very top of the viewport as a slim full-width horizontal strip. On the left side, place a horizontal row of short key-value metric pairs sitting side by side on the same baseline with consistent spacing (each pair is composed of a short label followed by a prominently styled value). On the right side of the same strip, place a locale and currency selector row: a small flag icon paired with a language label and a trailing dropdown chevron, followed by a currency code with a trailing dropdown chevron.

**Primary navbar** sits directly below the announcement bar as a full-width horizontal bar. From left to right on the same baseline: a hamburger menu icon; a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right; a search input field with a leading search icon and placeholder text; then grouped on the right end of the bar, a compact primary action button composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label, a small icon-only theme toggle button, a small icon-only notification bell button, a small circular user avatar, and a text logout link.

**Breadcrumb and actions bar** sits directly below the primary navbar as a full-width horizontal bar with a thin border or subtle background shift to visually separate it. On the left side, place a breadcrumb row composed of icon-and-label segments separated by chevron or arrow dividers, where each segment may include a trailing dropdown chevron. On the right side of the same bar, place a row of action controls: a secondary button composed of a small leading icon and a short label, followed by a primary action button composed of a short label and a trailing plus icon.

**Main content area** fills the remaining viewport height below the breadcrumb bar. Content placeholder regions are arranged as two equal-width columns sitting side by side inside a centered max-width container with comfortable padding.

**Sizing rules.** The shell occupies the full viewport: it spans the viewport width edge to edge and stretches from the very top to the very bottom of the viewport with no surrounding page padding, no outer rounded frame, and no enclosing max-width container around the shell itself. Each of the two dotted (dashed-outline) placeholder columns inside the main content area is a tall vertical block approximately 800 pixels tall — taller than every other variant in this set — and never grows to absorb remaining vertical space; the two columns sit side by side at the top of the content area and any empty space below them remains visible as the content-area background, scrolling vertically if the placeholder height exceeds the available viewport room. Every visible action button inside the shell (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, full-width submit, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links or tab triggers, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports the announcement bar may collapse into a horizontally scrollable strip or hide behind a toggle. The primary navbar compresses to essential elements. The breadcrumb bar may truncate to the last segment with a back arrow. The two-column layout stacks vertically in reading order.

items.name: Featured Portfolio Asymmetric Grid
items.promptText:
Create a portfolio section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered supporting paragraph at a comfortable reading width. Directly below the paragraph, place a horizontal row of two text links sitting side by side on the same baseline, each link composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header block, place a three-column asymmetric grid on large 1280px width breakpoints. The **left column** and the **right column** are narrow and equal in width; each stacks two small cards vertically with consistent spacing between them. The **center column** is wider and holds a single tall featured card whose height spans both rows of the side columns.

Inside each **small card**, stack from top to bottom: a brand logo or mark centered on its own line; a project title centered on its own line directly below the logo; a short centered description paragraph directly below the title; and a text-style link at the bottom of the card composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

Inside the **featured center card**, stack from top to bottom: a brand logo or mark centered on its own line; a project title centered on its own line directly below the logo; a two-column checklist of service or scope labels (each row composed of a small circular check icon at the left and a short label to its right on the same baseline); and a horizontal row of two action elements at the bottom — a text-style link on the left composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon, and a primary button on the right composed of a small leading icon and a short label.

On narrow viewports, stack all five cards in a single column with the featured card first, followed by the side cards in left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order.

items.name: Threaded QA With Sort Search And Ask Drawer
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce help-center threaded Q&A: a heading with a sort select, search field, and ask action, an alternating stack of question cards and indented answer cards (with helpful-vote controls), pagination, and an "ask a question" side drawer. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section (and its drawer) so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1024 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up) and a 24-pixel rhythm between regions. **Header.** A block that becomes a bottom-aligned space-between row with a 16-pixel gap from the large breakpoint up: a non-shrinking, growing ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Questions (147)", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) and a **controls cluster** (16px above it on mobile; becoming an end-aligned, 16-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up): a non-shrinking **sort select** (host select input, options "Most helpful" / "Most recent", host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, ~10px vertical / ~10px start / ~40px end padding for its chevron, ~14px text, screen-reader-only label) and a search form pairing the same **search field** as variant 1 (capped ~384 pixels) with an **"Ask a question" brand button** that opens the side drawer. **Thread.** A stack with a consistent **24-pixel gap between every card** — including between each question card and its following answer card, and between one question/answer pair and the next — so the cards never sit flush against each other: - **Question cards** — a card with a ~12-pixel internal rhythm, host rounded corners, a thin border, the host primary/neutral surface, a small shadow, and 24px padding: a header row (12-pixel gap) with a ~16px semibold hover-underline author link and a ~14px muted timestamp; a ~16px muted question body; and a footer row (16-pixel gap) pairing a ~14px medium muted "I have the same question" prompt with a **helpful/vote radio pair** (per the vote rule, e.g. "Yes: 8" / "No: 0"). - **Answer cards** — the same card indented ~48px from the start at the small breakpoint up, leading with an **"Answer" success badge** (inline-flex, host rounded corners, ~10px/2px padding, ~12px medium label, leading 12-by-12-pixel check glyph), then the same author/timestamp header, a ~16px muted answer body, and a footer pairing a ~14px medium muted "Was it helpful to you?" prompt with a helpful/vote radio pair. Use about four question/answer pairs. **Vote radio rule.** A helpful/vote pair is two single-select radios (16-by-16 pixels) with ~14px medium labels 8px after them (e.g. "Yes: 8" and "No: 0"), grouped on one row with a 16-pixel gap and rendered as the host design system's radio component. **Pager.** A centered joined numbered pager (24px above it, 32 from the small breakpoint up, 48 from the large breakpoint up): a 32px-tall row with overlapping 1px borders of a previous-arrow control (leading rounded side), numbered page links (~14px, ~12px horizontal padding), an overflow ellipsis, the last page, and a next-arrow control (trailing rounded side); the current page uses the host's brand-tinted surface, border, and text. **Ask drawer.** A right-anchored, full-height side drawer (full-width, capped ~448 pixels, ~16px padding, host surface, slide-in transition): a ~14px semibold, uppercase muted "Ask a question" label, a top-right icon-only close button (~20px glyph), and the shared ask-a-question form (from variant 1) in a single-column arrangement (the type and priority selects stacked), ending with a full-width "Submit question" brand button. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the sort select, search field, ask button, question/answer cards, the "Answer" badges, the vote radios, author links, the pager, and the drawer with its form controls and buttons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the sort select, the search input, the vote radios, and the drawer's textarea/selects/file/checkbox — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Ask a question" and "Submit question" primary buttons use ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with ~14px medium labels; the pager controls are 32px-tall with ~12px horizontal padding; the drawer close is an icon-only button; primaries use the host brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1024 pixels, the search field at ~384 pixels, the answer-card indent at ~48 pixels, the drawer at ~448 pixels, the badge glyph at 12-by-12 pixels, the vote radios at 16-by-16 pixels, and the pager row at 32 pixels tall. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/semantic accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The header stacks the title over the sort/search/ask controls until the small/large breakpoints; the answer cards lose their indent below the small breakpoint; the drawer spans the available width up to its cap; the pager stays centered.

items.name: FAQ Accordion With Helpful Votes
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce FAQ accordion: a heading, a flush accordion of questions that each expand to an answer (author, date, body, and helpful-vote controls), and a closing "ask a question" prompt. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up) and a 24-pixel rhythm between regions. A ~20px semibold heading-color title ("General questions", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) sits at the top. **Accordion.** A flush accordion (24px below the heading). Each item is: - A full-width **trigger** (a header button): a space-between, vertically-centered row with a 12-pixel gap, a bottom divider, ~20px of vertical padding, a left-aligned **16px, medium-weight** (not normal, not semibold/bold) heading-color question, and a trailing 20-by-20-pixel chevron glyph that rotates when the panel is open; the active item shows its heading-color text, inactive items the muted color. - An expandable **answer panel** (collapsed by default except the first): a body with a ~16px rhythm, a bottom divider, and ~20px of vertical padding — a header row (12-pixel gap) with a ~16px semibold heading-color author name and a ~14px muted date; one or more ~16px muted answer paragraphs (some may begin with a bolded heading-color lead-in label); and a footer row (16-pixel gap) pairing a ~14px medium muted "Was it helpful to you?" prompt with a helpful/vote radio pair (two 16-by-16-pixel radios with ~14px medium labels such as "Yes: 16" / "No: 3"). Use about ten accordion items, the first expanded. **Closing prompt.** Below the accordion (24px above it, 32 from the small breakpoint up), a ~18px muted line ("Didn't find the answer?") containing a brand, underlined, hover-no-underline "Ask a question" link. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the accordion triggers and panels, the chevron glyphs, author/date text, answer paragraphs, the vote radios, and the ask link — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the helpful/vote radios — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The accordion triggers are full-width header buttons with ~20px vertical padding and no horizontal box padding (flush), driven by the host's accordion/disclosure component; the vote radios and ask link follow the host's radio and link components. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the trigger chevrons are 20-by-20 pixels, the vote radios 16-by-16 pixels, the trigger question text 16px medium, the answer text ~16px, and the closing prompt ~18px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/semantic accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The accordion is full-width at every breakpoint; triggers keep their question and chevron on one space-between row (the question wrapping as needed); the closing prompt wraps naturally.

items.name: Segmented Metrics Area Chart Widget
items.promptText:
Create an application dashboard widget as a self-contained surface card intended to sit inside a dashboard grid cell. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent widgets; only output this widget component code.

**Widget shell.** Wrap the entire widget in a surface card container with a fixed canvas height of 540 pixels, 24 pixels of internal padding on large screens and 16 pixels on mobile and small screens, 12 pixels of corner radius using the medium (md) radius token, background set to the host design system's primary surface color, an optional 1 pixel default border, and optional subtle elevation shadow.

**Header row.** At the top, place a horizontal row with space between regions. On the left, stack a widget title (such as a domain name) in a semibold weight above a muted date-range subtitle (such as "31 Nov – 31 Dec") using tabular numerals where applicable. On the right end, place a secondary outlined "Export" button. Separate the header from the body with a thin horizontal divider below it.

**Channel toggle.** Below the header, place a segmented control or toggle button group with two options (such as "Organic" and "Paid") sharing one connected bordered container. Highlight the active segment with a filled background treatment. Do not add drop shadows to the segmented control.

**Metric rows.** Below the toggle, render three horizontal metric rows separated by thin horizontal dividers between rows. Each row is a horizontal strip with space between regions: on the left, a full-width single-series inline area chart that fills the remaining row width before the metrics block. Render one trend line with a matching gradient fill beneath it in a semantic color (green for positive metrics, red for negative), using straight line segments with no axes and no grid lines; on the right, a stacked block with twenty-four pixels of horizontal spacing from the area chart, containing a muted label (such as "Users", "Customers", or "Revenue"), a large bold value (such as "232.7k", "238", or "$4268") using tabular numerals, and a delta line with a directional arrow and comparison text (such as "2% vs last month") colored to match the trend direction.

**Footer row.** Below the metric rows, separated by a thin horizontal divider above it, place a secondary outlined button on the left labeled "View report" with a small leading eye icon on the same baseline.

**Chart implementation.** Wire the chart to realistic typed sample data — not a static SVG mock, CSS-only placeholder, or decorative illustration. Use the chart library already present in the target project; if none exists, add a well-supported option with the target app's package manager and install dependencies only in that app workspace (do not assume npm, yarn, pnpm, bun, or any specific package name). Keep the visualization responsive within the widget shell. Enable hover tooltips with human-readable labels and formatted values (currency, counts, or percentages as appropriate). Map fills and strokes to host design system tokens (such as brand, success, and danger). Use smooth curves for line and area series where supported; round bar corners where appropriate.

**Data binding.** Store datasets in typed constants or reactive state. Interactive controls (segmented time ranges, tabs, toggles, checkboxes, or dropdowns) must update the values shown in the chart, map, or summary metrics — not just restyle the UI.

**Sizing rules.** The widget spans the full width of its grid cell with a fixed canvas height of exactly 540 pixels. Use tabular numerals for all numeric values. Area chart gradient fills, segmented control treatments, borders, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

**Padding rule.** Use 24 pixels of internal card padding on large screens and 16 pixels on mobile and small screens.

**Divider rule.** Use horizontal divider lines only below the widget header and above the widget footer. Do not place horizontal dividers between other widget sections; separate them with spacing only.

**Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button uses padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px.

**Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports preserve the 540-pixel widget height, use 16-pixel card padding on mobile and small screens. The header stacks title and export button vertically. Each metric row keeps the area chart and values on one row when possible; otherwise stack the area chart above values. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Stacked Portfolio Image Overlay Cards
items.promptText:
Create a portfolio section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered heading on its own line; directly below the heading, a centered text link composed of a short label paired with a trailing arrow icon.

Below the header, stack three full-width cards vertically with consistent spacing between them. Each card is a large rounded container whose background is a full-bleed photographic or screenshot image covering the entire card area edge-to-edge. Layer a semi-transparent dimming gradient over the image so all foreground content remains readable. Anchor all foreground content to the lower-left area of the card with comfortable inset padding.

Inside each card overlay, stack from bottom to top (visually anchored to the card's lower-left corner): a short description paragraph on its own line; a prominent project title on its own line directly above the description; a horizontal row of small tech-stack or tool icons sitting side by side on the same baseline directly above the title.

On narrow viewports, keep the same stacked full-width card layout; reduce card height proportionally and ensure the overlaid text and icons remain legible with sufficient contrast against the dimmed background.

items.name: Alternating Split Features with Diamond Media
items.promptText:
Create a feature section composed of two stacked bands separated by generous vertical space inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Each band is a two-column split on large 1280px width breakpoints.

**First band** — the **left column** carries the text stack and the **right column** carries the media block.

**Second band** — swap so the **left column** carries the media block and the **right column** carries the text stack.

In each **text column**, stack a left-aligned vertical composition containing, in order: a large left-aligned heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a thin horizontal rule spanning the column width; a vertical list of items where each item is a horizontal row composed of a small checkmark icon anchored to the left and a single line of descriptive text to the right on the same baseline; optionally a second thin horizontal rule below the list followed by a short closing paragraph on its own line.

In each **media column**, place one photograph inside a square frame with rounded corners that is rotated approximately 45 degrees so the photograph reads as a diamond shape. Behind the diamond frame, position a faint dotted diamond or lattice motif that extends slightly past the photo frame on all sides, creating a soft decorative halo around the image.

On narrow viewports, stack each band as a single column with the media block first and the text stack second; preserve all internal reading order within each stack.

items.name: Selectable Option Form Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Create item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a wide surface-card dialog constrained to a large two-pane width. The dialog has internal padding, host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, a soft elevation shadow, and scrolls internally when tall. **Header.** A top row with a short title (such as "Add item") on the left and a small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) on the right, separated from the body by a thin bottom divider. **Body.** A form split into two equal columns from the small breakpoint up (stacked on mobile) with the columns aligned to the top. - **Left column** is its own responsive field grid (one column on mobile, two from the small breakpoint up): a primary name text input, a secondary short text input, a numeric value input, a category-style single-select, a cluster of four compact numeric inputs each with a small leading icon, and a full-width subsection containing a group label and a horizontal row of two selectable option cards. Each option card is a bordered surface tile holding a glyph, a bold option title, a short supporting description, and a radio control aligned to the top-end corner; selecting a card reflects a checked state and the cards behave as one single-choice radio group. - **Right column** stacks a full-width multi-line description textarea, a full-width image upload dropzone (dashed-border drop area with upload glyph, instruction line, max-file-size hint, and a "Browse file" button plus a hidden native file input), and a full-width inline single-choice radio group with two options on one baseline. Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk beside the label. **Footer.** A top-divider-separated action row with a primary submit button carrying a small leading plus icon (such as "Add item"), a secondary outlined button with a leading icon (such as "Schedule"), and a final secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close") pushed to the far end on wide viewports. **Sizing rules.** The dialog width stays bounded to its large maximum and never spans edge to edge. Option cards share equal sizing and a consistent selected treatment. Surfaces, borders, dashed outlines, card selection rings, focus rings, dividers, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button (trigger, submit, secondary action, dismiss, and "Browse") uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Input padding rule.** Standard fields use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; icon-prefixed inputs reserve start padding for the icon; the textarea uses 14px of padding on all sides. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control with a tint pulled from the same neutral tone as the dialog surface, nudged one step lighter — the identical hue and shade, only brighter, never a different color — so the fields separate from the dialog background through a soft, subtle contrast rather than a color shift. Apply this same fill uniformly across all text, numeric, icon-prefixed, and select inputs, the textarea, and the upload dropzone drop area, and keep the host default border (or dashed border for the dropzone) and focus ring so each field reads as a cleanly bounded, slightly lifted surface. The selectable option cards may share this same fill so they sit in the same tonal family as the fields. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the two panes stack into one column (left pane first, right pane second), every inner grid collapses to a single column, the option cards stack vertically, the dropzone spans full width, and footer actions stretch to full width and stack in primary-then-secondary-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Static FAQ Card Grid
items.promptText:
Create a FAQ section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large centered heading on its own line.

Below the heading, place a three-column grid of almost 16 FAQ entry cards with consistent gutters between columns and rows on large breakpoints. Each card is a rounded rectangular panel containing a left-aligned vertical stack, in order: a bold question title on its own line at the top of the card; a multi-paragraph answer block directly below the title, left-aligned with comfortable internal padding on all sides. All entries are permanently visible (no accordion collapse). Inline text links may appear within the answer copy.

Distribute the entries across rows of three cards, filling left-to-right top-to-bottom. Allow varying card heights based on content length while keeping cards within each row top-aligned.

On narrow viewports collapse the grid to two columns first, then to a single column on the narrowest breakpoints; preserve left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order throughout.

items.name: Condition Builder Select Dropdown
items.promptText: Create a self-contained dropdown menu triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its dropdown panel so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Filter by properties") whose label is followed by a 16-by-16-pixel chevron glyph set 6 pixels after the text; activating it toggles the dropdown panel. **Dropdown panel.** A floating form panel anchored beneath the trigger on a raised stacking layer; on large screens it is 768 pixels wide, and on mobile / narrow viewports it spans the full available width. It has 12 pixels of internal padding, the primary surface background, a host-token medium (md) corner radius, and a large elevation shadow. **Textured inner panel.** Inside the panel, a single rounded inner region with 16 pixels of padding, a thin light border, hidden overflow, and a very subtle brand-tinted top-to-bottom gradient overlaid with a faint decorative grain noise texture (purely cosmetic, behind the content). **Condition rows.** Within the inner panel, a vertical stack of repeatable condition rows; each row is a horizontal group with 12 pixels between its parts and 16 pixels below it, containing: - A responsive field group that fills the available width, holding, in order, two single-select dropdowns (such as an "Include" select with options and a "Referring domain" select with options) and two text inputs (placeholders such as "Exactly matching" and "Enter domain"). On large screens the four fields sit on one line as four equal columns with 12 pixels of gap; on mobile / narrow viewports they stack as full-width block-level fields (one per line) with 8 pixels of gap instead of laying out side by side. - A trailing icon-only delete button in the host danger color (with a faint danger hover) carrying a 20-by-20-pixel trash glyph and a visually hidden "Delete" label. Render two such condition rows. **Add-condition button.** Below the rows, a full-width outlined secondary button that centers a 16-by-16-pixel plus glyph (6 pixels before the label) next to a label such as "Add condition". **Footer.** Outside the inner panel, with 16 pixels of space above it, a horizontal action row with 12 pixels between two auto-width buttons: a secondary outlined button (such as "Clear all") followed by a primary button (such as "Apply"). **Sizing rules.** The panel is 768 pixels wide on large screens and spans the full available width on mobile. The gradient, grain texture, select chevrons, delete glyph, plus glyph, surfaces, borders, focus rings, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system; the gradient and danger accents come from host tokens. **Panel radius and concentric item rule.** The dropdown panel uses the host design system's medium (md) corner radius — not the base radius — together with 12 pixels of internal padding. Every interactive nav/option row inside the panel uses 8 pixels of padding and a smaller, concentric corner radius derived from the panel's medium radius minus the panel padding, so the inner rounding nests cleanly inside the panel's corners (for example, a 16-pixel panel radius pairs with an 8-pixel row radius). **Section heading rule.** Every panel section heading uses a 14-pixel semibold type size in the heading color with 12 pixels of margin beneath it. **Button padding rule.** The trigger uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the add-condition, clear-all, and apply buttons use padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. The icon-only delete button is sized to its glyph. **Input padding rule.** Every select and text input uses 12px horizontal and 8px vertical padding. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill the selects and text inputs with the primary surface and a host default border so they read as bounded fields against the tinted inner panel, and keep the host default focus ring. **Control border rule.** The borders of any checkboxes, radios, text inputs, and selects in this panel are taken from the host design system tokens — their resting, hover, focus, and checked-state border colors all come from the design system rather than any hard-coded value. **Mobile layout rule.** On mobile / narrow viewports the panel spans the full available width; within each condition row the four fields stop laying out side by side and stack as full-width block-level fields (one per line), with the delete button dropping to the end of that stacked group, and the footer keeps its two actions inline in clear-all-then-apply order. On large screens the panel is 768 pixels wide with the four fields on a single row.

items.name: Full Bleed Alert Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Delete item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a medium surface-card dialog constrained to a maximum width of 448 pixels, with host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, and a soft elevation shadow. The dialog itself carries no uniform internal padding; instead each region manages its own padding so a banner can span the full dialog width. **Close affordance.** A small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) absolutely positioned in the top-end corner of the dialog. **Body.** A start-aligned stack: a short dialog title (such as "Delete item?") in a medium heading weight with its own padding, a muted supporting paragraph beneath it with horizontal padding, then a full-bleed alert banner that spans the entire dialog width edge to edge (no side gutters), separated from the content above and below by thin top and bottom borders, filled with a soft semantic-tinted background and holding a short emphasis message in the matching semantic foreground color. **Footer.** A horizontal action row where both buttons stretch to equal full width and sit side by side with consistent spacing: a primary confirm button (such as "Continue") and a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "No, cancel"), with their own padding above and to the sides. **Sizing rules.** The dialog stays bounded to its 448-pixel maximum and never spans edge to edge. The alert banner is the only full-bleed element and reaches both side edges of the dialog; its semantic tint and foreground, plus all surfaces, borders, focus rings, and radii, stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** The trigger button uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the footer confirm and dismiss buttons use padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the dialog grows toward the full available width, the heading and paragraph keep their padding, the alert banner stays full-bleed to the dialog edges, and the two footer buttons each remain full width and stack vertically in confirm-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Radio Select Card Drawer
items.promptText: Create a self-contained off-canvas drawer triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its drawer panel so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Show drawer") that opens the drawer. **Drawer shell.** A fixed panel pinned to the start (inline-start) edge of the viewport, spanning the full viewport height, on a high stacking layer. It slides in horizontally from off-canvas and rests against the start edge, constrained to a maximum width of 672 pixels, with 16 pixels of internal padding, the primary surface background, a thin border on its end (inline-end) edge, and its own vertical scroll when content overflows. On the start (left) edge, a short drawer title (such as "New item") in a medium weight and the body text color. A 36-by-36-pixel icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) sits at the end (right) of that same row in the normal flow — never absolutely positioned — so it stays vertically centered with the title rather than dropping below it. **Body.** A grid that is one column on mobile, two columns from the small breakpoint up, and three columns from the medium breakpoint up, with 16 pixels of gap. Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk and put each label 10 pixels above its control in a small text size and medium weight using the heading color. - **Left column** stacks its fields with 16 pixels of space: an icon-prefixed full-name text input, an icon-prefixed email input, an icon-prefixed username input, then a phone-number composite, a country single-select, an account-type single-select, an icon-prefixed password input, and an icon-prefixed confirm-password input. Every icon-prefixed input reserves 36 pixels of start padding for its leading glyph and 12 pixels of end padding. The phone-number composite is a single attached group: a country-code trigger button on the start edge (a small leading flag, a dial code such as "+1", and a trailing chevron) joined to a patterned phone input that fills the remaining width; the trigger opens a floating menu (about 216 pixels wide) listing countries, each row a small flag beside a country name and dial code. - **Right column** spans two of the three columns from the medium breakpoint up and stacks its fields with 16 pixels of space: an upload-profile-picture row (a 64-by-64-pixel rounded avatar thumbnail beside a native file input with a small extra-small helper line beneath it); a user-role subsection rendered as a responsive row (stacked on mobile, side by side from the small breakpoint up) of two selectable option cards, each a full-width bordered tile on the filled field surface with 16 pixels of inner padding holding a 28-by-28-pixel glyph above a title (small text, medium weight) and a muted small-size description, with a 16-by-16-pixel radio pinned 16 pixels from the top and end and the two cards behaving as one single-choice group; a biography rich text editor (a bordered surface on the filled field surface whose top toolbar holds grouped icon-only formatting buttons separated by thin dividers plus a trailing full-screen toggle with a tooltip, above a multi-line textarea of about eight rows); and a status subsection of four inline radio options (16-by-16-pixel radios with labels 8 pixels to their end in a small text size and medium weight). **Label wrapping rule.** Each inline radio option label and each country menu row stays on a single line and never wraps (truncating with an ellipsis on overflow); option-card titles and multi-line descriptions are exempt. **Footer.** Pushed to the bottom of the panel above a thin top divider with 20 pixels of space above and below the footer content, a horizontal action row with 16 pixels between its buttons: a primary submit button carrying a small leading plus icon (such as "Add item") followed by a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close"). **Sizing rules.** The panel stays bounded to its 672-pixel maximum.
