items.name: Application Navbar With Region Selector
items.promptText:
Create an application navbar as a single fixed horizontal bar pinned to the top of the viewport, spanning the full viewport width edge to edge with no surrounding page padding and no enclosing max-width container. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks below the navbar; only output the navbar code.

**Primary navbar** is the only bar in this layout and contains, from left to right on the same baseline: a hamburger menu icon on the left; a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline directly after the hamburger; then grouped on the right end of the bar, a small icon-only grid-view toggle, a small icon-only notification bell, a compact search trigger composed of a small leading search icon paired with a short "Search" label on the same baseline, a region selector composed of a small flag or location glyph paired with a location label and a trailing dropdown chevron, and finally a user identity block composed of a small circular avatar paired with the user's name and a small role badge in parentheses on the same baseline. A thin vertical divider may sit between adjacent grouped elements on the right end to visually separate them.

**Sizing rules.** The navbar spans the full viewport width edge to edge with no surrounding page padding and no enclosing max-width container around the bar itself. Every visible action button inside the navbar (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports the search trigger, region selector, and role badge may collapse off-screen or behind a menu toggle; the user identity block may reduce to avatar-only; utility icons may group behind an overflow menu. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Feature Cards With Action Links
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce promotional feature section: a centered heading over a grid of icon feature cards, each ending in an action link. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on a soft secondary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Heading block.** A center-aligned block with 16 pixels beneath it (32 from the medium breakpoint up): a ~24px bold heading-color title with tight tracking and 12 pixels beneath it (~36px from the medium breakpoint up, e.g. "Why [Brand] Shop?") over a ~16px muted subtitle (~20px from the medium breakpoint up). **Feature grid.** A one-column grid that becomes two columns from the small breakpoint up and three from the large breakpoint up with a 16-pixel gap (32 from the xl breakpoint up; 32 pixels above it from the small breakpoint up). Each cell is a **feature card** — a thin-bordered, host-rounded card on the host primary surface with a small shadow, 16 pixels of padding (24 from the small breakpoint up), and center-aligned content: - A centered 48-by-48-pixel muted feature glyph with 16 pixels beneath it. - A ~20px semibold heading-color title with 12 pixels beneath it. - A muted supporting paragraph with 16 pixels beneath it. - An **action link** — a centered row in the brand foreground color, ~18px medium weight, underlining on hover, trailing an 18-by-18-pixel arrow glyph 4 pixels after its label (e.g. "How to make the payments", "Get premium delivery", "Activate your account"). Use about three feature cards. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the heading and subtitle, the feature cards (glyphs, titles, paragraphs, and action links) — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. Every link must be the host design system's own link component, with its color, states, focus ring, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The action links are ~18px inline text links trailing an 18-by-18-pixel arrow glyph; there are no box buttons in this section. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the feature glyphs at 48-by-48 pixels, the action links at ~18px with 18-by-18-pixel arrows, the heading at ~24–36px, the subtitle at ~16–20px, and the card titles at ~20px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The feature grid steps from one to two to three columns across the small and large breakpoints; each card stays center-aligned with its glyph, title, paragraph, and action link stacked.

items.name: Split Forgot Password Card With Illustration
items.promptText:
Create a forgot-password page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**Left column** contains a single elevated card with rounded corners and a light surface treatment, vertically centered within the column height. Inside the card, stack from top to bottom: a small brand icon or logo mark on its own line paired with a brand name label immediately to the right of the icon on the same baseline; a bold heading on its own line directly below the brand row (e.g. "Forgot your password?"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, reassuring the user and explaining the reset flow; a labeled email input row placed below the paragraph (the label sits above the input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting an email address); a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text confirms acceptance of linked terms and conditions (with the terms phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width primary action button at the bottom of the card with a short label (e.g. "Reset password").

**Right column** holds one large illustrative scene that fills most of the column area, vertically centered within the column. The illustration depicts a figure sitting at a workstation with a monitor displaying a user profile or authentication interface, plants or office elements in the background, conveying a calm account-recovery theme without relying on photographic imagery.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the form card first and the illustration directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce promotional section: a single rounded promo card pairing a product image with a headline, supporting paragraph, and call-to-action. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome (global navbar, footer, cart drawer, breadcrumb) beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 16 pixels of horizontal padding and 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up). **Promo card.** A centered max-width container of about 1280 pixels rendered as a host-rounded card on a soft secondary surface with 16 pixels of padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up, 64 from the large breakpoint up), laid out as a twelve-column grid from the large breakpoint up with a 32-pixel gap (64 from the xl breakpoint up) — stacked otherwise: - An **image column** spanning 5 of the 12 columns: a single **real product photograph** (a photographic JPG/PNG image, not a line-art SVG illustration) wrapped in a link, with 16 pixels beneath it; ~224-by-224 pixels on mobile, ~384-by-384 pixels from the small breakpoint up, and filling its column from the medium breakpoint up. - A **text column** spanning the remaining 7 of the 12 columns, vertically centered and start-aligned with an auto end margin: a ~24px bold heading-color headline with tight line-height and tracking and 12 pixels beneath it (scaling to ~36px from the medium breakpoint up, allowed to break across two lines, e.g. "Save $500 today on your purchase of a new [product]."); a muted supporting paragraph with 24 pixels beneath it; and a **primary brand call-to-action button** styled as a link (~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding, ~16px medium label, e.g. "Pre-order now"). **Design system rule.** Every element here — the product image link, the headline, the supporting paragraph, and the call-to-action button — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. The promo card uses the host's soft secondary surface token; every button or link must be the host design system's own button and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. The product image is a real photographic asset, never a line-art SVG illustration. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The call-to-action uses ~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding with a ~16px medium label. Primaries use the host brand button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the image at ~224 pixels square (~384 from the small breakpoint up, filling the column from the medium breakpoint up), the headline at ~24–36px, and the CTA label at ~16px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The card stacks the image above the text column until the large breakpoint, where it becomes a 5/7 twelve-column split; the headline, paragraph, and CTA stay start-aligned and stacked.

items.name: Centered Dual-Button CTA
items.promptText:
Create a CTA section as one centered vertical stack inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large multi-line primary heading centered horizontally on its own line. Below the heading, place a supporting paragraph set at a restrained max width and centered horizontally so long lines do not stretch edge to edge.

Below the paragraph, center a single horizontal row containing two buttons sitting side by side with a small gap between them (approximately 16 px). The first button is a solid primary brand button with a short label; the second button is a secondary outlined button with a short label. Both buttons use pill-shaped or softly rounded corners and share the same height so they read as one balanced pair. The row itself is centered beneath the paragraph (one flex row, items centered, never wrapping to a second line on any viewport wider than the minimum supported width).

items.name: Tabbed Description Reviews Questions Highlights
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce "product information" section: a tabbed interface with four panels — Description (with spec cards), Reviews (summary plus review list), Questions (Q&A accordion), and Highlights (feature cards) — plus a hidden report modal and a hidden write-a-review modal. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding; centered in a ~1280-pixel max-width container with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Tab strip.** A centered, ~14px medium muted tab list that gains a bottom border rule from the small breakpoint up; tabs wrap in a row with a 16-pixel horizontal gap. Each tab is a button with a 2-pixel bottom border and 12 pixels of padding; the active tab reads as selected and the rest darken on hover. Tabs, in order: "Description", "Reviews", "Questions", "Highlights". Only the active panel shows. **Description panel.** A grid that is one column by default and, from the large breakpoint up, five columns with a 32-pixel gap, with 16 pixels of vertical padding (32 from the small breakpoint up): - A **main column** spanning three of the five columns, a 24-pixel-spaced stack: two 24-pixel-spaced groups of ~16px muted description paragraphs (some led by a ~16px semibold heading-color term), a hidden duplicate "more info" group, and a **show-more** control — a ~16px medium brand-foreground row with a trailing 16-by-16-pixel chevron that underlines on hover. - A **spec aside** spanning two columns — one column by default (a 2-column grid below the large breakpoint), becoming an 8-pixel-spaced vertical stack from the large breakpoint up. Each **spec card** is a host-rounded panel on a soft secondary surface with a thin border and 16 pixels of padding (24 from the medium breakpoint up): a ~20px semibold heading-color title (e.g. "Display", "Processor", "RAM memory", "Storage") over a divider-separated definition list whose rows each split a ~14px medium heading-color term and a ~14px normal muted value across 8 pixels of vertical padding (e.g. Screen Type / light, Diagonal / 24 inches, Resolution / 4480 x 2520, Format / 4k). **Reviews panel.** A stack: - A **summary card** — a wrapped flex row on the host primary surface with a thin border, small shadow, and 16-to-32-pixel padding/gaps — holding: an **average rating** block (a ~30px bold "5/5", a ~16px muted "Average rating" label, and a row of five 20-by-20-pixel amber stars with a ~14px muted "(3,657 reviews)" count); a thin vertical divider (large screens only); a **clients** block (a ~30px bold "100M+", a ~16px muted "Worldwide Clients" label, and a 16-pixel-gap row of conventional partner brand logos kept as their own marks); another divider; and a **rate-product** block (a ~20px semibold heading-color prompt "Do you own or have you used the product?", a ~16px muted subline, a row of five 24-by-24-pixel muted outline stars with a ~14px medium "Give a note" link, and a brand "Write a customer review" button — solid brand surface, inverse text, 20px/8px padding, ~14px medium — that opens the review modal). - A **list controls row** that splits from the small breakpoint up: a ~14px heading-color "Showing 5,768 Customer Reviews" line (the number in a semibold span) and two **selects** (a review-type select defaulting to "All Reviews" and a time select defaulting to "Recently Added"), each a bordered, soft-input-surface, host-rounded select with ~14px text. - A **review list** — a divider-separated list with a top border rule, each review an article with 24 pixels of vertical padding: a header row with a 40-by-40-pixel host-rounded avatar (a **real photo**) beside a ~14px medium name and a ~14px muted "Total Reviews: N" line (the count in a heading-color span); a ~20px semibold heading-color review title; a row of five 16-by-16-pixel amber stars with a ~14px muted date; one or two ~16px muted body paragraphs; and a footer row with a small bordered neutral "Helpful (N)" button (~12px medium, 8px/6px padding) and, 16 pixels after it, a ~14px medium heading-color "Report" link with a leading 20-by-20-pixel flag glyph that opens the report modal. Provide five reviews. - A **pager**: a centered column with a ~14px muted "Showing 1 to 5 of 53 Customer Reviews" line (numbers in semibold heading-color spans) over two adjoining 32-pixel-tall buttons on a dark/inverse surface with inverse ~14px medium labels ("Previous" host-rounded on its start, "Next" host-rounded on its end). **Questions panel.** With 24 pixels above (32 from the small breakpoint up), a flush accordion of question entries: each **header** a full-width split-ends row with a 12-pixel gap, a bottom border rule, 20 pixels of vertical padding, a left-aligned ~20px semibold heading-color question, and a 20-by-20-pixel chevron; each open **body** a 16-pixel-spaced block with a bottom border rule and 20 pixels of vertical padding holding an author + date row (a ~16px semibold heading-color author and a ~14px muted timestamp), one or more ~16px muted answer paragraphs (some led by a ~16px semibold heading-color term), and a "Was it helpful to you?" row — a ~14px medium muted prompt beside two radio options ("Yes: N", "No: N"). Provide several entries (the first open). Below the accordion, with 24 pixels above (32 from the small breakpoint up), a ~18px muted "Didn't find the answer?" line with a brand underlined "Ask a question" link. **Highlights panel.** With 24 pixels above (32 from the small breakpoint up), a grid with a 16-pixel gap: one column by default, two from the small breakpoint up, three from the large. Each **highlight card** is a host-rounded panel on a soft secondary surface with a thin border and 16 pixels of padding: a ~16px muted eyebrow label (e.g. "Processor Model", "Graphics", "System Memory (RAM)", "Display Type", "Total Storage Capacity", "Screen Resolution"), a ~18px bold heading-color value beneath, a 16-pixel-vertical-margin check list with 4-pixel spacing (each item a row of a 20-by-20-pixel success-color check glyph and a ~16px muted label), and a ~16px medium brand-foreground link that underlines on hover. Provide six cards. **Report modal.** A hidden, fixed, centered, scrollable overlay holding a ~512-pixel-max-width host-rounded panel on the host primary surface with a shadow: a bordered header (a ~18px semibold heading-color "File a report" title and an icon-only close button with a small X glyph) and a form with 16-pixel-gapped fields — an issue-type radio group ("Report listing abuse", "Report a violation"), a "Report reason" text input, a "Describe your issue" textarea (~6 rows), an "Add an attachment" file input, and a terms-agreement checkbox with an inline brand link — over a bordered footer with a brand "Send report" submit button and a bordered neutral "Cancel" button. **Review modal.** A hidden, fixed, centered, scrollable overlay holding a ~672-pixel-max-width host-rounded panel on the host primary surface with a shadow: a bordered header (a ~18px semibold heading-color "Add a review for:" title over a brand product-name link, plus a top-end icon-only close button) and a form with 16-pixel-gapped fields — a star-rating row (five 24-by-24-pixel stars, amber for the chosen rating and muted after, with a ~18px bold "3.0 out of 5" label), a "Review title" text input, a "Review description" textarea (~6 rows) with a ~12px muted "Send a report" hint, a "Add real photos of the product" **dropzone** (a 208-pixel- tall dashed-border soft-secondary upload area with an upload glyph, a "Click to upload or drag and drop" prompt, and a format/size hint), and a terms-agreement checkbox with an inline brand link — over a bordered footer with a brand "Add review" submit button and a bordered neutral "Cancel" button. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The tab strip, description paragraphs and show-more link, spec cards and definition lists, reviews summary (rating, partner logos, rate-product block), list controls and selects, review articles (avatars, ratings, helpful/report controls), dark pager, questions accordion and helpfulness radios, highlight cards and check glyphs, and both modals (inputs, textareas, file/dropzone uploads, checkboxes, buttons) must all use the host design system's components/tokens (surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, brand/heading/muted text, amber rating stamp, success-color stamp, soft secondary and soft input surfaces, dark/inverse surface, hover/focus states). Treat review avatars and any product photos as real photographic assets, and keep partner brand logos as their own conventional marks. Pixel values define only spacing, sizing, and layout rhythm.

items.name: Split 404 Page With Quick Links
items.promptText:
Create a 404 page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack, vertically centered within the column height, containing in order: a large multi-line heading stating the error status and a brief descriptive phrase on its own line; a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width suggesting the user refresh or return to the homepage; a horizontal row of three compact card-style link blocks placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, sitting side by side on the same baseline with consistent gutters between them. Each link block is a centered vertical stack composed of a small icon centered at the top (holding a single glyph) and a short label centered directly below the icon; the entire block behaves as a single clickable surface.

**Right column** holds one large illustrative scene that fills most of the column area, vertically centered within the column. The illustration depicts a figure or character in a questioning or searching pose alongside oversized question-mark shapes, conveying a lighthearted "lost" theme without relying on photographic imagery.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the content column first and the illustration directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Centered Two-Factor Verification Page
items.promptText:
Create a two-factor authentication page as one centered vertical stack on a full-width section background, vertically centered within the viewport height. Stack from top to bottom: a small brand icon or logo mark centered horizontally on its own line; a brand name label centered on its own line directly below the icon; a large bold centered heading on its own line directly below the brand name stating the purpose of the page (e.g. "Two-factor authentication"); a centered paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, instructing the user to open their authenticator app to view the code and verify their identity; a labeled field group placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, composed of a short left-aligned label on its own line (e.g. "Enter verification code") above a horizontal row of six equally sized square single-character numeric input fields on the same baseline (each field is a real input element that accepts exactly one digit, auto-advances focus to the next field on entry, supports backspace to move focus back to the previous field, and the currently focused field displays a visible focus ring or cursor indicator); a short helper line directly below the input row at a subdued weight explaining where the code was sent; one primary action button placed below the helper text on its own line, composed of a small leading checkmark icon paired with a short label (e.g. "Verify").

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack with comfortable side padding; allow the six input fields to scale slightly while preserving center alignment throughout.

items.name: Split Maintenance Page With Contact Support
items.promptText:
Create a maintenance page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack, vertically centered within the column height, containing in order: a large multi-line heading stating the maintenance status on its own line; a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, explaining that the site is undergoing planned maintenance and will return soon, containing an inline bold text link pointing to the blog or status page embedded naturally within the sentence; a contact information group placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, arranged as a horizontal row of two blocks on the same baseline — the first block is a vertical stack composed of a small leading icon paired with a bold label on the same baseline at the top (indicating a physical location or brand entity), followed by a multi-line postal address beneath the label; the second block is a vertical stack composed of a small leading icon paired with a bold label on the same baseline at the top (indicating email contact), followed by a single mailto text link beneath the label; a compact outlined button placed below the contact group on its own line, composed of a small leading chat or message icon paired with a short label (e.g. "Speak with us").

**Right column** holds one large illustrative scene that fills most of the column area, vertically centered within the column. The illustration depicts a figure sitting on or beside server hardware or storage boxes, working at a laptop, conveying a calm maintenance-in-progress theme without relying on photographic imagery.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the content column first and the illustration directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Centered Illustrated Maintenance Page
items.promptText:
Create a maintenance page as one centered vertical stack on a full-width section background, vertically centered within the viewport height. Stack from top to bottom: a large illustrative scene centered horizontally on its own line, depicting a figure working at a laptop with stylized UI elements or browser windows floating in the background (conveying an active-but-paused development mood without relying on photographic imagery); a large bold centered heading on its own line directly below the illustration stating the maintenance status (e.g. "Down for Maintenance"); a centered paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, explaining that the site is temporarily offline for planned maintenance and will return soon, containing an inline bold text link pointing to the blog or status page embedded naturally within the sentence.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack; allow the illustration to scale down proportionally while preserving center alignment and comfortable side padding throughout.

items.name: Centered Maintenance Message Page
items.promptText:
Create a maintenance page as one centered vertical stack on a full-width section background, vertically centered within the viewport height. Stack from top to bottom: a small brand icon or logo mark centered horizontally on its own line; a brand name label centered on its own line directly below the icon; a large bold centered heading on its own line directly below the brand name delivering a positive forward-looking message (e.g. "We've got something special for you"); a single centered paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, explaining that the site is temporarily down for maintenance and will return with improvements.

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack with comfortable side padding; allow the heading to wrap naturally while preserving center alignment throughout.

items.name: Full-Width Split Maintenance Page With Resources
items.promptText:
Create a maintenance page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints that spans the full available width of the viewport with no outer margin.

**Left column** uses a plain page background and contains a left-aligned vertical stack with comfortable inset padding, vertically centered within the column height. Stack from top to bottom: a large multi-line heading delivering a positive forward-looking message on its own line (e.g. "We've got something special for you"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, explaining that the site is temporarily down for maintenance and will return with improvements; a social proof row placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, composed of slightly overlapping circular user avatars on the left and a short line of bold text immediately to the right of the avatars on the same baseline stating a usage metric (e.g. "Used by over 15M people around the world"); a compact outlined button placed below the social proof row on its own line, composed of a small leading chat or message icon paired with a short label (e.g. "Speak with us").

**Right column** uses a distinct filled background that spans the full column area edge-to-edge, with a very subtle geometric wave or line texture layered behind the content. Inside the column, place a vertical stack of three resource cards with consistent spacing between them, vertically centered within the column height. Each card is a left-aligned vertical stack composed of a small rounded-square icon container at the top (holding a single centered glyph); a bold title on its own line directly below the icon; a short two-line description paragraph directly below the title; and a text-style link on its own line below the paragraph whose label includes a trailing arrow icon at the end of the link text.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the left column first and the resource column directly below it; each internal stack preserves its original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Project Application Sidebar
items.promptText:
Create an application sidenav as a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to one edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks beside the sidenav; only output the sidenav code.

**User identity header.** At the very top of the panel, place a user identity block composed of a medium circular avatar on the left, a two-line text group to its right (the user's full name on the first line in a prominent weight and the user's email on the second line in a lighter weight), and a small trailing up-down chevron icon on the far right indicating account switching. The header carries a bottom border with 16 pixels of padding below the content and 16 pixels of margin below the border, separating it from the primary navigation list.

**Primary navigation list.** Below the user identity header, stack a vertical list of navigation items. Each primary item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. One item carries a highlight state indicated by a contrasting background fill or left accent and a distinct label color. No trailing chevrons or dropdowns in this primary section.

**Projects section.** Below the primary navigation, separated by a thin horizontal divider, place a section heading in a bold weight (such as "My projects") on its own line. Below the heading, stack a vertical list of project items. Each project item is a horizontal row composed of a small colored square dot or indicator on the left (each with a distinct color) and a project name label to its right on the same baseline. Below the project list, place a secondary button composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label (such as "+ Add new project") spanning the full panel width.

**Bottom utility group.** Anchored to the very bottom of the panel, stack a vertical list of icon-and-label utility links (such as Settings, Help & Terms, Invite teammates) on separate lines, each composed of a small leading icon and a text label on the same baseline.

**Interaction behavior.** The account switch chevron triggers account selection. The add project button triggers creation flow. Project items navigate to the project's view. The active navigation item shows a distinct visual treatment.

**Sizing and layout rules.** The sidenav panel height is exactly 100 vh, always spanning the full viewport height with no gap above or below. The panel width is fixed. The bottom utility group is pinned to the bottom. The navigation and projects sections scroll if content overflows.

On narrow viewports the sidenav collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via an external toggle. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Music Application Sidebar
items.promptText:
Create an application sidenav as a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to one edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks beside the sidenav; only output the sidenav code.

**Brand header.** At the very top of the panel, place a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline.

**Search field.** Directly below the brand header, place a search input field spanning the full panel width with a leading search icon and placeholder text relevant to the content domain (such as "Search for a song").

**Primary navigation list.** Below the search field, stack a vertical list of navigation items. Each item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Items represent core navigation destinations (such as Home, Discover, Albums, Tracks, Genres). No dropdowns in this section.

**Playlists section.** Below the primary navigation, separated by a thin horizontal divider, place a section header row composed of a bold section title on the left (such as "My playlists") and a small icon-only add button (plus icon) on the far right on the same baseline. Below the header, stack a vertical list of playlist items. Each playlist item is a horizontal row composed of a small square thumbnail image on the left, and a two-line text group to its right: the playlist name on the first line and a short subtitle or metadata line (such as "Playlist · 67 songs") on the second line in a lighter weight. One playlist item carries a highlight state (active color on its name) to indicate the currently playing or selected playlist. Below the playlist list, center a secondary text link with a small leading eye or view icon (such as "See all albums").

**Upgrade CTA card.** Anchored to the bottom of the panel, place a promotional card with a subtle border or distinct background containing: a bold title on its own line; a short multi-line description paragraph below the title; and a full-width primary action button with a short label and a small trailing arrow icon (such as "Upgrade now →") at the bottom of the card.

**Interaction behavior.** The add button in the playlist section header triggers a create-new-playlist action. Playlist items navigate to the corresponding playlist view. The upgrade CTA button navigates to the upgrade flow.

**Sizing and layout rules.** The sidenav panel height is exactly 100 vh, always spanning the full viewport height with no gap above or below. The panel width is fixed. The upgrade CTA card is pinned to the bottom of the panel. The playlists list scrolls if it overflows, while the brand header, search field, and CTA card remain fixed.

On narrow viewports the sidenav collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via an external toggle. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Double-Panel Application Sidebar
items.promptText:
Create a double-panel sidenav composed of a narrow icon-only rail on the leading edge and an expanded text navigation panel adjacent to it, together forming a fixed-width side region anchored to one edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks beside the sidenav; only output the sidenav code.

**Icon rail.** The narrow leading strip contains a brand logo icon at the very top, followed by a vertical stack of small icon-only navigation buttons below it, each centered horizontally in the rail with consistent vertical spacing between them. Icons represent top-level navigation categories. The rail stretches the full viewport height.

**Expanded panel.** Adjacent to the icon rail, the wider panel stretches the full viewport height and contains the following from top to bottom:

*Panel header.* A header row composed of a short title label (such as the application name or "dashboard") on the left and a small icon-only add or new-item button (plus icon) on the far right, sitting on the same baseline.

*Search field.* Below the panel header, a search input field spanning the full panel width with a leading search icon and placeholder text.

*Navigation list.* Below the search field, a vertical list of navigation items. Each item is a horizontal row composed of a text label on the left and optionally a trailing chevron icon on the right indicating a collapsible dropdown submenu. When expanded, indented child links appear below the parent. One item includes a small circular numeric badge whose text is vertically and horizontally centered within the circle using line-height: 1. One section carries a highlight state with an expanded dropdown.

*User identity block.* Anchored to the very bottom of the panel, place a user identity block composed of a small circular avatar on the left, a two-line text group to its right (user name and email), and a small trailing up-down chevron icon on the far right.

**Interaction behavior.** Clicking an icon in the rail highlights it and may update the expanded panel's content to match that category. Dropdown items in the expanded panel toggle their child links and rotate their chevrons on click. The user identity chevron triggers account switching.

**Sizing and layout rules.** The sidenav panel height is exactly 100 vh, always spanning the full viewport height with no gap above or below. The icon rail has a narrow fixed width (approximately 48–64 pixels). The expanded panel has a wider fixed width. Together they form the sidenav region. The user identity block is pinned to the bottom of the expanded panel.

On narrow viewports both the icon rail and expanded panel collapse off-screen and become accessible via an external toggle. The sidenav may slide in as an overlay. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Collections Application Sidebar
items.promptText:
Create an application sidenav as a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to one edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks beside the sidenav; only output the sidenav code.

**User identity header.** At the very top of the panel, place a user identity dropdown trigger composed of a medium circular avatar on the left, a two-line text group to its right showing the currently active user (full name on the first line in a prominent weight and email on the second line in a lighter weight), and a small trailing up-down chevron icon on the far right. The entire row acts as a single clickable control with 8 pixels of internal padding so the hover state does not touch the panel edges, and opens a dropdown menu listing additional user accounts to switch between. Each dropdown item is composed of a small circular avatar paired with a two-line text group (name and email) on the same baseline as the header layout. The currently active account is visually distinguished within the menu. Selecting an item updates the active user shown in the header and closes the menu.

**Action row.** Below the user identity header, place a horizontal row containing a secondary outlined button with a small leading plus icon and a short label (such as "Add new") occupying most of the row width, and a small icon-only search button on the far right of the same baseline. The row carries a single bottom border with 16 pixels of padding below the content and 16 pixels of margin below the border, separating it from the primary navigation list. Do not add any additional top border on the navigation list — one divider line only.

**Primary navigation list.** Below the action row, stack a vertical list of navigation items with no top or bottom border of its own — only comfortable vertical spacing separating it from the action row above and the collections band below. Each primary item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline (such as Activity, Projects, Tasks, Contacts). One item includes a trailing chevron icon indicating a collapsible dropdown submenu.

**Collections section.** Below the primary navigation list, place the collections area inside a full-width band that is the only section in this layout carrying both a top border and a bottom border, separated from the navigation above by 16 pixels of margin on top and from content below by 16 pixels of margin on bottom, with 16 pixels of padding on top and bottom inside the bordered area. At the top of the band, place a section header row composed of a bold section title (such as "Collections") on the left and a small icon-only search button on the far right on the same baseline. Below the header, stack a vertical list of collection items. Each collection item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a collection name label to its right on the same baseline (such as Sales, Design, Fundraising, Internal, Customer Success, Network, Legal). Below the collection list, place a secondary outlined button composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label (such as "Add collection") spanning the full panel width.

**Interaction behavior.** The user identity dropdown opens a menu of available accounts; selecting an account switches the active user shown in the header. The add-new button triggers the primary creation action. The search button in the action row opens a search interface. The collections search button filters the collection list. The add-collection button triggers collection creation flow.

**Sizing and layout rules.** The sidenav panel height is exactly 100 vh, always spanning the full viewport height with no gap above or below. The panel width is fixed. Content scrolls vertically if it overflows.

On narrow viewports the sidenav collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via an external toggle. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Application Sidebar With Alert Card
items.promptText:
Create an application sidenav as a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to one edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks beside the sidenav; only output the sidenav code.

**Brand header.** At the very top of the panel, place a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline, separated from navigation below by a thin horizontal divider.

**Primary navigation list.** Below the brand header, stack a vertical list of navigation items. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Some items include a trailing chevron icon indicating a collapsible dropdown submenu; when expanded, indented child links appear directly below the parent item. One section carries a highlight state with an expanded dropdown visible. One navigation item includes a small circular numeric badge whose text is vertically and horizontally centered within the circle using line-height: 1. Below the primary navigation, separated by a thin divider, place a secondary group of utility links (such as Docs, Components, Help), each following the icon-plus-label row pattern.

**Alert info card.** Below the secondary utility links, place a floating card with a subtle border or elevated surface containing: a header row composed of a small leading info icon paired with a bold title on the same baseline and a small dismiss (close/X) button anchored to the top right; a short multi-line description paragraph below the header; and a full-width primary action button with a small leading download or action icon and a short label at the bottom of the card.

**Bottom utility group.** Anchored to the very bottom of the panel below the alert card, place a row of icon-and-label links on separate lines (such as Settings, Help & Terms, Invite teammates), each composed of a small leading icon and a text label on the same baseline.

**Interaction behavior.** The alert card dismiss button removes the card from view. Dropdown navigation items toggle their child links and rotate their chevrons on click.

**Sizing and layout rules.** The sidenav panel height is exactly 100 vh, always spanning the full viewport height with no gap above or below. The panel width is fixed. The bottom utility group is pinned to the bottom of the panel. The alert card is positioned between the navigation and the bottom utility group. If content overflows, the navigation list scrolls while the bottom utility group remains anchored.

On narrow viewports the sidenav collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via an external toggle. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Mailbox Application Sidebar
items.promptText:
Create an application sidenav as a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to one edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks beside the sidenav; only output the sidenav code.

**Primary action button.** At the very top of the panel, place a full-width primary action button composed of a small leading compose or edit icon and a short label (such as "Compose"). The button spans the full panel width with comfortable horizontal padding.

**Mailbox navigation list.** Below the primary action button, stack a vertical list of mailbox navigation items. Each item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. One item includes a small circular numeric badge on the far right of the row indicating an unread count — the badge text is vertically and horizontally centered within the circle using line-height: 1 so the number never sits off-center. One item includes a trailing chevron icon indicating a collapsible dropdown submenu; when expanded, indented child links appear directly below the parent (such as category sub-folders). The expanded section's chevron rotates to indicate the open state.

**Labels section.** Below the mailbox navigation, separated by a thin horizontal divider, place a section heading in a bold or heavier weight (such as "Labels") on its own line. Below the heading, stack a vertical list of label items. Each label item is a horizontal row composed of a small colored tag or bookmark icon on the left (each with a distinct color) and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Below the label list, place a secondary button or text link composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label (such as "+ Create new label").

**Bottom utility group.** Anchored to the very bottom of the panel, stack a vertical list of icon-and-label utility links (such as Settings, Invite teammates) on separate lines, each composed of a small leading icon and a text label on the same baseline.

**Interaction behavior.** The compose button triggers the primary creation action (opening a compose modal or navigating to compose view). The collapsible category section toggles open/closed on click with chevron rotation. Label items navigate to the corresponding filtered view.

**Sizing and layout rules.** The sidenav panel height is exactly 100 vh, always spanning the full viewport height with no gap above or below. The panel width is fixed. The bottom utility group is pinned to the bottom. The labels section and mailbox list scroll if content overflows.

On narrow viewports the sidenav collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via an external toggle. Preserve reading order throughout.

Create an application sidenav as a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to one edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks beside the sidenav; only output the sidenav code.

**Brand header.** At the very top of the panel, place a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline.

**Primary navigation list.** Below the brand header, stack a vertical list of navigation items. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Some items include a trailing chevron icon indicating a collapsible dropdown submenu; when expanded, indented child links appear directly below the parent item. One section carries a highlight state with an expanded dropdown visible. One navigation item includes a small circular numeric badge whose text is vertically and horizontally centered within the circle using line-height: 1.

**Active contacts section.** Below the primary navigation, separated by a thin horizontal divider, place a section heading (such as "Active contacts") on its own line. Below the heading, stack a vertical list of user contact items. Each contact item is a horizontal row composed of a small circular avatar with a colored online-status ring or indicator on the left, and the contact's name label to its right on the same baseline.

**Bottom utility row.** Anchored to the very bottom of the panel, place a horizontal row of icon-and-label utility links sitting side by side on the same baseline (such as Settings and FAQ & support), separated by consistent horizontal spacing.

**Sizing and layout rules.** The sidenav panel height is exactly 100 vh, always spanning the full viewport height with no gap above or below. The panel width is fixed. The bottom utility row is pinned to the bottom of the panel. If the contacts list overflows, the section scrolls independently.

On narrow viewports the sidenav collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via an external toggle. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Application Sidebar With Storage Indicator
items.promptText:
Create an application sidenav as a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to one edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks beside the sidenav; only output the sidenav code.

**Brand header.** At the very top of the panel, place a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline.

**Search field.** Directly below the brand header, place a search input field spanning the full panel width with a leading search icon and placeholder text.

**Primary navigation list.** Below the search field, stack a vertical list of navigation items. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Some items include a trailing chevron icon indicating a collapsible dropdown submenu; when expanded, indented child links appear directly below the parent item as plain text labels without leading icons. One section carries a highlight state (active color and expanded submenu visible). One navigation item includes a small circular numeric badge to the right of its label indicating an unread count; the badge text is vertically and horizontally centered within the circle using line-height: 1 so the number never sits off-center.

**Storage indicator.** Anchored to the bottom of the panel, place a storage usage block composed of a short descriptive label (such as "Space left") on its own line, a usage fraction or count in a prominent weight (such as "70 of 150 GB") on the next line, a horizontal progress bar beneath the count that visually represents usage as a filled segment relative to total capacity, and a full-width secondary button with a small leading icon and a short upgrade label (such as "Upgrade to pro") below the progress bar.

**Interaction behavior.** Clicking a parent item with a trailing chevron toggles the dropdown open or closed and rotates the chevron. The search field filters visible navigation items or triggers a search action.

**Sizing and layout rules.** The sidenav panel height is exactly 100 vh, always spanning the full viewport height with no gap above or below. The panel width is fixed. The storage indicator block is pinned to the bottom of the panel and does not scroll with the navigation list. If the navigation list overflows, it scrolls independently while the brand header and storage block remain fixed.

On narrow viewports the sidenav collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via an external toggle. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Account Application Sidebar
items.promptText:
Create an application sidenav as a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to one edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks beside the sidenav; only output the sidenav code.

**User identity header.** At the very top of the panel, place a user identity block composed of a medium circular avatar on the left, a two-line text group to its right (the user's full name on the first line in a prominent weight and the user's email on the second line in a lighter weight), and a small trailing up-down chevron or sort icon on the far right indicating the account can be switched.

**Quick-action buttons row.** Below the user identity header, place a horizontal row of equally-spaced quick-action buttons sitting side by side on the same baseline, wrapped in a full-width band separated from the header above and the navigation below by 16 pixels of margin on top and bottom. The band carries a top border and a bottom border, with 16 pixels of padding on top and bottom inside the bordered area. Each quick-action button is a small vertical stack containing a small icon centered on the top line and a short text label centered directly beneath the icon, all enclosed in a rounded bordered container or pill. The row contains three buttons (such as Profile, Gifts, Support).

**Primary navigation list.** Below the quick-action row, stack a vertical list of navigation items. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Some items include a trailing chevron icon indicating a collapsible dropdown submenu; when expanded, indented child links appear directly below the parent item as plain text labels. One section carries a highlight state (active color and expanded dropdown visible with child links showing).

**Bottom utility group.** Anchored to the very bottom of the panel, separated from the primary navigation by generous vertical whitespace, stack a vertical list of utility links on separate lines. Each is composed of a small leading icon and a text label on the same baseline. The last item (such as "Log out") uses a distinct destructive or warning color to differentiate it from the others.

**Interaction behavior.** The account switch chevron triggers a dropdown or modal with available accounts. Quick-action buttons navigate to their respective views. Dropdown navigation items toggle their child links and rotate their chevrons on click.

**Sizing and layout rules.** The sidenav panel height is exactly 100 vh, always spanning the full viewport height with no gap above or below. The panel width is fixed. The bottom utility group is pinned to the bottom. The navigation list scrolls if it overflows.

On narrow viewports the sidenav collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via an external toggle. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Filtered Metric Bar Chart Widget
items.promptText:
Create an application dashboard widget as a self-contained surface card intended to sit inside a dashboard grid cell. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent widgets; only output this widget component code.

**Widget shell.** Wrap the entire widget in a surface card container with a fixed canvas height of 540 pixels, 24 pixels of internal padding on large screens and 16 pixels on mobile and small screens, 12 pixels of corner radius using the medium (md) radius token, background set to the host design system's primary surface color, an optional 1 pixel default border, and optional subtle elevation shadow.

**Header row.** At the top, place a horizontal row with space between regions. On the left, stack a large bold primary metric value (such as "385,756") using tabular numerals above a short metric label (such as "Users by country") in a muted secondary weight. On the right end, group two compact filter dropdown triggers side by side on the same baseline: one showing a small flag glyph, a region label (such as "United States"), and a trailing chevron; the other showing a small device icon, a device label (such as "Desktop"), and a trailing chevron. Separate the header from the body with a thin horizontal divider below it.

**Chart body.** Below the header, fill the remaining canvas height with a responsive single-series vertical bar chart spanning seven time buckets labeled Mon through Sun on the x-axis. Render each bar in a solid brand color with flat tops. Center a numeric data label directly above each bar (such as "2139", "2466", "2856") using tabular numerals and a small semibold weight. Omit grid lines to keep the chart minimal.

**Footer row.** Below the chart, separated by a thin horizontal divider above it, place a horizontal footer row with space between regions. On the left, place a period dropdown trigger styled as a bordered pill with a calendar icon, a range label (such as "Last 7 days"), and a trailing chevron. On the right, place a secondary outlined button labeled "View report".

**Chart implementation.** Wire the chart to realistic typed sample data — not a static SVG mock, CSS-only placeholder, or decorative illustration. Use the chart library already present in the target project; if none exists, add a well-supported option with the target app's package manager and install dependencies only in that app workspace (do not assume npm, yarn, pnpm, bun, or any specific package name). Keep the visualization responsive within the widget shell. Enable hover tooltips with human-readable labels and formatted values (currency, counts, or percentages as appropriate). Map fills and strokes to host design system tokens (such as brand, success, and danger). Use smooth curves for line and area series where supported; round bar corners where appropriate.

**Sizing rules.** The widget spans the full width of its grid cell with a fixed canvas height of exactly 540 pixels. Use tabular numerals for all metrics and data labels. Colors, borders, chart treatments, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

**Padding rule.** Use 24 pixels of internal card padding on large screens and 16 pixels on mobile and small screens.

**Divider rule.** Use horizontal divider lines only below the widget header and above the widget footer. Do not place horizontal dividers between other widget sections; separate them with spacing only.

**Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button and dropdown trigger uses padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px.

**Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports preserve the 540-pixel widget height, use 16-pixel card padding on mobile and small screens, stack the header vertically: metric and label first, then the two filter dropdowns wrapping to full width. The chart scales to full card width. The footer stacks period dropdown above the view-report button. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Application Sidebar Navigation
items.promptText:
Create an application sidenav as a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to one edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks beside the sidenav; only output the sidenav code.

**Brand header.** At the very top of the panel, place a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline, separated from the navigation below by a thin horizontal divider.

**Primary navigation list.** Below the brand header, stack a vertical list of navigation items from top to bottom. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Some items include a trailing chevron icon on the far right of the row indicating a collapsible dropdown submenu; the chevron rotates to point upward when the submenu is expanded. When expanded, indented child links appear directly below the parent item as plain text labels without leading icons, each on its own line with consistent vertical spacing. One navigation section carries a highlight state (active color on the label and icon, with the dropdown expanded and child links visible). One navigation item includes a small circular numeric badge to the right of its label indicating an unread count; the badge text is vertically and horizontally centered within the circle using line-height: 1 so the number never sits off-center.

**Secondary utility group.** Below the primary navigation, separated by a thin horizontal divider or additional vertical whitespace, place a secondary group of navigation links at the bottom portion of the panel. Each follows the same icon-plus-label horizontal row pattern but belongs to a distinct utility category (such as documentation, component library, or help resources).

**Interaction behavior.** Clicking a parent item that has a trailing chevron toggles the visibility of its child links and rotates the chevron between its collapsed (pointing down) and expanded (pointing up) states. Only one dropdown may be expanded at a time, or multiple may be open simultaneously — follow the host design system's convention. The active state visually distinguishes the currently selected item from all others using color, font weight, or a left-edge accent indicator.

**Sizing and layout rules.** The sidenav panel height is exactly 100 vh, always spanning the full viewport height with no gap above or below. The panel width is fixed and does not stretch with the viewport. Navigation items have comfortable vertical padding between them. Child links are indented by a consistent left offset relative to parent items. The entire panel scrolls vertically if content exceeds the viewport height, with the brand header optionally remaining sticky at the top.

On narrow viewports the sidenav collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via an external hamburger or toggle control. The panel slides in as an overlay or pushes the content area. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Dual Sidebar Application Shell
items.promptText:
Create an application shell composed of a fixed left sidebar spanning the full viewport height, a fixed right sidebar spanning the full viewport height, and the main content area filling the horizontal space between the two sidebars. There is no top navbar in this layout; the brand mark lives inside the left sidebar.

**Left sidebar** is a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to the left edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. At the very top of the sidebar, place a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline. Below the brand mark, stack a vertical navigation list. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Some items include a trailing chevron icon indicating an expandable submenu; when expanded, indented child links appear directly below the parent item. One section carries a highlight state (active color and expanded submenu). One navigation item includes a small colored numeric badge to the right of the label. Below the main navigation group, separate a secondary group of utility links at the bottom of the sidebar (such as Docs, Components, Help), each following the same icon-plus-label row pattern.

**Right sidebar** is a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to the right edge of the viewport, stretching the full viewport height. At the top of the sidebar, center a user profile block as a vertical stack: a large circular user avatar centered horizontally on its own line; the user's full name centered on its own line directly below the avatar; the user's email centered on its own line directly below the name; a full-width outlined secondary button with a leading logout icon and a short label directly below the email. Below the profile block, center a small horizontal row of icon-only utility buttons (such as a grid toggle, a settings gear, and a help circle) on the same baseline. Below the utility row, stack a vertical navigation list specific to the user's profile context. Each item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right. One section carries a highlight state and is expanded to show indented child links (such as task-status sub-items like To do, In progress, Completed).

**Main content area** fills the remaining horizontal space between the two sidebars. Content placeholder regions stack vertically as full-width blocks with consistent vertical spacing between them.

**Sizing rules.** The shell occupies the full viewport: it spans the viewport width edge to edge and stretches from the very top to the very bottom of the viewport with no surrounding page padding, no outer rounded frame, and no enclosing max-width container around the shell itself. Every dotted (dashed-outline) placeholder region inside the main content area is a short horizontal block approximately 240 pixels tall and never grows to absorb remaining vertical space; empty space below the last placeholder remains visible as the content-area background. Every visible action button inside the shell (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, full-width submit, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links or tab triggers, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports both sidebars collapse off-screen. The left sidebar becomes accessible via a hamburger icon. The right sidebar becomes accessible via the user avatar or a dedicated toggle. The brand mark moves into a mobile header bar. The main content area expands to the full viewport width and regions stack vertically.

items.name: Top Navbar Application Shell With Sidebar and Right Rail
items.promptText:
Create an application shell composed of a fixed top navbar spanning the full viewport width, a fixed left sidebar below the navbar, the main content area in the center, and a narrow icon-only rail on the far right edge.

**Top navbar** is pinned to the top of the viewport as a full-width horizontal bar spanning above all columns. From left to right on the same baseline: a hamburger menu icon; a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right; a search input field with a leading search icon and placeholder text; then grouped on the right end of the bar, a compact primary action button composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label, a small icon-only theme toggle button, a small icon-only notification bell button, a small circular user avatar, and a text logout link.

**Left sidebar** is a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to the left edge of the viewport below the navbar, stretching from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport. Inside the sidebar, stack a vertical navigation list from top to bottom. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Some items include a trailing chevron icon indicating an expandable submenu; when expanded, indented child links appear directly below the parent item. One section carries a highlight state (active color and expanded submenu). One navigation item includes a small colored numeric badge to the right of the label. Below the main navigation group, separate a secondary group of utility links at the bottom of the sidebar (such as Docs, Components, Help), each following the same icon-plus-label row pattern. Above the secondary utility links, a floating toast notification card is anchored to the lower-left area of the sidebar, containing a small leading info icon paired with a bold title on the same baseline, a close button on the right, a short multi-line description paragraph below the title, and a full-width primary action button at the bottom of the card. Below the toast (or below the main navigation when dismissed), anchor a bottom utility group of icon-and-label links (such as Settings, Help & Terms, Invite teammates).

**Right icon rail** is a narrow fixed-width vertical strip anchored to the far right edge of the viewport below the navbar, stretching from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport. It contains a vertical stack of small icon-only buttons centered horizontally in the strip with consistent vertical spacing between them.

**Main content area** fills the remaining horizontal space between the left sidebar and the right icon rail, and vertically from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport. Content placeholder regions are arranged as a dashboard grid: a top row of three equal-width regions, a middle row of three equal-width regions arranged as two rows of three, and a full-width region at the bottom.

**Sizing rules.** The shell occupies the full viewport: it spans the viewport width edge to edge and stretches from the very top to the very bottom of the viewport with no surrounding page padding, no outer rounded frame, and no enclosing max-width container around the shell itself. Every dotted (dashed-outline) placeholder region inside the main content area is a short horizontal block approximately 240 pixels tall and never grows to absorb remaining vertical space; empty space below the last placeholder remains visible as the content-area background. Every visible action button inside the shell (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, full-width submit, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links or tab triggers, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports the sidebar and right icon rail collapse off-screen. The sidebar becomes accessible via the hamburger icon. The toast notification repositions to the bottom of the viewport as a fixed banner. The main content area expands to the full viewport width. Grid columns stack vertically in reading order.

items.name: Three-Bar Application Shell With Two-Column Content
items.promptText:
Create an application shell composed of three fixed horizontal bars stacked at the top of the viewport, with the remaining vertical space below given entirely to the main content area. There is no sidebar in this layout.

**Announcement bar** is pinned to the very top of the viewport as a slim full-width horizontal strip. On the left side, place a horizontal row of short key-value metric pairs sitting side by side on the same baseline with consistent spacing (each pair is composed of a short label followed by a prominently styled value). On the right side of the same strip, place a locale and currency selector row: a small flag icon paired with a language label and a trailing dropdown chevron, followed by a currency code with a trailing dropdown chevron.

**Primary navbar** sits directly below the announcement bar as a full-width horizontal bar. From left to right on the same baseline: a hamburger menu icon; a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right; a search input field with a leading search icon and placeholder text; then grouped on the right end of the bar, a compact primary action button composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label, a small icon-only theme toggle button, a small icon-only notification bell button, a small circular user avatar, and a text logout link.

**Breadcrumb and actions bar** sits directly below the primary navbar as a full-width horizontal bar with a thin border or subtle background shift to visually separate it. On the left side, place a breadcrumb row composed of icon-and-label segments separated by chevron or arrow dividers, where each segment may include a trailing dropdown chevron. On the right side of the same bar, place a row of action controls: a secondary button composed of a small leading icon and a short label, followed by a primary action button composed of a short label and a trailing plus icon.

**Main content area** fills the remaining viewport height below the breadcrumb bar. Content placeholder regions are arranged as two equal-width columns sitting side by side inside a centered max-width container with comfortable padding.

**Sizing rules.** The shell occupies the full viewport: it spans the viewport width edge to edge and stretches from the very top to the very bottom of the viewport with no surrounding page padding, no outer rounded frame, and no enclosing max-width container around the shell itself. Each of the two dotted (dashed-outline) placeholder columns inside the main content area is a tall vertical block approximately 800 pixels tall — taller than every other variant in this set — and never grows to absorb remaining vertical space; the two columns sit side by side at the top of the content area and any empty space below them remains visible as the content-area background, scrolling vertically if the placeholder height exceeds the available viewport room. Every visible action button inside the shell (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, full-width submit, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links or tab triggers, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports the announcement bar may collapse into a horizontally scrollable strip or hide behind a toggle. The primary navbar compresses to essential elements. The breadcrumb bar may truncate to the last segment with a back arrow. The two-column layout stacks vertically in reading order.

items.name: Full-Viewport Application Shell With Dual Rails
items.promptText:
Create an application shell composed of a fixed top navbar spanning the full viewport width, a narrow icon-only rail on the far left edge, an expanded text sidebar panel adjacent to the icon rail, the main content area in the center, and a narrow icon-only rail on the far right edge.

**Top navbar** is pinned to the top of the viewport as a full-width horizontal bar spanning above all columns. From left to right on the same baseline: a hamburger menu icon; a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right; a search input field with a leading search icon and placeholder text; then grouped on the right end of the bar, a compact primary action button composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label, a small icon-only theme toggle button, a small icon-only notification bell button, a small circular user avatar, and a text logout link.

**Left icon rail** is a narrow fixed-width vertical strip anchored to the far left edge of the viewport below the navbar, stretching from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport. It contains a vertical stack of small icon-only buttons, each representing a top-level navigation category, centered horizontally in the strip with consistent vertical spacing between them.

**Expanded sidebar panel** sits immediately to the right of the icon rail as a wider fixed-width vertical panel stretching from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport. At the top of the panel, place a header row composed of a short title label on the left and a compact icon-only add button on the right on the same baseline. Below the header, place a search input field with a leading search icon and placeholder text spanning the full panel width. Below the search field, stack a vertical navigation list. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a text label on the left and a trailing chevron icon on the right. One section carries a highlight state (active color) and is expanded to show indented child links below the parent. One item includes a small colored numeric badge to the right of the label. At the very bottom of the panel, anchor a user identity block composed of a small circular avatar on the left, a two-line text group (user name on the first line and email on the second line) to the right of the avatar, and a small trailing chevron or caret icon.

**Right icon rail** is a narrow fixed-width vertical strip anchored to the far right edge of the viewport below the navbar, mirroring the left icon rail in width and structure. It contains a vertical stack of small icon-only buttons centered horizontally with consistent vertical spacing.

**Main content area** fills the remaining horizontal space between the expanded sidebar panel and the right icon rail, and vertically from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport.
