Content placeholder regions are arranged as a dashboard grid: a top row of three equal-width regions, a middle row of three equal-width regions, and a full-width region at the bottom.

**Sizing rules.** The shell occupies the full viewport: it spans the viewport width edge to edge and stretches from the very top to the very bottom of the viewport with no surrounding page padding, no outer rounded frame, and no enclosing max-width container around the shell itself. Every dotted (dashed-outline) placeholder region inside the main content area is a short horizontal block approximately 240 pixels tall and never grows to absorb remaining vertical space; empty space below the last placeholder remains visible as the content-area background. Every visible action button inside the shell (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, full-width submit, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links or tab triggers, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports both icon rails and the expanded sidebar panel collapse off-screen. The sidebar becomes accessible via the hamburger icon. The main content area expands to the full viewport width. Grid columns stack vertically in reading order.

items.name: Top Navbar Sidebar Application Shell
items.promptText:
Create an application shell composed of a fixed top navbar spanning the full viewport width and a fixed left sidebar below the navbar, with the remaining space to the right of the sidebar and below the navbar given entirely to the main content area.

**Top navbar** is pinned to the top of the viewport as a full-width horizontal bar. From left to right on the same baseline: a hamburger menu icon; a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right; a search input field with a leading search icon and placeholder text; then grouped on the right end of the bar, a compact primary action button composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label, a small icon-only theme toggle button, a small icon-only notification bell button, a small circular user avatar, and a text logout link.

**Left sidebar** is a fixed-width vertical panel anchored to the left edge of the viewport below the navbar, stretching from the bottom of the navbar to the bottom of the viewport. Inside the sidebar, stack a vertical navigation list from top to bottom. Each primary navigation item is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a text label to its right on the same baseline. Some items include a trailing chevron icon indicating an expandable submenu; when expanded, indented child links appear directly below the parent item as plain text labels without icons. One section carries a highlight state (active color on the label and an expanded submenu visible). One navigation item includes a small colored numeric badge to the right of the label indicating a count. Below the main navigation group, separate a secondary group of utility links at the bottom of the sidebar (such as Docs, Components, Help), each following the same icon-plus-label row pattern.

**Main content area** fills the remaining space to the right of the sidebar and below the navbar. Content placeholder regions are arranged as a dashboard grid inside a centered container with comfortable padding: a full-width region at the top row; a three-column equal-width row of regions in the middle; a two-column unequal-width row (wider left, narrower right) below; and a full-width region at the bottom.

**Sizing rules.** The shell occupies the full viewport: it spans the viewport width edge to edge and stretches from the very top to the very bottom of the viewport with no surrounding page padding, no outer rounded frame, and no enclosing max-width container around the shell itself. Every dotted (dashed-outline) placeholder region inside the main content area is a short horizontal block approximately 240 pixels tall and never grows to absorb remaining vertical space; empty space below the last placeholder remains visible as the content-area background. Every visible action button inside the shell (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, full-width submit, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links or tab triggers, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports the sidebar collapses off-screen and becomes accessible via the hamburger icon in the navbar. The main content area expands to the full viewport width. Grid columns stack vertically in reading order.

items.name: Application Shell With Toolbar
items.promptText:
Create an application shell composed of two fixed horizontal bars stacked at the top of the viewport, with the remaining vertical space below given entirely to the main content area.

**Primary navbar** is pinned to the very top of the viewport as a full-width horizontal bar. From left to right on the same baseline: a hamburger menu icon; a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right; a search input field with a leading search icon and placeholder text; then grouped on the right end of the bar, a row of small icon-only utility buttons (such as a theme toggle, a dark-mode toggle, and a grid-view toggle) sitting side by side on the same baseline, followed by a compact primary action button composed of a small leading plus icon and a short label, and finally a user identity block composed of a small circular avatar paired with the user's name and a trailing dropdown chevron to its right.

**Secondary toolbar** sits directly below the primary navbar as a full-width horizontal bar with a subtly different background or a thin top border to separate it from the navbar. On the left side of the bar, place a horizontal row of text navigation links sitting side by side on the same baseline with consistent spacing (one entry may include a trailing chevron icon indicating a dropdown submenu, and the row may end with a small overflow icon for additional links). On the right side of the same bar, place a horizontal row of filter or search widgets on the same baseline: a dropdown selector, a text input field, another dropdown selector, and a compact icon-only search button at the far right.

**Main content area** fills the remaining viewport height below the secondary toolbar inside a centered max-width container with comfortable side padding. Content placeholder regions stack vertically with consistent vertical spacing between them.

**Sizing rules.** The shell occupies the full viewport: it spans the viewport width edge to edge and stretches from the very top to the very bottom of the viewport with no surrounding page padding, no outer rounded frame, and no enclosing max-width container around the shell itself. Every dotted (dashed-outline) placeholder region inside the main content area is a short horizontal block approximately 240 pixels tall and never grows to absorb remaining vertical space; empty space below the last placeholder remains visible as the content-area background. Every visible action button inside the shell (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, full-width submit, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links or tab triggers, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports collapse the primary navbar into a mobile-friendly layout (hide or condense the search field; group utility icons behind a menu or shrink to essential ones; the user block may reduce to avatar-only). The secondary toolbar stacks or collapses: the navigation links may move into a hamburger or horizontal scroll strip, and the widget row may stack below the links or collapse behind a filter toggle. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Split Forgot Password With Proof Points
items.promptText:
Create a forgot-password page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The two columns are separated by a thin vertical border running the full height of the section.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack, vertically centered within the column height, containing in order: a large bold heading stating a trust metric on its own line (e.g. "Over 200,000+ happy clients"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, describing the platform's value proposition for teams; a vertical list of three proof points placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, each proof point is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a vertical stack to the right of the icon containing a bold metric label on its own line (e.g. "35+ finished projects") and a short supporting sentence directly below the label.

**Right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack, vertically centered within the column height, containing a compact reset-password form. Stack from top to bottom: a bold heading on its own line (e.g. "Forgot your password?"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, reassuring the user and explaining the reset flow; a labeled email input row placed below the paragraph (the label sits above the input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting an email address); a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text confirms acceptance of linked terms and conditions (with the terms phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width primary action button at the bottom with a short label (e.g. "Reset password").

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the social proof column first and the form column directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Split Forgot Password With Technology Showcase
items.promptText:
Create a forgot-password page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack, vertically centered within the column height, containing a compact reset-password form. Stack from top to bottom: a bold heading on its own line (e.g. "Forgot your password?"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, reassuring the user and explaining the reset flow; a labeled email input row placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space (the label sits above the input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting an email address); a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text confirms acceptance of linked terms and conditions (with the terms phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width primary action button below the checkbox with a short label (e.g. "Reset password").

**Right column** uses a subtle filled background with rounded corners and contains a centered vertical stack vertically centered within the column height. Inside the column, place a circular arrangement of technology or partner brand icons distributed evenly around an invisible orbital ring (each icon sits inside a small rounded container); below the orbital graphic, place a bold centered heading stating a technology count or integration metric on its own line (e.g. "Over 200+ technologies"); a centered supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading describing the platform's integration breadth.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the form column first and the technology showcase directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Full-Width Split Forgot Password Page
items.promptText:
Create a forgot-password page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints that spans the full available width of the viewport with no outer margin.

**Left column** uses a plain page background and contains a left-aligned vertical stack constrained to a 424px max width, vertically and horizontally centered within the column. Stack from top to bottom: a bold heading on its own line (e.g. "Forgot your password?"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, reassuring the user and explaining the reset flow; a labeled email input row placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space (the label sits above the input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting an email address); a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text confirms acceptance of linked terms and conditions (with the terms phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width primary action button below the checkbox with a short label (e.g. "Reset password").

**Right column** uses a distinct filled background that spans the full column area edge-to-edge. Inside the column, place a centered vertical stack vertically centered within the column height containing: a small brand icon or logo mark on its own line paired with a brand name label immediately to the right of the icon on the same baseline; a large bold heading on its own line directly below the brand row delivering a compelling value statement (e.g. "Explore the world's leading design portfolios."); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width describing the platform community; a social proof row placed below the paragraph, composed of slightly overlapping circular user avatars on the left and a short line of text immediately to the right of the avatars on the same baseline stating a review metric (e.g. "Rated best over 15.7k reviews").

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the form column first and the branded column directly below it; each internal stack preserves its original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Split Forgot Password Card With Illustration
items.promptText:
Create a forgot-password page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**Left column** contains a single elevated card with rounded corners and a light surface treatment, vertically centered within the column height. Inside the card, stack from top to bottom: a small brand icon or logo mark on its own line paired with a brand name label immediately to the right of the icon on the same baseline; a bold heading on its own line directly below the brand row (e.g. "Forgot your password?"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, reassuring the user and explaining the reset flow; a labeled email input row placed below the paragraph (the label sits above the input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting an email address); a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text confirms acceptance of linked terms and conditions (with the terms phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width primary action button at the bottom of the card with a short label (e.g. "Reset password").

**Right column** holds one large illustrative scene that fills most of the column area, vertically centered within the column. The illustration depicts a figure sitting at a workstation with a monitor displaying a user profile or authentication interface, plants or office elements in the background, conveying a calm account-recovery theme without relying on photographic imagery.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the form card first and the illustration directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Feature Grid With Testimonial Carousel
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce promotional section pairing a three-column feature grid with a testimonial carousel. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Heading block.** A center-aligned block with 16 pixels beneath it (32 from the medium breakpoint up): a ~24px bold heading-color title with tight tracking and 12 pixels beneath it (~36px from the medium breakpoint up, e.g. "Why us?") over a ~16px muted subtitle (~20px from the medium breakpoint up). **Feature block.** A block with full-width top and bottom borders drawn from the design system's border token, 24 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the small breakpoint up, 32 from the medium breakpoint up), and 16 pixels beneath it (32 from the medium breakpoint up): a one-column grid that becomes three columns from the large breakpoint up with a 64-pixel column gap and 24-pixel row gap (32 from the medium breakpoint up). Each cell is a top-aligned, 16-pixel-gapped flex row of a non-shrinking 36-by-36-pixel muted glyph and a growing, min-width-0 body: - A ~14px semibold uppercase heading-color label with 16 pixels beneath it. - A ~14px muted paragraph with 12 pixels beneath it. - Then either a **link list** — a vertical list of ~14px medium links 12 pixels apart, each a row in the brand foreground color that is underlined and loses its underline on hover, trailing a 20-by-20-pixel arrow glyph 4 pixels after its label (e.g. "Track Your Order", "Schedule Delivery", "Apply Now", "Manage Your Shop") — or a **contact list** — a vertical list of ~14px muted rows 12 pixels apart, each a vertically-centered, 8-pixel-gapped row leading with a 16-by-16-pixel muted glyph (e.g. an office phone line, and a support line whose email is a hover-underline link). Use three feature cells (e.g. "Real time order tracking", "Your marketplace", "Premium support"). **Testimonial carousel.** A sliding carousel about 196 pixels tall (236 from the small breakpoint up, 240 from the large breakpoint up, 200 from the xl breakpoint up) with hidden overflow, holding a set of sliding panels (render about four). Each panel is a one-column grid that becomes two columns from the small breakpoint up and three from the large breakpoint up with a 16-pixel gap, of **testimonial figures**. Each figure is a host-rounded card on a soft secondary surface with 24 pixels of padding: a blockquote of a ~18px semibold heading-color title over a ~14px muted quote paragraph with 16 pixels of vertical margin, and a figcaption — a vertically-centered, 12-pixel-gapped row of a 32-by-32-pixel round **real avatar photo** and a ~16px medium heading-color name. Beneath the carousel, a centered row with 16 pixels above it (24 from the medium breakpoint up) holding previous and next icon-only ghost buttons (the previous with a 16px end margin), each a 28-by-28-pixel arrow glyph in the muted body color shifting to the heading color on hover. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the heading and subtitle, the feature block and its dividers, the feature glyphs, labels, paragraphs, link lists and contact lists (with their arrow and contact glyphs and the email link), and the testimonial carousel (figures, titles, quotes, avatars, names, and the previous/next controls) — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. Every link or button must be the host design system's own link and button components, with their colors, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; the testimonial figures use the host's soft secondary surface token and the avatars are real photographic assets. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The link-list and contact-list links are inline text links (the link list trailing a 20-by-20-pixel arrow glyph); the carousel previous/next buttons are icon-only ghost buttons sized to their 28-by-28-pixel glyphs. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the feature glyphs at 36-by-36 pixels, the link arrows at 20-by-20 pixels, the contact glyphs at 16-by-16 pixels, the carousel at ~196/236/240/200 pixels tall across the small, large, and xl breakpoints, the avatars at 32-by-32 pixels, the carousel arrows at 28-by-28 pixels, the heading at ~24–36px, the feature labels at ~14px, and the testimonial titles at ~18px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The feature block steps from one to three columns at the large breakpoint (each cell keeping its leading glyph beside the text); each carousel panel steps from one to two to three columns across the small and large breakpoints; the carousel keeps its previous/next controls centered beneath it.

items.name: Wide Form Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Create item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay that centers a surface-card dialog constrained to a comfortable form width (a roomy two-column form) with a maximum width of 672 pixels. The dialog has internal padding, host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, a soft elevation shadow, and scrolls internally when its content is tall. **Header.** A top row with a short title (such as "Add item") on the left and a small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) on the right, separated from the body by a thin bottom divider. **Body.** A form laid out as a responsive grid that is one column on mobile and four columns from the small breakpoint up. Include, in order: a primary name text input spanning two columns; a secondary short text input spanning two columns; a numeric value input spanning two columns; a category-style single-select spanning two columns; then a row of four compact numeric inputs, each a single column wide, each with a small leading icon inside the field on the start edge and a muted placeholder (a cluster of measurement or attribute fields); a full-width multi-line description textarea; a full-width image upload dropzone rendered as a dashed-border drop area containing a centered upload glyph, a short instruction line, a max-file-size hint, and a primary "Browse file" button, paired with a visually hidden native file input; and a full-width inline single-choice radio group with three options on one baseline. Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk beside the label. **Footer.** A top-divider-separated action row with a primary submit button carrying a small leading plus icon (such as "Add item"), a secondary outlined button carrying a small leading icon (such as a "Schedule" action), and a final secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close") pushed to the far end on wide viewports. **Sizing rules.** The dialog width stays bounded and never spans edge to edge. Leading field icons align to the input's vertical center. Surfaces, borders, dashed outlines, focus rings, dividers, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system; the required-asterisk and any semantic accents use host semantic tokens. **Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button (trigger, submit, secondary action, dismiss, and the dropzone "Browse" button) uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Input padding rule.** Standard text, numeric, and select fields use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; icon-prefixed inputs reserve start padding for the leading icon; the textarea uses 14px of padding on all sides. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control with a tint pulled from the same neutral tone as the dialog surface, nudged one step lighter — the identical hue and shade, only brighter, never a different color — so the fields separate from the dialog background through a soft, subtle contrast rather than a color shift. Apply this same fill uniformly across all text, numeric, icon-prefixed, and select inputs, the textarea, and the upload dropzone drop area, and keep the host default border (or dashed border for the dropzone) and focus ring so each field reads as a cleanly bounded, slightly lifted surface. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the dialog grows toward the full available width, the four-column grid collapses to a single column in reading order (the four compact numeric inputs stack), the dropzone and inline radio group span full width, and the footer actions each stretch to full width and stack in primary-then-secondary-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Accordion Form Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Add item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a surface-card dialog constrained to a comfortable two-column form width, with internal padding, host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, a soft elevation shadow, and internal scrolling when tall. **Header.** A top row with a short title (such as "Add item") on the left and a small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) on the right, separated from the body by a thin bottom divider. **Body.** A vertical collapse-style accordion of two stacked panels. Each panel header is a full-width button row with a section label on the left and a chevron icon on the right that rotates to indicate expanded state; the first panel is expanded by default and the second collapsed. - **Panel one (primary details)** reveals a responsive field grid (one column on mobile, two from the small breakpoint up). Each field has a small leading icon inside the input on the start edge. Include: a primary name text input, a contact-style text input, an identifier-style text input, a role-style single-select, a phone-number composite field made of a leading country-code dropdown trigger (small flag glyph, dial code, and chevron) attached to a phone text input with a guiding pattern and a scrollable menu of country options each showing a flag and a "(+code)" label, a region single-select, a type single-select, a status single-select, a password input, and a confirm-password input. - **Panel two (extended details)** reveals a full-width rich text editor (a bordered surface with a toolbar row of icon-only formatting buttons grouped and divided, a trailing full-screen toggle with a tooltip, and a multi-line textarea beneath), a full-width image upload dropzone with a "Browse" button and hidden native file input, a tag-style text input, a language single-select, a date-picker input with a leading calendar icon, and a timezone single-select. Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk beside the label. **Footer.** A top-divider-separated action row with a primary submit button carrying a small leading plus icon (such as "Create item") and a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close"). **Sizing rules.** The dialog width stays bounded and never spans edge to edge. Accordion panel headers share consistent height and chevron rotation; the expanded panel removes its rounded bottom and shadow to merge with its body. Surfaces, borders, focus rings, dividers, radii, the country-code menu, and the editor toolbar stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button (trigger, submit, dismiss, country-code trigger, and "Browse") uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button, accordion chevron, or editor toolbar icon buttons. **Input padding rule.** Icon-prefixed inputs reserve start padding for the leading icon and use 10px vertical padding; selects and plain inputs use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; the editor textarea sits flush inside its padded toolbar container. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control with a tint pulled from the same neutral tone as the dialog surface, nudged one step lighter — the identical hue and shade, only brighter, never a different color — so the fields separate from the dialog background through a soft, subtle contrast rather than a color shift. Apply this same fill uniformly across all icon-prefixed inputs, plain inputs, selects, the phone-number composite (its country-code trigger and phone input alike), the date-picker input, the rich text editor surface, and the upload dropzone drop area, and keep the host default border (or dashed border for the dropzone) and focus ring so each field reads as a cleanly bounded, slightly lifted surface. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the dialog grows toward full width, each panel's field grid collapses to a single column in reading order, the phone composite keeps its country trigger attached above or inline with the input, the editor toolbar wraps, and the footer actions stack in primary-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Full Bleed Alert Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Delete item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a medium surface-card dialog constrained to a maximum width of 448 pixels, with host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, and a soft elevation shadow. The dialog itself carries no uniform internal padding; instead each region manages its own padding so a banner can span the full dialog width. **Close affordance.** A small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) absolutely positioned in the top-end corner of the dialog. **Body.** A start-aligned stack: a short dialog title (such as "Delete item?") in a medium heading weight with its own padding, a muted supporting paragraph beneath it with horizontal padding, then a full-bleed alert banner that spans the entire dialog width edge to edge (no side gutters), separated from the content above and below by thin top and bottom borders, filled with a soft semantic-tinted background and holding a short emphasis message in the matching semantic foreground color. **Footer.** A horizontal action row where both buttons stretch to equal full width and sit side by side with consistent spacing: a primary confirm button (such as "Continue") and a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "No, cancel"), with their own padding above and to the sides. **Sizing rules.** The dialog stays bounded to its 448-pixel maximum and never spans edge to edge. The alert banner is the only full-bleed element and reaches both side edges of the dialog; its semantic tint and foreground, plus all surfaces, borders, focus rings, and radii, stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** The trigger button uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the footer confirm and dismiss buttons use padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the dialog grows toward the full available width, the heading and paragraph keep their padding, the alert banner stays full-bleed to the dialog edges, and the two footer buttons each remain full width and stack vertically in confirm-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Icon List Result Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Delete item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a small-to-medium surface-card dialog constrained to a compact confirmation width, with internal padding, host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, and a soft elevation shadow. **Close affordance.** A small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) absolutely positioned in the top-end corner of the dialog. **Body.** A start-aligned stack: a short dialog title (such as "Items successfully deleted") in a medium heading weight, a muted supporting paragraph beneath it (such as "The following items have been removed from your list:"), then a vertical list of result rows with consistent spacing. Each row is a horizontal pair: a small success glyph (a checkmark inside a circle) in a strong success foreground color on the start edge, followed by an item label. **Footer.** A horizontal action row on the same baseline: a primary confirm button (such as "Continue") followed by a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "No, cancel"). **Sizing rules.** The dialog stays bounded to its compact maximum and never spans edge to edge. List rows share consistent spacing and glyph alignment. Success glyph colors, surfaces, borders, focus rings, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** The trigger button uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the footer confirm and dismiss buttons use padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the dialog grows toward the full available width, the result list keeps its glyph-plus-label rows in reading order, and the footer keeps its actions inline or stacks them while preserving confirm-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Illustrated Single Action Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Delete item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a small surface-card dialog constrained to a narrow confirmation width, with internal padding, host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, and a soft elevation shadow. **Close affordance.** A small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) absolutely positioned in the top-end corner of the dialog. **Body.** A center-aligned stack: a larger decorative illustration graphic centered horizontally at the top (an illustrative spot graphic, not a functional control), followed by a short result heading (such as "All done!") in a medium weight, and a muted center-aligned supporting paragraph beneath it (such as "The selected item has been permanently removed from your list."). **Footer.** A single centered primary action button (such as "Continue") that confirms and dismisses the modal. **Sizing rules.** The dialog stays bounded to its narrow maximum and never spans edge to edge. The illustration is decorative and may keep its own artwork colors, while surfaces, borders, focus rings, radii, and text colors stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** The trigger button uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the footer action button uses padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the dialog grows toward the full available width; the illustration, heading, paragraph, and single action button preserve their stacked, center-aligned reading order.

items.name: Checklist Date Range Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Create item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a surface-card dialog constrained to a comfortable two-column form width, with internal padding, host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, a soft elevation shadow, and internal scrolling when tall. **Header.** A top row with a short title (such as "Add item") on the left and a small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) on the right, separated from the body by a thin bottom divider. **Body.** A form laid out as a responsive grid (one column on mobile, two from the small breakpoint up). Include, in reading order: a primary name text input, a category-style single-select, a numeric value input, a secondary short text input, then a full-width checklist subsection enclosed by thin top and bottom dividers — a group label above a vertical list of checkbox rows (each a checkbox with a wrapping text label, some pre-checked) followed by a full-width outlined "Add new entry" button with a leading plus icon. After the checklist: a tag-style text input whose label carries a trailing muted "N remaining" counter, a secondary text input, a full-width date-range picker composed of two side-by-side date inputs (a start and an end) each with a leading calendar icon, a status single-select, a notification-period single-select, and a full-width multi-line description textarea. Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk beside the label. **Footer.** A top-divider-separated action row with a primary submit button (such as "Add item") and a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close"). **Sizing rules.** The dialog width stays bounded and never spans edge to edge. The checklist subsection is visually fenced by dividers and its rows share consistent spacing. Checkbox controls, surfaces, borders, focus rings, dividers, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button (trigger, submit, dismiss, and "Add new entry") uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Input padding rule.** Plain inputs and selects use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; date-range inputs reserve start padding for the leading calendar icon; the textarea uses 14px of padding on all sides. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control with a tint pulled from the same neutral tone as the dialog surface, nudged one step lighter — the identical hue and shade, only brighter, never a different color — so the fields separate from the dialog background through a soft, subtle contrast rather than a color shift. Apply this same fill uniformly across all text inputs, numeric inputs, selects, the date-range start and end inputs, the tag input, and the textarea, and keep the host default border and focus ring so each field reads as a cleanly bounded, slightly lifted surface. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the dialog grows toward full width, the field grid collapses to a single column in reading order, the date-range picker stacks its start and end inputs vertically, the checklist and "Add new entry" button span full width, and the footer stacks actions in primary-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Two-Column Feature List with CTA
items.promptText:
Create a feature section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a centered header block composed of a large heading centered on its own line followed by a centered supporting paragraph directly beneath it at a moderate reading width.

Below the header, place a two-column layout on large 1280px width breakpoints separated by a single thin vertical divider running the full height of the column area. Each column stacks three feature items vertically (six items total across both columns) with consistent spacing between them. Each item is a horizontal row composed of a small circular icon container anchored to the left (holding a single centered glyph) and a text block to the right of the icon containing a medium-weight heading on its own line and a short multi-line paragraph directly beneath the heading.

Below the two-column block, place one centered pill-shaped primary button on its own line whose label includes a trailing arrow icon at the end of the button text.

On narrow viewports, stack the two columns vertically in reading order and replace the vertical divider with a thin horizontal rule between the two halves; keep the primary button centered below both column stacks.

items.name: Selectable Option Form Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Create item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a wide surface-card dialog constrained to a large two-pane width. The dialog has internal padding, host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, a soft elevation shadow, and scrolls internally when tall. **Header.** A top row with a short title (such as "Add item") on the left and a small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) on the right, separated from the body by a thin bottom divider. **Body.** A form split into two equal columns from the small breakpoint up (stacked on mobile) with the columns aligned to the top. - **Left column** is its own responsive field grid (one column on mobile, two from the small breakpoint up): a primary name text input, a secondary short text input, a numeric value input, a category-style single-select, a cluster of four compact numeric inputs each with a small leading icon, and a full-width subsection containing a group label and a horizontal row of two selectable option cards. Each option card is a bordered surface tile holding a glyph, a bold option title, a short supporting description, and a radio control aligned to the top-end corner; selecting a card reflects a checked state and the cards behave as one single-choice radio group. - **Right column** stacks a full-width multi-line description textarea, a full-width image upload dropzone (dashed-border drop area with upload glyph, instruction line, max-file-size hint, and a "Browse file" button plus a hidden native file input), and a full-width inline single-choice radio group with two options on one baseline. Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk beside the label. **Footer.** A top-divider-separated action row with a primary submit button carrying a small leading plus icon (such as "Add item"), a secondary outlined button with a leading icon (such as "Schedule"), and a final secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close") pushed to the far end on wide viewports. **Sizing rules.** The dialog width stays bounded to its large maximum and never spans edge to edge. Option cards share equal sizing and a consistent selected treatment. Surfaces, borders, dashed outlines, card selection rings, focus rings, dividers, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button (trigger, submit, secondary action, dismiss, and "Browse") uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Input padding rule.** Standard fields use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; icon-prefixed inputs reserve start padding for the icon; the textarea uses 14px of padding on all sides. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control with a tint pulled from the same neutral tone as the dialog surface, nudged one step lighter — the identical hue and shade, only brighter, never a different color — so the fields separate from the dialog background through a soft, subtle contrast rather than a color shift. Apply this same fill uniformly across all text, numeric, icon-prefixed, and select inputs, the textarea, and the upload dropzone drop area, and keep the host default border (or dashed border for the dropzone) and focus ring so each field reads as a cleanly bounded, slightly lifted surface. The selectable option cards may share this same fill so they sit in the same tonal family as the fields. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the two panes stack into one column (left pane first, right pane second), every inner grid collapses to a single column, the option cards stack vertically, the dropzone spans full width, and footer actions stretch to full width and stack in primary-then-secondary-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Avatar Role Color Picker Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Create item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a wide surface-card dialog constrained to a large two-pane width, with internal padding, host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, a soft elevation shadow, and internal scrolling when tall. **Header.** A top row with a short title (such as "Add new item") on the left and a small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) on the right, separated from the body by a thin bottom divider. **Body.** A form split into two equal columns from the small breakpoint up (stacked on mobile), columns aligned to the top. - **Left column** stacks an avatar/cover upload row (a small rounded thumbnail beside a native file input and a small format/size helper line), a primary name text input, a secondary short text input, and a full-width rich text editor (bordered surface with a grouped icon-only formatting toolbar, a trailing full-screen toggle with tooltip, and a multi-line textarea). - **Right column** stacks a search-style text input with a leading search icon for adding associated entries, then a vertical list of associated entry rows. Each row shows, on the left, a small circular avatar beside a stacked primary label and muted secondary label; and on the right, an inline role dropdown trigger (current role text plus chevron) that opens a small menu of role options. The opened menu is a floating surface panel with its own elevated background, a hairline default border, a host radius token, and a drop shadow, sized to a compact fixed width; it holds a vertically stacked list of selectable role rows, each a full-width option with its own internal padding, a rounded hover background, and a text-emphasis hover state. Rows are separated by thin bottom dividers. Below the list, a "tag color" subsection with a group label above a horizontal row of selectable color swatch buttons, where the active swatch shows a checkmark and a selection ring and choosing another swatch moves the selected state. Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk beside the label. **Footer.** A top-divider-separated action row with a primary submit button carrying a small leading plus icon (such as "Add item"), a secondary outlined button with a leading icon (such as "Schedule"), and a final secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close") pushed to the far end on wide viewports. **Sizing rules.** The dialog width stays bounded to its large maximum and never spans edge to edge. Associated-entry rows share consistent height and alignment; color swatches are equal squares with a consistent selected ring. The swatch palette is illustrative — map each swatch to a host design-system color token rather than a hardcoded hex value. Surfaces, borders, focus rings, dividers, radii, the editor toolbar, and role menus stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Role dropdown menu rule.** The role dropdown menu's padding, border radius, border, shadow, and colors are all agnostic and resolved from the host design system — never hardcoded. Inside the menu, the option rows must use a concentric (nested) corner radius so they nest cleanly within the rounded menu container: compute each inner option's radius as the menu container's radius minus the menu's inner padding, so the curves stay visually parallel. For example, a 16px menu container with 8px of inner padding gives 8px option rows; a 12px container with 8px padding gives ~4px rows. Whatever radius the host design system assigns the menu container, derive the option radius from it rather than fixing a separate value, keeping a consistent gap between the option edge and the container edge on all sides. **Button padding rule.** Every labeled action button (trigger, submit, secondary action, dismiss) uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. This does not apply to icon-only buttons (close, editor toolbar), inline role-dropdown triggers, or color-swatch buttons. **Input padding rule.** The search input reserves start padding for its leading icon; plain inputs use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; the editor textarea sits flush inside its padded container. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control with a tint pulled from the same neutral tone as the dialog surface, nudged one step lighter — the identical hue and shade, only brighter, never a different color — so the fields separate from the dialog background through a soft, subtle contrast rather than a color shift. Apply this same fill uniformly across the search-style input, the plain text inputs, and the rich text editor surface, and keep the host default border and focus ring so each field reads as a cleanly bounded, slightly lifted surface. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the two panes stack into one column (left first, right second), the avatar upload row stacks thumbnail above input, the editor toolbar wraps, associated-entry rows keep avatar and labels inline with the role dropdown wrapping beneath if space is tight, the color swatches wrap onto multiple lines, and footer actions stretch to full width and stack in primary-then-secondary-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Contained Warning Alert Modal
items.promptText: Create a self-contained modal dialog triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its overlay modal so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Delete item") that opens the modal. **Overlay and dialog shell.** A fixed full-viewport overlay centering a medium surface-card dialog constrained to a compact confirmation width, with internal padding (slightly larger from the small breakpoint up), host-token rounded corners, the primary surface background, and a soft elevation shadow. **Close affordance.** A small icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) absolutely positioned in the top-end corner of the dialog, dismissing the modal on activation. **Body.** A start-aligned stack with deliberate spacing: - A short dialog title (such as "Delete item?") in a medium heading weight, with 8 pixels of space below it. - A muted supporting paragraph directly beneath the title (such as "Are you sure you want to delete this item?"). - A contained warning alert separated from the paragraph above and the footer below by 24 pixels of vertical margin on each side. The alert is a fully enclosed box (a continuous border on all four sides and host-token rounded corners, not a full-bleed banner), filled with a soft warning-tinted background and its text in the matching warning foreground color. Inside, an inline header row places a 16-by-16-pixel warning glyph on the start edge beside a bold "Warning" label on the same baseline, followed 8 pixels below by a short warning body message describing the side effects of the action (such as "Deleting this item will also remove its associated entries permanently. Are you sure you want to proceed?"). **Footer.** A horizontal action row with the two buttons separated by 16 pixels of horizontal space, on the same baseline: a primary destructive confirm button using a danger semantic treatment (danger fill, danger hover, danger focus ring) carrying a small leading trash icon and a destructive label (such as "Yes, delete item"), followed by a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "No, cancel"). **Sizing rules.** The dialog stays bounded to its compact maximum and never spans edge to edge. The destructive button's danger colors and the alert's warning tint and foreground come from host semantic tokens; surfaces, borders, focus rings, dividers, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** The trigger button uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the footer destructive confirm and dismiss buttons use padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px, with the leading trash icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the dialog grows toward the full available width, the title-paragraph-alert stack preserves its 8-pixel and 24-pixel spacing in reading order, the warning alert keeps its full enclosing border, and the footer keeps its actions inline or stacks them while preserving destructive-confirm-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Split Forgot Password With Proof Points
items.promptText:
Create a forgot-password page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The two columns are separated by a thin vertical border running the full height of the section.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack, vertically centered within the column height, containing in order: a large bold heading stating a trust metric on its own line (e.g. "Over 200,000+ happy clients"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, describing the platform's value proposition for teams; a vertical list of three proof points placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, each proof point is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a vertical stack to the right of the icon containing a bold metric label on its own line (e.g. "35+ finished projects") and a short supporting sentence directly below the label.

**Right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack, vertically centered within the column height, containing a compact reset-password form. Stack from top to bottom: a bold heading on its own line (e.g. "Forgot your password?"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, reassuring the user and explaining the reset flow; a labeled email input row placed below the paragraph (the label sits above the input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting an email address); a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text confirms acceptance of linked terms and conditions (with the terms phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width primary action button at the bottom with a short label (e.g. "Reset password").

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the social proof column first and the form column directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Reset Password With Illustration Split
items.promptText:
Create a reset-password page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

**Left column** contains a single elevated card with rounded corners and a light surface treatment, vertically centered within the column height. Inside the card, stack from top to bottom: a small brand icon or logo mark on its own line paired with a brand name label immediately to the right of the icon on the same baseline; a bold heading on its own line directly below the brand row (e.g. "Change you password."); a short supporting sentence directly below the heading explaining that the new password must differ from previous ones; a labeled email input row placed below the supporting text (the label sits above the input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting an email address); a two-column field row placed below the email input with comfortable column gaps — required password input on the left (label above with required-field marker; masked dots placeholder inside) and required repeat-password input on the right (same shape); a single checkbox row spanning the full form width containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text confirms acceptance of linked terms and conditions (with the terms phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width primary action button at the bottom of the card with a short label (e.g. "Reset password").

**Right column** holds one large illustrative scene that fills most of the column area, vertically centered within the column. The illustration depicts a figure sitting at a workstation with a monitor displaying a user profile or authentication interface, plants or office elements in the background, conveying a calm account-recovery theme without relying on photographic imagery.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the form card first and the illustration directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Split Reset Password With Trust Metrics
items.promptText:
Create a reset-password page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The two columns are separated by a thin vertical border running the full height of the section.

**Left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack, vertically centered within the column height, containing in order: a large bold heading stating a trust metric on its own line (e.g. "Over 200,000+ happy clients"); a supporting paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, describing the platform's value proposition for teams; a vertical list of three proof points placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, each proof point is a horizontal row composed of a small leading icon on the left and a vertical stack to the right of the icon containing a bold metric label on its own line (e.g. "35+ finished projects") and a short supporting sentence directly below the label.

**Right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack, vertically centered within the column height, containing a compact reset-password form. Stack from top to bottom: a bold heading on its own line (e.g. "Create new password"); a labeled email input row placed below the heading after extra vertical space (the label sits above the input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting an email address); a two-column field row placed below the email input with comfortable column gaps — required new-password input on the left (label above with required-field marker; masked dots placeholder inside) and required confirm-password input on the right (same shape); a single checkbox row spanning the full form width containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text confirms acceptance of linked terms and conditions (with the terms phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width primary action button at the bottom with a short label (e.g. "Reset password").

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the social proof column first and the form column directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Centered Reset Password Card
items.promptText:
Create a reset-password page as one centered vertical stack on a full-width section background that may include a very subtle repeating dot or grid texture behind the content, vertically centered within the viewport height. Stack from top to bottom: a small brand icon or logo mark centered horizontally on its own line paired with a brand name label immediately to the right of the icon on the same baseline; a single elevated card with rounded corners placed directly below the brand row, centered horizontally and constrained to a comfortable form width. Inside the card, stack from top to bottom: a bold heading on its own line (e.g. "Change password"); a labeled email input row placed below the heading (the label sits above the input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text; the input carries a leading envelope icon affordance flush-left inside the field and a placeholder suggesting an email address); a labeled new-password input row directly below (label above with required-field marker; masked dots placeholder inside); a labeled confirm-password input row directly below (same shape); a single checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text confirms acceptance of linked terms and conditions (with the terms phrase rendered as an inline text link); one full-width primary action button at the bottom of the card with a short label (e.g. "Reset password").

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack with comfortable side padding; allow the card to span the full content width while preserving center alignment throughout.

items.name: Split Marketing Register Page
items.promptText:
Create a register page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The left column is a marketing column carrying copy and a short feature list; the right column is the form column. The two columns share the same vertical center line.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large multi-line heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph below the heading at a comfortable reading width; a vertical list of about three feature rows each composed of a small leading icon at the left, a bold one-line title to the right of the icon on the same baseline, and a short supporting line directly beneath the title that sits flush-left under the icon-and-title row. Allow a very subtle decorative line or wireframe pattern to sit behind the left column so it reads as a textured marketing surface without competing with the copy.

The **right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a heading on its own line; a horizontal row of two equal third-party provider buttons sitting side by side (each button carries a small leading provider glyph and a short provider label); a horizontal "or" separator made of a thin rule, a centered short word, and another thin rule; a two-column field grid pairing a short text input on the left with a short text input on the right (first name / last name); a second two-column field grid pairing a short text input on the left with a single dropdown select on the right (email / country); a third two-column field grid pairing a password input on the left with a repeat-password input on the right (every label sits above its input with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text where applicable); one checkbox row containing a small square checkbox and an inline multi-line label whose copy may contain inline text links to legal documents; one full-width primary submit button beneath the checkbox row; finally a small helper line containing a short prompt sentence followed by an inline text link to the sign-in flow.

On narrow viewports, stack with the form column first and the marketing column second so the user reaches the form quickly; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Two-Column Register With Decorative Panel
items.promptText:
Create a register page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a heading on its own line; a horizontal row of two equal third-party provider buttons sitting side by side (each button carries a small leading provider glyph and a short provider label); a horizontal "or" separator made of a thin rule, a centered short word, and another thin rule; a two-column field grid where the first row pairs a short text input on the left with a short text input on the right; a labeled date-of-birth row whose label is followed by a tiny circular question-mark information affordance to its right and whose control area is a single horizontal row of three inline dropdown selects (one for day, one for month, one for year) sitting on the same line; a second two-column field grid pairing a password input on the left with a repeat-password input on the right; one checkbox row containing a small square checkbox and an inline multi-line label whose copy may contain inline text links to legal documents; one full-width primary submit button beneath the checkbox row; finally a small helper line containing a short prompt sentence followed by an inline text link to the sign-in flow.

The **right column** holds a single rounded decorative panel vertically centered relative to the form column. Inside the panel, arrange a loose decorative cluster of small circular technology glyphs distributed in a soft arc-style composition (no single rigid grid), then under the cluster center a short bold heading on its own line and a single short supporting paragraph centered beneath the heading.

On narrow viewports, stack with the form column first and the decorative panel second.

items.name: Split Register Card With Illustration
items.promptText:
Create a register page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The left column carries a single form card with rounded corners; the right column carries one decorative vector illustration. The two columns share the same vertical center line.

Inside the **left card**, stack from top to bottom: a small brand-mark row at the top of the card pairing a circular logo glyph and a short brand wordmark; a heading on its own line below the brand mark; a single sub-line directly below the heading combining a short supporting sentence with an inline text link to the sign-in flow at the end of the same line; a two-column field grid pairing a short text input on the left with a short text input on the right; a second two-column field grid pairing a password input on the left with a repeat-password input on the right (every label sits above its input with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text where applicable); a horizontal "or" separator made of a thin rule, a centered short word, and another thin rule; a stack of two full-width third-party provider buttons placed one above the other, each beginning with a small leading provider glyph followed by short provider label copy; a vertical stack of two checkbox rows with multi-line inline labels that may contain inline text links; one full-width primary submit button at the bottom of the card.

The **right column** have a single vector full width illustration sized to fill the column visually (for example a person sitting beside a device, with simple background shapes such as plants and a silhouette of a screen). Vertically center the illustration relative to the form card.

On narrow viewports, stack with the form card first and the illustration second; the illustration may shrink or be hidden when space is constrained.

items.name: Centered Register Card Page
items.promptText: Create a register page as one centered vertical 448px card on a full-page background. At the very top, place a small brand mark composed of a circular logo glyph followed by a short brand wordmark, both centered horizontally on the page. Below the brand mark, place one centered form card with rounded corners and a moderate max width. Inside the card, stack from top to bottom: a card heading on its own line; a labeled email input row (the label sits above the input on its own line and pairs a short label text with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label); a labeled password input row in the same shape directly below; a labeled repeat-password input row in the same shape directly below that; one checkbox row containing a small square checkbox at the left and an inline label whose text includes a single in-line text link; one full-width primary button beneath the checkbox row; finally, a small centered helper line containing a short prompt sentence followed by an inline text link to the sign-in flow. Treat the area outside the card as a subtle decorative field (for example a sparse dot or grid pattern). On narrow viewports keep the same single-column stack inside the card and let the card occupy the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Input Select Filter Dropdown
items.promptText: Create a self-contained dropdown menu triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its dropdown panel so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Forms filter") whose label is followed by a 16-by-16-pixel chevron glyph set 6 pixels after the text; activating it toggles the dropdown panel. **Dropdown panel.** A floating panel anchored directly beneath the trigger on a raised stacking layer, constrained to a fixed width of 288 pixels, with 12 pixels of internal padding, the primary surface background, a thin default border, a host-token medium (md) corner radius, and a large elevation shadow. **Body.** A 14-pixel semibold heading (such as "Filter") in the heading color with 12 pixels beneath it, then a vertical form with 16 pixels between its fields and 16 pixels above the first field. Each field is a full-width labeled control: a small-size medium-weight label in the heading color with 10 pixels beneath it, above its control. items.promptText:
