items.name: Advanced Range Filter Dropdown
items.promptText: Create a self-contained dropdown menu triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its dropdown panel so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Advanced filter") whose label is followed by a 16-by-16-pixel chevron glyph set 6 pixels after the text; activating it toggles the dropdown panel. **Dropdown panel.** A floating panel anchored directly beneath the trigger on a raised stacking layer, constrained to a fixed width of 320 pixels, with 12 pixels of internal padding, the primary surface background, a thin default border, a host-token medium (md) corner radius, and a large elevation shadow. **Body.** A vertical stack of labeled sections. Each section opens with a 14-pixel semibold heading in the heading color; the first heading has 12 pixels beneath it, and every later heading has 16 pixels above it and 12 pixels beneath it. Provide these sections in order: - A price section: a full-width single-track range slider (about 8 pixels tall on a rounded muted track with a draggable thumb) with 16 pixels beneath it, then two equal text inputs side by side with 12 pixels between them and 8 pixels of vertical padding (placeholders such as "From" and "To"). - A sales-volume section: the same full-width range slider with 16 pixels beneath it, followed by the same "From"/"To" input pair. - A category section: a two-column grid of selectable option cards with 10 pixels of gap. Each card is a full-width centered small-size medium-weight label with 8 pixels of padding, a muted neutral fill, a thin border, and host-token rounded corners; on hover and when selected it switches to a brand-tinted fill, border, and text. Render about six cards (such as "Gaming", "Electronics", "Phone", "TV/Monitor", "Laptop", "Watch") with some pre-selected. - A condition section: a single horizontal segmented control — a bordered, rounded, muted-filled bar split into equal-width segments by thin vertical dividers, each segment a 16-by-16-pixel radio with 12 pixels of start inset, an 8-pixel gap to its label, and small-size medium-weight text (such as "All", "New", "Used"), with one pre-selected. - A color section: a single-choice radio list with 2 pixels between rows; each row (8 pixels of padding, subtle hover surface, rounded corners) is a 16-by-16-pixel radio beside a label that leads with a 10-by-10-pixel round color dot (6 pixels before the name). **Footer.** With 16 pixels of space above it, a horizontal action row of two equal full-width buttons separated by 12 pixels: a secondary outlined reset button (such as "Reset") followed by a primary apply button (such as "Apply"). **Label wrapping rule.** Each option-card, segment, and color label stays on a single line and never wraps, truncating with an ellipsis if it would overflow so every card and row stays one line tall and the controls stay aligned. **Sizing rules.** The panel stays fixed at its 320-pixel width. The range sliders, option cards, segmented control, radio controls, color dots, surfaces, borders, focus rings, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system; brand accents come from host tokens. **Panel radius and concentric item rule.** The dropdown panel uses the host design system's medium (md) corner radius — not the base radius — together with 12 pixels of internal padding. Every interactive nav/option row inside the panel uses 8 pixels of padding and a smaller, concentric corner radius derived from the panel's medium radius minus the panel padding, so the inner rounding nests cleanly inside the panel's corners (for example, a 16-pixel panel radius pairs with an 8-pixel row radius). **Section heading rule.** Every panel section heading uses a 14-pixel semibold type size in the heading color with 12 pixels of margin beneath it. **Button padding rule.** The trigger uses padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the footer reset and apply buttons use padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. **Input padding rule.** The "From"/"To" text inputs use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding. **Input surface rule.** Fill the text inputs and the radio backgrounds with a filled host secondary/muted neutral surface that reads as a clearly bounded field, and keep the host default border and focus ring. **Radio style rule.** Every radio is a 16-by-16-pixel circle. In the unchecked state it uses a host design-system surface and border. In the checked state the circle is filled with the brand color AND a solid white (#ffffff) dot is explicitly drawn and centered on top of that fill. That center dot is always present and always white — never missing, never the brand color, never the fill or text color — so the white dot stays clearly visible against the brand fill in every design system. **Control border rule.** The borders of any checkboxes, radios, text inputs, and selects in this panel are taken from the host design system tokens — their resting, hover, focus, and checked-state border colors all come from the design system rather than any hard-coded value. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the panel may grow toward the available width while staying anchored to the trigger; the range sliders stay full width, the From/To inputs stay side by side, the option-card grid keeps two columns, and the segmented condition control stays a single inline bar.

items.name: Full-Width Utility Application Navbar
items.promptText:
Create an application navbar composed of two fixed horizontal bars stacked at the top of the viewport, both spanning the full viewport width edge to edge with no surrounding page padding and no enclosing max-width container around the bars themselves.

**Top utility bar** is pinned to the very top of the viewport as a slim full-width horizontal strip. On the left side, place a horizontal row of contact details sitting side by side on the same baseline (a small phone icon paired with a phone number, and a small email or company icon paired with an email address). On the right side of the same strip, place a row of controls on the same baseline: a small flag icon paired with a language label and a trailing dropdown chevron, followed by a horizontal row of small social-media icon links sitting side by side with consistent spacing between them, and a text login link with a small leading or trailing arrow icon at the far right.

**Primary navbar** sits directly below the top utility bar as a full-width horizontal bar. The bar is divided into three regions on the same baseline. On the left side, place a pair of compact secondary button controls sitting side by side (such as a labeled "Open app" button followed by a labeled "More" dropdown button with a trailing up-down caret icon). In the horizontal center of the bar, place a brand mark composed of a small logo icon paired with the brand name to its right on the same baseline. On the right side, place a horizontal row of utility controls on the same baseline: a small icon-only grid toggle, a small icon-only notification bell, a region selector composed of a location label and a trailing dropdown chevron, and a user identity block composed of a small circular avatar paired with the user's name and a small role badge in parentheses.

**Sizing rules.** The navbar spans the full viewport width edge to edge with no surrounding page padding and no enclosing max-width container around the bars themselves. Do not generate any main content area or placeholder blocks below the navbar; only output the navbar code. Every visible action button inside the navbar (primary, secondary outlined, dashed, and any inline composite action button with a label) shares one sizing rule: 12 pixels of horizontal padding on each side, 6 pixels of vertical padding on top and bottom, label text at 12 pixels in a medium font weight, and any small leading or trailing icon aligned to the label's vertical center. This button sizing rule does not apply to icon-only utility buttons, to text-only navigation links, or to user-identity buttons. Colors, borders, surfaces, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

On narrow viewports the top utility bar may condense or hide behind a toggle; the primary navbar compresses to essential elements with the brand mark remaining visible; the left button pair and right utility group collapse behind a menu toggle; the user block reduces to avatar-only. Preserve reading order throughout.

items.name: Filterable Management Data Table
items.promptText:
Create an application data table as a self-contained component inside a surface card container with 12 pixels of corner radius using the medium (md) radius token, background set to the host design system's primary surface color, an optional 1 pixel default border, and optional subtle elevation shadow. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, or breadcrumb chrome; only output the table component code.

**Page title row.** At the top, place a bold page title on the left (such as "All items"). On the right, grouped on the same baseline, place two secondary outlined buttons: one with a list icon and a view-mode label, and one with an export icon and an export label.

**Search and filter bar.** Below the title row, place a horizontal control bar. On the left, place a wide search input with placeholder text (no separate search submit button). Continuing on the same row, place a filter dropdown button with a funnel icon, a configurations button with a gear icon, and a compact primary "Add item" button anchored to the far right.

**Status radio filter row.** Directly above the table, place a horizontal "Show only:" label followed by a row of radio-style filter options (such as All, Active items, Pending items, Inactive items) sitting side by side on the same baseline with one option visually selected.

**Table header row.** The table header row contains column labels for: item; category; brand; price with a sort icon; stock with a sort icon; total sales with a sort icon; status; and an empty actions column.

**Table body rows.** Each body row is separated by a thin horizontal divider. The item cell pairs a small placeholder image icon with the item name. Category and brand cells show plain text. Price, stock, and total sales cells show formatted numeric values. The status cell holds a pill badge with a short status label (such as active, inactive, or suspended). The actions cell holds a small icon-only vertical ellipsis button.

**Sample data rule.** Populate the table body with exactly ten sample rows of realistic placeholder data. Vary item names, brands, prices, stock counts, sales totals, and status badges across rows.

**Row actions menu rule.** The vertical ellipsis trigger in each row must open a workable dropdown menu anchored to the trigger. The menu lists exactly three items in this order: Archive item, Edit item, and Delete item. Each item shows a leading icon on the same baseline as its label; Delete item uses destructive text and icon coloring per the design system.

**Action dots trigger rule.** Icon-only ellipsis triggers (vertical or horizontal three-dot buttons) must be exactly 36px wide and 36px tall, with the dots icon centered vertically and horizontally inside the button, and md border-radius (12px per radius.md) on the trigger surface.

**Row actions dropdown styling rule.** Style the menu per the design-system dropdown specs: the menu container uses neutral-primary-soft background, a 1px border-default border, shadow-lg, md radius (12px per radius.md), and 8px padding on all sides. Each menu item is a full-width inline-flex nav row with 8px padding on all sides and md radius (12px per radius.md); use 14px medium body text, a 16×16px leading icon, and an 8px gap between icon and label. Item hover state uses neutral-tertiary-medium background and heading text color.

Clicking the trigger toggles the menu; clicking outside or pressing Escape closes it. Selecting any item closes the menu and executes that row action.

**Footer summary bar.** Below the table body, place a footer bar split into two regions. On the left, show two inline summary metrics as label–value pairs (such as purchase price and total selling price, each value in a heavier weight). On the right, place text-style action links (such as "Print" and "Duplicate") followed by a compact primary "Export CSV" button.

**Interaction behavior.** Radio filters narrow visible rows by status. Sortable column headers toggle sort direction on click. The row ellipsis opens the Archive item, Edit item, and Delete item menu described above.

**Sizing and typography rules.** Use tabular numerals for all numeric and currency values. Colors, borders, and hover or focus states stay agnostic and follow the host design system.

**Button padding rule.** Every button uses padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px.

**Group button rule.** Segmented button groups — pagination controls (previous, numbered pages, next) and similar connected control strips — must share the same height and the same internal padding on every button in the group. Separate inline button clusters (such as Edit and Delete side by side) are not segmented groups; keep those as inline-flex siblings with normal spacing between them.

**Input padding rule.** Every search, text, number, and date input uses padding-left 10px, padding-right 10px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. Toggle switches, checkboxes, and radio buttons are exempt.

**Single-line cell rule.** Table body cell (`td`) text must stay on one line — apply `white-space: nowrap` (or equivalent such as `whitespace-nowrap`) so cell content does not wrap to two rows; truncate with ellipsis when horizontal space is tight.

items.name: Grouped Item Comparison Table

**Single-line cell rule.** Table body cell (`td`) text must stay on one line — apply `white-space: nowrap` (or equivalent such as `whitespace-nowrap`) so cell content does not wrap to two rows; truncate with ellipsis when horizontal space is tight. items.name: Checklist Date Range Drawer
items.promptText: Create a self-contained off-canvas drawer triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its drawer panel so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Show drawer") that opens the drawer. **Drawer shell.** A fixed panel pinned to the start (inline-start) edge of the viewport, spanning the full viewport height, on a high stacking layer. It slides in horizontally from off-canvas and rests against the start edge with a 384-pixel width, 16 pixels of internal padding, the primary surface background, a thin border on its end (inline-end) edge, and its own vertical scroll when content overflows. The panel is a flex column so its footer can sink to the bottom. **Header.** A top row that spreads its two items with space between them — the drawer title on the start edge and the close button on the end edge, both in the normal flow and vertically centered with each other on the same baseline — separated from the body by a thin bottom divider with 20 pixels of padding below the header content and 20 pixels of margin beneath the divider. On the start (left) edge, a short drawer title (such as "New item") in a medium weight and the body text color. A 36-by-36-pixel icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) sits at the end (right) of that same row in the normal flow — never absolutely positioned — so it stays vertically centered with the title rather than dropping below it. **Body.** A two-column grid with 16 pixels of gap. Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk and put each label 10 pixels above its control in a small text size and medium weight using the heading color. In order: - A project-name text input spanning both columns. - A category-style single-select spanning both columns. - An add-team-member text input spanning both columns. - A numeric budget input and a beneficiary text input, each a single column. - A tags text input spanning both columns whose label is a full-width row with the label text (and an inline muted "(optional)" note) on the start edge and an extra-small muted counter (such as "12 tags remaining") on the end edge. - A date-range row spanning both columns: two equal date inputs side by side with 16 pixels between them, each with a small leading calendar glyph (reserving 36 pixels of start padding) and its own start/due label. - A full-width to-do subsection enclosed by thin top and bottom dividers with 24 pixels of vertical padding inside and 8 pixels of vertical margin outside: a label, then a checklist of rows separated by 16 pixels (each row a 16-by-16-pixel checkbox nudged to align with the first text line, beside a small-size label in the body color 8 pixels to its end) with 24 pixels of space below the list, then a full-width outlined "Add new task" button with a small leading plus glyph. - A full-width upload-attachments dropzone (a 192-pixel-tall dashed-border drop area on the filled field surface, centered content with a 32-by-32-pixel upload glyph, a small-size instruction line, an extra-small max-file-size hint with the value emphasized, and a compact primary "Browse file" button with a small leading search glyph, paired with a hidden native file input), with a small extra-small helper line beneath it. - A full-width multi-line description textarea (about four rows). **Label wrapping rule.** Each checklist label stays on a single line and never wraps, truncating with an ellipsis if it would overflow, so every row stays one line tall and the checkboxes align. **Footer.** Pushed to the bottom of the panel above a thin top divider with 20 pixels of space above and below the footer content, a horizontal action row with 16 pixels between its buttons: a primary submit button carrying a small leading plus icon (such as "Add item") followed by a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close"). **Sizing rules.** The panel stays fixed at its 384-pixel width. The dropzone, checklist controls, date inputs, glyphs, surfaces, borders, dashed outlines, dividers, focus rings, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** The trigger, submit, dismiss, and "Add new task" buttons use padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the dropzone "Browse file" button uses padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Input padding rule.** Standard text, numeric, and select fields use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; the date inputs reserve 36px of start padding for the leading calendar glyph and 12px of end padding; the textarea uses 14px of padding on all sides. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control (text, numeric, select, and date inputs, the textarea, the dropzone drop area, and the checkbox backgrounds) with a filled host secondary/muted neutral surface that reads as a clearly bounded, slightly contrasting field against the drawer's primary surface (not a faint tint), and keep the host default border (or dashed border for the dropzone) and focus ring. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the panel grows toward the full available width, the grid collapses to a single column in reading order, the date-range pair stacks, the dropzone and checklist span full width, and the footer keeps its actions inline or stacks them in primary-then-dismiss order.

Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk and put each label 10 pixels above its control in a small text size and medium weight using the heading color. - **Left column** spans two of the three columns from the medium breakpoint up and stacks its fields with 16 pixels of space: a primary name text input; a multi-line description textarea (about four rows); a full-width image upload dropzone (a 192-pixel-tall dashed-border drop area on the filled field surface, centered content with a 32-by-32-pixel upload glyph, a small-size instruction line, an extra-small max-file-size hint with the value emphasized, and a compact primary "Browse file" button with a small leading search glyph, paired with a hidden native file input); and a selling-type subsection rendered as a responsive row (stacked on mobile, side by side from the small breakpoint up) of two selectable option cards. Each card is a full-width bordered tile on the filled field surface holding, with 16 pixels of inner padding, a 28-by-28-pixel glyph above a title in a small text size and medium weight and a muted supporting description in a small size, with a 16-by-16-pixel radio pinned toward the top-end corner (16 pixels from the top and end), the two cards behaving as one single-choice group. - **Right column** stacks its fields with 16 pixels of space: a brand-style text input, a category-style single-select, a numeric price input, four icon-prefixed numeric dimension fields (such as weight, length, breadth, and width; each reserves 36 pixels of start padding for its leading glyph and 12 pixels of end padding), and an image-copyright subsection of two inline radio options (16-by-16-pixel radios with labels 8 pixels to their end in a small text size and medium weight). **Label wrapping rule.** Each inline radio option label stays on a single line and never wraps (truncating with an ellipsis on overflow); option-card titles and multi-line descriptions are exempt. **Footer.** Pushed to the bottom of the panel above a thin top divider with 20 pixels of space above and below the footer content, a horizontal action row with 16 pixels between its buttons: a primary submit button carrying a small leading plus icon (such as "Add item") followed by a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close"). **Sizing rules.** The panel stays bounded to its 672-pixel maximum. Option cards share equal sizing and a consistent selected treatment; the dropzone, glyphs, radios, surfaces, borders, dashed outlines, focus rings, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** The trigger, submit, and dismiss buttons use padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the dropzone "Browse file" button uses padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Input padding rule.** Standard text, numeric, and select fields use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; icon-prefixed inputs reserve 36px of start padding for the leading glyph and 12px of end padding; the textarea uses 14px of padding on all sides. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control (text, numeric, icon-prefixed inputs, the select, the textarea, the dropzone drop area, and the option cards) with a filled host secondary/muted neutral surface that reads as a clearly bounded, slightly contrasting field against the drawer's primary surface (not a faint tint), and keep the host default border (or dashed border for the dropzone) and focus ring. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the panel grows toward the full available width, the columns collapse into one in reading order (left column first), the option cards stack, the dimension fields stack, and the footer keeps its actions inline or stacks them in primary-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Radio Select Card Drawer
items.promptText: Create a self-contained off-canvas drawer triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its drawer panel so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Show drawer") that opens the drawer. **Drawer shell.** A fixed panel pinned to the start (inline-start) edge of the viewport, spanning the full viewport height, on a high stacking layer. It slides in horizontally from off-canvas and rests against the start edge, constrained to a maximum width of 672 pixels, with 16 pixels of internal padding, the primary surface background, a thin border on its end (inline-end) edge, and its own vertical scroll when content overflows. The panel is a flex column so its footer can sink to the bottom. **Header.** A top row that spreads its two items with space between them — the drawer title on the start edge and the close button on the end edge, both in the normal flow and vertically centered with each other on the same baseline — separated from the body by a thin bottom divider with 20 pixels of padding below the header content and 20 pixels of margin beneath the divider. On the start (left) edge, a short drawer title (such as "New item") in a medium weight and the body text color. A 36-by-36-pixel icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) sits at the end (right) of that same row in the normal flow — never absolutely positioned — so it stays vertically centered with the title rather than dropping below it. **Body.** A grid that is one column on mobile, two columns from the small breakpoint up, and three columns from the medium breakpoint up, with 16 pixels of gap. Mark required fields with a small danger-colored asterisk and put each label 10 pixels above its control in a small text size and medium weight using the heading color. - **Left column** stacks its fields with 16 pixels of space: an icon-prefixed full-name text input, an icon-prefixed email input, an icon-prefixed username input, then a phone-number composite, a country single-select, an account-type single-select, an icon-prefixed password input, and an icon-prefixed confirm-password input. Every icon-prefixed input reserves 36 pixels of start padding for its leading glyph and 12 pixels of end padding. The phone-number composite is a single attached group: a country-code trigger button on the start edge (a small leading flag, a dial code such as "+1", and a trailing chevron) joined to a patterned phone input that fills the remaining width; the trigger opens a floating menu (about 216 pixels wide) listing countries, each row a small flag beside a country name and dial code. - **Right column** spans two of the three columns from the medium breakpoint up and stacks its fields with 16 pixels of space: an upload-profile-picture row (a 64-by-64-pixel rounded avatar thumbnail beside a native file input with a small extra-small helper line beneath it); a user-role subsection rendered as a responsive row (stacked on mobile, side by side from the small breakpoint up) of two selectable option cards, each a full-width bordered tile on the filled field surface with 16 pixels of inner padding holding a 28-by-28-pixel glyph above a title (small text, medium weight) and a muted small-size description, with a 16-by-16-pixel radio pinned 16 pixels from the top and end and the two cards behaving as one single-choice group; a biography rich text editor (a bordered surface on the filled field surface whose top toolbar holds grouped icon-only formatting buttons separated by thin dividers plus a trailing full-screen toggle with a tooltip, above a multi-line textarea of about eight rows); and a status subsection of four inline radio options (16-by-16-pixel radios with labels 8 pixels to their end in a small text size and medium weight). **Label wrapping rule.** Each inline radio option label and each country menu row stays on a single line and never wraps (truncating with an ellipsis on overflow); option-card titles and multi-line descriptions are exempt. **Footer.** Pushed to the bottom of the panel above a thin top divider with 20 pixels of space above and below the footer content, a horizontal action row with 16 pixels between its buttons: a primary submit button carrying a small leading plus icon (such as "Add item") followed by a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close"). **Sizing rules.** The panel stays bounded to its 672-pixel maximum. Option cards share equal sizing and a consistent selected treatment; the avatar, country menu, editor toolbar, glyphs, radios, surfaces, borders, focus rings, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system. **Button padding rule.** The trigger, submit, dismiss, and country-code trigger buttons use padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. This does not apply to icon-only buttons (close and the editor toolbar). **Input padding rule.** Plain selects use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; icon-prefixed inputs reserve 36px of start padding for the leading glyph and 12px of end padding; the phone input and editor textarea use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control (icon-prefixed inputs, the phone composite trigger and input, selects, the file input, the editor surface and its textarea, and the option cards) with a filled host secondary/muted neutral surface that reads as a clearly bounded, slightly contrasting field against the drawer's primary surface (not a faint tint), and keep the host default border and focus ring. The floating country menu sits on an elevated surface a step lighter than the panel. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the panel grows toward the full available width, the columns collapse into one in reading order (left column first), the phone composite keeps its country trigger attached, the option cards stack, the editor toolbar wraps, the avatar row stacks thumbnail above input, and the footer keeps its actions inline or stacks them in primary-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Dimension Dropzone Form Drawer
items.promptText: Create a self-contained off-canvas drawer triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its drawer panel so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Show drawer") that opens the drawer. **Drawer shell.** A fixed panel pinned to the start (inline-start) edge of the viewport, spanning the full viewport height, on a high stacking layer. It slides in horizontally from off-canvas and rests against the start edge with a 320-pixel width, 16 pixels of internal padding, the primary surface background, a thin border on its end (inline-end) edge, and its own vertical scroll when content overflows. The panel is a flex column so its footer can sink to the bottom. **Header.** A top row that spreads its two items with space between them — the drawer title on the start edge and the close button on the end edge, both in the normal flow and vertically centered with each other on the same baseline — separated from the body by a thin bottom divider with 20 pixels of padding below the header content and 20 pixels of margin beneath the divider. On the start (left) edge, a short drawer title (such as "New item") in a medium weight and the body text color. A 36-by-36-pixel icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) sits at the end (right) of that same row in the normal flow — never absolutely positioned — so it stays vertically centered with the title rather than dropping below it. **Body.** A two-column grid with 16 pixels of gap. Mark every required field with a small danger-colored asterisk beside its label, and place each label 10 pixels above its control in a small text size and medium weight using the heading color. In order: - A primary name text input, a brand-style text input, a numeric price input, and a category-style single-select, each spanning both columns (full width). - Four single-column dimension fields (such as weight, length, breadth, and width), each a numeric input with a small leading glyph inside the field on the start edge; the input reserves 36 pixels of start padding for the icon and 12 pixels of end padding. - A full-width multi-line description textarea (about four rows). - A full-width image upload dropzone: a 192-pixel-tall dashed-border drop area on the same filled field surface, centered content with a 32-by-32-pixel upload glyph above a short instruction line in a small text size, a max-file-size hint in an extra-small size with the size value emphasized, and a compact primary "Browse file" button carrying a small leading search glyph, paired with a visually hidden native file input. - A full-width selling-type subsection: a label above a wrap-friendly horizontal row (16-pixel gap) of three inline radio options, each a 16-by-16-pixel radio with its label 8 pixels to its end in a small text size and medium weight. **Label wrapping rule.** Each radio option label stays on a single line and never wraps; truncate with an ellipsis if it would overflow so every option row stays one line tall. **Footer.** Pushed to the bottom of the panel above a thin top divider with 20 pixels of space above and below the footer content, a horizontal action row with 16 pixels between its buttons: a primary submit button carrying a small leading plus icon (such as "Add item") followed by a secondary outlined dismiss button (such as "Close"). **Sizing rules.** The panel stays fixed at its 320-pixel width. The dropzone, icon glyphs, radios, surfaces, borders, dashed outlines, focus rings, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system; the required asterisk uses a host danger token. **Button padding rule.** The trigger, submit, and dismiss buttons use padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px; the dropzone "Browse file" button uses padding-left 12px, padding-right 12px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Input padding rule.** Standard text, numeric, and select fields use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; icon-prefixed inputs reserve 36px of start padding for the leading glyph and 12px of end padding; the textarea uses 14px of padding on all sides. **Select chevron padding rule.** Every single-select dropdown keeps at least 12 pixels of padding on its end (right) side so the dropdown chevron is never glued to the field's border; preserve that 12-pixel gap between the chevron and the edge and give the selected text enough trailing room that the value never sits beneath the chevron. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control (text, numeric, icon-prefixed inputs, the select, the textarea, and the dropzone drop area) with a filled host secondary/muted neutral surface that reads as a clearly bounded, slightly contrasting field against the drawer's primary surface (not a faint tint), and keep the host default border (or dashed border for the dropzone) and focus ring. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the panel grows toward the full available width, the two-column grid collapses so the dimension fields stack in reading order, the dropzone and radio row span full width, and the footer keeps its actions inline or stacks them in primary-then-dismiss order.

items.name: Advanced Range Filter Drawer
items.promptText: Create a self-contained off-canvas drawer triggered by a single action button. Do not generate any surrounding page shell, sidebar, navbar, breadcrumb chrome, or adjacent content; output only the trigger button and its drawer panel so the component can be dropped into any host screen. **Trigger.** A single horizontally centered primary action button (such as "Show drawer") that opens the drawer. **Drawer shell.** A fixed panel pinned to the start (inline-start) edge of the viewport, spanning the full viewport height, on a high stacking layer. It slides in horizontally from off-canvas and rests against the start edge, constrained to a maximum width of 512 pixels, with 16 pixels of internal padding, the primary surface background, a thin border on its end (inline-end) edge, and its own vertical scroll when content overflows. The panel is a flex column so its footer can sink to the bottom. **Header.** A top row that spreads its two items with space between them — the drawer title on the start edge and the close button on the end edge, both in the normal flow and vertically centered with each other on the same baseline — separated from the body by a thin bottom divider with 20 pixels of padding below the header content and 20 pixels of margin beneath the divider. On the start (left) edge, a short drawer title (such as "Filters") in a medium weight and the body text color. A 36-by-36-pixel icon-only close button (X glyph with accessible label) sits at the end (right) of that same row in the normal flow — never absolutely positioned — so it stays vertically centered with the title rather than dropping below it. **Body.** A vertical sequence of filter sections, each separated by 20 pixels of space, with every section heading in a small text size and medium weight using the heading color sitting 10 pixels above its controls: - A two-column grid (16-pixel gap) of two text inputs (such as a brand input and a model input), each with a required danger-colored asterisk in its label. - A manufacture-year date range: a heading above two date inputs side by side with 16 pixels between them, each with a small leading calendar glyph (reserving 36 pixels of start padding). - A price-range subsection: a label above a dual-handle range slider on a thin 6-pixel-tall rounded track (a muted track with a brand-colored filled segment between two round 20-pixel handles, each with a 2-pixel light ring and a soft shadow), set 20 pixels below the label and 8 pixels above what follows, then 24 pixels of space between the slider and a "from"/"to" pair of text inputs sitting side by side with 12 pixels between them. - A condition subsection: a heading above a horizontal segmented radio list — a single bordered, rounded container split into equal cells divided by inner borders (stacking vertically below the small breakpoint), each cell a 16-by-16-pixel radio beside a full-width small-size medium-weight label with 12 pixels of vertical padding. - A two-column grid (24-pixel gap) holding a color radio list and a rating radio list, each column's rows spaced 14 pixels apart: color rows lead with a 10-by-10-pixel round color dot (6 pixels before the name); rating rows show five star glyphs (about 18 pixels each, 2 pixels apart) in filled and muted states. - A delivery subsection: a heading above a grid of selectable radio option cards (one column on mobile, two from the medium breakpoint up, 16-pixel gap), each a full-width bordered tile with 20 pixels of padding holding a medium-weight title above a small-size supporting line, the selected card adopting a host brand-tinted surface, border, and foreground. **Label wrapping rule.** Each radio, condition, and color label stays on a single line and never wraps (truncating with an ellipsis on overflow) so every row stays one line tall and the controls align; option-card titles and descriptions are exempt. **Footer.** Pushed to the bottom of the panel above a thin top divider with 20 pixels of space above and below the footer content, a horizontal action row with 16 pixels between its buttons where both stretch to equal full width: a secondary outlined reset button (such as "Clear all") followed by a primary apply button (such as "Show results"). **Sizing rules.** The panel stays bounded to its 512-pixel maximum. The range slider track/fill/handles, segmented condition list, checkbox and radio controls, color dots, star glyphs, option-card selected states, date inputs, surfaces, borders, focus rings, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system; brand and rating accents come from host tokens. **Button padding rule.** The trigger and both footer buttons use padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. This does not apply to the icon-only close button. **Input padding rule.** Standard text and numeric inputs use 12px horizontal and 10px vertical padding; the date inputs reserve 36px of start padding for the leading calendar glyph and 12px of end padding. **Input surface rule.** Fill every field control (text, numeric, and date inputs and the checkbox/radio backgrounds) with a filled host secondary/muted neutral surface that reads as a clearly bounded, slightly contrasting field against the drawer's primary surface (not a faint tint), and keep the host default border and focus ring. **Mobile layout rule.** On narrow viewports the panel grows toward the full available width, the two-column grids collapse to one column in reading order, the date-range and from/to pairs stack, the segmented condition list stacks its cells, the delivery cards stack, and the footer keeps its two full-width actions inline or stacks them in reset-then-apply order.

items.name: Centered Login Card Page
items.promptText: Create a login page as one centered vertical stack on a full-page background. At the very top, place a small brand mark composed of a circular logo glyph followed by a short brand wordmark, both centered horizontally on the page. Below the brand mark, place one centered form card with rounded corners and a moderate max width. Inside the card, stack from top to bottom: a card heading on its own line; a labeled email input row (the label sits above the input on its own line and pairs a short label text with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label; the input includes a small leading icon glyph inside the field); a labeled password input row in the same shape directly below (also carrying a small leading icon glyph inside the field); a single horizontal row composed of a small square "remember me" checkbox paired with an inline label on the left and a "forgot password" text link on the right; one full-width primary submit button beneath the checkbox row; finally, a small centered helper line containing a short prompt sentence followed by an inline text link to the sign-up flow. Treat the area outside the card as a subtle decorative field (for example a sparse dot or grid pattern). On narrow viewports keep the same single-column stack inside the card and let the card occupy the full content width with comfortable side padding.

items.name: Two-Column Login With Decorative Panel
items.promptText:
Create a login page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a heading on its own line; a two-column field grid where the first column holds a labeled email input and the second column holds a labeled password input on the same row (every label sits above its input on its own line with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text); a single horizontal row composed of a small square "remember me" checkbox paired with an inline label on the left and a "forgot password" text link on the right; one full-width primary submit button beneath the checkbox row; a small helper line containing a short prompt sentence followed by an inline text link to the sign-up flow; a horizontal "or" separator made of a thin rule, a centered short word, and another thin rule; a horizontal row of two equal-width third-party provider buttons sitting side by side (each button carries a small leading provider glyph and a short provider label).

The **right column** holds a single rounded decorative panel vertically centered relative to the form column. Inside the panel, arrange a loose decorative cluster of small circular technology glyphs distributed in a soft arc-style composition (no single rigid grid), then under the cluster center a short bold heading on its own line and a single short supporting paragraph centered beneath the heading.

On narrow viewports, stack with the form column first and the decorative panel second; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Centered Two-Factor Verification Page
items.promptText:
Create a two-factor authentication page as one centered vertical stack on a full-width section background, vertically centered within the viewport height. Stack from top to bottom: a small brand icon or logo mark centered horizontally on its own line; a brand name label centered on its own line directly below the icon; a large bold centered heading on its own line directly below the brand name stating the purpose of the page (e.g. "Two-factor authentication"); a centered paragraph of one or two sentences directly below the heading at a comfortable reading width, instructing the user to open their authenticator app to view the code and verify their identity; a labeled field group placed below the paragraph after extra vertical space, composed of a short left-aligned label on its own line (e.g. "Enter verification code") above a horizontal row of six equally sized square single-character numeric input fields on the same baseline (each field is a real input element that accepts exactly one digit, auto-advances focus to the next field on entry, supports backspace to move focus back to the previous field, and the currently focused field displays a visible focus ring or cursor indicator); a short helper line directly below the input row at a subdued weight explaining where the code was sent; one primary action button placed below the helper text on its own line, composed of a small leading checkmark icon paired with a short label (e.g. "Verify").

On narrow viewports keep the same single-column centered stack with comfortable side padding; allow the six input fields to scale slightly while preserving center alignment throughout.

items.name: Split Marketing Login Page
items.promptText:
Create a login page split into two columns on large 1280px width breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. The left column is a marketing column carrying copy and a short feature list; the right column is the form column. The two columns share the same vertical center line.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large multi-line heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph below the heading at a comfortable reading width; a vertical list of about three feature rows each composed of a small leading icon at the left, a bold one-line title to the right of the icon on the same baseline, and a short supporting line directly beneath the title that sits flush-left under the icon-and-title row.

The **right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a heading on its own line; a horizontal row of two equal third-party provider buttons sitting side by side (each button carries a small leading provider glyph and a short provider label); a horizontal "or" separator made of a thin rule, a centered short word, and another thin rule; a two-column field grid containing two labeled inputs on one row (email input on the left and password input on the right) — every label sits above its input with a tiny required-field marker to the right of the label text; a single horizontal row composed of a small square "remember me" checkbox paired with an inline label on the left and a "forgot password" text link on the right; one full-width primary submit button beneath the checkbox row; finally a small helper line containing a short prompt sentence followed by an inline text link to the sign-up flow.

On narrow viewports, stack with the form column first and the marketing column second so the user reaches the form quickly; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Two-Column Social Proof Narrative With Stats Row
items.promptText:
Create a social proof section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a two-column layout on large 1280px width breakpoints.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large left-aligned multi-line heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width.

The **right column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing multiple body paragraphs stacked vertically with consistent spacing between them, providing extended narrative or descriptive copy.

Below the two-column block, after generous vertical space, place a single horizontal row of four stat blocks spanning the full container width on the same baseline with consistent spacing between them. Each stat block is a centered vertical stack composed of one large prominent numeric value on its own line at the top and a short descriptive label directly beneath the value.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically in reading order with the heading column first and the narrative column second; the stat row collapses into a two-column grid preserving left-to-right top-to-bottom reading order.

items.name: Filter Toolbar With Carousel Product Cards
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce product-listing section: a multi-row filter toolbar panel (with dropdown filters, an info modal, a seller filter, an order-by control, a list/grid view toggle, and an installments alert) over a grid of product cards (each with an image carousel, title, description, installments link, price, color swatches, and wishlist/buy-now buttons), and a pagination control. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on a soft secondary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (48 from the medium breakpoint up); centered in a ~1280-pixel max-width container with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Toolbar panel.** A host-rounded, bordered, small-shadowed container on the host primary surface with 16 pixels of padding (24 from the medium breakpoint up) and 16 pixels below it, its rows separated by horizontal divider rules: - **Title row** (16 pixels of bottom padding, ends split from the medium breakpoint up): a ~20px semibold heading-color title with a trailing ~18px medium muted count ("Electronics - Top Products 298 products") and an **info button** — a host-rounded ~14px medium muted row (8px padding, neutral hover) with a leading 16-by-16-pixel info glyph and the text "How the results are ordered" — that opens an **info modal**: a hidden, centered, ~576-pixel-max-width host-rounded panel on the host primary surface with a bordered header (a semibold heading-color title and an X close glyph), a ~14px muted intro paragraph, a disc bullet list of six sort-type explanations (each lead term in medium heading-color: Most Popular, Ascending Price, Descending Price, No. Reviews, Discount%, Newest), and a bordered footer with a brand "I understand" button. - **Dropdown-filters row** (16 pixels of vertical padding, becoming a flex row from the large breakpoint up): on the start, a 16-pixel-gap cluster (2-column grid below the medium breakpoint) of four bordered neutral dropdown buttons — "Brands", "Price", "Rating", and "Shipping to: Americas" — each with a leading 16-by-16-pixel funnel glyph and a trailing 16-by-16-pixel down chevron, each opening a hidden host-rounded panel: Brands (~192px wide, brand checkbox rows each with a trailing count, plus a brand "See all 1,011 results" button), Price (~192px wide, price-range checkbox rows, plus a "See all 100 results" button), Rating (~224px wide, star-row checkbox rows with counts, plus a results button), and Shipping (~288px wide, a stack of selectable region cards plus a results button). On the end, a non-shrinking **Seller** group laid out as a single horizontal, vertically-centered row from the small breakpoint up — a ~16px medium "Seller:" caption on the same line as (not stacked above) a wrapped 12-pixel-gap row of three checkbox options ("Flowbite", "BestBuy", "Amazon"), separated from the caption by a 16-pixel gap. - **Order-by row** (16 pixels of top padding): a row whose ends split from the medium breakpoint up — on the start, a ~16px medium "Order by:" caption and a wrapped 12-pixel-gap row of four radio options ("Newest", "Increasing price", "Decreasing price", "Most popular"); on the end (shown from the medium breakpoint up), a **view toggle** — a bordered host-rounded group with 4 pixels of padding holding two icon-only buttons (a 20-by-20-pixel list glyph and a 20-by-20-pixel grid glyph, neutral hover, each with a tooltip). Beneath the row, a full-width **installments alert** — a host-rounded bar in a soft brand tint with 16 pixels of padding, ~14px brand text, a leading 24-by-24-pixel glyph (shown from the medium breakpoint up), and inline underlined links ("FlowWallet", "how it works"). **Product grid.** A 16-pixel-gap grid: one column by default, two from the small breakpoint up, three from the large. Each cell is a **product card** — a 16-pixel-spaced, 24-pixel-padded, host-rounded panel on the host primary surface with a thin border and small shadow: - A **carousel**: a full-width region with a 16-pixel-bottom, ~288-pixel-tall, host-rounded overflow-clipped frame in which each slide holds a centered, full-height **real product photograph**; one slide is active by default. Beneath it, a centered 16-pixel-gap controls row: a ghost previous button (6 pixels of padding, a 28-by-28-pixel arrow), a ~16px medium muted "1 of 4" counter, and a ghost next button (28-by-28-pixel arrow). - A text block: a ~18px semibold heading-color title link (underlining on hover, e.g. "Apple iMac 27\"") and a ~16px normal muted description 8 pixels below. - An **installments link**: an 8-pixel-gap row of a 16-by-16-pixel glyph and ~14px medium brand-foreground text ("Buy in installments with Flowbite Wallet"), underlining on hover. - A **price-and-swatches row** with split ends and a 16-pixel gap: a ~24px extrabold heading-color price ("$1199") and, on the end, an 8-pixel-gap cluster of round color swatches (each a ~28-pixel circle as a hidden radio with a thin token border, showing a ring when checked). - An **action row** with a 16-pixel gap: a bordered neutral **Wishlist** button (full-width, leading 20-by-20-pixel heart glyph) and a brand **Buy now** button (full-width, solid brand surface, inverse text, leading 20-by-20-pixel cart glyph), both with 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium, and focus rings. Provide six cards (e.g. iMac 27" $1199, PlayStation 5 Slim $499, iPad Pro $1199, Xbox Series S $499, iPhone 15 Pro Max $1299, iMac 24" $1999) with their own descriptions and swatch sets. **Pagination.** Below the grid, the same centered nav as variant 2: a host-rounded group of 32-pixel-tall ~14px cells with collapsed adjacent borders — a "Previous" cell with a 16-by-16-pixel chevron, numbered page cells ("1", "2", an active "3" in a soft brand tint, "…", "100"), and a "Next" cell with a 16-by-16-pixel chevron. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The toolbar panel and its dividers, dropdown buttons and panels, info button/modal, seller and order-by controls, view toggle, installments alert, product cards, carousels and their controls, installments links, prices, color swatches, wishlist/buy-now buttons, and pagination must all use the host design system's components/tokens (surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, brand/heading/muted text, amber rating stamp, soft brand tint, hover/focus states). Treat every product image as a real photographic asset, not an illustration. Pixel values define only spacing, sizing, and layout rhythm.

items.name: Invoice Paid Receipt Card
items.promptText: Create a self-contained payment-receipt ("invoice paid") screen: a brand mark, a centered light receipt card, and a footer, all sitting on a dark full-page surface. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width, full-height band on a host dark/inverse surface, vertically and horizontally centering a single ~420-pixel-max-width column with 16 pixels of horizontal padding and generous vertical padding. The column stacks a brand mark, the receipt card, and a footer. **Brand mark.** Aligned to the start of the column, a 8-pixel-gapped row of a small (~24-pixel) brand logo glyph and a ~16px medium inverse-foreground wordmark ("TypeUI"). **Receipt card.** A block 24 pixels below the brand mark: a host-rounded card on the host primary (light) surface with a soft shadow and ~32 pixels of padding, its content centered. Top to bottom: - A centered **status icon** — a ~48-pixel muted line-art invoice/document glyph with a small success-color circular check badge overlapping its bottom-end corner. - A ~14px muted "Invoice paid" label 12 pixels beneath it. - A ~36px bold heading-color **amount** ("$72.60"). - A **"View invoice and payment details"** link — a ~14px muted text row with a trailing small chevron, centered, that darkens/underlines on hover. - A **details list** 24 pixels below, with split rows (each a justify-between, 16-pixel-gapped pair with ~4 pixels of vertical padding) whose left side is a ~14px muted term and whose right side is an end-aligned ~14px heading-color value: "Charge amount" / "RON 339.15" (the value semibold), "Invoice number" / "YSTQHIKL-0001", "Payment date" / "May 19, 2026", "Payment method" / "Visa •••• 4634" (the brand name followed by masking dots and the last four digits). - A **button pair** 24 pixels below: a two-up, equal-width, 12-pixel-gapped row of a secondary **"Download invoice"** button (bordered, on the host primary surface, host-rounded corners, ~10px vertical padding, a ~14px medium heading-color label, a subtle hover) and a primary **"Download receipt"** button (a solid dark/inverse fill with an inverse ~14px medium label, the same rounding and padding, and a darker hover). **Footer.** A block 24 pixels below the card, centered: a ~12px muted "Powered by" line ending in a payment-provider wordmark ("polar.sh", kept as its own conventional mark), then a 16-pixel-gapped row of ~12px muted "Terms" and "Privacy" links that underline on hover. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The dark page surface, brand mark, light receipt card (status icon and success badge, amount, details link, details rows, and both download buttons), and footer must all use the host design system's components/tokens (dark/inverse and primary/light surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, heading/muted/inverse text, success-color badge, hover/focus states). Keep the brand logo and the payment-provider wordmark as their own conventional marks. Pixel values define only spacing, sizing, and layout rhythm.

items.name: Alternating Three-Band CTA
items.promptText:
Create a CTA section composed of three separate vertical bands stacked with generous spacing between them, all inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. Each band is a two-column split on large 1280 px width breakpoints; alternate which side carries the illustration and which carries the text so the stacking pattern reads as illustration–text for the first band, text–illustration for the second band, and illustration–text for the third band.

In every **text column**, stack from top to bottom in this order: a large heading on its own line; one or two body paragraphs at a comfortable reading width directly beneath the heading; a vertical feature list where each item begins with a small leading icon at the left followed by either a single descriptive line to the right of the icon on the same baseline, or a bold title line on the same baseline as the icon with a short supporting line stacked directly beneath the title (choose one style per band and keep it consistent within that band); a closing sentence on its own line beneath the feature list; a horizontal row containing a solid primary button (the primary button may pair with a small trailing arrow or a small leading icon, varying per band) and a bordered secondary button to its right (the secondary button may pair with a small leading icon). The two buttons stay **side by side on one row** and never wrap to a second line (treat this as the global two-button row rule).

In every **illustration column**, place one vector or raster illustration sized to fill the column area comfortably, vertically centered relative to the adjacent text column.

On narrow viewports, stack each band's columns so that the illustration sits above the text in the first and third bands and below the text in the second band, preserving the alternating visual rhythm.

items.name: Promo Top Bar With Illustration And Actions
items.promptText: Create a self-contained, dismissible full-width promo bar that pins to the top of the viewport, pairing an illustration and message with a primary action and a close control. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this banner so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A fixed, top-pinned, full-width bar above page content (a high stacking order) on a soft brand-tinted surface with a thin brand-tinted bottom border, 16 pixels of horizontal padding, and 12 pixels of vertical padding (16 from the large breakpoint up). It is a row that splits its content cluster and a trailing close button to the start and end with a 32-pixel gap; parts top-align on mobile and vertically center from the small breakpoint up. **Content cluster.** A horizontally-centered (auto-margined) group that becomes a 16-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up; its contents are centered — both the cluster itself and the items inside each row are horizontally centered within the banner rather than packed to the start. It holds two parts: - A **message row** in a brand-toned color at ~14px (~16px from the medium breakpoint up), centered (its illustration and paragraph sit centered, not start-aligned), with 16 pixels beneath it on mobile (removed from the small breakpoint up): a leading **illustration** about 48 pixels tall with 16 pixels of end padding, then a paragraph that from the small breakpoint up gains a thin brand-tinted start divider and 16 pixels of start padding; the paragraph opens with a medium-weight lead span ("50% Off!"), an emoji, and supporting copy. - An **actions row** (vertically centered, non-shrinking from the small breakpoint up): a primary **"Shop Now" button** — full-width, a brand fill with a white ~12px medium label, host rounded corners, 12px horizontal / 8px vertical padding, a darker brand hover, and a brand focus ring — and, only below the small breakpoint, a secondary **"Close" button** styled like an input: a full-width bordered button on the host primary/neutral surface with a ~12px medium heading-color label, host rounded corners, the same 12px/8px padding, a subtle hover fill with brand-foreground hover text, and a focus ring. **Close button (icon).** A trailing icon button shown only from the small breakpoint up (hidden below it): host rounded corners, 6 pixels of padding, a brand-muted tone, and a brand-tinted hover fill that shifts the icon to the brand foreground, wrapping a 20-by-20-pixel filled X glyph (with a screen-reader "Close"/"Dismiss" label). **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The bar surface/border, the "Shop Now" primary button, the "Close" secondary button, and the close icon-button must reuse the host design system's predefined components/tokens (surfaces, borders, radii, hover/focus states, focus rings, brand/heading/muted colors) rather than ad-hoc values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Shop Now" and "Close" text buttons use 12px horizontal / 8px vertical padding with a ~12px medium label; the close icon-button uses 6 pixels of padding around a 20-by-20-pixel glyph. **Sizing rules.** The bar spans the full viewport width and the illustration is about 48 pixels tall. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; the bar padding, the 32-pixel outer gap, the 16-pixel cluster gap, the illustration/divider spacing, the button padding, and the 20-pixel close glyph are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** Below the small breakpoint the cluster stacks (message row over actions row), the message paragraph drops its start divider, and dismissal is the full-width "Close" text button; from the small breakpoint up the cluster becomes a single row, the paragraph gains its start divider, and dismissal moves to the trailing close icon-button.

items.name: Dismissible Top Bar Text Banner
items.promptText: Create a self-contained, dismissible full-width announcement bar that pins to the top of the viewport, holding a single centered promo line and a close button. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this banner so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A fixed, top-pinned, full-width bar above page content (a high stacking order) on a soft secondary surface with a thin default bottom border, 16 pixels of horizontal padding, and 12 pixels of vertical padding (16 from the large breakpoint up). It is a row that splits its two parts to the start and end with a 32-pixel gap; the parts align to the top on mobile and vertically center from the small breakpoint up. **Message.** A horizontally-centered (auto-margined) ~16px paragraph in the muted color: it opens with a medium-weight heading-color lead span ("Autumn Sale is Here!"), then an emoji and supporting copy, and ends with an inline medium heading-color link that is underlined by default and drops its underline on hover ("to shop!"). **Close button.** A trailing icon button — vertically-centered, host rounded corners, 6 pixels of padding, a muted ~14px tone, and a subtle neutral hover fill that shifts the icon to the heading color — wrapping a 20-by-20-pixel filled X glyph (with a screen-reader "Close"/"Dismiss" label). **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The bar surface, border, the message link, and the close icon-button must reuse the host design system's predefined components/tokens (surfaces, borders, radii, hover states, heading/muted text colors) rather than ad-hoc values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Sizing rules.** The bar spans the full viewport width. Type, surfaces, borders, and radii stay agnostic and follow the host design system; the 16px horizontal / 12–16px vertical padding, the 32-pixel gap, the 6-pixel button padding, and the 20-pixel close glyph are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** On mobile the two parts top-align (the message may wrap to multiple lines beside the close button); from the small breakpoint up they vertically center. The message stays horizontally centered within the bar at every width.

items.name: Social Icons And Centered Shipping Bar
items.promptText: Create a self-contained full-width utility bar on the host brand fill that places a row of social media icons at the start and a single centered, wide-tracked shipping message across the bar. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this banner so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width bar on the host brand fill (a solid accent surface) with about 16 pixels of horizontal padding and 12 pixels of vertical padding. It is a single vertically-centered row that spans the full width, with the social icons pinned to the start edge and the message optically centered across the whole bar (so the message reads centered regardless of the icon cluster on the start). **Social icons (start).** A start-pinned row of icon links with about 12–16 pixels between them, each a ~20-by-20-pixel glyph in the brand's on-fill contrast color (the light/white tone that reads against the bright bar) with a subtle opacity or tone shift on hover and a screen-reader label naming the network. Provide four: a Facebook, an Instagram, a TikTok, and a Pinterest icon link. **Shipping message (center).** A horizontally-centered, single-line label in the same on-fill contrast color: ~12px, medium/semibold weight, set in all caps with generous letter-spacing (wide tracking), such as "FREE EXPRESS SHIPPING ON ALL ORDERS OVER $100*". **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The bar's brand surface, the social icon links, and the message text must reuse the host design system's predefined brand fill and its on-fill contrast token (plus the host's hover state) rather than ad-hoc values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Sizing rules.** The bar spans the full viewport width and the social glyphs are about 20-by-20 pixels. The brand fill and on-fill text/icon color stay agnostic and follow the host design system; the ~16px horizontal / ~12px vertical padding, the ~12–16px icon gap, the ~12px uppercase wide-tracked type, and the icon size are the fixed values. **Mobile layout rule.** The social icon row stays pinned to the start at every width; on narrow viewports the centered message may sit closer to the icons (or truncate) but remains on a single line — the bar never wraps to a second row or stacks the two parts.

items.name: Floating Centered Announcement Banner
items.promptText: Create a self-contained, dismissible floating announcement card that pins near the top of the viewport, horizontally centered and capped to a comfortable width, pairing a badged icon and message with an inline link and a close control. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this banner so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A fixed wrapper pinned to the top and horizontally centered (left-half offset, translated back by half its own width), full width but capped at about 1024 pixels, with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up) and 16 pixels of vertical padding — so the card floats inset from the viewport edges rather than spanning them. **Banner card.** A relatively-positioned row (a high stacking order) on a soft brand-tinted surface with a thin brand-tinted border, host rounded corners, 16 pixels of horizontal padding, and 12 pixels of vertical padding (16 from the large breakpoint up); it splits a content cluster and a close button to the start and end with a 32-pixel gap, top-aligned on mobile and vertically centered from the small breakpoint up. **Content cluster.** A brand-toned group that becomes a 12-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up: - A **badged icon** — a non-shrinking 32-by-32-pixel tile on a brand-tinted fill with host rounded corners and a brand-foreground 20-by-20-pixel glyph, centered; it carries 16 pixels of bottom margin on mobile (removed from the small breakpoint up). - A **message** paragraph: a medium-weight lead span ("BLACK FRIDAY!"), supporting copy, and an inline-flex medium "Shop now" link that underlines on hover with a trailing 20-by-20-pixel arrow. **Close button.** An icon button positioned absolutely 12 pixels from the top and end edges on mobile, then flowing inline (static, flush) from the small breakpoint up: host rounded corners, 6 pixels of padding, a brand-muted tone, and a brand-tinted hover fill that shifts the icon to the brand foreground, wrapping a 20-by-20-pixel filled X glyph (with a screen-reader "Close"/"Dismiss" label). **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The card surface/border, the badged icon tile, the "Shop now" link, and the close icon-button must reuse the host design system's predefined components/tokens (surfaces, borders, radii, hover states, brand/heading/muted colors) rather than ad-hoc values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Sizing rules.** The floating wrapper caps at ~1024 pixels and the badged icon tile is 32-by-32 pixels around a 20-by-20-pixel glyph. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; the wrapper/card padding, the 32-pixel outer gap, the 12-pixel cluster gap, the 6-pixel button padding, and the 20-pixel close/arrow glyphs are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** On mobile the cluster stacks (badged icon over message) and the close button floats in the card's top-end corner; from the small breakpoint up the cluster becomes a single 12-pixel-gapped row and the close button flows inline at the end. The wrapper stays horizontally centered and inset at every width.

items.name: Image Promo Card With CTA
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce promotional section: a single rounded promo card pairing a product image with a headline, supporting paragraph, and call-to-action. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome (global navbar, footer, cart drawer, breadcrumb) beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 16 pixels of horizontal padding and 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up). **Promo card.** A centered max-width container of about 1280 pixels rendered as a host-rounded card on a soft secondary surface with 16 pixels of padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up, 64 from the large breakpoint up), laid out as a twelve-column grid from the large breakpoint up with a 32-pixel gap (64 from the xl breakpoint up) — stacked otherwise: - An **image column** spanning 5 of the 12 columns: a single **real product photograph** (a photographic JPG/PNG image, not a line-art SVG illustration) wrapped in a link, with 16 pixels beneath it; ~224-by-224 pixels on mobile, ~384-by-384 pixels from the small breakpoint up, and filling its column from the medium breakpoint up. - A **text column** spanning the remaining 7 of the 12 columns, vertically centered and start-aligned with an auto end margin: a ~24px bold heading-color headline with tight line-height and tracking and 12 pixels beneath it (scaling to ~36px from the medium breakpoint up, allowed to break across two lines, e.g. "Save $500 today on your purchase of a new [product]."); a muted supporting paragraph with 24 pixels beneath it; and a **primary brand call-to-action button** styled as a link (~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding, ~16px medium label, e.g. "Pre-order now"). **Design system rule.** Every element here — the product image link, the headline, the supporting paragraph, and the call-to-action button — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. The promo card uses the host's soft secondary surface token; every button or link must be the host design system's own button and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. The product image is a real photographic asset, never a line-art SVG illustration. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The call-to-action uses ~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding with a ~16px medium label. Primaries use the host brand button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the image at ~224 pixels square (~384 from the small breakpoint up, filling the column from the medium breakpoint up), the headline at ~24–36px, and the CTA label at ~16px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The card stacks the image above the text column until the large breakpoint, where it becomes a 5/7 twelve-column split; the headline, paragraph, and CTA stay start-aligned and stacked.

items.name: Mobile App Promo With Feature Grid
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce promotional section pairing a mobile-app pitch and app-store badges with a small feature grid. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on a soft secondary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up), vertically centered and laid out as a two-column grid from the large breakpoint up with a 32-pixel gap (64 from the xl breakpoint up) — stacked otherwise. **Pitch column.** A column with 32 pixels beneath it: a ~24px bold heading-color title with tight line-height and tracking, 12 pixels above it and 16 pixels beneath it (~36px from the medium breakpoint up, e.g. "Buy faster and from anywhere with our mobile application"); a muted supporting paragraph (~20px from the small breakpoint up); and an **app-store badge row** 24 pixels below — a column with 16-pixel spacing that becomes a 16-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up.
