content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Overview row.** A block that becomes a two-column grid from the large breakpoint up with a 32-pixel gap (64 from the xl breakpoint up) — stacked on mobile. - **Image column** — a non-shrinking column capped at ~448 pixels (and ~512 pixels from the large breakpoint up) and centered, holding a single full-width **real product photograph** (a photographic JPG/PNG product image, not a line-art SVG illustration). - **Details column** — 24 pixels above it on mobile (32 from the small breakpoint up, removed from the large breakpoint up), holding: - A **product name** — a ~20px semibold heading-color title (~24px from the small breakpoint up), allowed to wrap across two lines. - A **price + rating row** 16 pixels below the name that becomes a vertically-centered, 16-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up (stacked otherwise): a **price** (~24px extrabold heading-color, ~30px from the small breakpoint up) and a **rating cluster** (8px above it on mobile, removed from the small breakpoint up) — a 4-pixel-gapped row of five 16-by-16-pixel filled star glyphs in the host rating accent (a warm/amber star color), then a ~14px medium muted score ("(5.0)"), then a ~14px medium heading-color "345 Reviews" link that is underlined and loses its underline on hover. - An **actions row** 24 pixels below (32 from the small breakpoint up) that becomes a vertically-centered, 16-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up (stacked otherwise): a **secondary "Add to favorites" button** (bordered neutral, ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium label, leading 20-by-20-pixel heart glyph with an 8px end margin) and a **primary "Add to cart" brand button** (~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium label, leading 20-by-20-pixel cart glyph; 16px above it on mobile, removed from the small breakpoint up). - A **full-width divider** drawn from the design system's border token with 24 pixels of vertical margin (32 from the medium breakpoint up). - Two **description paragraphs** in the muted body color, the first with 24 pixels beneath it. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the product name, price, star rating and review link, the "Add to favorites" and "Add to cart" buttons, the divider, and the description paragraphs — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. Every button or link must be the host design system's own button and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; the star glyphs may keep their conventional warm/amber rating color. The product image is a real photographic asset, never a line-art SVG illustration. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Add to favorites" (secondary bordered) and "Add to cart" (brand) buttons use ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with ~14px medium labels; each leads with a 20-by-20-pixel glyph carrying an 8px end margin. Primaries use the host brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the image column at ~448 pixels (~512 from the large breakpoint up), the star glyphs at 16-by-16 pixels, the action glyphs at 20-by-20 pixels, the name at ~20–24px, and the price at ~24–30px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The overview row stacks the image above the details until the large breakpoint; the price/rating row stacks the rating beneath the price until the small breakpoint; the actions stack the "Add to cart" button beneath "Add to favorites" (both may go full-width) until the small breakpoint.

items.name: Vertical Gallery Accordion With Buy Card
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce product-overview section with a vertical-thumbnail image gallery and a details accordion on the left, paired with a bordered buy card on the right. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up, 96 from the xl breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels. The body becomes a space-between row from the large breakpoint up (stacked otherwise). **Gallery + accordion column.** A column with 16 pixels of horizontal padding: - A **gallery** with 16 pixels of bottom margin, capped at ~448 pixels and centered on mobile (uncapped from the large breakpoint up), that becomes a horizontal row from the large breakpoint up: - A **vertical thumbnail list** ordered second on mobile / first from the large breakpoint up — a four-column grid on mobile that becomes a vertical stack from the large breakpoint up with a 16-pixel gap, 32 pixels above it on mobile (removed from the large breakpoint up). Every thumbnail is identical in size — an 80-by-80-pixel button (96-by-96 pixels from the medium breakpoint up) with a 2-pixel border, host rounded corners, 8 pixels of padding, hidden overflow, and a centered, fully-contained **real product photograph**; the selected thumbnail carries the design system's border token while the rest stay transparent and reveal the border on hover. - A **main image panel** ordered first on mobile / second from the large breakpoint up — a growing, host-rounded panel with 16 pixels of horizontal padding that fills the remaining width of the gallery container; inside it the active **real product photograph** fills the panel's full width and height, centered both ways, sized to contain (the whole product visible, never cropped). Only the active panel shows, and one panel is active by default. - A **details accordion** below — a flush accordion of three collapsible items, each a full-width header button with 20 pixels of vertical padding, a thin bottom divider, ~14px+ medium muted (active heading-color) label, a 12-pixel gap, and a trailing 20-by-20-pixel chevron glyph that rotates on toggle; the open body has 20 pixels of vertical padding, a thin bottom divider, and muted body paragraphs (the first with 8 pixels beneath it). Use "Product Details", "Specifications", and "Warranty". **Buy card column.** A full-width column 24 pixels above it on mobile (removed from the large breakpoint up), capped at ~512 pixels and non-shrinking from the large breakpoint up, with 16 pixels of horizontal padding; inside it a **bordered card** — a thin-bordered, host-rounded card on a soft secondary/tinted surface with 16 pixels of padding (24 from the small breakpoint up, 32 from the large breakpoint up): - A **product name** — a ~20px semibold heading-color title. - A **badge + rating row** 16 pixels below that becomes a vertically-centered, 16-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up: a **danger badge** (a small inline pill in the host danger palette — a soft danger fill with danger-strong text, ~10px horizontal / 2px vertical padding, host rounded corners, ~12px medium label, 8px end margin, e.g. "the last 2 products") and a **rating cluster** (16px above it on mobile, removed from the small breakpoint up) — five 16-by-16-pixel star glyphs in the rating accent and a ~14px medium heading-color underlined "345 Reviews" link. - A **delivery line** 16 pixels below — a 4-pixel-gapped row of a 20-by-20-pixel brand-foreground location-pin glyph and a ~14px medium brand-foreground "Deliver to [Name]- [City] [ZIP]" line. - A **price + quantity row** 16 pixels below (24 from the medium breakpoint up) laid out vertically centered and space-between: a **price** (~24px extrabold heading-color, ~30px from the small breakpoint up) and a **quantity form** — a 8-pixel-gapped row of a "Quantity" cluster (a ~14px medium heading-color label beside a muted info button with a 16-by-16-pixel help glyph and dark tooltip) and a 64-pixel-wide select (~10px padding) per the **select rule**. - An **actions block** 16 pixels below (24 from the medium breakpoint up) that becomes a vertically-centered row from the small breakpoint up and a stacked column again from the large breakpoint up with a 16-pixel gap: a full-width **secondary "Add to favorites" button** and a full-width **primary "Add to cart" brand button** (per the button-padding rule, each leading a 20-by-20-pixel glyph with an 8px end margin). - A **retailer note** 16 pixels below (24 from the medium breakpoint up) — a ~14px normal muted line with brand-foreground underlined inline links that lose their underline on hover (e.g. "Also available at competitive prices from [authorized retailers], with optional Premium delivery for expedited shipping."). - An **options block** separated by a **full-width top divider** drawn from the design system's border token with 32 pixels of top padding and margin, holding a 24-pixel rhythm: - **Colour** — a ~16px medium heading-color label over (8px below) a wrapping, 8-pixel-gapped row of **option chips** (per the chip rule): "Green", "Pink", "Silver", "Blue". - **SSD capacity** — the same label + chip pattern: "256GB", "512GB", "1TB". - **Pickup** — a label over (8px below) a column of three **radio options** 16px apart, each a 16-by-16-pixel radio beside a text cell (8px start margin) with a ~14px medium label over a ~12px muted helper (one helper a brand underlined link), including a disabled "Pickup from our store" / "Not available" option. - **Add extra warranty** — a label over (8px below) a wrapping, 16-pixel-gapped row of three radio options, each a 16-by-16-pixel radio beside a ~14px medium label (8px start margin): "1 year - $39", "2 years - $69", "3 years - $99". **Chip rule.** Each option chip is a relative label wrapping a visually-hidden radio input and a selectable box: a centered box with ~8px horizontal / 4px vertical padding, a thin border, host rounded corners, the card surface fill, hidden overflow, muted ~14px medium text, and a hover surface; when checked the box takes the host brand-tinted fill, brand border, and brand-foreground text. **Select rule.** The quantity select is the host form-control select: a neutral surface, a thin default border, host rounded corners, ~14px text, ~10px padding, a fixed 64-pixel width, and the host focus ring. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the gallery panel and vertical thumbnails, the details accordion (headers, chevrons, bodies), the product name, the danger badge, the star rating and review link, the delivery line, the price, the quantity form, the "Add to favorites" and "Add to cart" buttons, the retailer note and its inline links, the divider, the colour/capacity chips, and the pickup/warranty radios — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, the buy card uses the host's soft secondary/tinted surface token; every form control — the select, radio inputs, and option chips — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; the danger badge uses a semantic danger token and the star glyphs may keep their conventional warm/amber color. The gallery images are real photographic assets, never line-art SVG illustrations. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Add to favorites" (secondary bordered) and "Add to cart" (brand) buttons are full-width with ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium labels, and a leading 20-by-20-pixel glyph (8px end margin); the accordion headers use 20px vertical padding; the info button is icon-only around a 16-by-16-pixel glyph; the select uses ~10px padding. Primaries use the host brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels and the buy card at ~512 pixels, the thumbnails at 80-by-80 pixels (96-by-96 from the medium breakpoint up), the accordion chevrons at 20-by-20 pixels, the star glyphs at 16-by-16 pixels, the delivery/action glyphs at 20-by-20 pixels, the info/help glyph at 16-by-16 pixels, the radio controls at 16-by-16 pixels, the quantity select at 64 pixels wide, the name at ~20px, and the price at ~24–30px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The body stacks the gallery/accordion column above the buy card until the large breakpoint; the gallery stacks the main image above a four-column thumbnail row on mobile and becomes a thumbnail rail beside the image from the large breakpoint up; the badge/rating row stacks the rating beneath the badge until the small breakpoint; the actions row becomes horizontal at the small breakpoint and returns to a stacked full-width column from the large breakpoint up; the pickup options stay stacked.

items.name: Carousel Overview With Pickup And Payment Options
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce product-overview section with a full-width title and rating header, then a three-part body of an image carousel, a pickup/benefits rail, and a buy column with discounted pricing, payment-plan options, and a seller block. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Header.** A **product name** — a ~24px semibold heading-color title spanning the full width — over a **rating + delivery row** 16 pixels below that becomes a vertically-centered, 16-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up: a **rating cluster** (five 16-by-16-pixel star glyphs in the rating accent, a ~14px medium muted "(5.0)", and a ~14px medium heading-color underlined "345 Reviews" link) and a **delivery line** (16px above it on mobile, removed from the small breakpoint up) — a 4-pixel-gapped row of a 20-by-20-pixel brand-foreground location-pin glyph and a ~14px medium brand-foreground "Deliver to [Name]- [City] [ZIP]" line. **Body.** A block 32 pixels below the header that becomes a top-aligned three-part row from the large breakpoint up with a 32-pixel gap (stacked otherwise): - **Carousel** — a full-width column capped at ~576 pixels from the large breakpoint up: a relative slider whose image area has 20 pixels of bottom margin, 320 pixels of height (340 from the large breakpoint up, 400 from the xl breakpoint up), hidden overflow, and host rounded corners, holding **real product photographs** (photographic JPG/PNG images, not line-art SVG illustrations) that each fill the full width of the carousel column and span its full height, sized to cover the image area; render about five slides. Beneath it a centered, 16-pixel-gapped controls row: a previous button (a host-rounded ghost button with ~6px padding and a hover surface holding a 28-by-28-pixel muted arrow glyph that shifts to the heading color on hover), a ~16px medium muted "[current] of [total]" counter, and a matching next button. - **Pickup + benefits rail** — 24 pixels above it on mobile (removed from the large breakpoint up); a one-column grid that becomes two columns from the small breakpoint up and one again from the large breakpoint up with a 24-pixel gap, a minimum width of ~288 pixels (non-shrinking), and from the large breakpoint up a fixed ~192-pixel width with a thin end (right) divider and 32 pixels of end padding: - A **pickup group** with an 8-pixel rhythm — a ~14px semibold heading-color "Personal pick up from:" label, a thin-bordered host-rounded box on a soft secondary surface with 16 pixels of padding holding a ~14px medium heading-color location name, a ~14px normal muted date range, and a ~14px medium success-color "Free of charge" line, then a ~14px medium brand-foreground underlined "See all delivery options" link (losing its underline on hover) trailing a 16-by-16-pixel chevron glyph. - A **benefits group** — a ~14px semibold heading-color "Benefits" label (8px beneath it) over a ~14px muted bullet list 4 pixels apart, each item a 8-pixel-gapped row leading with a 16-by-16-pixel check glyph (e.g. "Free return within 30 days", "Warranty included", "Damage and theft insurance"), then a ~14px medium brand-foreground underlined "More details" link. - **Buy column** — 24 pixels above it on mobile (32 from the small breakpoint up, removed from the large breakpoint up), a minimum width of ~384 pixels, with a 24-pixel rhythm: - A **price block** — a top-aligned, space-between, 16-pixel-gapped row: on the start side a ~16px gapped pair of a ~20px bold heading-color struck-through original price and a **warning/amber discount badge** (a soft amber fill with amber-strong text, ~10px horizontal / 2px vertical padding, host rounded corners, ~12px medium label, e.g. "-15%"), then a ~30px extrabold heading-color sale price beneath; on the end side a non-shrinking ~14px medium status list 4px apart — a success-color "In Stock" item and a muted "Free Delivery" item, each leading a 16-by-16-pixel glyph. - A **payment-type group** — a one-column grid that becomes three columns from the medium breakpoint up and one again from the large breakpoint up with an 8-pixel gap, of three **payment cards**; each is a relative label wrapping a 16-by-16-pixel radio control pinned ~16px from the top-left and a selectable card (a thin border, host rounded corners, 16 pixels of vertical padding, a 40-pixel start padding that clears the radio, 16 pixels of end padding, hidden overflow, and a ~2px internal rhythm) holding a ~14px medium heading-color leading line and a ~12px normal muted sub-line; when checked the card takes the host brand border. Use "One Time Payment", a checked "24-Month Financing with [Brand]", and "4 equal installments, with [My Wallet]" (the wallet name a brand underlined inline link). - An **actions row** — a 16-pixel-spaced, vertically-centered row of a full-width **primary "Add to cart" brand button** (~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium label, leading 20-by-20-pixel cart glyph with an 8px end margin) and a **favorite icon button** (a bordered neutral icon button with ~10px padding around a 20-by-20-pixel heart glyph, opening an "Add to favorites" dark tooltip). - A **full-width divider** drawn from the design system's border token. - A **seller block** — a ~14px normal muted "Sold and shipped by [Brand]" line (the brand name a semibold heading-color span), a rating row 8 pixels below (five 16-by-16-pixel star glyphs in the rating accent, a ~14px medium muted "(5.0)", and a ~14px medium heading-color underlined "345 Reviews" link), and a ~14px medium brand-foreground underlined "View seller information" link. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the product name, the star rating and review link, the delivery line, the carousel image area and its previous/next/counter controls, the pickup box and its link, the benefits list and link, the price with its struck original price and discount badge, the stock/delivery status list, the payment-type radio cards, the "Add to cart" button and favorite icon button with its tooltip, the divider, and the seller block — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the payment-type radio inputs — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; the discount badge uses a semantic warning/amber token, the in-stock and free-of-charge lines use a semantic success token, and the star glyphs may keep their conventional warm/amber color. The carousel images are real photographic assets, never line-art SVG illustrations. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Add to cart" brand button uses ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label and a leading 20-by-20-pixel cart glyph (8px end margin); the favorite icon button uses ~10px padding around a 20-by-20-pixel glyph; the carousel previous/next buttons are ghost buttons with ~6px padding around 28-by-28-pixel glyphs. Primaries use the host brand button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the carousel column at ~576 pixels with a 320/340/400-pixel image height across the large and xl breakpoints, the benefits rail at a ~288-pixel minimum (~192 pixels fixed from the large breakpoint up), the buy column at a ~384-pixel minimum, the star glyphs at 16-by-16 pixels, the delivery/cart/heart glyphs at 20-by-20 pixels, the carousel arrows at 28-by-28 pixels, the check/chevron/status glyphs at 16-by-16 pixels, the payment-card radios at 16-by-16 pixels, the name at ~24px, the original price at ~20px, and the sale price at ~30px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The rating/delivery header stacks the delivery line beneath the rating until the small breakpoint; the body stacks the carousel, then the pickup/benefits rail, then the buy column until the large breakpoint (the rail itself steps from one to two columns at the small breakpoint and drops its end divider when stacked); the payment-type cards step from one to three to one column across the medium and large breakpoints; the carousel keeps its previous/next controls and counter centered beneath the image.

items.name: Horizontal Progress Stepper With Items And Details
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce order-tracking section: a tracking heading above a horizontal icon progress stepper, then a two-column layout pairing an itemized list with an order-details card and actions. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); centered in a ~1280-pixel max-width container with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Heading.** A ~24px bold heading-color title ("Track the delivery of order #957684673"). **Progress stepper.** A block 24 pixels below the heading: a horizontal row of about six **steps** (allowed to scroll or stack below the medium breakpoint), each a centered column of a ~24-pixel status icon, a ~12px datetime line, and a ~14px label — completed and current steps rendered in the brand-foreground color, upcoming steps muted. Use: "19 Nov 2023: 10:45" / "Order placed"; "19 Nov 2023: 10:47" / "Payment accepted"; "22 Nov 2023: 12:27" / "Products delivered to the courier - DHL"; "23 Nov 2023: 15:15" / "Products in the courier's warehouse"; "Today" / "Products in delivery progress"; "Estimated delivery tomorrow" / "Products delivered". Directly below the icons, a full-width host-rounded **progress track** on a soft secondary surface with a brand-colored filled portion reaching the current step and a muted remainder. **Two-column body.** A block 32 pixels below the stepper: a grid that is one column by default and, from the large breakpoint up, two columns with a 32-pixel gap. - **Line-item list.** A divider-separated list whose items each carry vertical padding and pair a leading 40-by-40-pixel host-rounded thumbnail (a **real product photograph**) and a ~14px/16px medium heading-color name with a ~14px muted "x{qty}" and an end-aligned ~16px medium heading-color price. Provide about seven items: "Apple iMac 27\"" / x2 / "$1,499"; "Apple iPhone 14" / x1 / "$1,998"; "Apple iPad Air" / x2 / "$898"; "Xbox Series S" / x4 / "$4,499"; "PlayStation 5" / x1 / "$499"; "Xbox Series X" / x1 / "$499"; "Apple Watch SE" / x2 / "$799". - **Order-details card.** A host-rounded card on a soft secondary surface in a distinctly darker shade than the white (host primary) section background and the line-item column, so it reads as a filled gray card, with 24 pixels of padding: a ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Order Details") over a list of split rows (each a justify-between pair of a ~14px muted term and an end-aligned ~14px/16px medium heading-color value) — "Order date" / "24 November 2023", "Email" / "name@example.com", "Phone" / "+123 456 7890", "Payment method" / a "Credit Card" value preceded by a small conventional card-network logo (kept as its own mark), "Shipping address" / "6 Miles Drive St, San Franciso USA", and a **"Total price"** row with an ~18px bold "$7,191.00" value. Below the rows, a 16-pixel-gapped row of a primary **"Order details"** button (brand fill, inverse ~14px medium label, host-rounded corners, 20px/10px padding, darker brand hover, brand focus ring) and a **"Cancel the order"** button (host danger fill, inverse ~14px medium label, same rounding/padding, darker danger hover, danger focus ring). **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The heading, horizontal icon stepper and progress track, line-item list with thumbnails, order-details card (rows, card-network mark, total), and both buttons must all use the host design system's components/tokens (surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, brand/heading/muted text, soft secondary surface, danger-color cancel action, hover/focus states). Treat product thumbnails as real photographic assets and keep the card-network logo as its own conventional mark. Pixel values define only spacing, sizing, and layout rhythm.

items.name: Shipment Dashboard With Live Map
items.promptText: Create a self-contained shipment-tracking dashboard: a two-pane layout pairing a detail panel (shipment header and actions, status badges, route, a node progress track, time stats, a delay alert, and a status timeline) with a live map pane. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A two-pane layout centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels (with 16 pixels of horizontal padding, 0 from the 2xl breakpoint up) — not full-bleed to the viewport — that stacks on mobile and becomes a side-by-side row from the large breakpoint up. It is presented as plain content, NOT as a card, so it has no surrounding border, rounded corners, or wrapper/card padding: a **detail panel** on the host primary surface (the start, scrollable) and a **map pane** filling the end half. **Shipment header.** A row splitting a start group of a back-chevron icon button and a ~24px bold heading-color shipment code ("SHP-3092") from an end group of two buttons — a secondary **"Cancel Order"** button (bordered, host primary surface, host-rounded, ~14px medium heading-color label, subtle hover) and a primary **"Notify Customer"** button (a solid brand fill in the host design system's brand color with an inverse ~14px medium label, the same rounding, a darker brand hover, and a brand focus ring). **Status line.** A wrapping, vertically-centered row 16 pixels below: an **"In Progress"** status badge (a small host-rounded chip in a soft info tint with info-foreground text), a **"Delay"** badge (a soft warning/amber tint with warning-foreground text), and a ~14px muted line ("Shipping date: Mar 02, 2024 Order ID: Order-48190") whose order id is an underlined heading-color link. **Route.** A block 16 pixels below: two stacked address lines, each led by a small dot marker joined by a vertical connector, in ~14px heading-color ("482 Maple Hollow Rd, Brookfield, 41207" and "915 Sandstone Ave, Westhaven, 30654"); at the end of the block, a carrier **logo** (e.g. a courier mark) kept as its own conventional mark. **Node progress track.** A horizontal line with about five evenly-spaced node dots — completed nodes filled in a solid dark/heading color and connected by a solid segment, upcoming nodes muted on a faint segment — spanning the panel width. **Time stats.** A row 16 pixels below of three stat blocks, each a ~12px/14px muted label over a ~14px heading-color value: "Total Time" / "18 days, 4 hours", "Departure Time" / "09 Sep 24 09:25 AM", "Expected Arrival" / "27 Sep 24 16:40 PM". **Delay alert.** A host-rounded banner on a soft danger tint with a leading warning glyph and ~14px danger-foreground text ("High volume. During peak seasons like holidays, there can be a significant increase in the number of packages being shipped, leading to delays."). **Shipment status timeline.** A ~16px semibold heading-color subtitle ("Shipment Status") over a vertical **timeline** whose items each carry a leading round status marker joined by a connecting line — completed markers a solid dark/heading fill with an inverse glyph, the pending marker a muted empty circle — a middle block of a ~14px semibold heading-color title, a ~12px/14px muted subline, and an optional ~12px muted location line, plus an end-aligned ~14px muted datetime. Provide about four steps: "Order Placed" / "Shipment information received by seller" / "Cedar Ridge, OR" — "12 Sep 2024 11:10 AM"; "Preparing to ship" / "Seller is preparing to ship your order" — "12 Sep 2024 11:45 AM"; "Confirm Shipment" / "Shipment information received by carrier" — "12 Sep 2024 13:05 PM"; "Picked up" (pending) — "12 Sep 2024 13:30 PM". **Map pane.** An embedded interactive **map** filling the end pane, showing the route area, with a floating info tooltip card near the top-start (a ~14px semibold heading-color place name "Northgate Depot" over a ~12px muted address "326 Birchwood Parkway, Glenmoor") and, anchored to the bottom-end, a pair of toggle buttons — a "Satellite View" and a "Map View" (the active one a solid dark/inverse fill, the other bordered on the host primary surface), each with a leading glyph and a ~14px medium label. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The shipment header and its two buttons, status/delay badges, route markers, node progress track, time stats, delay alert, status timeline (markers, titles, sublines, datetimes), and the map pane (info tooltip and view-toggle buttons) must all use the host design system's components/tokens (surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, brand/heading/muted/inverse text, soft info/warning/danger tints, dark/inverse surface, hover/focus states). Keep the carrier logo as its own conventional mark and treat the map as a real embedded map view. Pixel values define only spacing, sizing, and layout rhythm.

items.name: Search Left Centered Logo Navbar With Category Row
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce storefront navbar that pairs a search field, a centered logo, and a secondary category-link row. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this navbar so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width bar on the primary surface; content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Top row.** A row split into three parts, vertically centered, with 16 pixels of vertical padding and a thin bottom divider: - A **floating-label search form** (hidden below the medium breakpoint): a relative group with a leading 16-by-16-pixel search glyph; a borderless, transparent text input at ~14px with its text inset 24 pixels from the start and no focus ring; and an animated "Search" label that floats up and shrinks on focus/value, adopting the brand foreground when active. - A **centered logo** — a non-shrinking link about 32 pixels tall. - An **actions cluster** on the end with an 8-pixel gap from the large breakpoint up: a mobile-only search icon-button; a cart trigger; and an account trigger. **Cart trigger + dropdown.** The trigger is an icon button (8px padding, host rounded corners, subtle hover) wrapping a 20-by-20-pixel cart glyph that carries a 16-pixel round count badge in the host danger color (white ~12px label) pinned 6 pixels past its top-end corner; from the small breakpoint up it adds a ~14px price label (such as "$109.12") and a trailing 16-by-16-pixel chevron. The dropdown is a floating panel about 360 pixels wide on a neutral surface with host rounded corners, a large shadow, 16 pixels of padding, and 16 pixels between parts: a header row with a semibold "Your shopping cart" term and a muted "4 items" value over a thin bottom divider; four product rows, each a four-column grid where a two-column cell pairs a 36-by-36-pixel product image with a truncating ~14px semibold product link over a ~14px muted subtitle, a centered muted "x1" quantity cell, and an end cell with a ~14px semibold price and a danger remove icon-button (16px glyph + "Remove" tooltip); a divided total row (semibold "Total" / value); and a full-width primary "See your cart" button. **Account trigger + dropdown.** The trigger is an icon button with a leading 20-by-20-pixel user glyph, an "Account" label, and a 16-by-16-pixel chevron. The dropdown is a floating panel about 240 pixels wide on a neutral surface with host rounded corners, a shadow, and thin dividers: an avatar header link (a 32px round avatar beside a truncating ~14px semibold name over a ~14px muted email, 16px horizontal / 12px vertical padding, subtle hover), then grouped lists of icon links (each leading with a 16-by-16-pixel muted glyph that adopts the heading color on hover, ~14px, 12px/8px padding, rounded, subtle hover) such as "My Account", "My Orders", "My Lists", "My Wallet", "Favourites Items", "Vouchers and gift cards", "Service", "My Returns", "My Reviews", "My Guarantees", "Billing Data", "Subscriptions", and a danger "Log out" link with a soft danger hover fill. **Collapsible search.** Beneath the top row, a hidden-by-default search form with 16 pixels of top padding: a full-width search input (16px padding) on a soft secondary surface with a thin default border and host rounded corners, plus a trailing brand-filled "Search" button pinned to the end edge and vertically centered (12px horizontal / 6px vertical padding). **Category row.** A centered row with 12 pixels of vertical padding holding a horizontal category-link list with a 24-pixel gap (32 from the medium breakpoint up): ~14px medium heading-color links that shift to the brand foreground on hover (such as "Home", "Best Sellers", "Gift Ideas", "Games", "PC", "Music", "Books", "Electronics", "Home & Garden"); the later links progressively hide below the small, large, and extra-large breakpoints. A trailing icon-button (a 24-pixel 3-dot glyph) sits 16 pixels after the list, shown only below the large breakpoint, opening a 224-pixel category dropdown of block links ("Games", "PC", "Music", "Books", "Electronics", "Home & Garden") plus a divided "View all categories" link. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any control styling. Every control and component here — buttons, icon-buttons, triggers, the search/text inputs (inline, floating-label, and collapsible), links, badges, and the dropdown/menu surfaces — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, reusing its built-in variants, tokens, and interaction states (fills, borders, radii, shadows, hover/focus/active states, focus rings) rather than ad-hoc or hardcoded values. The pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** Icon-only triggers use 8 pixels of padding on all sides. Primary "Search"/"See your cart" buttons use a brand fill with a white ~14px medium label; the collapsible "Search" button uses 12px horizontal / 6px vertical padding and the primary panel buttons use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the cart panel at ~360 pixels, the account panel at ~240 pixels, and the category dropdown at ~224 pixels. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand/danger accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; spacing, the 32-pixel logo height, product-image and avatar sizes, badge size, and icon sizes are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** Below the medium breakpoint the inline search hides and the mobile search icon-button + collapsible search take over; cart/account labels and chevrons collapse to icons below the small breakpoint; the category row trims its trailing links and exposes the 3-dot category dropdown.

items.name: Default Navbar With Centered Nav And Login CTA
items.promptText: Create a self-contained single-tier marketing-site navbar: brand on the start side, primary navigation in the center, and login plus upgrade CTAs on the end side. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this navbar so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width bar on the primary surface with 16 pixels of vertical padding and a thin bottom divider. Content is centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). The bar is a row with three regions vertically centered. **Brand (start).** A non-shrinking logo link about 32 pixels tall pairing a small brand glyph with a ~16px semibold heading-color wordmark. **Primary links (center).** A horizontal link list, hidden below the large breakpoint, with a 24-pixel gap (32 from the medium breakpoint up): ~14px medium heading-color links — "Company", "Marketplace", "Features", "Products" (trailing 16-by-16-pixel chevron), "Team", "Contact" — each shifting to the brand foreground on hover. **Actions (end).** A row with an 8-pixel gap: a secondary **"Login"** button (bordered, host primary/neutral surface, host-rounded corners, ~14px medium heading-color label, 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, subtle hover, focus ring); a primary **"Upgrade to PRO"** button (brand fill, inverse ~14px medium label, host-rounded corners, 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, darker brand hover, brand focus ring); and a **menu toggle** — shown only on viewports **768px wide and below**, an icon button (8px padding, host rounded corners, subtle hover) holding a 20-by-20-pixel hamburger glyph with a screen-reader "Open Menu" label. **Mobile menu.** A collapsible panel beneath the bar stacking the primary links at 12-pixel intervals on a soft secondary surface with host-token rounded corners and a thin border. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any control styling. Buttons, links, icon-buttons, and the mobile menu must use the host design system's predefined components and tokens. **Button padding rule.** Icon-only triggers use 8px padding. Labeled buttons use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding. **Sizing rules.** Container caps at ~1280 pixels. Logo height ~32 pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** Below the large breakpoint primary links hide; the menu toggle appears only on viewports **768px wide and below**. **Navbar item rules.** - Every navbar icon glyph is **18 pixels wide × 18 pixels tall** with **8 pixels** of space between the icon and its label or link text. - **Icon-only button groups.** In action and utility rows, group adjacent icon-only buttons and icon-buttons (no visible label) together; use **4 pixels** of gap between controls within each icon-only group. - **Text-labeled spacing.** Use **16 pixels** of gap between adjacent labeled buttons, text links, pickers, and other navbar items that include visible text; also **16 pixels** between an icon-only button group and the nearest text-labeled item. - Every **dropdown trigger with a text label** (nav submenus, language/currency pickers, category selectors) includes a **chevron or angle-down icon** indicating it opens a menu — never on ellipsis overflow triggers (see below). - The **user avatar** is always a **profile dropdown** — a circular avatar trigger that opens a profile/account menu; never a static, non-interactive avatar. The avatar trigger stands alone — **never** place a chevron, angle-down, or any other icon beside it; the avatar itself is the only affordance. - An **ellipsis overflow trigger** (three dots) stands alone — never place a chevron or second icon beside it; the overflow affordance is implied by the ellipsis. **Icon-only triggers** use a single glyph only — never stack a second icon on the same control. - **Menu toggle (hamburger).** The three-bar icon must **not** appear on screens **wider than 768px** — show it only on **mobile and tablet** viewports (**768px and below**), where it opens the collapsible navigation menu. Hide it entirely above 768px. Implement with the host design system's menu-toggle modifier (e.g. `.ds-menu-toggle`) and an explicit `@media (min-width: 768px) { display: none }` rule — **never** rely on utility `hidden`/`md:hidden` alone on icon-button components whose base styles set `display: inline-flex`, or the hamburger will remain visible on desktop.

items.name: Three Tier Navbar With Promo Utility Bar Joined Search And Mega Menu
items.promptText: Create a self-contained three-tier e-commerce storefront navbar: a utility bar with contact + promo + language/location pickers, a main bar with a joined category+search field and cart/account menus, and a categories bar with a full-width "All categories" mega menu. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this navbar so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width stack of three tiers on the primary surface; every tier centers its content in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Utility bar.** A band on a soft secondary surface with 10 pixels of vertical padding and a thin bottom divider, laying out three parts in a row: - A start **contact** item (shown only from the large breakpoint up): a 4-pixel-gapped row with a 20-by-20-pixel phone glyph and a ~14px medium hover-underline link in the muted color (such as "(555) 555-1234"). - A centered **promo** group (shown from the small breakpoint up): a ~14px heading-color line ("Get 50% off on Member Exclusive Month") followed, across a thin vertical divider, by a ~14px medium underlined "Shop Now" link (2 pixels of start padding) that drops its underline on hover. - An end **pickers** cluster (full width and split on mobile, end-aligned with a 16-pixel gap from the small breakpoint up): a **language picker** (a 16-pixel flag, an "English (USA)" label, and a trailing 16-by-16-pixel chevron; hover-underline) opening a 224-pixel menu with a search field on top and flag+language link rows; and a **location picker** ("Location", a leading 20-by-20-pixel pin glyph, a trailing 16px chevron) opening a 288-pixel menu whose first block is a wrapping continents checkbox grid (each a 16px checkbox + ~14px medium label, with one region pre-checked) over a divided searchable country list of 16px-checkbox + 16px-flag + ~14px country rows. **Main bar.** A row with 16 pixels of vertical padding, a thin bottom divider, and a 32-pixel gap, splitting into three parts: - A non-shrinking **logo** link about 32 pixels tall. - A **joined category+search group** that grows (hidden below the large breakpoint) laid out as a row with a small negative overlap: an "Electronics" category dropdown trigger with a start-rounded edge on a soft secondary surface (~14px medium label + trailing 16px chevron, 10px vertical / 16px horizontal padding, focus ring) opening a 192-pixel menu of icon category links (each a leading 16px muted glyph that adopts the heading color on hover, ~14px, 12px/8px padding, rounded, subtle hover) such as "Electronics", "Sports & Outdoors", "Fashion", "Food & Grocery", "Health & Beauty", "Books & School"; a full-width search input on a soft secondary fill (10px padding, end-rounded edge); and a trailing brand-filled icon "Search" button (16px glyph, full-height, end-rounded edge). - An **actions cluster** on the end (8-pixel gap from the large breakpoint up): a mobile-only search icon-button; a **cart trigger + dropdown**; and an **account trigger + dropdown**. **Cart dropdown.** The trigger is an icon button (8px padding, host rounded corners, subtle hover) wrapping a 20-by-20-pixel cart glyph with a 16-pixel round danger count badge (white ~12px label) pinned 6 pixels past its top-end corner, then from the small breakpoint up a ~14px "My Cart" label and a trailing 16px chevron. The panel is about 384 pixels wide on a neutral surface with host rounded corners, a large shadow, 16 pixels of padding, and 16 pixels between parts: a header row (semibold "Your shopping cart" / muted "4 items") over a thin bottom divider; four-column product rows where a two-column cell pairs a 36-by-36-pixel image with a truncating ~14px semibold link over a ~14px muted subtitle, a centered muted "x1" cell, and an end cell with a ~14px semibold price and a danger remove icon-button (16px glyph + "Remove" tooltip); a divided "Total" / value row; and a full-width primary "See your cart" button. **Account dropdown.** The trigger is an icon button with a leading 20px user glyph, an "Account" label, and a 16px chevron. The panel is wider — about 512 pixels wide — on a neutral surface with host rounded corners, a shadow, hidden overflow, and thin horizontal dividers between its switcher header and its body: - An **account switcher** header: a full-width button (16px padding, subtle hover, no focus outline) whose inner row splits into a start cluster and an end glyph. The start cluster pairs a 32-by-32-pixel rounded avatar (12 pixels of end margin) with a left-aligned text block — a semibold heading-color name line (tight leading, 2 pixels of bottom margin, such as "[Name] (Personal)") over a ~14px muted email. The end is a 20-by-20-pixel up/down switch glyph in the heading color. The button opens a nested ~510-pixel panel holding a single alternate **company account** row (a flex link, 16px horizontal / 12px vertical padding, host rounded corners, subtle hover) — a 32-by-32-pixel rounded logo (12px end margin) beside a semibold company name (tight leading, 2px bottom margin) over a ~14px muted company email. - A two-section body (16px vertical padding, ~14px medium type, two equal-height columns from the small breakpoint up). The first column is a "My Wish Lists" group: a ~16px heading-color heading (16px horizontal / 8px bottom padding), then block links (16px/8px padding, subtle hover) "Family gifts", "Beauty", "Gaming/Relax", and a brand-foreground "Create a new list" link with a leading 16px plus glyph (4px gap) and a soft brand hover fill; below the small breakpoint this column carries a bottom divider with 16px of bottom padding and margin that are dropped from the small breakpoint up. The second column (with a start divider from the small breakpoint up) is a "My Account" group: a ~16px heading-color heading, then icon links (each a leading 16px muted glyph that adopts the heading color on hover, 8px gap, 16px/8px padding, subtle hover) "My Account", "My Orders", "My Wallet", "Favourite Items", "Vouchers and gift cards", "Service", "My Returns", "My Reviews", "My Guarantees", "Billing Data", "Plans & Subscriptions", and a danger "Log out" link (leading 16px danger glyph) with a soft danger hover fill. **Collapsible search.** Beneath the main bar, a hidden-by-default search form with 16px top padding and 16px horizontal padding: a full-width search input (12px padding) on a soft secondary surface with a thin default border and host rounded corners, plus a trailing brand "Search" button pinned to the end edge and vertically centered (12px horizontal / 6px vertical padding). **Categories bar.** A row with 12 pixels of vertical padding holding a 4-pixel-gapped (32 from the large breakpoint up) cluster: an "All categories" trigger (a leading 16px grid glyph, a ~14px medium heading-color label, a trailing 16px chevron, brand-foreground hover) followed by ~14px medium category links shown only from the large breakpoint up ("Best Sellers", "Gift Cards", "Gift Ideas", "Deal of the day", "Top Deals", "Membership Deals", "New Releases"). On smaller screens a "Deals" link (leading 16px tag glyph) shows and a "Menu" icon+label toggle is pushed to the end. **Full-width mega menu.** A floating panel anchored directly beneath the "All categories" trigger, spanning the container (full width, capped at about 1280 pixels from the extra-large breakpoint up) on a neutral surface with host rounded corners, a large shadow, and hidden overflow. From the large breakpoint up it is a two-pane row whose panes stretch to equal height; below that it collapses to the single category rail described below. - **Category rail (start).** A non-shrinking column about 288 pixels wide from the large breakpoint up, with 16 pixels of padding (24 from the small breakpoint up), a right divider from the large breakpoint up, and 8 pixels between its rows. Every row is a full-width link with a 16-pixel gap, 16px horizontal / 8px vertical padding, host-token rounded corners, and a ~14px semibold heading-color label between a leading 16-by-16-pixel glyph and a trailing 16-by-16-pixel forward arrow. The **first row is the active/selected category** ("Computer & Office") shown on a tertiary neutral fill with its glyph and arrow in the heading color and the arrow always visible. Every other row is unstyled until hover, where it takes a subtle neutral fill; its leading glyph sits in the muted color and adopts the heading color on hover, and its trailing arrow stays hidden and slightly shifted toward the start until hover, when it fades and slides into place. List, in order: "Fashion/Clothes", "Electronics", "Gaming/Consoles", "TV/Projectors", "Collectibles & Toys", "Sports & Outdoors", "Food & Grocery", "Health & Beauty", "Car & Motorbike", "Books", "Home Air Quality", "Photo/Video". - **Active-category panel (end).** A growing, min-width-0 pane shown only from the large breakpoint up, on a soft secondary surface with 24 pixels of padding, holding the subcategories of the active rail item. It is a one-column grid that becomes three columns from the small breakpoint up with a 16-pixel gap; each column stacks several link groups 24 pixels apart, and each group is a ~14px semibold heading-color heading over ~14px muted links (8 pixels between rows) that darken to the heading color on hover. Use these groups across the three columns: column one — "Laptops" (Gaming, 2 in 1, Business, Home Office, Ultrabook), "Monitors" (Build-In Speakers, Audio & HiFi, Headphones, Home Cinema, Sat Nav & Car Electronics), "Desktop PC" (Gaming PC, Home Office, Servers, Mini PC, All in One PC); column two — "Tablets" (Best Sellers, Phone Call Functionality, Supports USB OTG, IOS, Android, Global Store), "Memory & Storage" (Primary Storage Devices, Magnetic Storage Devices, Flash Memory Devices, Optical Storage Devices, Cloud and Virtual Storage), "Printers & Ink" (Best Sellers, Laser Printers, Inkjet Printers); column three — "Computer Components" (Graphics Cards, Memory, Motherboards, Computer Cases, Power Supplies, CPUs, Network Cards, External Optical Drives, External Sound Cards, Fans & Cooling), "Software" (Operating Systems, Antivirus & Security, Home & Hobbies, Language & Travel, Programming & Web Development, Music, Photography & Graphic Design). - **Small-screen behavior.** Below the large breakpoint the end panel is hidden and the whole menu is just the category rail; the active category ("Computer & Office") instead reveals its subcategories inline, as the same three-column group grid rendered on a soft secondary surface (16px padding, host rounded corners) directly beneath that rail row. **Mobile menu.** A collapsible panel under the categories bar with 8 pixels above it, on a soft secondary surface with a thin default border, host rounded corners, and 16px/12px padding, stacking ~14px heading-color links with 12 pixels between them ("Home", "Best Sellers", "Gift Ideas", "Games", "Electronics", "Home & Garden"). **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any control styling. Every control and component here — buttons, icon-buttons, triggers, the joined category+search group (category trigger, search input, and search button), the collapsible search input, checkboxes, badges, links, and the category/account/cart dropdowns and their menu surfaces — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, reusing its built-in variants, tokens, and interaction states (fills, borders, radii, shadows, hover/focus/active states, focus rings) rather than ad-hoc or hardcoded values. The pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** Icon-only triggers use 8 pixels of padding; the category trigger and search input use 10px vertical / 16px horizontal padding. Primary buttons use a brand fill with a white ~14px medium label (20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding for "See your cart"; the collapsible "Search" button uses 12px/6px). **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the language menu at ~224 pixels, the location menu at ~288 pixels, the joined-search category menu at ~192 pixels, the cart panel at ~384 pixels, the account panel at ~512 pixels (its nested company panel ~510 pixels), and the mega-menu start column at ~288 pixels with the menu itself at the full container width. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand/danger accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system (flags keep their fixed colors); spacing, the 32-pixel logo height, avatar and product-image sizes, badge size, and icon sizes are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** Below the large breakpoint the contact item hides, the joined search collapses into the mobile search icon-button + collapsible search, the categories-bar links collapse to "Deals" + the "Menu" toggle, and the mega-menu link columns hide (the active category expanding inline instead); the utility-bar promo group hides below the small breakpoint and the pickers wrap to full width; cart/account labels reduce to icons below the small breakpoint.

Every control and component here — buttons, icon-buttons, triggers, links, and the mobile menu surface — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, reusing its built-in variants, tokens, and interaction states rather than ad-hoc or hardcoded values. Pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** Icon-only triggers use 8 pixels of padding on all sides. Primary and secondary labeled buttons use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; spacing, the 32-pixel logo height, and icon sizes are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** Below the large breakpoint the primary-link list hides; the menu toggle appears only on viewports **768px wide and below**; "Talk to sales" hides below the medium breakpoint. **Navbar item rules.** - Every navbar icon glyph is **18 pixels wide × 18 pixels tall** with **8 pixels** of space between the icon and its label or link text. - **Icon-only button groups.** In action and utility rows, group adjacent icon-only buttons and icon-buttons (no visible label) together; use **4 pixels** of gap between controls within each icon-only group. - **Text-labeled spacing.** Use **16 pixels** of gap between adjacent labeled buttons, text links, pickers, and other navbar items that include visible text; also **16 pixels** between an icon-only button group and the nearest text-labeled item. - Every **dropdown trigger with a text label** (nav submenus, language/currency pickers, category selectors) includes a **chevron or angle-down icon** indicating it opens a menu — never on ellipsis overflow triggers (see below). - The **user avatar** is always a **profile dropdown** — a circular avatar trigger that opens a profile/account menu; never a static, non-interactive avatar. The avatar trigger stands alone — **never** place a chevron, angle-down, or any other icon beside it; the avatar itself is the only affordance. - An **ellipsis overflow trigger** (three dots) stands alone — never place a chevron or second icon beside it; the overflow affordance is implied by the ellipsis. **Icon-only triggers** use a single glyph only — never stack a second icon on the same control. - **Menu toggle (hamburger).** The three-bar icon must **not** appear on screens **wider than 768px** — show it only on **mobile and tablet** viewports (**768px and below**), where it opens the collapsible navigation menu. Hide it entirely above 768px. Implement with the host design system's menu-toggle modifier (e.g. `.ds-menu-toggle`) and an explicit `@media (min-width: 768px) { display: none }` rule — **never** rely on utility `hidden`/`md:hidden` alone on icon-button components whose base styles set `display: inline-flex`, or the hamburger will remain visible on desktop.

items.name: Saved Payment Methods With Add Card And Perks

items.name: Bank Transfer Payment Form

Each half-width field spans both columns on mobile and one column from the small breakpoint up unless noted: - "To\*" (placeholder "TypeUI"). - "Account Number\*" (placeholder "e.g FB00 1234 5678 91011"). - "Address (optional)". - "Postal code (optional)" (numeric). - "Ammount" — a joined input group with a shared host small shadow, host-token rounded corners, and a 1-pixel negative overlap between segments: a full-width amount input that leads with a 16-by-16-pixel currency/money icon inset 14 pixels from the start edge (start-rounded edge, placeholder "Enter amount"), joined to a currency dropdown trigger (end-rounded edge) in the secondary button style that leads with a 16-by-16-pixel country flag, shows a label such as "USD", and trails a 16-by-16-pixel chevron. The trigger opens a 128-pixel floating menu panel on a neutral surface with a thin border, host-token rounded corners, a large shadow, and 8 pixels of padding, listing currency links (each leading with a 16-by-16-pixel flag) such as "USD", "GPB", "EUR", "CAD". - "BIC/SWIFT" (numeric). - "Payment purpose" — spans both columns; a four-row textarea (placeholder "e.g. Payment for professional consulting services provided"). - "Fees (optional)" — spans both columns; a select with options such as "SHA-Fees are splitted between sender and receipt", "Fees are paid by sender", "Fees are paid by beneficiary". - "Send on\*" — a half-width field with a leading 16-by-16-pixel calendar icon (placeholder "Select date"). - "Email confirmation (optional)" — a half-width field with a leading 16-by-16-pixel envelope icon (placeholder "e.g. name@company.com"). **Priority row.** With 16 pixels above and below it (growing to 24 from the medium breakpoint up), a 16-pixel-gapped row of two radio options, each a 16-by-16-pixel radio with an 8-pixel-gapped ~14px medium heading-color label: "Urgent (within 24 hours)" (selected) and "Instant (today)". **Submit + footer.** A full-width primary "Pay now" submit button, then a body-color "Payment processed by [Polar.sh] for [TypeUI] - United States Of America" paragraph with underlined heading-color links that drop the underline on hover. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any input or button styling. All form controls (text inputs, selects, textareas, checkboxes, radios) and all buttons must reuse the host design system's predefined input and button styles (components/tokens for fills, borders, radii, shadows, hover/focus/disabled states, and focus rings) rather than ad-hoc values; the descriptions and pixel measurements below only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Input field style.** Every input, select, and textarea uses a muted neutral fill (host secondary surface), a thin default border, heading-color text at about 14 pixels, host-token rounded corners, a host small shadow, a muted placeholder, and the host brand focus ring/border; each is full width with 12 pixels of horizontal and 10 pixels of vertical padding. Fields with a leading icon begin their text 36 pixels in. **Label style.** Block, 10 pixels beneath, ~14px medium-weight heading color. **Button padding rule.** The "Pay now" button and the currency dropdown trigger use padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. The amount input uses 12px horizontal / 10px vertical padding. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~672 pixels and the currency panel at 128 pixels. Type sizes, neutral surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system (the flag glyphs keep their own colors); spacing and icon sizes are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** On mobile each half-width field spans the full width (one per row); the amount group keeps its joined input + currency trigger, and the priority radios stay in their row.

items.name: Two Column Order Summary With Steps
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce order-summary review with a checkout step indicator: an item list beside an order-details + order-amount sidebar that ends in a place-order action and a benefits panel. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Step indicator.** A full-width, start/left-aligned ordered list at ~14px medium (~16px from the small breakpoint up) in the default body text color. It holds three steps: - A **completed step** in the brand foreground, leading with a 20-by-20-pixel check-circle glyph (6 pixels of end margin) before its label. - **Upcoming steps** in the default body color, each leading with a small numbered badge ("2", "3") with 8 pixels of end margin before its label. - Each **label** is a primary word always shown plus an optional secondary word that is hidden below the small breakpoint and revealed (with 8 pixels of start margin) from the small breakpoint up — e.g. "Personal Info", "Account Info", "Confirmation" (the last has no secondary word). The first two (non-final) steps grow from the medium breakpoint up. Between steps, from the small breakpoint up a thin full-width connector line (a ~1px bottom border) sits after each step's label with 24 pixels of horizontal margin (40 from the extra-large breakpoint up); below the small breakpoint that line is hidden and a "/" separator in the disabled/muted color (8 pixels of horizontal margin) stands between steps instead. The final step has no connector or separator. **Body layout.** A block 24 pixels below the steps (32 from the small breakpoint up) that becomes a top-aligned two-column row with a 32-pixel gap from the large breakpoint up — a growing item list on the start and a fixed-width sidebar on the end. **Product list (start).** A growing, min-width-0 card with thin internal row dividers, host rounded corners, a thin border, the host primary/neutral surface, and a small shadow. Each row matches variant 2's item row: a 24-pixel-padded, wrapping, vertically-centered row whose item cell pairs an 80-by-80-pixel square image link with a ~16px medium hover-underline name, plus an ~32-pixel quantity cell (~16px normal "xN") and an ~96-pixel end-aligned price cell (~16px bold). Use about five rows with long item names. **Sidebar (end).** A full-width card (24px above it on mobile, 32 from the small breakpoint up, 0 from the large breakpoint up) capped at about 320 pixels from the large breakpoint up (448 from the extra-large), with thin section dividers, host rounded corners, a thin border, and hidden overflow. It stacks three blocks: - **Order Details** (24px padding): a ~20px semibold heading-color subtitle 16 pixels above a divided list of split rows (16px vertical padding each, stacking on mobile and becoming a justify-between row from the small breakpoint up) — each a semibold heading-color term and an end-aligned muted value (8 pixels beneath the term on mobile): "Order date" / "24 November 2023", "Email" / "name@example.com", "Phone" / "+123 456 7890", "Payment method" / a 20-pixel-wide card logo beside "Credit Card", and "Shipping address" / an address line. - **Order amount** (24px padding, 16px between parts): a ~20px semibold subtitle, a totals group (8-pixel-spaced rows for "Original price" / "$6,592.00", "Savings" / "-$299.00" in the success color, "Store Pickup" / "$99", "Tax" / "$799") over a divided bold "Total" / "$7,191.00" row (thin top divider, 8px top padding); a full-width primary "Place your order" button (brand fill, white ~14px medium label, 20px/10px padding, brand focus ring); and a ~14px muted note capped ~320px with inline underlined brand "privacy note" and "terms of use" links. - **Benefits** (24px padding, 16px between parts, on a soft secondary surface): a ~14px medium heading-color "Your benefits:" line, a disc bullet list (4 pixels between ~14px muted items: "Pre-order guarantee", "Free shipping", "Best price"), an inline underlined brand "How are shipping costs calculated?" link, and a ~14px muted closing note about applied membership shipping benefits. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the step indicator, buttons, links, the item list, the sidebar cards/sections, the totals, and the bullet list — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; brand card logos keep their fixed colors; the pixel measurements only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Place your order" primary button uses 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with a white ~14px medium label. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the step list at ~672 pixels, the sidebar at ~320 pixels (~448 from the extra-large breakpoint up), the item image at 80-by-80 pixels, the quantity cell at ~32 pixels, the price cell at ~96 pixels, the step check glyph at 20-by-20 pixels, and the payment card logo at ~20 pixels wide. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand/success accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system (brand logos keep their colors); padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** Below the large breakpoint the item list and sidebar stack (list above sidebar); item rows stack image/name over quantity and price until the small/medium breakpoints align them; the step indicator shows "/" separators on mobile and connector lines from the small breakpoint up; each sidebar detail row stacks its term over its value on mobile and splits into a justified row from the small breakpoint up.

items.name: Cart Item Cards With Summary Sidebar
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce shopping-cart page: a heading, a stacked list of item cards (each with image, name, quantity stepper, price, and favorite/remove actions), an optional "people also bought" upsell grid, and a sticky-feeling order summary sidebar with a voucher form. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). A ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Shopping Cart", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) sits above the body. **Two-column layout.** A block 24 pixels below the heading (32 from the small breakpoint up) that becomes a top-aligned two-column row from the large breakpoint up with a 24-pixel column gap (32 from the xl breakpoint up): a **cart column** (full-width, intrinsic from the large breakpoint up, capped ~672 pixels at large and ~896 pixels at xl) and a **summary column** (centered, capped ~896 pixels, growing to fill the rest from the large breakpoint up). **Item cards.** Inside the cart column, a stack of cards 24 pixels apart. Each card has host rounded corners, a thin default border, the host primary/neutral surface, a small shadow, and 16 pixels of padding (24 from the medium breakpoint up). Its contents stack with a 16-pixel rhythm on mobile and become a single vertically-centered, space-between row with a 24-pixel gap from the medium breakpoint up, reordered into image → name → quantity/price: - An **item-image link** (80-by-80 pixels, never shrinking) ordered first on the row. - A **quantity + price group** (a space-between row that right-aligns from the medium breakpoint up): a **quantity stepper** — a row holding a 20-by-20-pixel decrement button (host rounded corners, a thin border, a soft secondary fill, hover, focus ring) with a ~10-pixel minus glyph, then a 40-pixel-wide borderless transparent center-aligned ~14px medium numeric input, then a matching increment button with a ~10-pixel plus glyph — and a **price** (right-aligned, ~128 pixels wide from the medium breakpoint up) shown as ~16px bold. - A **details cell** (growing, min-width-0, 16 pixels between its parts, capped ~448 pixels from the medium breakpoint up) ordered second: a ~16px medium hover-underline item name, then a 16-pixel-gapped actions row — an "Add to Favorites" button (~14px medium, muted with heading-color + underline on hover, leading 20-by-20-pixel heart glyph 6px before the label) and a "Remove" button (~14px medium, danger color, underline on hover, leading 20-by-20-pixel close glyph). Use about five items with long names, individual quantities, and prices. **"People also bought" upsell.** Below the cards, a block shown only from the xl breakpoint up (32px above it): a ~24px semibold heading-color title ("People also bought") over a three-column grid (24px above it, 32 from the small breakpoint up) with a 16-pixel gap. Each upsell card has 24 pixels between its parts, host rounded corners, a thin border, the host primary/neutral surface, 24 pixels of padding, a small shadow, and hidden overflow: a centered 176-by-176-pixel item image; a text group with a ~18px semibold tight-leading hover-underline name and a ~16px muted description (8px above it); a price group with a ~18px bold struck-through original price over a ~18px bold danger tight-leading sale price; and an actions row (24px above it, 10-pixel gap) holding an icon-only favorite button (a bordered neutral button, 10px padding, 20-by-20-pixel heart glyph) with a hover tooltip, plus a full-width primary "Add to cart" button (brand button, 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium label, leading 20-by-20-pixel cart glyph). **Order summary card.** In the summary column, a card with 16 pixels between its parts, host rounded corners, a thin border, the host primary/neutral surface, a small shadow, and 16 pixels of padding (24 from the small breakpoint up): a ~20px semibold heading-color "Order summary" title; a body (16 pixels between groups) with a tight 8-pixel-spaced group of label/value rows (each a space-between row with a 16-pixel gap, a ~16px normal muted term and a ~16px medium value) for "Original price", "Savings" (a success-color negative value), "Store Pickup", and "Tax", then a "Total" row separated by a top divider with 8px of padding above it and a ~16px bold term and value; a primary "Proceed to Checkout" button spanning the full width of the summary card; and a centered "or / Continue Shopping" row (8-pixel gap) pairing ~14px muted "or" text with a ~14px medium brand link (underlined, no underline on hover) carrying a trailing 20-by-20-pixel arrow glyph. **Voucher card.** Below the summary, a matching card (same surface, border, radius, shadow, and padding) holding a form with 16 pixels between parts: a ~14px medium "Do you have a voucher or gift card?" label (8px beneath it) over a full-width text input (host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, 10px padding, ~14px text), then a full-width primary "Apply Code" button. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the item cards, quantity steppers, favorite/remove actions, upsell cards, tooltips, the summary and voucher cards, and all buttons and links — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the numeric quantity input, the voucher text input, and the stepper buttons — and every button must be the host design system's own form-control and button components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Add to cart", "Proceed to Checkout", and "Apply Code" primary buttons use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the icon-only favorite button uses 10px padding; the inline favorite/remove actions are text+glyph buttons with no box padding; all use the host design system's brand or neutral button as appropriate. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the cart column at ~672/~896 pixels (large/xl), the summary column at ~896 pixels, the item image at 80-by-80 pixels, the stepper buttons at 20-by-20 pixels, the numeric input at 40 pixels wide, the price cell at ~128 pixels, the details cell at ~448 pixels, the upsell image at 176-by-176 pixels, and inline action glyphs at 20-by-20 pixels. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/success accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** Each item card stacks image, quantity/price, and details vertically and becomes a reordered space-between row from the medium breakpoint up; the "people also bought" grid is hidden until the xl breakpoint; the cart and summary columns stack until the large breakpoint, where they sit side by side.

items.name: Cart With Volume Discount Progress And Totals Panel
items.promptText: Create a self-contained, narrow-column software / digital-product cart: a title, a single-item volume-discount progress meter, a divided item list (segmented license-quantity steppers with inline price and favorite/remove text actions), a coupon link, and a soft totals panel — sized for a single column, drawer, or sidebar. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Frame.** A centered single column capped to about 512 pixels wide on the host primary surface, with comfortable vertical padding. The header and the volume-discount progress block are each closed by a full-width bottom border with 32px padding-bottom and 32px margin-bottom (see below); the remaining regions use full-width thin horizontal dividers in the divider color. **Header.** A ~20px semibold heading-color title ("My Shopping Cart", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) styled exactly like variant 2's heading. The header closes with a full-width bottom border, 32 pixels of padding beneath the title, and 32 pixels of margin separating it from the next block. **Volume-discount progress.** Below the header: a ~14px message in muted text, scoped to the single item in the cart, with the incentive and threshold emphasized in heading-color bold (e.g. "Add **1 more license** to unlock a **20% volume discount**."). Beneath it (~8px) a **progress meter** — a full-width ~6–8px-tall rounded track on a soft secondary surface with a brand-filled portion (host rounded corners) showing the current license count's progress toward the discount threshold. Beneath the meter (~8px) a ~13px medium brand link ("See volume pricing") carrying a trailing ~16px arrow glyph.
