This whole progress block closes the same way as the header — a full-width bottom border, 32 pixels of padding beneath it, and 32 pixels of margin before the item list. **Item list.** A vertical list with thin row dividers; each row has ~16px of vertical padding and is a top-aligned row with a ~16px gap: - A **thumbnail** — a ~56-by-56-pixel square holding the software item's app icon/logo, never shrinking. - A **details cell** (growing, min-width-0, ~12px between its parts): a ~16px medium heading-color software item name (e.g. a plan/license such as "Design Suite Pro — Annual License"); a row (~16px gap, vertically centered) holding a **segmented license-quantity stepper** — a single bordered, host-rounded control split into a "−" button, a center ~14px medium license-count value, and a "+" button, each segment a ~32-by-32-pixel tap target with a muted glyph, internal dividers between segments, and host hover/focus states with a focus ring — followed by the item **price** as a ~16px bold heading-color amount; and an **actions row** (~16px gap) with two text+glyph buttons: "Move to Favorites" (~14px medium muted, leading ~16–20px heart glyph, heading-color + underline on hover) and "Remove" (~14px medium danger color, leading ~16–20px trash glyph, underline on hover). Use a single software item (one license/subscription) with its name, license quantity, and price — the cart is built around this one item. **Coupon link.** Below the list, a ~14px medium brand link ("Add coupon code"). **Totals panel.** A soft secondary, host-rounded filled panel containing a stack of space-between label/value rows, each with ~12–16px vertical padding and separated by thin dividers: "Subtotal", "Savings" (a success-color value), "Store Pickup", and "Tax" — each a ~14–16px normal muted term with a ~14–16px medium heading-color value — then a final **"Total"** row with a ~16px bold term and a ~16px bold value. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the volume-discount progress meter, item rows, thumbnails, segmented license-quantity steppers, favorite/remove actions, the coupon link, and the totals panel and its rows/dividers — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the stepper buttons and quantity value — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The segmented stepper uses ~32-by-32-pixel icon segments around a ~14px medium value; the "Move to Favorites" and "Remove" actions are text+glyph buttons with no box padding; the "How can I get this?" and "Add coupon code" links are inline text links — all driven by the host design system's button and link components. **Sizing rules.** The column caps at ~512 pixels, the thumbnail is 56-by-56 pixels, the stepper segments are ~32-by-32 pixels, the progress meter is ~6–8 pixels tall, the inline action and link glyphs are ~16–20 pixels, the title is ~20/24px, and the header and volume-discount progress blocks each have a bottom border with 32px of padding-bottom and 32px of margin-bottom. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/success accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The column spans the available width up to its ~512-pixel cap; the progress meter and its message stay full-width; each item row keeps its thumbnail beside the details cell, with the stepper, price, and favorite/remove actions stacking within the details cell as space narrows; the totals panel stays full-width.

items.name: Compact Cart Table With Summary
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce shopping-cart page in a compact, centered table layout: a heading, a horizontally-scrollable cart table (item, quantity stepper, price, remove), an order summary, and back/checkout actions. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up), and inside that a centered inner column capped to about 768 pixels. A ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Shopping Cart", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) sits at the top. **Cart table.** A horizontally-scrollable wrapper 24 pixels below the heading (32 from the small breakpoint up) with a bottom divider border. Inside, a full-width left-aligned ~16px table that uses a fixed layout from the medium breakpoint up, with thin row dividers between body rows. Each row has four cells: - **Item cell** (~384 pixels wide, ~224 minimum, no wrapping, 16px vertical padding): a hover-underline medium link that is a 16-pixel-gapped vertically-centered row of a 40-by-40-pixel square item image and the item name. - **Quantity cell** (16px padding): a **quantity stepper** identical to variant 1 — a 20-by-20-pixel decrement button (host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, hover, focus ring) with a ~10-pixel minus glyph, a 40-pixel-wide borderless transparent center-aligned ~14px medium numeric input, and a matching increment button with a ~10-pixel plus glyph. - **Price cell** (16px padding, right-aligned, ~16px bold). - **Remove cell** (16px vertical padding): a right-pushed icon-only remove button (host rounded corners, 8px padding, muted color, soft fill + heading color on hover, 20-by-20-pixel trash glyph) with a screen-reader-only "Remove" label and a hover tooltip. Use about seven items with individual quantities and prices. **Order summary.** A block 16 pixels below the table: a ~20px semibold heading-color "Order summary" title, then a body 24px below it with 16 pixels between groups — a tight 8-pixel-spaced group of space-between label/value rows (~16px normal muted term, ~16px medium value) for "Original price", "Savings" (a success-color negative value), "Store Pickup", and "Tax", then a "Total" row separated by a top divider with 8px of padding above it and a ~16px bold term and value. **Actions.** A group 24 pixels below the summary with a 16-pixel gap that becomes a centered row from the small breakpoint up: a secondary "Continue Shopping" button (full-width, centered label) and a primary "Proceed to Checkout" button (16px top margin on mobile only, full-width, removed top margin from the small breakpoint up). **Design system rule.** Every component here — the cart table and its dividers, the item links, quantity steppers, remove buttons, tooltips, and the back/checkout buttons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the numeric quantity input and the stepper buttons — and every button must be the host design system's own form-control and button components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Continue Shopping" secondary and "Proceed to Checkout" primary buttons use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the stepper buttons are 20-by-20-pixel icon buttons; the remove button uses 8px padding around a 20-by-20-pixel glyph; primaries use the design system's brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the inner column at ~768 pixels, the item cell at ~384 pixels (≥~224), the item image at 40-by-40 pixels, the stepper buttons at 20-by-20 pixels, the numeric input at 40 pixels wide, and the remove glyph at 20-by-20 pixels. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/success accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The table scrolls horizontally within its wrapper on narrow screens (becoming a fixed layout from the medium breakpoint up); the action buttons stack full-width until the small breakpoint, then sit centered in a row.

items.name: Fullwidth Image Slider Carousel
items.promptText: Create a self-contained full-width e-commerce image-slider hero. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band; content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 64 pixels of vertical padding. **Carousel.** A rounded, hidden-overflow slider about 512 pixels tall holding a set of sliding image panels (render three). Each panel has a cover-positioned, centered, non-repeating background image with a translucent dark overlay (about 50% opacity) above the image and below the content. **Slide content.** A content column capped at about 512 pixels wide, vertically centered with 16 pixels of horizontal padding on mobile, growing to at least 96 pixels of horizontal inset from the carousel edges from the small breakpoint up so the content clears the full-height navigation controls, alternating between start-aligned (offset toward the start edge) and end-aligned (offset toward the end edge) from the small breakpoint up so consecutive slides mirror each other: - An alert pill: an inline row with 4 pixels of padding (8 pixels on the end), fully rounded, on a muted neutral surface at reduced opacity, holding a small rounded tag chip with a quaternary neutral fill and 2 pixels vertical / 8 pixels horizontal padding (such as "Sale"), then a small-size medium-weight link 8 pixels after it that underlines on hover, and a trailing 16-by-16-pixel chevron glyph (such as "Up to 30% OFF if you order today."). - A heading with 48 pixels above it and 24 pixels beneath it, semibold, white, about 30 pixels (scaling to ~48 on large), tight line-height (such as "Save today on your new iMac computer."). - A supporting paragraph with 48 pixels beneath it in white at reduced opacity. - One or more calls to action: a primary brand-filled button, optionally paired in a 12-pixel-spaced row with a secondary outlined button that leads with a 16-by-16-pixel icon, or a single brand button that leads with a 20-by-20-pixel icon (such as "Pre-order now", "Buy now" / "Find a store"). **Slide indicators.** Centered near the bottom (about 20 pixels up), a row of three 12-by-12-pixel round dots with 12 pixels between them on a translucent white fill, marking the active slide. **Slider controls.** Previous and next controls pinned to the start and end edges spanning the full height, hidden on mobile and shown from the medium breakpoint up; each centers a 40-by-40-pixel round translucent-white button (brightening on hover) holding a 20-by-20-pixel white arrow glyph. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels and slides at ~512 pixels tall. Type sizes, the background-image treatment, overlay, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; spacing, the slider height, dot, control, and icon sizes are fixed in pixels. **Button padding rule.** The slide call-to-action buttons use padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. **Mobile layout rule.** On mobile the slider keeps its full height with each slide's content centered horizontally (no start/end mirroring), the previous and next edge controls are hidden, and navigation relies on the bottom dot indicators.

items.name: Category Sidebar With Promo Panel
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce storefront hero section pairing a category sidebar with a promotional panel. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the secondary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (growing to 64 pixels from medium up) and 16 pixels of horizontal padding. Inside, a max-width container of about 1280 pixels rendered as a rounded card on a soft primary surface with 16 pixels of padding (growing to 24 from medium up). **Layout.** A stacked column that becomes a horizontal row from the medium breakpoint, holding a category sidebar and a promo panel. **Category sidebar.** A fixed 320-pixel-wide column from medium up (full width when stacked) with 8 pixels between its rows; from medium up it carries a thin end (right) divider with 24 pixels of end padding, and a bottom padding of 16 pixels when stacked. It holds a vertical list of category links: - A selected/active link with a muted neutral fill, host-token rounded corners, 16 pixels horizontal and 8 pixels vertical padding, small-size semibold text in the heading color, a leading 16-by-16-pixel icon, and a trailing 16-by-16-pixel arrow glyph (such as "Computer & Office"). - The remaining links use the same padding and rounding with small-size medium-weight text, a leading 16-by-16-pixel icon that sits in the body color and shifts to the heading color on hover, a subtle hover surface, and a trailing 16-by-16-pixel arrow glyph that is hidden by default and slides in (translating into place and fading to full opacity) on hover (such as "Fashion/Clothes", "Electronics", "Gaming/Consoles", "TV/Projectors", "Collectibles & Toys", "Sports & Outdoors", "Food & Grocery", "Health & Beauty", "Car & Motorbike", "Books", "Home Air Quality", "Photo/Video"). **Promo panel.** The other column (ordered before the sidebar on mobile, after it from medium up), centered as a grid that becomes a 5-column grid from large with a 32-pixel gap, with 64 pixels of horizontal padding from medium up and a thin bottom divider with 32 pixels beneath it on mobile: - A product image side, hidden on mobile and shown from medium up, spanning 2 of the 5 columns. - A text side spanning 3 of the 5 columns: a heading with 24 pixels beneath it, bold, about 24 pixels (scaling to ~36 on large), tight line-height and tracking (such as "Save $500 today on your new dream iMac."); a supporting paragraph with 32 pixels beneath it in the body color, up to ~18 pixels from medium; and a primary brand-filled button, full width on mobile and auto width from medium up (such as "Pre-order now"). **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels and the sidebar at 320 pixels. Type sizes, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, the slide-in transition, and brand accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; spacing, icon, and arrow sizes are fixed in pixels. **Button padding rule.** The promo button uses padding-left 24px, padding-right 24px, padding-top 14px, and padding-bottom 14px. The sidebar links use padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 8px, and padding-bottom 8px. **Mobile layout rule.** On mobile the promo panel appears first (full width with its image hidden and text centered), the category sidebar follows beneath it as a full-width list without the end divider, and the trailing arrows may show without the hover slide-in.

items.name: Member Deals Hero With Category Cards And Logo Strip
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce storefront hero section. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (growing to 64 pixels from medium up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding. **Hero row.** A twelve-column grid that stacks until the extra-large breakpoint, where it splits with a 64-pixel gap. - A text column spanning 5 of 12 columns, centered until extra-large (then start-aligned): - A large display heading with 24 pixels beneath it, semibold, tight line-height and tracking, about 36 pixels scaling to ~48 and ~60 pixels on larger screens (such as "Don't miss out on exclusive deals."). - A supporting paragraph with 32 pixels beneath it in the body color, up to about 18–20 pixels on larger screens. - A pair of actions in a horizontal row with 16 pixels between them (centered until extra-large, then start-aligned): a primary brand-filled button (such as "Shop Now") and a secondary outlined button (such as "Learn more") that trails a 20-by-20-pixel arrow glyph 6 pixels after its label. - A cards column spanning the remaining 7 of 12 columns: a one-column grid that becomes two columns from the small breakpoint with a 16-pixel gap (growing to 32 pixels from extra-large). It holds two category cards. **Category card.** A rounded, thin-bordered card on the primary surface with a very subtle brand-tinted top-to-bottom gradient overlaid by a faint decorative grain texture (cosmetic, behind the content), hidden overflow, 24 pixels of padding, a small shadow, and 16 pixels between its stacked parts (growing to 24 from medium up): - A section heading of about 18 pixels, semibold, in the heading color (such as "Top categories"). - A two-column tile grid divided by thin internal vertical and horizontal dividers; each tile has about 16 pixels of inset padding on its inner sides, an 80-pixel-tall product image with 16 pixels beneath it, and a medium-weight category label link that underlines on hover (such as "Computers", "Gaming", "Tablets", "Fashion"). - A trailing "Shop now" link in the brand foreground color that underlines on hover and trails a 20-by-20-pixel arrow glyph. **Brand logo strip.** Beneath the hero with 64 pixels of space above it, a max-width container with a thin top and bottom divider and 32 pixels of vertical padding, holding a responsive grid of monochrome partner logos: 2 columns on mobile, 3 from small, 8 from large, with a 32-pixel gap (growing to 48 from small) and 16 pixels of horizontal padding. Each logo is a link about 32–40 pixels tall in the muted body color, shifting to the heading color on hover. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels. Type sizes, the gradient, grain texture, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; spacing, image, and logo heights are fixed in pixels. **Button padding rule.** The two hero actions use padding-left 24px, padding-right 24px, padding-top 14px, and padding-bottom 14px. **Mobile layout rule.** On mobile the text column stacks centered above the cards; the two cards stack into a single column (two columns from the small breakpoint), each tile grid keeps its two columns, and the logo strip drops to two columns.

items.name: Image Background Hero With Overlapping Category Icons
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce storefront hero section. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the secondary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (growing to 64 pixels from medium up). **Image hero.** A full-bleed banner whose background is a cover-positioned, centered, non-repeating image. Over it, a centered content column capped at about a 2xl max-width with 16 pixels of horizontal padding, 8 pixels of top padding (growing to 64 from large), and 128 pixels of bottom padding (leaving room for the overlapping grid below). The text is centered: - A large display heading about 36 pixels (scaling to ~60 on large), semibold, tight line-height and tracking, in the brand-strong foreground color (such as "Don't miss out on exclusive deals."). - A supporting paragraph with 32 pixels of vertical margin in the brand foreground color, up to about 20 pixels on large screens. - A primary brand-filled button (such as "Shop now"). **Overlapping category grid.** A max-width container of about 1280 pixels pulled upward by 80 pixels so it overlaps the bottom of the banner, with 16 pixels of horizontal padding. It is a rounded, thin-bordered card on a soft primary surface with a small shadow and 32 pixels of vertical padding (32 pixels all around from medium up), laid out as a responsive grid: 2 columns on mobile, 3 from small, 4 from medium, and 8 from large, with a 16-pixel column gap and 32-pixel row gap. Each cell is centered and holds: - A 64-by-64-pixel square icon tile with host-token rounded corners, a thin border, a muted neutral fill, and a subtle hover surface, centering an icon glyph about 20 pixels (growing to ~36 on large) in the body color, with 16 pixels beneath the tile. - A category label link of about 18 pixels, medium weight, in the heading color, that underlines on hover (such as "Servers", "Fashion", "Electronics", "Gaming", "TV/Projectors", "Toys", "Sport", "Grocery"). **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels. Type sizes, the background image treatment, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; spacing and the icon-tile size are fixed in pixels. **Button padding rule.** The hero button uses padding-left 24px, padding-right 24px, padding-top 14px, and padding-bottom 14px. **Mobile layout rule.** On mobile the hero text stays centered with the button beneath it, and the overlapping category grid drops to two columns while keeping its upward overlap onto the banner.

items.name: Compact Cart Table With Summary
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce shopping-cart page in a compact, centered table layout: a heading, a horizontally-scrollable cart table (item, quantity stepper, price, remove), an order summary, and back/checkout actions. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up), and inside that a centered inner column capped to about 768 pixels. A ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Shopping Cart", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) sits at the top. **Cart table.** A horizontally-scrollable wrapper 24 pixels below the heading (32 from the small breakpoint up) with a bottom divider border. Inside, a full-width left-aligned ~16px table that uses a fixed layout from the medium breakpoint up, with thin row dividers between body rows. Each row has four cells: - **Item cell** (~384 pixels wide, ~224 minimum, no wrapping, 16px vertical padding): a hover-underline medium link that is a 16-pixel-gapped vertically-centered row of a 40-by-40-pixel square item image and the item name. - **Quantity cell** (16px padding): a **quantity stepper** identical to variant 1 — a 20-by-20-pixel decrement button (host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, hover, focus ring) with a ~10-pixel minus glyph, a 40-pixel-wide borderless transparent center-aligned ~14px medium numeric input, and a matching increment button with a ~10-pixel plus glyph. - **Price cell** (16px padding, right-aligned, ~16px bold). - **Remove cell** (16px vertical padding): a right-pushed icon-only remove button (host rounded corners, 8px padding, muted color, soft fill + heading color on hover, 20-by-20-pixel trash glyph) with a screen-reader-only "Remove" label and a hover tooltip. Use about seven items with individual quantities and prices. **Order summary.** A block 16 pixels below the table: a ~20px semibold heading-color "Order summary" title, then a body 24px below it with 16 pixels between groups — a tight 8-pixel-spaced group of space-between label/value rows (~16px normal muted term, ~16px medium value) for "Original price", "Savings" (a success-color negative value), "Store Pickup", and "Tax", then a "Total" row separated by a top divider with 8px of padding above it and a ~16px bold term and value. **Actions.** A group 24 pixels below the summary with a 16-pixel gap that becomes a centered row from the small breakpoint up: a secondary "Continue Shopping" button (full-width, centered label) and a primary "Proceed to Checkout" button (16px top margin on mobile only, full-width, removed top margin from the small breakpoint up). **Design system rule.** Every component here — the cart table and its dividers, the item links, quantity steppers, remove buttons, tooltips, and the back/checkout buttons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the numeric quantity input and the stepper buttons — and every button must be the host design system's own form-control and button components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Continue Shopping" secondary and "Proceed to Checkout" primary buttons use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the stepper buttons are 20-by-20-pixel icon buttons; the remove button uses 8px padding around a 20-by-20-pixel glyph; primaries use the design system's brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the inner column at ~768 pixels, the item cell at ~384 pixels (≥~224), the item image at 40-by-40 pixels, the stepper buttons at 20-by-20 pixels, the numeric input at 40 pixels wide, and the remove glyph at 20-by-20 pixels. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/success accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The table scrolls horizontally within its wrapper on narrow screens (becoming a fixed layout from the medium breakpoint up); the action buttons stack full-width until the small breakpoint, then sit centered in a row.

items.name: Billing Delivery Rail With Order List
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce checkout page pairing a left rail of billing, delivery, and payment cards with a right column of order item cards and an order-summary card. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); the whole section is a single **form** centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). A ~20px semibold heading-color "Checkout" title (~24px from the small breakpoint up) sits above the body. **Two-column layout.** A block 24 pixels below the heading (32 from the small breakpoint up) that becomes a top-aligned two-column row from the large breakpoint up with a 24-pixel gap: a **left rail** (full-width, capped ~384 pixels at large and ~512 pixels at xl) with a 16-pixel rhythm (24 from the small breakpoint up) and a growing, min-width-0 **order column** with a 24-pixel rhythm. **Card rule.** Every card in this layout is a thin-bordered, host-rounded card on the host primary surface with a small shadow and 16 pixels of padding (24 from the small breakpoint up), opening with a ~20px semibold heading-color title and a 16-pixel rhythm. **Billing address card.** A card whose body is a field grid that is one column and becomes two from the small breakpoint up with a 16-pixel gap: - An **address-type radio row** spanning both columns — a 16-pixel-gapped row of two inline options, each a 16-by-16-pixel radio control beside a ~14px medium heading-color label (8px start margin): a checked "Individual" and "Company". - A **collapsible company group** spanning both columns (hidden until "Company" is chosen) — a two-column, 16-pixel-gapped grid of "Company name" and "VAT number" text fields. - A **"Saved Address" select** spanning both columns (per the field rule) whose label row pairs the ~14px medium label with a muted info button (a 16-by-16-pixel help glyph shifting to the heading color on hover, opening a dark tooltip); the select offers a "Choose one of your saved address" placeholder and saved address options. - Two **text fields** ("First Name\*", "Last Name\*"). - A **phone field** ("Phone Number\*") spanning both columns (per the phone rule). - A **"Shipping Address\*" four-row textarea** spanning both columns (per the field rule). - Two **select fields** ("Country\*", "City\*"). - A **save-address checkbox row** spanning both columns — a 16-by-16-pixel checkbox beside a ~14px medium heading-color label (8px start margin, "Save the data in the address list"). **Delivery address card.** A card whose body is a 16-pixel-rhythm radio list: a checked "Delivery to the same address" and "Delivery to another address" (each a 16-by-16-pixel radio beside a ~14px medium heading-color label, 8px start margin), then a **store-pickup option** — a top-aligned row of a 16-by-16-pixel radio and a text cell (8px start margin) with a ~14px medium heading-color label over a ~12px normal muted helper ("Store pickup" / "(Choose the store from which you want to pick up the products)"). **Payment details card.** A card whose body is a 16-pixel-rhythm radio list: a checked "Online with bank card", a **"Flowbite online installments"** option (a 16-by-16-pixel radio beside a text cell with a ~14px medium label over a ~12px normal muted helper, e.g. "You have interest from 1%/month until [date]."), "Online with [Brand] STAR Card", and "Payment order", each a 16-by-16-pixel radio beside a ~14px medium heading-color label (8px start margin). **Order item cards.** A stack with a 16-pixel rhythm (24 from the small breakpoint up) of order cards; each is a thin-bordered, host-rounded card on the host primary surface with a small shadow and 24 pixels of padding, laid out as a 16-pixel-rhythm column that becomes a vertically-centered, space-between row from the medium breakpoint up with a 24-pixel gap: - An **80-by-80-pixel square product-image link** (never shrinking) holding a **real product photograph** (a photographic JPG/PNG image, not a line-art SVG illustration). - A growing, min-width-0 **name cell** (capped ~448 pixels from the medium breakpoint up) with a ~16px medium heading-color hover-underline product-name link. - A **quantity + price group** — a vertically-centered, space-between, 16-pixel-gapped row (end-aligned from the medium breakpoint up) of a non-shrinking ~32-pixel-wide ~16px normal "x[n]" quantity and an end-aligned ~16px bold price (~128 pixels wide from the medium breakpoint up). Use about five order cards with long product names, quantities, and prices. **Order summary card.** A card (per the card rule) whose body holds: a totals group with a 16-pixel rhythm — a sub-list with 8 pixels between four justify-between, 16-pixel-gapped rows (a ~16px normal muted term and a ~16px medium value): "Original price" / "$6,592.00", "Savings" / "-$299.00" (the value in the host success color), "Store Pickup" / "$99", "Tax" / "$799"; then a **total row** with a thin top divider and 8px of top padding pairing a ~16px bold "Total" with a ~16px bold value ("$7,191.00") — then a full-width **"Continue to payment" brand button** (~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium label) and a centered, 8-pixel-gapped row of a ~14px normal muted "or" and a ~14px medium brand-foreground underlined "Return to Shopping" link (losing its underline on hover) trailing a 20-by-20-pixel arrow glyph. **Field rule.** Each field is a ~14px medium heading-color block label with an 8px bottom margin over the host form control — a full-width text input, select, or textarea on a soft secondary/neutral fill with a thin default border, host rounded corners, ~14px heading-color text, ~10px padding, a muted placeholder, and the host brand focus ring/border. **Phone rule.** The phone field is a ~14px medium heading-color label (8px beneath it) over a joined input group: a non-shrinking start-rounded bordered neutral **country-code dropdown trigger** (~16px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium label) leading with a 16-by-16-pixel country flag (8px end margin) and a dial-code label, trailing a 16-by-16-pixel chevron, then a growing end-rounded phone input sharing the border with no double edge (~10px padding, ~14px text, "123-456-7890" placeholder); the trigger opens a ~224-pixel menu of country rows (each a ~14px muted row with ~12px horizontal / ~8px vertical padding, a 16-by-16-pixel flag with an 8px end margin, a hover fill, and a "[Country] (+[code])" label). **Design system rule.** Every element here — the "Checkout" heading, the billing, delivery, and payment cards (titles, radios, the address-type and save-address controls, the saved-address select with its info tooltip, the text fields, phone trigger/menu, and textareas), the order item cards (product photos, name links, quantities, prices), and the order-summary card (totals list, "Continue to payment" button, and "Return to Shopping" link) — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — text inputs, selects, textareas, radios, the checkbox, the phone trigger/menu — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, link, and menu components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; the country flags keep their conventional colors and the savings value uses a semantic success token. Product images are real photographic assets, never line-art SVG illustrations. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Continue to payment" brand button is full-width with ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding and a ~14px medium label; the phone trigger uses ~16px horizontal / 10px vertical padding; the info button is icon-only around a 16-by-16-pixel glyph; the "Return to Shopping" is an inline text link. Primaries use the host brand button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the left rail at ~384 pixels (~512 from the xl breakpoint up), the order name cell at ~448 pixels and price at ~128 pixels from the medium breakpoint up, the product-image links at 80-by-80 pixels, the radio controls and checkbox at 16-by-16 pixels, the phone flags/chevron and info glyph at 16-by-16 pixels, the phone menu at ~224 pixels, the quantity at ~32 pixels wide, the return arrow glyph at 20-by-20 pixels, and the card titles at ~20px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The layout stacks the left rail above the order column until the large breakpoint; each card's field grid steps from one to two columns at the small breakpoint (the address-type row, company group, saved-address select, phone, shipping textarea, and save-address row always spanning both); the order item cards stack the image, name, and quantity/price until the medium breakpoint, where they become a space-between row; the order-summary card keeps its button above the centered "Return to Shopping" link.

items.name: Split Subscription Summary And Card Payment
items.promptText: Create a self-contained subscription-checkout page split into two panels: a dark brand-gradient plan summary on one side and a "Pay With Card" form on the other. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width, full-height-feeling block laid out as a single column that becomes a two-panel row from the large breakpoint up, each panel taking half the width; both panels stretch to equal height. There is no outer max-width cap — the panels span the viewport — but each panel centers its own content in a column capped at ~448 pixels. **Summary panel.** A panel on a **dark brand gradient** — a top-to-bottom (or diagonal) gradient built from the host design system's brand and dark/inverse surface tokens, going from a darker brand shade into the dark/inverse surface (never hardcoded hex; compose it only from brand-strong and dark surface tokens) — with all text in the inverse light/muted tokens, ~32px of padding (48 from the large breakpoint up), and its content top-aligned in the ~448-pixel column: - A **brand row** — a vertically-centered row of a 24-by-24-pixel inverse back-arrow icon button, a 24-by-24-pixel circular brand glyph (12px after it), and a ~16px medium inverse brand name ("Dolens"). - A **plan caption** 32 pixels below — a ~14px inverse-muted "Subscribe to [Plan]" line. - A **price** 8 pixels below — a vertically-baseline row of a ~48px extrabold inverse amount ("US$ 19.99") and a non-shrinking ~14px inverse-muted "Per month" label (8px after it) that stays on a single line and never wraps. - A **plan blurb** 8 pixels below — a ~14px inverse-muted feature line ("Unlimited contacts, 500 Messages per month"). - A **plan card** 24 pixels below — a host-rounded card on a slightly raised inverse surface (a translucent light overlay over the dark surface) with 16 pixels of padding and a 16-pixel rhythm: a space-between top row of a stacked label (a ~14px medium inverse "[Plan] Standard" over a ~12px inverse-muted "Billed monthly") and a ~14px medium inverse price ("US$ 19.99"); a thin inverse divider; and an **annual-billing row** — a vertically-centered, space-between row of a start cluster (a host toggle switch, a small **"Save $200" badge** in the host success palette with ~8px horizontal / 2px vertical padding and a ~12px medium label, and a ~14px inverse-muted "with annual billing" label) and a ~14px inverse-muted end price ("US$ 1,149.99/year"). - A **totals list** below, its rows split by thin inverse dividers (each row ~12px vertical padding): a **subtotal row** (a ~16px inverse "Subtotal" and a ~16px medium inverse "US$ 19.99"); an **"Add promotion code"** row — a ~14px medium inverse underlined text button that loses its underline on hover; a **tax row** (a ~14px inverse-muted "Tax" leading-aligned with a trailing ~16px inverse-muted info glyph, and a ~14px inverse-muted "US$ 0.00"); and a **total row** (a ~16px medium inverse "Total due today" and a ~16px medium inverse "US$ 19.99"). - A **panel footer** pinned toward the bottom — a vertically-centered row of a ~12px inverse-muted "© [year] All rights reserved" line and a 16-pixel-gapped group of ~12px medium inverse underlined "Terms" and "Privacy" links. **Payment panel.** A panel on the host primary surface with ~32px of padding (48 from the large breakpoint up) and its content top-aligned in the ~448-pixel column with a 24-pixel rhythm: - A **"Pay With Card"** heading — a ~24px bold heading-color title. - An **"Email" field** (per the field rule) with an "example@gmail.com" placeholder. - A **"Name on card" field** (per the field rule) with a "John Smith" placeholder. - A **"Card Details" group** — a ~14px medium heading-color label (8px beneath it) over a **joined field group** (per the joined-group rule): a top **card-number input** (full width, a "1234 1234 1234 1234" placeholder, trailing a 16-pixel-tall row of card-brand glyphs keeping their conventional marks) over a two-column row of an **expiry input** ("MM/YY" placeholder) and a **security-code input** ("CVC" placeholder), all sharing borders with no double edges. - A **"Billing address" group** — a ~14px medium heading-color label (8px beneath it) over a **joined field group**: a top **country select** (leading a 16-by-16-pixel flag keeping its conventional colors, trailing a 16-by-16-pixel chevron) over an **address input** ("Address" placeholder), sharing borders with no double edge. - A **save-info consent card** — a thin-bordered, host-rounded card with 16 pixels of padding holding a top-aligned row of a 16-by-16-pixel checkbox and a text cell (12px start margin) with a ~14px medium heading-color label ("Securely save my information for 1-click checkout") over a ~12px normal muted helper ("Pay faster on [Brand] and everywhere [Link] is accepted"). - A **"Subscribe" primary brand button** — full-width (~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding, ~14px medium label). - A **fine-print note** — a center-aligned ~12px normal muted legal paragraph (e.g. "By confirming your subscription, you allow us to charge your card for this and future payments in accordance with terms. You can always cancel your subscription"). **Field rule.** Each field is a ~14px medium heading-color block label with an 8px bottom margin over the host form control — a full-width text input or select with a thin default border, host rounded corners, ~14px heading-color text, ~12px padding, a muted placeholder, and the host brand focus ring/border. **Joined-group rule.** A joined group stacks its controls into one bordered, host-rounded unit so adjacent controls share a single hairline border (no doubled edges): the top control rounds only its top corners, inner controls stay square, the bottom control rounds only its bottom corners, and side-by-side controls within a row share their middle vertical border; the whole group shows one host brand focus ring on the focused control. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the back-arrow and brand glyph, the brand name, the plan caption, price and blurb, the plan card (labels, prices, divider, toggle switch, "Save" badge), the totals list ("Add promotion code" button, tax info glyph, and rows), the footer copyright and legal links, the "Pay With Card" heading, the email, name-on-card, card-detail, and billing-address fields (labels, inputs, select, flag, chevron, and card-brand glyphs), the consent card (checkbox, label, helper), the "Subscribe" button, and the fine-print note — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. The summary panel's dark brand gradient is composed only from the host's brand-strong and dark/inverse surface tokens with the inverse light/muted text tokens (never hardcoded); in particular, every form control — text inputs, the select, the checkbox, the toggle switch — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, link, and switch components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; the "Save" badge uses a semantic success token while the country flag and card-brand glyphs keep their conventional colors. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Subscribe" brand button is full-width with ~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding and a ~14px medium label; the back-arrow is a 24-by-24-pixel icon button; the "Add promotion code", "Terms", and "Privacy" are inline text links. Primaries use the host brand button. **Sizing rules.** Each panel content column caps at ~448 pixels, the brand glyph and back-arrow at 24-by-24 pixels, the price at ~48px, the card-brand and info glyphs and the flag/chevron at ~16px, the checkbox at 16-by-16 pixels, and the "Pay With Card" heading at ~24px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The two panels stack into a single column until the large breakpoint (the summary panel above the payment panel), each keeping its centered ~448-pixel content column and reduced padding; the card-detail and billing-address joined groups keep their stacked, shared-border layout (the MM/YY and CVC inputs staying in their two-column row); the "Subscribe" button stays full-width.

items.name: Checkout Stepper Card Form With Alternative Pay
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce payment section that stacks a checkout progress stepper, a credit-card form with alternative pay buttons, and an order summary. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the primary surface; content centered in a max-width container of about 672 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding and 32 pixels of vertical padding (growing to 64 pixels from the large breakpoint up). The whole section is a single form with 32 pixels between its stacked blocks. **Progress stepper.** A full-width ordered list laid out as a horizontal row, about 14 pixels (growing to ~16 from the small breakpoint up), medium weight, centered text. It holds four steps — "Cart", "Checkout", "Order", "Payment" — each leading with an 18-by-18-pixel check-circle glyph 6 pixels before its label, all in the host brand foreground color. From the small breakpoint up, every step except the last is followed by a 32-pixel-wide, 4-pixel-tall bottom-border connector with a 24-pixel horizontal margin (growing to 40 pixels from the extra-large breakpoint up); below the small breakpoint the connector is hidden and a muted "/" separator with an 8-pixel horizontal margin sits between steps instead. **Payment block.** A stack with 16 pixels between parts (growing to 24 from small and 32 from large): - A group titled with a heading in the heading color, semibold, about 20 pixels (scaling to ~24 from small up) and 32 pixels beneath it, reading "Pay with your Credit Card", followed by a two-column field grid (16-pixel gap, 16 pixels above it) holding the same four fields as variant 1: "Full name (as displayed on card)\*", "Card number\*", "Card expiration\*" (leading calendar icon), and "CVV\*" (label with info-tooltip button). - An "or" divider: a centered row with a full-width hairline rule on each side (a 1-pixel light line) and the body-color word "or" with 20 pixels of horizontal padding between them. - A row of two equal alternative-pay buttons with a 16-pixel gap, each full width in the secondary button style and leading with a 16-by-16-pixel brand logo 6 pixels before its label: "Google Pay" and "Paypal". **Order summary card.** A card on a soft secondary surface with a thin default border, host-token rounded corners, and 24 pixels of padding, with 16 pixels between its parts: the same line-item rows (12 pixels apart) and divided total row as variant 1, then a full-width primary "Pay now" submit button. **Footer note.** With 24 pixels above it (growing to 32 from small up), the body-color "Payment processed by [Polar.sh] for [TypeUI] - United States Of America" paragraph with two underlined heading-color links that drop the underline on hover. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any input or button styling. All form controls (text inputs, selects, textareas, checkboxes, radios) and all buttons must reuse the host design system's predefined input and button styles (components/tokens for fills, borders, radii, shadows, hover/focus/disabled states, and focus rings) rather than ad-hoc values; the descriptions and pixel measurements below only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Input field style.** Same as variant 1: muted neutral fill, thin default border, ~14px heading text, host rounded corners, host small shadow, muted placeholder, brand focus ring/border, full width, 12px horizontal / 10px vertical padding. **Label style.** Block, 10 pixels beneath, ~14px medium-weight heading color. **Button padding rule.** The primary "Pay now" button and both secondary alternative-pay buttons use padding-left 16px, padding-right 16px, padding-top 10px, and padding-bottom 10px. The primary button is a brand fill with a white label darkening to the strong brand on hover; the secondary buttons are a muted neutral fill with a thin default border and a body-color label that shifts to the heading color on hover. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~672 pixels. Type sizes, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; spacing, the connector size, and icon sizes are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** On mobile the stepper connectors collapse to "/" separators, the card fields keep their two-column grid (each half-width field on its own half-row), and the two alternative-pay buttons stay in their row.

items.name: Centered Description With Showcase And Video
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce "product description" section: a centered, single-column long-form description with a full-width showcase image, intro paragraphs, a key-features bullet list, an embedded product video, closing paragraphs, and a "show more" button. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); its content is centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (dropping to 0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). Inside, a centered ~1024-pixel max-width column holds everything. **Heading.** A ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Product description"), growing to ~24px from the small breakpoint up. **Showcase image.** With 32 pixels of vertical margin (and, from the xl breakpoint up, 48 pixels above / 64 below), a full-width **real product photograph** (a photographic JPG/PNG image, not a line-art SVG illustration) showing the product in context. **Intro copy.** A left-aligned ~672-pixel max-width column (anchored to the start of the section column, not centered) with 24-pixel vertical spacing between blocks: two ~16px normal muted paragraphs of product overview, then a ~16px semibold heading-color label ("Key Features and Benefits:"), then a **feature bullet list** — an outside disc list indented 16 pixels with 16-pixel spacing between items, each item a ~16px normal muted paragraph that begins with a ~16px semibold heading-color lead-in term (e.g. "Brilliant 4.5K Retina display:", "1080p FaceTime HD camera:", "Studio-quality mics for high-quality conversations:", "Six-speaker sound system:", "M1 chip:") followed by its explanatory text. **Product video.** With 24 pixels of vertical margin (48 from the medium breakpoint up), a full-width, host-rounded embedded video player that is 260 pixels tall (540 pixels from the medium breakpoint up). **Closing copy.** A left-aligned ~768-pixel max-width column (anchored to the start of the section column, not centered) with 24-pixel vertical spacing and 24 pixels below it (48 from the medium breakpoint up): two ~16px normal muted paragraphs covering connectivity and condition/warranty notes. **Show more.** A single bordered neutral "Show more..." link styled as a button on the host primary surface with 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium heading-color text, a neutral hover, and a focus ring. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The heading, paragraphs, feature list, video frame, and show-more button must all be rendered using the host design system's predefined components/tokens (surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, heading/muted text, hover/focus states). Treat the showcase image as a real photographic asset, not an illustration. The pixel values above define only spacing, sizing, and layout rhythm, not colors or chrome.

items.name: Flush Accordion Description Specs Questions Warranty
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce "product information" section: a flush (border-divided) accordion with four collapsible panels — Product description, Technical details, Questions, and Warranty. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); centered in a ~1280-pixel max-width container with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Accordion.** A flush accordion of four groups. Each **group header** is a full-width row with split ends, a 12-pixel gap, a bottom border rule, 20 pixels of vertical padding, a ~20px medium heading-color label (growing to ~24px from the small breakpoint up), and a 24-by-24-pixel chevron that flips with state. Each open **group body** carries a bottom border rule and 24 pixels of vertical padding (32 from the large breakpoint up). Groups, in order: - **Product description** (open by default): the same **alternating description rows** as variant 2 — a 24-pixel-spaced (64 from the large breakpoint up) stack of three two-column rows that alternate a 24-pixel-spaced muted text column (some paragraphs led by a semibold heading-color term) with a centered, large-screen-only **real product photograph** column (rear view, then front view, then side view). - **Technical details**: the same horizontally-scrollable, two-column striped **specification table** as variant 2 (Display, Processor, Video Support and Camera, Connections and Expansion, Wireless, In the Box, Height, Width, Depth, Weight). - **Questions**: a divided list of question-and-answer entries (a divider rule between each). Each entry is a 16-pixel-spaced block with 32 pixels of vertical padding; a row that, from the medium breakpoint up, reverses to place a non-shrinking **answer-count badge** (a small host-rounded chip in a soft success tint with success-foreground text, ~12px medium, 10px horizontal / 2px vertical padding, e.g. "1 answer", "3 answers", "12 answers") on the end and a ~20px semibold heading-color question on the start; a ~16px normal muted answer paragraph; and a ~14px medium muted "Answered … ago by" line whose author is a heading-color link that underlines on hover. Provide five entries. - **Warranty**: a single ~16px muted paragraph of warranty/returns text. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The accordion headers and chevrons, description rows and images, striped table, question entries and success badges, author links, and warranty text must all use the host design system's components/tokens (surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, heading/muted text, soft success tint). Treat every product image as a real photographic asset, not an illustration. Pixel values define only spacing, sizing, and layout rhythm.

items.name: Tabbed Description Reviews Questions Highlights
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce "product information" section: a tabbed interface with four panels — Description (with spec cards), Reviews (summary plus review list), Questions (Q&A accordion), and Highlights (feature cards) — plus a hidden report modal and a hidden write-a-review modal. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding; centered in a ~1280-pixel max-width container with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Tab strip.** A centered, ~14px medium muted tab list that gains a bottom border rule from the small breakpoint up; tabs wrap in a row with a 16-pixel horizontal gap. Each tab is a button with a 2-pixel bottom border and 12 pixels of padding; the active tab reads as selected and the rest darken on hover. Tabs, in order: "Description", "Reviews", "Questions", "Highlights". Only the active panel shows. **Description panel.** A grid that is one column by default and, from the large breakpoint up, five columns with a 32-pixel gap, with 16 pixels of vertical padding (32 from the small breakpoint up): - A **main column** spanning three of the five columns, a 24-pixel-spaced stack: two 24-pixel-spaced groups of ~16px muted description paragraphs (some led by a ~16px semibold heading-color term), a hidden duplicate "more info" group, and a **show-more** control — a ~16px medium brand-foreground row with a trailing 16-by-16-pixel chevron that underlines on hover. - A **spec aside** spanning two columns — one column by default (a 2-column grid below the large breakpoint), becoming an 8-pixel-spaced vertical stack from the large breakpoint up. Each **spec card** is a host-rounded panel on a soft secondary surface with a thin border and 16 pixels of padding (24 from the medium breakpoint up): a ~20px semibold heading-color title (e.g. "Display", "Processor", "RAM memory", "Storage") over a divider-separated definition list whose rows each split a ~14px medium heading-color term and a ~14px normal muted value across 8 pixels of vertical padding (e.g. Screen Type / light, Diagonal / 24 inches, Resolution / 4480 x 2520, Format / 4k). **Reviews panel.** A stack: - A **summary card** — a wrapped flex row on the host primary surface with a thin border, small shadow, and 16-to-32-pixel padding/gaps — holding: an **average rating** block (a ~30px bold "5/5", a ~16px muted "Average rating" label, and a row of five 20-by-20-pixel amber stars with a ~14px muted "(3,657 reviews)" count); a thin vertical divider (large screens only); a **clients** block (a ~30px bold "100M+", a ~16px muted "Worldwide Clients" label, and a 16-pixel-gap row of conventional partner brand logos kept as their own marks); another divider; and a **rate-product** block (a ~20px semibold heading-color prompt "Do you own or have you used the product?", a ~16px muted subline, a row of five 24-by-24-pixel muted outline stars with a ~14px medium "Give a note" link, and a brand "Write a customer review" button — solid brand surface, inverse text, 20px/8px padding, ~14px medium — that opens the review modal). - A **list controls row** that splits from the small breakpoint up: a ~14px heading-color "Showing 5,768 Customer Reviews" line (the number in a semibold span) and two **selects** (a review-type select defaulting to "All Reviews" and a time select defaulting to "Recently Added"), each a bordered, soft-input-surface, host-rounded select with ~14px text. - A **review list** — a divider-separated list with a top border rule, each review an article with 24 pixels of vertical padding: a header row with a 40-by-40-pixel host-rounded avatar (a **real photo**) beside a ~14px medium name and a ~14px muted "Total Reviews: N" line (the count in a heading-color span); a ~20px semibold heading-color review title; a row of five 16-by-16-pixel amber stars with a ~14px muted date; one or two ~16px muted body paragraphs; and a footer row with a small bordered neutral "Helpful (N)" button (~12px medium, 8px/6px padding) and, 16 pixels after it, a ~14px medium heading-color "Report" link with a leading 20-by-20-pixel flag glyph that opens the report modal. Provide five reviews. - A **pager**: a centered column with a ~14px muted "Showing 1 to 5 of 53 Customer Reviews" line (numbers in semibold heading-color spans) over two adjoining 32-pixel-tall buttons on a dark/inverse surface with inverse ~14px medium labels ("Previous" host-rounded on its start, "Next" host-rounded on its end). **Questions panel.** With 24 pixels above (32 from the small breakpoint up), a flush accordion of question entries: each **header** a full-width split-ends row with a 12-pixel gap, a bottom border rule, 20 pixels of vertical padding, a left-aligned ~20px semibold heading-color question, and a 20-by-20-pixel chevron; each open **body** a 16-pixel-spaced block with a bottom border rule and 20 pixels of vertical padding holding an author + date row (a ~16px semibold heading-color author and a ~14px muted timestamp), one or more ~16px muted answer paragraphs (some led by a ~16px semibold heading-color term), and a "Was it helpful to you?" row — a ~14px medium muted prompt beside two radio options ("Yes: N", "No: N"). Provide several entries (the first open). Below the accordion, with 24 pixels above (32 from the small breakpoint up), a ~18px muted "Didn't find the answer?" line with a brand underlined "Ask a question" link. **Highlights panel.** With 24 pixels above (32 from the small breakpoint up), a grid with a 16-pixel gap: one column by default, two from the small breakpoint up, three from the large. Each **highlight card** is a host-rounded panel on a soft secondary surface with a thin border and 16 pixels of padding: a ~16px muted eyebrow label (e.g. "Processor Model", "Graphics", "System Memory (RAM)", "Display Type", "Total Storage Capacity", "Screen Resolution"), a ~18px bold heading-color value beneath, a 16-pixel-vertical-margin check list with 4-pixel spacing (each item a row of a 20-by-20-pixel success-color check glyph and a ~16px muted label), and a ~16px medium brand-foreground link that underlines on hover. Provide six cards. **Report modal.** A hidden, fixed, centered, scrollable overlay holding a ~512-pixel-max-width host-rounded panel on the host primary surface with a shadow: a bordered header (a ~18px semibold heading-color "File a report" title and an icon-only close button with a small X glyph) and a form with 16-pixel-gapped fields — an issue-type radio group ("Report listing abuse", "Report a violation"), a "Report reason" text input, a "Describe your issue" textarea (~6 rows), an "Add an attachment" file input, and a terms-agreement checkbox with an inline brand link — over a bordered footer with a brand "Send report" submit button and a bordered neutral "Cancel" button. **Review modal.** A hidden, fixed, centered, scrollable overlay holding a ~672-pixel-max-width host-rounded panel on the host primary surface with a shadow: a bordered header (a ~18px semibold heading-color "Add a review for:" title over a brand product-name link, plus a top-end icon-only close button) and a form with 16-pixel-gapped fields — a star-rating row (five 24-by-24-pixel stars, amber for the chosen rating and muted after, with a ~18px bold "3.0 out of 5" label), a "Review title" text input, a "Review description" textarea (~6 rows) with a ~12px muted "Send a report" hint, a "Add real photos of the product" **dropzone** (a 208-pixel- tall dashed-border soft-secondary upload area with an upload glyph, a "Click to upload or drag and drop" prompt, and a format/size hint), and a terms-agreement checkbox with an inline brand link — over a bordered footer with a brand "Add review" submit button and a bordered neutral "Cancel" button. **Design system rule.** Do not hardcode any styling. The tab strip, description paragraphs and show-more link, spec cards and definition lists, reviews summary (rating, partner logos, rate-product block), list controls and selects, review articles (avatars, ratings, helpful/report controls), dark pager, questions accordion and helpfulness radios, highlight cards and check glyphs, and both modals (inputs, textareas, file/dropzone uploads, checkboxes, buttons) must all use the host design system's components/tokens (surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, brand/heading/muted text, amber rating stamp, success-color stamp, soft secondary and soft input surfaces, dark/inverse surface, hover/focus states). Treat review avatars and any product photos as real photographic assets, and keep partner brand logos as their own conventional marks. Pixel values define only spacing, sizing, and layout rhythm.

items.name: Image Background Hero With Overlapping Category Icons
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce storefront hero section. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the secondary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (growing to 64 pixels from medium up). **Image hero.** A full-bleed banner whose background is a cover-positioned, centered, non-repeating image. Over it, a centered content column capped at about a 2xl max-width with 16 pixels of horizontal padding, 8 pixels of top padding (growing to 64 from large), and 128 pixels of bottom padding (leaving room for the overlapping grid below). The text is centered: - A large display heading about 36 pixels (scaling to ~60 on large), semibold, tight line-height and tracking, in the brand-strong foreground color (such as "Don't miss out on exclusive deals."). - A supporting paragraph with 32 pixels of vertical margin in the brand foreground color, up to about 20 pixels on large screens. - A primary brand-filled button (such as "Shop now"). **Overlapping category grid.** A max-width container of about 1280 pixels pulled upward by 80 pixels so it overlaps the bottom of the banner, with 16 pixels of horizontal padding. It is a rounded, thin-bordered card on a soft primary surface with a small shadow and 32 pixels of vertical padding (32 pixels all around from medium up), laid out as a responsive grid: 2 columns on mobile, 3 from small, 4 from medium, and 8 from large, with a 16-pixel column gap and 32-pixel row gap. Each cell is centered and holds: - A 64-by-64-pixel square icon tile with host-token rounded corners, a thin border, a muted neutral fill, and a subtle hover surface, centering an icon glyph about 20 pixels (growing to ~36 on large) in the body color, with 16 pixels beneath the tile. - A category label link of about 18 pixels, medium weight, in the heading color, that underlines on hover (such as "Servers", "Fashion", "Electronics", "Gaming", "TV/Projectors", "Toys", "Sport", "Grocery"). **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels. Type sizes, the background image treatment, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; spacing and the icon-tile size are fixed in pixels. **Button padding rule.** The hero button uses padding-left 24px, padding-right 24px, padding-top 14px, and padding-bottom 14px. **Mobile layout rule.** On mobile the hero text stays centered with the button beneath it, and the overlapping category grid drops to two columns while keeping its upward overlap onto the banner.

items.name: Threaded QA With Sort Search And Ask Drawer
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce help-center threaded Q&A: a heading with a sort select, search field, and ask action, an alternating stack of question cards and indented answer cards (with helpful-vote controls), pagination, and an "ask a question" side drawer. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section (and its drawer) so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1024 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up) and a 24-pixel rhythm between regions. **Header.** A block that becomes a bottom-aligned space-between row with a 16-pixel gap from the large breakpoint up: a non-shrinking, growing ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Questions (147)", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) and a **controls cluster** (16px above it on mobile; becoming an end-aligned, 16-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up): a non-shrinking **sort select** (host select input, options "Most helpful" / "Most recent", host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, ~10px vertical / ~10px start / ~40px end padding for its chevron, ~14px text, screen-reader-only label) and a search form pairing the same **search field** as variant 1 (capped ~384 pixels) with an **"Ask a question" brand button** that opens the side drawer. **Thread.** A stack with a consistent **24-pixel gap between every card** — including between each question card and its following answer card, and between one question/answer pair and the next — so the cards never sit flush against each other: - **Question cards** — a card with a ~12-pixel internal rhythm, host rounded corners, a thin border, the host primary/neutral surface, a small shadow, and 24px padding: a header row (12-pixel gap) with a ~16px semibold hover-underline author link and a ~14px muted timestamp; a ~16px muted question body; and a footer row (16-pixel gap) pairing a ~14px medium muted "I have the same question" prompt with a **helpful/vote radio pair** (per the vote rule, e.g. "Yes: 8" / "No: 0"). - **Answer cards** — the same card indented ~48px from the start at the small breakpoint up, leading with an **"Answer" success badge** (inline-flex, host rounded corners, ~10px/2px padding, ~12px medium label, leading 12-by-12-pixel check glyph), then the same author/timestamp header, a ~16px muted answer body, and a footer pairing a ~14px medium muted "Was it helpful to you?" prompt with a helpful/vote radio pair. Use about four question/answer pairs. **Vote radio rule.** A helpful/vote pair is two single-select radios (16-by-16 pixels) with ~14px medium labels 8px after them (e.g. "Yes: 8" and "No: 0"), grouped on one row with a 16-pixel gap and rendered as the host design system's radio component. **Pager.** A centered joined numbered pager (24px above it, 32 from the small breakpoint up, 48 from the large breakpoint up): a 32px-tall row with overlapping 1px borders of a previous-arrow control (leading rounded side), numbered page links (~14px, ~12px horizontal padding), an overflow ellipsis, the last page, and a next-arrow control (trailing rounded side); the current page uses the host's brand-tinted surface, border, and text. **Ask drawer.** A right-anchored, full-height side drawer (full-width, capped ~448 pixels, ~16px padding, host surface, slide-in transition): a ~14px semibold, uppercase muted "Ask a question" label, a top-right icon-only close button (~20px glyph), and the shared ask-a-question form (from variant 1) in a single-column arrangement (the type and priority selects stacked), ending with a full-width "Submit question" brand button. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the sort select, search field, ask button, question/answer cards, the "Answer" badges, the vote radios, author links, the pager, and the drawer with its form controls and buttons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the sort select, the search input, the vote radios, and the drawer's textarea/selects/file/checkbox — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Ask a question" and "Submit question" primary buttons use ~20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with ~14px medium labels; the pager controls are 32px-tall with ~12px horizontal padding; the drawer close is an icon-only button; primaries use the host brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1024 pixels, the search field at ~384 pixels, the answer-card indent at ~48 pixels, the drawer at ~448 pixels, the badge glyph at 12-by-12 pixels, the vote radios at 16-by-16 pixels, and the pager row at 32 pixels tall. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/semantic accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The header stacks the title over the sort/search/ask controls until the small/large breakpoints; the answer cards lose their indent below the small breakpoint; the drawer spans the available width up to its cap; the pager stays centered.

items.name: FAQ Contact Info With Accordion
items.promptText:
Create a FAQ section split into two columns on large breakpoints inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding.

The **left column** is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a large left-aligned heading on its own line; a supporting paragraph directly beneath the heading at a comfortable reading width; a contact information block composed of two inline groups on the same baseline — the first group pairs a small location icon on the left with a multi-line address to its right, the second group pairs a small information icon on the left with a contact label and a linked email address to its right; and a compact button on its own line below the contact block whose label is preceded by a small leading icon.

The **right column** contains a vertical stack of accordion items with consistent spacing between them. Each item follows the same collapsible pattern: a horizontal row composed of a small question-mark icon on the left, a bold question label to the right of the icon on the same baseline, and a small chevron icon anchored to the far right of the row. When expanded, the chevron rotates and a content region appears directly below the question row containing one or more paragraphs of answer text at a comfortable reading width; inline text links may appear within the answer copy.

On narrow viewports stack the two columns vertically with the intro-and-contact column first and the accordion column directly below it; keep all internal stacks in their original reading order.

items.name: Static FAQ Answer Grid
items.promptText:
Create a FAQ section inside a centered page container with comfortable side padding. At the top, place a large left-aligned heading on its own line.

Below the heading, place one large rounded container that spans the full container width. Inside that container, arrange almost 16 FAQ entries in two equal-width columns on large breakpoints with consistent gutters between them. Each entry is a left-aligned vertical stack containing, in order: a horizontal row composed of a small question-mark icon anchored to the left and a bold question title to its right on the same baseline; a multi-paragraph answer block directly below the question row, left-aligned and matching the column width with comfortable internal padding. All entries are permanently visible (no accordion collapse). Inline text links may appear within the answer copy.

Distribute the entries evenly between the two columns so they read in a balanced left-to-right top-to-bottom order.

On narrow viewports collapse the two columns into a single column; stack all entries vertically in reading order while preserving comfortable spacing between them.

items.name: Return Form Step Select Items
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce return-flow step: the first screen of a multi-step "item return" wizard, with the form heading, a five-step progress tracker, a selectable list of returnable items, and back/next actions.
