Each step is a row with an 8-pixel gap that becomes a centered column (6-pixel gap) and grows equally from the medium breakpoint up (back to intrinsic width from the large breakpoint up), holding a 20-by-20-pixel check-circle glyph and a ~14px medium tight-leading label. A step that is done/active uses the brand foreground; an upcoming step uses the muted color. Between steps sits a thin 1-pixel-tall connector line that stays narrow — about 16 pixels wide (at most ~24 pixels at the large breakpoint up; deliberately short so the steps never stretch past the tracker's edges) — in the divider color, hidden on mobile and shown from the medium breakpoint up. The five steps are "My items", "Return reason", "Delivery option", "Refund choice", "Confirmation"; on this screen only "My items" is active (brand) and the other four are muted. **Step body.** A block with 24 pixels between its parts: a ~20px semibold heading-color subtitle ("1. Select the item you want to return:") over a divided card. **Item list.** A single card with thin internal row dividers, hidden overflow, host rounded corners, a thin default border, the host primary/neutral surface, and a small shadow. Each row is a 32-pixel-gapped, 24-pixel-padded row (top-aligned at the small breakpoint, vertically centered at the base and large breakpoints): - A **selection checkbox** (16-by-16 pixels, host rounded corners) with a screen-reader-only label. - A **growing content area** (min-width-0, becoming a 56-pixel-gapped vertically-centered row from the large breakpoint up) split into: an **item cell** (min-width-0, capped ~576 pixels, becoming a 24-pixel-gapped vertically-centered row from the small breakpoint up) pairing a 56-by-56-pixel square item-image link (16px beneath it on mobile, removed from the small breakpoint up) with a ~16px medium hover-underline item name; and a **meta cell** (16px above it on mobile; a column of two 8-pixel-gapped rows that becomes a justified row from the small breakpoint up and a left-aligned column again from the large breakpoint up) holding two label/value pairs (10-pixel gap): an "Order Number:" muted term (about 144 pixels wide from the large breakpoint up) with a hover-underline order-number value, and a "Return Term:" muted term with a date value. Use about five items (one pre-checked) with long descriptive names, order numbers, and return-term dates. **Actions.** A 16-pixel-gapped group that becomes a vertically-centered row from the small breakpoint up: a secondary "Cancel" button (full-width, auto-width from the small breakpoint up) and a primary "Next: Return reason" button (16px top margin on mobile only, full-width then auto-width from the small breakpoint up). **Design system rule.** Every component here — the step tracker, checkboxes, links, the item list/cards, and the back/next buttons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — radios, checkboxes, text inputs, and textareas — and every button must be the host design system's own form-control and button components, with their fills, borders, checked/selected states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Cancel" secondary button and the "Next: Return reason" primary button use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the primary uses the design system's brand button (brand fill/border, on-brand label, hover, focus ring), the secondary the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the form at ~1024 pixels, the item cell at ~576 pixels, the item image at 56-by-56 pixels, the step glyph at 20-by-20 pixels, the order-number term at ~144 pixels (from the large breakpoint up), and the step connector kept narrow at ~16 pixels wide (at most ~24 pixels from the large breakpoint up). Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The step tracker stacks vertically (its connectors hidden) and becomes a centered row from the medium breakpoint up; each item row stacks its image, name, and meta until the small/large breakpoints align them; the action buttons stack full-width until the small breakpoint, then sit auto-width in a row.

In particular, every form control — radios, checkboxes, text inputs, and textareas — and every button must be the host design system's own form-control and button components, with their fills, borders, checked/selected states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. items.name: Return Form Step Return Reason
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce return-flow step: the "return reason" screen of the item-return wizard, with the shared heading/tracker, a single-item summary, a two-panel condition/reason picker (each with an "other reason" modal), an informational note, and back/next actions. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame & header.** The same frame, heading ("Item return form"), and five-step tracker as step 1 (see "1-return-form-step-select-items"); on this screen the first two steps — "My items" and "Return reason" — are active (brand) and the remaining three are muted. **Step body.** A block with 24 pixels between its parts: a ~20px semibold heading-color subtitle ("2. Select the reason for returning:") with a ~16px muted helper line beneath it; then a single-item summary card, the two picker panels, an alert, and the actions. **Item summary card.** A divided card (host rounded corners, thin border, host primary/neutral surface, small shadow, hidden overflow) holding one 24-pixel-padded row that becomes a 56-pixel-gapped vertically-centered row from the medium breakpoint up: an **item cell** (min-width-0, capped ~672 pixels, a 24-pixel-gapped row from the small breakpoint up) pairing a 56-by-56-pixel square item-image link with a ~16px medium hover-underline item name; and a **meta cell** holding the same "Order Number:" and "Return Term:" label/value pairs as step 1. **Picker panels.** A grid (one column, two from the large breakpoint up) with a 24-pixel gap. Each panel has 24 pixels between its parts, host rounded corners, a thin border, the host primary/neutral surface, 16 pixels of padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up), and a small shadow: - **Condition panel** — a ~16px medium heading-color question ("What is the condition of the item?"), a radio group (16 pixels between rows) of five single-select radios with ~14px muted labels (one pre-selected), e.g. "I want to return a sealed item", "I want to return a mistaken order", "I want to return a functional but unsealed item", "I want to return a non-functional but unsealed item", "The item was not delivered"; then a secondary "Other condition" button (full-width, auto-width from the small breakpoint up) opening the condition modal. - **Reason panel** — a ~16px medium heading-color question ("What is the main reason for returning the item?"), a checkbox group (16 pixels between rows) of five multi-select checkboxes with ~14px muted labels (two pre-checked), e.g. "Defective or Damaged Item", "Incorrect Item Received", "Unsatisfactory Quality", "Changed Mind/Not as Expected", "Misleading Item Information"; then a secondary "I have another reason" button (full-width, auto-width from the small breakpoint up) with a leading 16-by-16-pixel edit glyph, opening the reason modal. **Reason modals.** Two centered, scroll-locked overlay modals, each a ~448-pixel panel on a neutral surface with host rounded corners, a shadow, and 16 pixels of padding (20 from the small breakpoint up): a ~14px medium label (8px beneath it) over a four-row textarea (16px beneath it, 20 from the small breakpoint up), then a centered pair of equal-width buttons (16-pixel gap, 12px horizontal / 8px vertical padding) — a primary "Add condition" / "Add your reason" and a secondary "Close". **Informational alert.** A full-width note on a soft brand-tinted surface with host rounded corners, 16 pixels of padding, and ~14px brand-toned text (~16px from the small breakpoint up). **Actions.** A 16-pixel-gapped group (a row from the small breakpoint up): a secondary "Prev: Choose the item" button and a primary "Next: Delivery method" button (same styling/behavior as step 1's actions). **Design system rule.** Every component here — the step tracker, radios, checkboxes, the item/picker cards, the modal textareas and buttons, the alert, and the back/next buttons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — radios, checkboxes, text inputs, and textareas — and every button must be the host design system's own form-control and button components, with their fills, borders, checked/selected states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The back/next and "Other condition" / "I have another reason" buttons use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the modal buttons use 12px horizontal / 8px vertical padding; primaries use the design system's brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the form at ~1024 pixels, the summary item cell at ~672 pixels, each modal at ~448 pixels, the item image at 56-by-56 pixels, and the step glyph at 20-by-20 pixels. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and brand accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The picker panels stack to one column (two from the large breakpoint up); the item summary stacks image/name over meta until the small/medium breakpoints align them; the panel buttons are full-width until the small breakpoint; the action buttons stack full-width until the small breakpoint, then sit auto-width in a row.

items.name: Centered Promo With Brand Links And App Badges
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce footer that opens with a centered conversion CTA, then a brand/links/app-badge row, then a legal + social bottom bar. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this footer so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Footer frame.** A full-width footer on the host primary surface; content centered in a max-width container with a hard cap of 1280 pixels and 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **CTA block.** A centered block with ~48px of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up): a center-aligned ~30px bold heading-color headline (~24px on mobile, e.g. "No long-term contracts. No catches. Simple."), a ~16px muted subtitle 12px below (e.g. "Start your 30-day free trial. Cancel anytime."), and a centered, 12-pixel-gapped button row 32px below — a **secondary "View demo" button** (bordered neutral, ~18px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium label, leading 20-by-20-pixel play-circle glyph) and a **primary "Get started" brand button** (~18px horizontal / 10px vertical padding, ~14px medium label). **Brand/links/app region.** A block separated from the CTA above it by a **full-width border drawn from the design system's border token** that runs the full width of the container as the midway divider between the two regions, with ~32px of vertical padding (48 from the medium breakpoint up); laid out as a top-aligned space-between row from the large breakpoint up (stacked with 32-pixel spacing otherwise): - A growing **brand column**: a row pairing a ~32px-tall logo mark with a ~18px semibold heading-color brand name (8px gap); a ~14px muted two-line description 24px below; and a wrapping, 16-pixel-gapped **nav-link row** 32px below of ~14px medium heading-color hover-color links ("Overview", "Features", "Pricing", "Careers", "Help", "Privacy"). - An **app column** two **app-store badge buttons** stacked 12px apart — each a dark pill (host rounded corners, ~16px horizontal / 8px vertical padding, ~40px tall) holding a store glyph beside a two-line label (~10px caption over ~14px semibold store name: "App Store", "Google Play"). **Bottom bar.** A block separated from the region above it by a **full-width border drawn from the design system's border token** running the full container width as the midway divider, with ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up); laid out as a space-between, vertically-centered row from the small breakpoint up (stacked with 16-pixel spacing otherwise): a ~14px muted copyright line ("© [year] [Brand]. All rights reserved.") and a **social row** — a 20-pixel-gapped row of icon-only links, each a 20-by-20-pixel brand social glyph in muted color shifting to the heading color on hover, keeping their own recognizable marks. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the CTA heading/subtitle, the "View demo" and "Get started" buttons, the logo and brand name, the description, the nav-link row, the "Get the app" label, the app-store badges, the copyright, and the social icons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. Every button or link must be the host design system's own button and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; the app-store pills' dark fill and the social marks may keep their conventional appearance, but their surrounding spacing, radii, and states still follow design-system tokens. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "View demo" (secondary bordered) and "Get started" (brand) buttons use ~18px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with ~14px medium labels; the app-store badges use ~16px horizontal / 8px vertical padding; the social links are icon-only. Primaries use the host brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the logo at ~32 pixels tall, the CTA play glyph at 20-by-20 pixels, the app-store badges at ~40 pixels tall, the social glyphs at 20-by-20 pixels, the headline at ~30px, and nav/links at ~14px. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The CTA block stays centered and stacks its buttons-row below the subtitle (buttons may go full-width); the brand/links/app region stacks the brand column above the app column until the large breakpoint; the bottom bar stacks the copyright above the social row until the small breakpoint.

items.name: Newsletter Social Grid And Store Locator Bar
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce footer with a newsletter + social top bar, a large multi-group link grid, a centered payment-logo band, and a bottom area with a store-locator note, copyright, legal links, and a language dropdown. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this footer so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Footer frame.** A full-width footer on the host primary surface; each region's content is centered in a max-width container with a hard cap of 1280 pixels and 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Top bar.** A block with a **full-width bottom border drawn from the design system's border token** that runs the full width of the container as the midway divider between this region and the columns region, and ~32px of vertical padding, laid out as a space-between, vertically-centered row with a 16-pixel gap from the small breakpoint up (stacked otherwise): a full-width **newsletter form** — a row pairing a relative, growing email field (~16px end margin, capped ~384 pixels from the medium breakpoint up; host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, ~12px padding, ~14px text, "Enter your email address" placeholder, label visually hidden) with a "Subscribe" brand button (~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding, ~14px medium label) — and a **social row** (16px above it on mobile, end-aligned from the small breakpoint up) of ~8px-gapped icon-only social links, each a 40-by-40-pixel host-rounded ghost button holding a 24-by-24-pixel brand social glyph with a hover fill. **Columns region.** A block with ~24px of vertical padding (64 from the small breakpoint up, 32 from the medium breakpoint up): a one-column grid that becomes two columns from the small breakpoint up and four from the large breakpoint up, with 32-pixel gaps. Each grid cell **stacks several link groups** 24px apart (32 from the medium breakpoint up). Each link group is a ~14px semibold uppercase heading-color heading with 16px beneath it over a vertical list of muted links 12px apart that shift to the heading color on hover (headings such as "Make money with us", "Company", "Payment Methods", "Orders & Shipment"). **Payment band.** A full-width band on a soft secondary surface with **full-width top and bottom borders drawn from the design system's border token** that serve as the midway dividers separating it from the columns region above and the bottom area below, and ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up); inside the 1280-pixel-capped container a centered, wrapping row of payment/partner brand logos at ~40–44px tall with ~32px gaps (~64px from the small breakpoint up), each keeping its own mark. **Bottom area.** A block with ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up) in the 1280-pixel-capped container: a **store-locator note** with a bottom divider and ~16px bottom padding — a ~14px muted line ("More ways to shop: Find a [Brand] Store or other authorized retailer near you. In particular, every form control — the email input — and every button, link, or menu must be the host design system's own form-control, button, link, and menu components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; payment, social, and flag marks keep their conventional colors. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Subscribe" brand button uses ~20px horizontal / 12px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the social buttons are 40-by-40-pixel icon buttons; the language trigger is a ghost/text button (its menu rows use ~12px horizontal / ~8px vertical padding). Primaries use the host brand button. **Sizing rules.** The containers cap hard at 1280 pixels, the email field at ~384 pixels, the social buttons at 40-by-40 pixels around 24-by-24-pixel glyphs, the payment logos at ~40–44 pixels tall, the language flag glyph at ~20px, the menu at ~176 pixels, the menu flag thumbnails at ~16px, the group headings at ~14px, and link rows 12px apart. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The top bar stacks the newsletter form above the social row until the small breakpoint; the columns grid steps from one to two to four columns across the small and large breakpoints (each cell stacking its link groups); the payment band centers and wraps; the bottom area stacks the copyright, legal links, and language dropdown until the xl breakpoint.

items.name: Country Bar Language And Five Columns
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce footer with a country/language top bar, a five-column link grid, and a tinted legal bottom bar. Every interactive control — the language trigger, menu items, and links — must be the host design system's own button, menu, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded; flag glyphs may keep their conventional colors. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The language trigger is a ghost/text button with no box fill (its menu rows use ~12px horizontal / ~8px vertical padding); links are inline text links. All states follow the host design system. **Sizing rules.** The container and bottom-bar container cap hard at 1280 pixels, the logo at ~32 pixels tall, the country dots at 6-by-6 pixels, the language flag glyph at ~20px, the menu at ~176 pixels, the menu flag thumbnails at ~16px, the group headings at ~14px, and link rows 12px apart. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The top bar stacks the logo/country cluster over the language dropdown until the large breakpoint (the logo and country list stacking until the medium breakpoint); the columns grid steps from one to three to five columns across the small and xl breakpoints; the bottom bar's legal links and copyright are start/left-aligned on mobile and centered from the small breakpoint up, with the copyright always sitting on its own line 16px below the legal-links row.

The region carries 48 pixels of bottom space separating it from the bottom bar. **Bottom bar.** A block separated from the links region above it by a **full-width border drawn from the design system's border token** running the full container width as the midway divider, with ~24px of vertical padding (32 from the medium breakpoint up); laid out as a space-between, vertically-centered row from the small breakpoint up (stacked with 16-pixel spacing otherwise): a ~14px muted **status/copyright cluster** (a 16-pixel-gapped row pairing a "© [year] [Brand]" copyright with a status item — a small ~8px round success-tinted status dot, an "All Systems Operational" label, and a trailing ~12px external-link glyph) and a **social row** — a 20-pixel-gapped row of icon-only links, each a 20-by-20-pixel brand social glyph in muted color shifting to the heading color on hover, keeping their own recognizable marks. **Design system rule.** Every element here — the dark promo card, its headline/paragraph and pill button, the logo, the link groups and links, the copyright, the system-status item, and the social icons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. The card uses the host's inverse/dark surface token and the button the host's inverse/light button token (never hardcoded); every button or link must be the host design system's own button and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens; the status dot uses a semantic success token and the social marks may keep their conventional appearance. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The pill action button uses ~24px horizontal / 12px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label and host pill/full corners, rendered as the host's inverse/light button; links are inline text links and the social links are icon-only. **Sizing rules.** The container caps hard at 1280 pixels, the promo card radius is ~24 pixels, the card paragraph caps at ~620 pixels, the logo at ~24 pixels tall, the headline at ~32px, the status dot at ~8 pixels, the external-link glyph at ~12px, the social glyphs at 20-by-20 pixels, the group headings at ~16px, and link rows 12px apart. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand accent stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The promo card stays centered with reduced padding; the links region stacks the logo above the link grid until the large breakpoint, and the grid steps from two to three to five columns across the small and large breakpoints; the bottom bar stacks the status/copyright cluster above the social row until the small breakpoint.

items.name: Cart With Steps Warranty And Summary
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce shopping-cart page with a checkout-steps breadcrumb, a divided item list (quantity select, remove, delivery estimate, and optional warranty upsell), and a soft order-summary sidebar with account note and voucher form. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up). **Steps breadcrumb.** An ordered list capped to ~672 pixels, start/left-aligned (the steps cluster at the left edge, not centered), ~14px medium muted (~16px from the small breakpoint up). Three steps — "Cart" (active, brand color), "Payment", and "Order summary" — each lead with a check-circle glyph (16-by-16 pixels, 20-by-20 from the small breakpoint up, 8px before the label). On mobile the steps are separated by a small "/" divider; from the medium breakpoint up each of the first two steps instead shows a short thin horizontal connector line to the next (a fixed ~24px segment, ~40px from the xl breakpoint up — the steps stay packed to the left rather than stretching to fill the row) and the last step shows no connector. **Heading.** A ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Your Cart", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) 24 pixels below the breadcrumb (32 from the small breakpoint up). **Two-column layout.** A block 24 pixels below the heading (32 from the small breakpoint up) that becomes a top-aligned two-column row from the large breakpoint up with a 48-pixel column gap (64 from the xl breakpoint up): a **cart column** (growing, min-width-0) and a **summary sidebar**. **Item list.** The cart column is a list with thin row dividers and a bottom border. Each item is a top-aligned row with a 16-pixel gap and 16px vertical padding (the first row only pads its bottom): - A **item-image link** (40-by-40 pixels, never shrinking). - A **details cell** (growing, min-width-0, 12 pixels between its parts): a ~16px medium hover-underline item name; a space-between row (16-pixel gap) whose left cluster (16-pixel gap) holds a **quantity select** (a ~64-pixel-wide dropdown with host rounded corners, a thin border, a soft secondary fill, ~10px horizontal / 8px vertical padding, ~14px text, options 1–10, and a screen-reader-only label) and a "Remove" button (~14px medium danger color, underline on hover, leading 20-by-20-pixel close glyph 6px before the label), with a mobile-only ~96-pixel right-aligned ~16px bold price (hidden from the small breakpoint up); a **delivery row** (8-pixel gap) pairing a 16-by-16-pixel muted shipping glyph with ~14px muted "Delivery on [date]" text; and, on some items, a **warranty upsell** (12 pixels between parts): a ~14px medium "Extend the standard warranty:" line over a radio group (8 pixels between rows) of single-select radios (16-by-16 pixels) with ~14px medium labels 8px after them, e.g. "Guarantee Plus 1 Year - $99" and "Guarantee Plus 2 Years - $199". - A **desktop-only price** (hidden until the small breakpoint up, ~96 pixels wide, right-aligned, ~16px bold). Use about five items, with at least one carrying the warranty upsell. **Order summary sidebar.** A right-pushed card 24 pixels below the list on mobile (32 from the small breakpoint up; flush to the top from the large breakpoint up), full-width then capped ~384 pixels at large and ~448 pixels at xl, with 24 pixels between its parts, host rounded corners, a thin border, a soft secondary surface, and 16 pixels of padding (24 from the medium breakpoint up): - A **totals group** rendered as a flow-root with thin dividers between rows, each row a space-between pair with 12px vertical padding (a ~16px normal muted term and a ~16px medium value): "Subtotal", "Savings" (success color), "Store Pickup", "Tax", and a ~16px bold "Total" row. - An **actions group** (12 pixels between parts): a primary "Proceed to Checkout" button spanning the full width of the summary card, then a ~14px muted note ("One or more items in your cart require an account.") containing a ~14px medium brand link ("Sign in or create an account now", underlined, no underline on hover). - A **voucher form** as a bottom-aligned row with a 16-pixel gap: a growing field (a ~14px medium "Do you have a voucher or gift card?" label 8px above a full-width text input with host rounded corners, a thin border, a neutral fill, 10px padding, and ~14px text) and a primary "Apply" button. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the steps breadcrumb, item rows, quantity selects, remove actions, warranty radios, delivery glyphs, the summary card, account link, and all buttons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the quantity select, the warranty radios, and the voucher text input — and every button must be the host design system's own form-control and button components, with their fills, borders, checked/selected states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Proceed to Checkout" and "Apply" primary buttons use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the quantity select uses ~10px horizontal / 8px vertical padding; the inline "Remove" action is a text+glyph button with no box padding; all use the host design system's brand or neutral component as appropriate. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the breadcrumb at ~672 pixels, the summary sidebar at ~384/~448 pixels (large/xl), the item image at 40-by-40 pixels, the quantity select at ~64 pixels wide, the breadcrumb glyphs at 16/20 pixels, the delivery glyph at 16-by-16 pixels, the warranty radios at 16-by-16 pixels, and the price cells at ~96 pixels. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/success accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The breadcrumb steps stay left-aligned, using "/" separators on mobile and short fixed connector lines from the medium breakpoint up (never stretching to fill the row); each item shows its price inline (mobile) versus in a trailing column (from the small breakpoint up); the cart column and summary sidebar stack until the large breakpoint, where they sit side by side with the sidebar pinned to the right.

items.name: Cart With Volume Discount Progress And Totals Panel
items.promptText: Create a self-contained, narrow-column software / digital-product cart: a title, a single-item volume-discount progress meter, a divided item list (segmented license-quantity steppers with inline price and favorite/remove text actions), a coupon link, and a soft totals panel — sized for a single column, drawer, or sidebar. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Frame.** A centered single column capped to about 512 pixels wide on the host primary surface, with comfortable vertical padding. The header and the volume-discount progress block are each closed by a full-width bottom border with 32px padding-bottom and 32px margin-bottom (see below); the remaining regions use full-width thin horizontal dividers in the divider color. **Header.** A ~20px semibold heading-color title ("My Shopping Cart", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) styled exactly like variant 2's heading. The header closes with a full-width bottom border, 32 pixels of padding beneath the title, and 32 pixels of margin separating it from the next block. **Volume-discount progress.** Below the header: a ~14px message in muted text, scoped to the single item in the cart, with the incentive and threshold emphasized in heading-color bold (e.g. "Add **1 more license** to unlock a **20% volume discount**."). Beneath it (~8px) a **progress meter** — a full-width ~6–8px-tall rounded track on a soft secondary surface with a brand-filled portion (host rounded corners) showing the current license count's progress toward the discount threshold. Beneath the meter (~8px) a ~13px medium brand link ("See volume pricing") carrying a trailing ~16px arrow glyph. This whole progress block closes the same way as the header — a full-width bottom border, 32 pixels of padding beneath it, and 32 pixels of margin before the item list. **Item list.** A vertical list with thin row dividers; each row has ~16px of vertical padding and is a top-aligned row with a ~16px gap: - A **thumbnail** — a ~56-by-56-pixel square holding the software item's app icon/logo, never shrinking. - A **details cell** (growing, min-width-0, ~12px between its parts): a ~16px medium heading-color software item name (e.g. a plan/license such as "Design Suite Pro — Annual License"); a row (~16px gap, vertically centered) holding a **segmented license-quantity stepper** — a single bordered, host-rounded control split into a "−" button, a center ~14px medium license-count value, and a "+" button, each segment a ~32-by-32-pixel tap target with a muted glyph, internal dividers between segments, and host hover/focus states with a focus ring — followed by the item **price** as a ~16px bold heading-color amount; and an **actions row** (~16px gap) with two text+glyph buttons: "Move to Favorites" (~14px medium muted, leading ~16–20px heart glyph, heading-color + underline on hover) and "Remove" (~14px medium danger color, leading ~16–20px trash glyph, underline on hover). Use a single software item (one license/subscription) with its name, license quantity, and price — the cart is built around this one item. **Coupon link.** Below the list, a ~14px medium brand link ("Add coupon code"). **Totals panel.** A soft secondary, host-rounded filled panel containing a stack of space-between label/value rows, each with ~12–16px vertical padding and separated by thin dividers: "Subtotal", "Savings" (a success-color value), "Store Pickup", and "Tax" — each a ~14–16px normal muted term with a ~14–16px medium heading-color value — then a final **"Total"** row with a ~16px bold term and a ~16px bold value. **Design system rule.** Every component here — the volume-discount progress meter, item rows, thumbnails, segmented license-quantity steppers, favorite/remove actions, the coupon link, and the totals panel and its rows/dividers — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the stepper buttons and quantity value — and every button or link must be the host design system's own form-control, button, and link components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The segmented stepper uses ~32-by-32-pixel icon segments around a ~14px medium value; the "Move to Favorites" and "Remove" actions are text+glyph buttons with no box padding; the "How can I get this?" and "Add coupon code" links are inline text links — all driven by the host design system's button and link components. **Sizing rules.** The column caps at ~512 pixels, the thumbnail is 56-by-56 pixels, the stepper segments are ~32-by-32 pixels, the progress meter is ~6–8 pixels tall, the inline action and link glyphs are ~16–20 pixels, the title is ~20/24px, and the header and volume-discount progress blocks each have a bottom border with 32px of padding-bottom and 32px of margin-bottom. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/success accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The column spans the available width up to its ~512-pixel cap; the progress meter and its message stay full-width; each item row keeps its thumbnail beside the details cell, with the stepper, price, and favorite/remove actions stacking within the details cell as space narrows; the totals panel stays full-width.

items.name: Compact Cart Table With Summary
items.promptText: Create a self-contained e-commerce shopping-cart page in a compact, centered table layout: a heading, a horizontally-scrollable cart table (item, quantity stepper, price, remove), an order summary, and back/checkout actions. Do not generate any surrounding site chrome beyond what is described; output only this section so it can drop into any host page. All colors, borders, radii, shadows, and type come from the host design system; the pixel values below define spacing and sizing. **Section frame.** A full-width band on the host primary surface with 32 pixels of vertical padding (64 from the medium breakpoint up); content centered in a max-width container of about 1280 pixels with 16 pixels of horizontal padding (0 from the 2xl breakpoint up), and inside that a centered inner column capped to about 768 pixels. A ~20px semibold heading-color title ("Shopping Cart", ~24px from the small breakpoint up) sits at the top. **Cart table.** A horizontally-scrollable wrapper 24 pixels below the heading (32 from the small breakpoint up) with a bottom divider border. Inside, a full-width left-aligned ~16px table that uses a fixed layout from the medium breakpoint up, with thin row dividers between body rows. Each row has four cells: - **Item cell** (~384 pixels wide, ~224 minimum, no wrapping, 16px vertical padding): a hover-underline medium link that is a 16-pixel-gapped vertically-centered row of a 40-by-40-pixel square item image and the item name. - **Quantity cell** (16px padding): a **quantity stepper** identical to variant 1 — a 20-by-20-pixel decrement button (host rounded corners, thin border, soft secondary fill, hover, focus ring) with a ~10-pixel minus glyph, a 40-pixel-wide borderless transparent center-aligned ~14px medium numeric input, and a matching increment button with a ~10-pixel plus glyph. - **Price cell** (16px padding, right-aligned, ~16px bold). - **Remove cell** (16px vertical padding): a right-pushed icon-only remove button (host rounded corners, 8px padding, muted color, soft fill + heading color on hover, 20-by-20-pixel trash glyph) with a screen-reader-only "Remove" label and a hover tooltip. Use about seven items with individual quantities and prices. **Order summary.** A block 16 pixels below the table: a ~20px semibold heading-color "Order summary" title, then a body 24px below it with 16 pixels between groups — a tight 8-pixel-spaced group of space-between label/value rows (~16px normal muted term, ~16px medium value) for "Original price", "Savings" (a success-color negative value), "Store Pickup", and "Tax", then a "Total" row separated by a top divider with 8px of padding above it and a ~16px bold term and value. **Actions.** A group 24 pixels below the summary with a 16-pixel gap that becomes a centered row from the small breakpoint up: a secondary "Continue Shopping" button (full-width, centered label) and a primary "Proceed to Checkout" button (16px top margin on mobile only, full-width, removed top margin from the small breakpoint up). **Design system rule.** Every component here — the cart table and its dividers, the item links, quantity steppers, remove buttons, tooltips, and the back/checkout buttons — must be rendered as an instance of the host design system's predefined component, and all colors, fills, borders, radii, shadows, dividers, hover/focus/active states, focus rings, and typography (font family, sizes, weights, letter-spacing) must come from the host design system's tokens. In particular, every form control — the numeric quantity input and the stepper buttons — and every button must be the host design system's own form-control and button components, with their fills, borders, states, focus rings, and label typography taken only from design-system tokens and never hardcoded. Do not hardcode styles and do not introduce any non-design-system, non-agnostic values; the pixel measurements here only fix dimensions, spacing, and layout. **Button padding rule.** The "Continue Shopping" secondary and "Proceed to Checkout" primary buttons use 20px horizontal / 10px vertical padding with a ~14px medium label; the stepper buttons are 20-by-20-pixel icon buttons; the remove button uses 8px padding around a 20-by-20-pixel glyph; primaries use the design system's brand button and secondaries the bordered neutral button. **Sizing rules.** The container caps at ~1280 pixels, the inner column at ~768 pixels, the item cell at ~384 pixels (≥~224), the item image at 40-by-40 pixels, the stepper buttons at 20-by-20 pixels, the numeric input at 40 pixels wide, and the remove glyph at 20-by-20 pixels. Type, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows, and the brand/success accents stay agnostic and follow the host design system; padding, gaps, and control sizing are fixed in pixels. **Mobile layout rule.** The table scrolls horizontally within its wrapper on narrow screens (becoming a fixed layout from the medium breakpoint up); the action buttons stack full-width until the small breakpoint, then sit centered in a row.
